pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh documentation

ForkMesh keeps the source code and releases of a project reachable and
verifiable when a hosting provider, domain or network fails it. Git stays the
source of truth; signed repositories replicate to independent mirrors, and the
desktop, web and phone apps work on them through one protocol.

This folder is the one source of truth for every ForkMesh document. It is
published at [forkmesh.com/docs](https://forkmesh.com/docs/library/), in the
desktop app's Docs tab and in the phone apps, with
[page history](https://forkmesh.com/docs/history/) and a
[document index](https://forkmesh.com/docs/documents/).

```text
   your desktop node        independent mirrors          phones · browser
   holds and serves         carry copies, serve          read, review, commit,
   your repositories        clone and fetch              steer agents
          │                        ▲                           │
          │ signed push            │ signed refs events        │ HTTPS
          ▼                        │                           ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  three equal core nodes · DNS round robin · no proxy in front        │
  │  accounts · web app · Git over HTTPS · chat · routing catalog        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            every record is signed, so any copy can be checked
```

## The six pillars

Everything ForkMesh promises rests on six short pages. Read them in order the
first time; each one links to the full detail.

```text
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │       Code and releases stay reachable and provably authentic,      │
    │           whichever host, domain, account or network fails          │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐
    │    1    │ │    2    │ │    3    │ │    4    │ │    5    │ │    6    │
    │         │ │         │ │         │ │         │ │         │ │         │
    │  Archi- │ │ Encryp- │ │ Mirror- │ │  Self-  │ │ Censor- │ │  Threat │
    │ tecture │ │   tion  │ │   ing   │ │ hosting │ │   ship  │ │  model  │
    │         │ │         │ │         │ │         │ │  resil- │ │         │
    │         │ │         │ │         │ │         │ │  ience  │ │         │
    └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
           Git, signed .forkmesh/ records and an open protocol suite
```

| | Pillar | Read it to learn | In one line |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🏗️ | **[Architecture and availability](architecture.md)** | How the network is built, and why no single server has to stay up | Three equal cores behind DNS round robin; with two down the third serves read-only |
| 🔐 | **[Encryption and signatures](encryption.md)** | What is signed and encrypted, with which algorithms, and the known gaps | Ed25519 everywhere; chat, calls and private repositories use X25519 + ML-KEM-768 |
| 🪞 | **[Mirroring and software distribution](mirroring.md)** | How copies stay in step, how clones are verified, how releases reach users | Clones go only to a mirror whose refs match the signed pin, and fail closed otherwise |
| 🏠 | **[Self-hosting](self-hosting.md)** | Run a node, a mirror, an instance or a fleet yourself | Four levels, from a desktop node to a fleet; an instance takes about 15 minutes |
| 🛡️ | **[Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)** | What still works when a host, domain, account or network is blocked | Mirrors, Tor and I2P transports, USB bundles and portable keys, with the limits stated |
| 🎯 | **[Threat model](protocol/threat-model.md)** | What the protocol defends against, and what is still open | A numbered register of threats, each with its severity, its status and the controls that answer it |

| 🛰️ | Fleet, deploys and operator tools | `deploy/`, `tools/next_*.py` | [operations/README.md](operations/README.md) |
| 📦 | Releases and installers | `tools/package/`, `.forkmesh/releases/` | [release/README.md](release/README.md) |

Special agents are workflows in `.forkmesh/workflows/`
([app/workflows.md](app/workflows.md#desktop-workflows-and-special-agents)):
[CFO](finance/cfo.md), [Hearth](community/hearth.md),
[Reddit scout](community/reddit.md), [site crawler](www/site-crawler.md) and
[Sentinel](security/sentinel.md). The
guide for outside coding agents is `app/public/forkmesh-agent.md`, served at
`https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md`. Keep it in step with
[instances](operations/instances.md), [start-config.md](start-config.md) and the
pull request section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`; `app/tests/test_start_instance_page.py`
checks the parts that must match.

## Writing docs

- **One home per topic.** Before adding a page, find the page that already
  covers the topic and extend it; link to it from elsewhere instead of
  repeating it. Summaries belong on the core pages above, detail on the area
  page.
- **Where a page goes.** User guides sit at the top of this folder (their
  addresses on forkmesh.com/docs stay fixed); everything else goes in the
  area folder of the code it describes. Source files hold no comments, so the
  reason behind a change goes on the page for that code (`AGENTS.md`).
- **Publishing.** `app/tools/docs_site.py` renders every page here except the
  internal `finance/`, `marketing/` and `community/` folders; the phone apps
  carry the user-facing areas. Code and tests read many pages by path: move or
  rename a page only together with every reference, and add a redirect in
  `www/public/_redirects` for a public address that goes away.
- **Look.** Open a page with one sentence on what it covers. Draw a diagram as
  a `text` code block of box-drawing characters (no emoji inside it, since
  they break the column widths); it renders the same on the site, in the
  desktop and in the phone apps. An icon is one emoji in a table's first
  column or at the start of a list item, never in a heading, so heading
  anchors stay the same in every renderer. Tables beat long paragraphs for
  lists of facts.
- **Style.** Short sentences, present tense, facts over stories. Say what still
  depends on one provider; never claim more than the design delivers.

pages.markdown:
# Architecture and availability

ForkMesh is built so that no single machine has to stay up for code to stay
reachable. Git data lives on hosts that developers and operators run; the
service at app.forkmesh.com runs on several equal core nodes that DNS hands out
in turn; independent mirrors serve clones on their own.

Part of the core documentation: [architecture](architecture.md) ·
[encryption](encryption.md) · [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) ·
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md) · [censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)
· [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).

```text
        browsers · desktop nodes · phones · mirrors · git
                           │
     DNS round robin: app.forkmesh.com, world.forkmesh.com
        (one A/AAAA record per healthy core, TTL 60 s)
           ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
        core n3         core n4         core n5      ◄─ WireGuard mesh
  Caddy · app · rqlite · Git gateway (each core is a full copy)
           ▲  outbound only: claim job, clone, run, push
     runner tier (untrusted, holds no core secrets)

  independent mirrors (anyone's server) ─► serve clones of the repositories they carry
  desktop nodes ─► hold and serve their own repositories
```

## The parts

| Part | What it does | Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop node | Holds bare repositories, serves clones, signs every record with its Ed25519 key, runs coding agents in isolated worktrees | `desktop/` |
| Mirror | A headless server that carries copies of repositories and serves `git clone` and `git fetch` | `server/` ([mirror node](operations/mirror-node.md)) |
| Core node | Accounts, the web app and API, Git over HTTPS, chat, the World, the routing catalog of mirrors | `app/`, `app/host/`, `server/` |
| Runner | Runs agent jobs and Actions in a per-job sandbox with a short-lived, single-branch push grant | `server/` |
| Phone apps | Mobile nodes with their own key and Git engine: they clone, commit and publish, and drive desktop agents; they never host or serve repositories to others ([phone apps](mobile/README.md)) | `native/` |

Collaboration records (issues, pull requests, reviews, discussions, releases)
are signed files under `.forkmesh/` in the repository, so every clone carries
them ([protocol](protocol/README.md)).

## No single point of failure

- **Equal cores, no leader in the request path.** Each core runs Caddy, the
  Python app, an rqlite (Raft) database member and the Go Git gateway. Any core
  answers any request. Membership, scheduled jobs and certificate renewal are
  leaderless: no core is special.
- **Direct DNS round robin.** `app.forkmesh.com` and `world.forkmesh.com` have
  one unproxied record per core with a 60-second TTL; clients connect straight
  to a core, with no proxy or CDN in between. A health loop probes every core's
  `/readyz` every 30 seconds and removes a core after three failures, so a dead
  core drops out of DNS within about two minutes. It never empties the set.
- **One core down:** the other two serve everything, reads and writes.
- **Two cores down:** the survivor has no database majority, so it switches to
  read-only mode on its own. Browsing, signed-in reads, `git clone`,
  `git fetch` and release downloads keep working from its full local copy;
  sign-in, pushes, edits and chat sends answer `503` with
  "ForkMesh is read-only while servers recover". It returns to normal when a
  second core comes back.
- **Per-core Git endpoints.** Every core also serves Git at its own name
  (`nN.next.forkmesh.com`) without touching the database, so a clone works even
  while the app is degraded.
- **Mirrors outside the fleet.** A public repository with a live mirror stays
  clonable when every ForkMesh server is unreachable: point Git at the mirror
  ([mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md)).
- **Untrusted work is separate.** Agent runs execute arbitrary code, so they run
  only on the runner tier, never on a core holding data or keys.

## What is still a dependency

We state these so nobody mistakes the design for more than it is:

- All three cores currently run with one hosting provider (Vultr) in one
  region. Losing that provider or region takes down the hosted service; mirrors
  and desktop nodes elsewhere keep serving their copies.
- DNS for forkmesh.com is one provider (Cloudflare DNS, unproxied for the app
  and World names). The website at `forkmesh.com` itself is still served from
  Cloudflare, and it forwards app paths such as `forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>`
  to the cores. `app.forkmesh.com` and the per-core names reach the cores
  directly.
- The DNS health loop runs on the operator's machine. If it stops, DNS keeps
  listing every core and clients still spread across them, but a failed core is
  not removed until it returns.
- Discovery of mirrors goes through the catalog on the cores; a mirror's own
  address works without it, but someone has to know that address.

## Where to read more

- Operators: [docs/operations/served-stack.md](operations/served-stack.md) (the served stack and read-only
  mode in detail), [docs/operations/README.md](operations/README.md) (runbook),
  [docs/codebase.md](codebase.md) (how the code fits together).
- Recovery from losing a domain, region, key or backup:
  [disaster recovery](disaster-recovery/README.md).
- What outside services see: [external dependency map](external-dependency-map.md).
- Developer index: [docs/README.md](README.md); public index:
  [README.md](README.md).

pages.markdown:
# Encryption and signatures

What ForkMesh signs, what it encrypts, with which algorithms, and what each
layer does not protect. Each section links the page with the full
specification.

Part of the core documentation: [architecture](architecture.md) ·
[encryption](encryption.md) · [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) ·
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md) · [censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)
· [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).

## At a glance

| What | Protection | Algorithms | Spec |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node and device identity | Signing key that never leaves the device | Ed25519 | [portable identities](portable-identities.md) |
| Issues, pull requests, reviews, releases | Signed records stored in the repository | Ed25519 over domain-separated canonical bytes | [signatures and authentication](protocol/signatures-and-authentication.md) |
| Requests from nodes (push, view, key rotation) | Time-bound signed proofs | Ed25519, 5-minute window, body digest bound | same |
| Repository integrity on mirrors | Signed refs digests; clones go only to a mirror whose refs match | SHA-256, Ed25519 | [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) |
| Chat in channels | Device-to-device sealing inside a room cipher | X25519 + ML-KEM-768 hybrid, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM | [chat encryption](security/sealed-chat.md) |
| Direct messages | The above plus a per-message ratchet and safety numbers | same | same |
| Group calls | Per-epoch media keys, signed frame digests, short verification code | X25519 + ML-KEM-768, AES-256-GCM, Ed25519 | `docs/server/call-e2ee.md` |
| Private repositories | Sealed on an authorized device before replication | AES-256-GCM content key wrapped to X25519 + ML-KEM-768 recipients | [private repository confidentiality](security/private-repository-confidentiality.md) |
| Stored service data | Row encryption and keyed lookups on the cores | AES-256-GCM under `DATA_KEY`; HMAC-SHA256 blind indexes | `docs/operations/rekey.md` |
| Service secrets | Sealed vault; nodes hold the key only in memory | HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM with per-row AAD | `docs/operations/vault.md` |
| Releases and installers | Signed manifest checked before install or update | Ed25519 key pinned in the installer and desktop | `docs/release/README.md` |
| Transport | HTTPS everywhere; WireGuard between cores | TLS (ACME certificates), WireGuard | [architecture](architecture.md) |
| Database backups | Pulled over SSH, verified, then stored only encrypted | age | `docs/operations/README.md` |
| Passwords | Salted hash; TOTP required for administrators | PBKDF2-SHA256 | `docs/app/auth-sessions.md` |

## Identity and signed records

Every desktop node, mirror and device has an Ed25519 key. Records are signed
over a frozen, scheme-specific prefix plus fields the verifier rebuilds itself,
so a signature for one scheme, version or HTTP method never verifies as
another. Verifiers reject malleable signatures, non-canonical points and
small-order keys (FM-SIG-001). A collaboration event binds its repository,
object and policy inside the signed bytes, so it cannot be replayed into
another repository. Because the records live under `.forkmesh/` in Git, anyone
with a clone can verify the project's history without trusting the server that
served it.

Key rotation is signed by the old key (`forkmesh-rotate-v1`). Recovery of a lost
key still relies on account credentials and the recovery kit; a normative,
independently verifiable recovery protocol is open work (TM-018 in the
[threat model](protocol/threat-model.md)).

## End-to-end encrypted chat and calls

Each device keeps an Ed25519 identity key and rotating prekeys, each an X25519
key paired with an ML-KEM-768 key, so a recording made today cannot be opened by
a future quantum computer. A message gets a fresh AES-256-GCM key, wrapped for
each approved device with a hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 exchange and
HKDF-SHA256; the whole frame is signed and carries a replay counter. Direct
messages add a per-message ratchet like Signal's Double Ratchet, hold new
devices until the other person approves them, and show a 60-digit safety
number. Group calls derive media keys per epoch (a new epoch on every join or
leave), sign batches of frame digests so one participant cannot forge another's
video, and use a commit-then-reveal round so a short code is safe to compare.

What it does not hide: the server still sees who talks to whom, when and how
much, and public channels are readable by anyone who joins, including the
server. Details and limits: [chat encryption](security/sealed-chat.md),
[safety numbers](chat-safety-numbers.md), [calls](calls.md).

## Private repositories

Repository objects are sealed on an authorized device into
`forkmesh.private-replica` ciphertext: a fresh AES-256-GCM content key per
update, wrapped to every recipient's X25519 and ML-KEM-768 keys. Mirror and
storage operators hold no recipient key and see only opaque identifiers, sizes
and timestamps. Removing a collaborator reseals to the new recipient set under
a new key epoch; copies they already hold cannot be erased. A missing recipient
key never falls back to plaintext. `tools/audit_private_surfaces.py` checks a
database export and replica files for leaks without any key.
Full contract: [private repository confidentiality](security/private-repository-confidentiality.md).

## Data on the service

On the cores, collaboration rows and account data are encrypted with
AES-256-GCM under the instance `DATA_KEY`, and equality lookups use HMAC-SHA256
blind indexes derived from it. `DATA_KEY` is never written to a core's disk: a
node starts sealed and receives the key into memory from the operator or an
unsealed peer, and service secrets are sealed under it in the vault. The key can
be rotated offline (`docs/operations/rekey.md`). An operator holding the running service and
`DATA_KEY` is inside this boundary; someone holding only a disk, a database copy,
a log or a backup is not. What the service keeps and for how long:
[relay data retention](relay-data-retention.md).

## Software distribution

Every release has a `release.json` manifest listing each file's SHA-256, signed
with one Ed25519 release key. `install.sh` and the desktop's updater pin that
key and refuse an unsigned or mismatched download, whichever mirror served it.
A checksum taken from the fetched manifest alone is never trusted. See
[mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md#software-distribution).

## Known gaps

- An independent cryptographic review is a release requirement for private
  repositories and has not been published yet.
- Open protocol threats, including legacy record replay (TM-004), unsigned
  catalog v1 fields (TM-006), event withholding (TM-008) and key recovery
  (TM-018), are tracked in the [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).
- Request proofs carry no nonce; a captured proof can be replayed inside its
  5-minute window (TM-012). Push proofs bind the body digest, so a replay can
  only resend the identical pack.
- Passwords use PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations, below current guidance for
  that function.
- Channels have per-prekey forward secrecy (up to 8 days), not per-message.
- A modified web client served by a compromised host can read what it shows;
  the desktop and phone apps ship as signed builds instead.

pages.title: Mirroring and software distribution
pages.description: How ForkMesh keeps copies of a repository on independent hosts, how a cloner knows a copy is authentic, and how releases reach users through those copies.
pages.markdown:
# Mirroring and software distribution

How ForkMesh keeps copies of a repository on independent hosts, how a cloner
knows a copy is authentic, and how releases reach users through those copies.

Part of the core documentation: [architecture](architecture.md) ·
[encryption](encryption.md) · [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) ·
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md) · [censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)
· [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).

## Who holds copies

- **The source node**: the developer's desktop, or the cores for a repository
  created on the web ([hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md)).
- **Mirrors**: headless servers running `forkmesh-mirror-node`, operated by the
  project, its friends, or anyone who chooses to carry it
  ([mirror node](operations/mirror-node.md)). The desktop can install and update
  a mirror on any Debian or Ubuntu server over SSH.
- **Every clone**: issues, pull requests, reviews and releases are signed files
  under `.forkmesh/`, so an ordinary `git clone` carries the collaboration
  history too.

A repository page shows how many copies are running and how healthy they are
([mirror goals](mirror-quota.md)).

## How a mirror stays in step

1. The source pushes, and the cores send each mirror carrying the repository a
   small event over its signed WebSocket. The event names the new signed refs
   digest.
2. The mirror fetches until its refs match that digest, retrying a stale peer
   with backoff; older generations are ignored. A safety pass reconciles every
   5 minutes in case an event was lost; a third-party upstream (GitHub, Gitea,
   Forgejo) is polled every 15 seconds by default.
3. The mirror publishes a signed catalog record for each repository and a lease
   on its HTTPS endpoint, renewed every 4 minutes. A mirror whose lease lapses
   stops receiving clones.
4. Web submissions (issues, pull requests, merges) are written into Git by the
   mirror and acknowledged with a signed `forkmesh-repostate-v1` statement of
   the resulting refs.

Code and traps: `docs/server/README.md`, `docs/server/intake-and-attestation.md`.

## How a cloner knows a copy is authentic

- **Refs pins.** For each repository the service keeps a pin set: the source's
  signed current state plus attested history. `git clone
  https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>` is routed only to a mirror whose live
  refs digest is in that set and whose signed health is fresh. A repository
  with no pin is not routed at all.
- **Fail closed.** A mirror whose gateway does not know the expected refs digest
  refuses to serve. When no healthy, matching copy exists, the clone fails; it
  never falls back to unverified bytes (TM-007 in the
  [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md)).
- **Verifiable without the service.** Git object IDs pin the content, and the
  signed `.forkmesh/` records can be checked with the authors' public keys
  ([signatures and authentication](protocol/signatures-and-authentication.md)).
- **Private repositories** are replicated only as ciphertext; a mirror cannot
  read them ([encryption](encryption.md#private-repositories)).

## Ways to reach a copy

| Route | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>` | Normal clone; routed to a verified mirror or a core |
| `https://nN.next.forkmesh.com/...` | A specific core's Git gateway; works while the app is degraded |
| A mirror's own HTTPS or SSH address | Works with no ForkMesh server at all ([direct HTTPS gateway](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md), [SSH gateway](operations/git-ssh-gateway.md)) |
| Signed offline bundle | USB stick or a slow, metered link, resumable ([offline sync](offline-sync.md)) |
| Tor, I2P, overlay or LAN | Device-side transport profiles ([transports](transports.md)) |

All of them are stock Git: no ForkMesh client is needed to read
([Git compatibility](git-compatibility.md),
[accountless reading](accountless-reading.md)).

## Software distribution

Releases are content-addressed: each file is stored and fetched by its SHA-256
(`/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/releases/blob/sha256/<hash>`), and the release host
seeds every file into mirror release stores. A signed `release.json` lists every
file's hash; `install.sh` and the desktop updater verify the manifest against a
pinned Ed25519 key, then verify each file against its hash. Any copy can serve
the bytes, because no copy is trusted for them. Release downloads keep working
when the service is read-only. Linux packages are also published as a signed
apt repository. Operator detail: `docs/release/README.md`, `docs/release/apt.md`.

## When things go wrong

- A project that could disappear soon follows the
  [crisis preservation](crisis-preservation.md) plan, which orders the work
  (Git refs first, then identity proofs and trusted mirrors in an urgent
  takedown) to fit the time and access left.
- [Availability proof](availability-proof.md) and
  [availability contracts](availability-contract.md) measure whether a
  repository really survives losing its source.
- The [product promise](product-promise.md) walks through it end to end:
  collaborate, add a mirror, take the source offline, clone again.
- Withholding of collaboration events by a relay or mirror is not yet
  detectable (TM-008). A mirror can serve stale or wrong bytes, but the refs
  pin keeps clones away from it.

Related: [architecture](architecture.md), [self-hosting](self-hosting.md),
[censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md), public index
[README.md](README.md).

pages.markdown:
# Self-hosting

Everything ForkMesh runs is open source and can run on your own machines. Pick
the level you need: a node on your computer, a mirror on a server, a whole
instance under your own name, or a multi-node fleet like forkmesh.com.

Part of the core documentation: [architecture](architecture.md) ·
[encryption](encryption.md) · [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) ·
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md) · [censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)
· [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).

## Choose a level

| Level | You get | Needs | Time | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop node | Your repositories hosted and served from your computer, coding agents, chat | Linux, macOS or Windows | not measured | [getting started](getting-started.md) |
| Mirror | A server that carries copies of chosen repositories and serves clones | A Linux server with a public HTTPS name | not measured | [mirror node](operations/mirror-node.md) |
| Instance | Your own ForkMesh: accounts, repositories, pull requests, chat, Actions, your domain and branding | Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04, 1 GB RAM, 6 GB disk, ports 80 and 443 | about 15 minutes | [start your own instance](start-your-own-instance.md) |
| Fleet | Several equal core nodes behind DNS round robin, a runner tier, sealed secrets | Three servers plus an operator machine | not measured | `docs/operations/README.md` |

## Desktop node

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

The installer verifies the signed release manifest before it installs
anything ([encryption](encryption.md#software-distribution)). Windows and macOS
packages are on [forkmesh.com/desktop](https://forkmesh.com/desktop); supported
platforms are in the [installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).
The desktop is a full node: it holds bare repositories, serves clones and signs
records with its own key ([desktop app guide](qt-client.md)).

## Mirror

Two ways in:

- **From the desktop.** Add a server in the desktop's host list; it installs and
  updates `forkmesh-mirror-node` over SSH and pushes your repositories to it.
- **Without the desktop.** One command on the server installs the service,
  links it to your account, waits for your DNS record and serves it over HTTPS
  with a Let's Encrypt certificate:

  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | \
    FORKMESH_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME=<host> FORKMESH_LINK_CODE=<code> FORKMESH_OWNER=<user> bash
  ```

  The six-digit link code comes from your account and expires after 30 minutes.
  The same script works as cloud-init user data. Detail:
  `docs/release/self-setup-node.md`.

A mirror ships with key-only SSH and a fail2ban jail. Back it up, check it and
move its key with [node backup and recovery](operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md);
set storage limits and takedown handling with the
[node operator policy](operations/node-operator-policy.md). A mirror that should
work with no ForkMesh server at all can serve its own dashboard, SSH writes and
forks ([direct HTTPS gateway](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md)).

## Instance

Start one at [forkmesh.com/start](https://forkmesh.com/start): fill in the page,
upload a [settings file](start-config.md), or let a
[coding agent](coding-agents.md) write the settings for you. ForkMesh connects
to your server over SSH, checks the host key and runs the installer while the
page shows each step. Your SSH password or key is used once and never stored.
Without a domain the instance gets a free `<ip>.sslip.io` address. An instance
nobody signs in to within five minutes removes itself.

After setup you control legal pages, privacy mode (no visitor logs),
moderation and whether to join the forkmesh.com directory:
[instance legal pages](app/instance-legal-pages.md),
[privacy mode](app/privacy-mode.md),
[instance federation](app/instance-federation.md). Operator detail:
[docs/operations/instances.md](operations/instances.md).

## Fleet

forkmesh.com itself runs as three core nodes and a runner tier
([architecture](architecture.md)). The same tooling (`tools/next_fleet.py`,
`tools/next_deploy.py`, `tools/next_dns.py`, `tools/next_vault.py`,
`tools/next_backup.py`) builds and runs any fleet described by a
`deploy/fleet.toml`. Start with [docs/operations/README.md](operations/README.md),
then [docs/operations/served-stack.md](operations/served-stack.md), [docs/operations/vault.md](operations/vault.md) and
[docs/operations/runners.md](operations/runners.md).

## Keep it running

- Recovery from losing a server, domain, key or backup:
  [disaster recovery](disaster-recovery/README.md).
- Identity export and recovery: [portable identities](portable-identities.md).
- Private repositories and backups:
  [private repository confidentiality](security/private-repository-confidentiality.md).

Related: [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md),
[censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md), public index
[README.md](README.md).

pages.markdown:
# Censorship resilience

ForkMesh exists so that the source code and releases of a project stay
reachable, and provably authentic, when a hosting provider, a domain, an
account or a country's network turns against it. This page says what happens
under each kind of block, what still works, and what is not solved.

Part of the core documentation: [architecture](architecture.md) ·
[encryption](encryption.md) · [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md) ·
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md) · [censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)
· [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md).

## Who it is for

Maintainers of tools people rely on under censorship or surveillance:
circumvention, privacy and security projects whose repositories and downloads
are blocked or taken down, and whose users need to know the copy they get is
the real one. The goal is continuity of access and integrity of the code, not
another general-purpose forge.

## What happens when something is blocked

| What is blocked or lost | What still works | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The original host (GitHub account suspended, repository removed) | Clone, issues, pull requests, releases | Import or sync the project first ([repository imports](repository-imports.md), [GitHub sync](forge-sync.md#connecting-a-repository-to-github)); the signed history and every mirror carry on without the original host. For a project at risk now: [crisis preservation](crisis-preservation.md). |
| The `forkmesh.com` website | The app, API and Git | Use `app.forkmesh.com`, a core's own name (`nN.next.forkmesh.com`) or a mirror's address. |
| The ForkMesh service entirely (all cores unreachable) | Clone and fetch of public repositories with a live mirror; releases from any copy | Point Git at a mirror's own HTTPS or SSH address ([mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md#ways-to-reach-a-copy)). Desktop nodes keep serving what they hold. |
| One or two cores | Everything with one down; reads, clone and downloads with two down | DNS round robin and read-only mode ([architecture](architecture.md#no-single-point-of-failure)). |
| The IP addresses of the cores | Mirrors on other networks | Any operator can run a mirror on a different provider and address ([self-hosting](self-hosting.md#mirror)). |
| Direct internet access to every known address | Clone and fetch through an anonymity or overlay network | Device transport profiles for Tor, I2P, WireGuard-style overlays and LAN, with leak tracing and no silent fallback ([transports](transports.md)). |
| The network itself (shutdown, metered or broken link) | Moving a repository by hand | Signed, resumable bundles on USB sticks or slow links ([offline sync](offline-sync.md)). |
| A user's account | Their identity and signed work | Keys can be exported and recovered; records are signed by keys, not by a server account ([portable identities](portable-identities.md)). |
| A tampering mirror or network | Detection, not service | Clones go only to copies whose refs match the signed pin; releases are checked against a pinned key ([encryption](encryption.md)). |

## Distributing tools, not only code

Many circumvention tools reach their users as downloads from a repository's
releases. ForkMesh releases are content-addressed and signed: any mirror can
serve the bytes, and the installer or user checks them against the signed
manifest, so a blocked origin does not stop distribution and an untrusted copy
cannot alter it ([software distribution](mirroring.md#software-distribution)).

## What is not solved

We avoid claiming more than the design delivers:

- **Discovery.** Finding a working mirror normally goes through the catalog on
  the cores. If those are blocked, a user needs a mirror address from somewhere
  else; out-of-band discovery is open work.
- **Visible traffic.** Connections to ForkMesh names and mirrors are ordinary
  HTTPS; the server name is visible to the network and can be filtered. There is
  no built-in traffic obfuscation; users in heavily filtered networks route
  through Tor or another tool they trust ([transports](transports.md)).
- **Metadata.** The service learns public repository names, sizes, node
  versions, presence and timing (TM-016 in the
  [threat model](protocol/threat-model.md)). Private repositories use opaque
  handles and ciphertext ([private repository confidentiality](security/private-repository-confidentiality.md)).
- **Operator concentration.** The hosted cores currently run with one provider
  in one region, and forkmesh.com uses one DNS provider. Real resilience needs
  mirrors run by different people on different networks and in different
  countries ([architecture](architecture.md#what-is-still-a-dependency)).
- **Withheld events.** A relay or mirror that silently drops collaboration
  events is not yet detected (TM-008).

## How we test it

What is tested today:

- The [product promise](product-promise.md) drill: collaborate, add a mirror,
  take the source offline, clone again.
- [Availability proofs](availability-proof.md) and
  [availability contracts](availability-contract.md) that measure whether a
  repository survives losing its source.
- Read-only survival of the cores with two of three stopped
  (`app/host/tests_rqlite/test_read_only_survivor.py`).
- Transport profiles refuse forbidden routes and trace leaks
  (`conformance/transports/v1`).
- [Disaster recovery](disaster-recovery/README.md) drills for losing a domain,
  region, key or backup.

Not yet done: testing inside real national filtering systems (DNS tampering, IP
and SNI blocking, throttling, shutdowns) with developers in the regions where
they happen. The results, negative ones included, will be published here.

Related: [mirroring and distribution](mirroring.md),
[self-hosting](self-hosting.md), public index [README.md](README.md).

pages.title: Threat model
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Register: conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Threat model

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Register: `conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json`
· Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

This model covers the wire protocol in this suite. Endpoint compromise,
hosting-provider compromise and supply-chain attacks against clients belong to
[SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md) and the [dependency
audit](../security/dependency-security-audit.md); blocking and takedowns are
covered in [censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md), and the
cryptography in [encryption and signatures](../encryption.md). The register
file is authoritative. The table below MUST match its severity and status, and
the suite verifier fails if they differ.

## Assets

- Private keys: device, account, router, and importer keys.
- Repository history and the integrity of refs.
- Signed collaboration history: issues, pulls, reviews, moderation.
- Private repository names, contents, and collaborator lists.
- Session and request authorizations.
- Availability of clone and collaboration flows.

## Trust boundaries

| ID | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| B1 | Client device and its key store |
| B2 | Client ↔ relay (HTTPS and WebSocket to the core nodes) |
| B3 | Relay ↔ mirror origin |
| B4 | Mirror ↔ source-of-truth node |
| B5 | Relay storage (rqlite on the core nodes, node-local caches) |
| B6 | External provider ↔ migration importer |
| B7 | Portable session ↔ independent mirror dashboard |

## Attacker capabilities

| ID | Attacker | Can | Cannot (assumed) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | Network attacker | Observe timing and sizes; drop or delay traffic | Break TLS 1.2+ or Ed25519/SHA-256 |
| A2 | Malicious or compromised relay operator | Read and rewrite anything the relay receives; withhold, reorder, or replay messages; read relay-layer room traffic | Forge user signatures |
| A3 | Malicious mirror operator | Serve any bytes; lie in its own attestations; log requests | Forge a source-of-truth attestation |
| A4 | Malicious registered user | Sign any content with its own keys; equivocate; craft malformed input | Sign with another user's key |
| A5 | Holder of a stolen device key | Everything that key authorizes until rotation or revocation | Use the account password or TOTP |
| A6 | Malicious migration provider | Return inconsistent, oversized, or hostile API data | Access ForkMesh keys |
| A7 | Resource-exhaustion attacker | Send many or large requests within the per-node limits | Exceed the request rules and rate limits on every core at once |

## Register

| ID | Threat | Boundaries | Attackers | Severity | Status | Controls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TM-001 | Forged authorship of signed objects | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-SIG-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-002 | Signature or encoding malleability that aliases event identities | B2 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-001, FM-ENC-004, FM-ENC-006, FM-ID-004 |
| TM-003 | Replay of collaboration events into another repository or policy epoch | B2, B5 | A2, A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-003, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-004 | Replay of legacy issue/discussion/pull records whose canonical strings omit owner and repository | B2 | A2, A4 | high | open | FM-SIG-002, FM-MIG-002 |
| TM-005 | Cross-scheme or cross-version signature confusion | B2 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-SIG-002, FM-VER-001, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-006 | Catalog v1 signatures, which do not bind visibility or descriptive fields, replayed for public records | B2, B5 | A2 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004, FM-VER-002 |
| TM-007 | Tampered or rolled-back history served to cloners | B3, B4 | A3 | high | mitigated | FM-REL-001, FM-REL-002, FM-ID-005 |
| TM-008 | Relay or mirror withholds collaboration events | B2, B3 | A2, A3 | high | open | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-009 | Signing-key equivocation | B2 | A4, A5 | high | mitigated | FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-010 | Clock or timestamp manipulation to win conflicts or extend tokens | B2 | A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-SYNC-002, FM-SYNC-003, FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-011 | Unauthorized moderation or role escalation | B2, B5 | A4 | high | mitigated | FM-ID-002, FM-SYNC-003 |
| TM-012 | Replay of view, rotate, or push proofs within the freshness window | B2 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-001, FM-AUTH-002 |
| TM-013 | Theft and replay of portable session bearer tokens | B7 | A1, A3 | medium | open | FM-AUTH-003 |
| TM-014 | Tunnelled node traffic trusts the relay as an authenticated intermediary | B2, B3 | A2 | high | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-015 | Relay operator reads the outer room layer, including public channel plaintext and presence | B2, B5 | A2 | medium | open | FM-SIG-002 |
| TM-016 | Metadata leakage through the catalog, presence, routing, and timing | B2, B5 | A1, A2 | medium | open | FM-REL-001 |
| TM-017 | Parser, verifier, or fold resource exhaustion | B2 | A7, A4 | medium | mitigated | FM-ENC-005, FM-SIG-004 |
| TM-018 | Account key compromise or loss without a specified recovery protocol | B1 | A5 | high | open | FM-AUTH-004 |
| TM-019 | Data loss through lossy migration, down-conversion, or snapshot trust | B5, B6 | A2, A6 | high | mitigated | FM-MIG-001, FM-MIG-002, FM-MIG-003, FM-SYNC-001 |
| TM-020 | Substituting the pack body of an authorized HTTPS push | B2, B3 | A2 | high | mitigated | FM-AUTH-002, FM-REL-003 |

Open high-severity threats — TM-004, TM-006, TM-008, TM-014, and TM-018 — block
a stable suite release until they are mitigated or explicitly accepted.

## Discussion by class

**Replay.** Collaboration v1 binds repository, object, and policy inside the
signed bytes (TM-003). The legacy `forkmesh-issue-event-v1` family binds only
type, number, author, timestamp, and a content hash. The same signed record can
therefore be presented to another repository that has a matching issue number
(TM-004). The mitigation path is FM-MIG-002 migration to collaboration v1 plus
a relay rule that stops accepting legacy inbox records after the migration
window. Request proofs carry no nonce, so capture inside the five-minute window
permits replay (TM-012). Push proofs bind the method and body digest, so a
replay can only resubmit the identical pack.

**Downgrade.** Exact identifier matching and distinct prefixes defeat
cross-version confusion (TM-005). `forkmesh-catalog-v1` is still accepted for
public records. Descriptive fields and visibility are not signed under v1, and
the rollback check permits an equal `updatedAt`. A relay-level replayer could
therefore reissue an old public record (TM-006). Removing v1 acceptance is a
major suite change (see the compatibility policy).

**Equivocation.** A key signing two events in one sequence slot loses both
(TM-009). Detection needs both events in the same fold, so equivocation hidden
by withholding reduces to TM-008.

**Omission and availability.** No fold detects missing events (TM-008).
Closing it requires availability receipts or peer exchange that cross-checks
relay-delivered logs. Clone availability degrades to fail-closed, never to
unverified bytes (TM-007).

**Metadata leakage.** The relay learns public repository names, sizes, node
versions, presence, and request timing (TM-016). Private repository names never
enter the public routing index; private reads use opaque handles and ciphertext
([private repository
confidentiality](../security/private-repository-confidentiality.md)). By
design, default rooms use a relay-derivable key; private channels add a
recipient layer (TM-015, [sealed chat](../security/sealed-chat.md)). Telemetry
exports counts only.

**Abuse.** Size and depth limits bound parsing (TM-017). Verification caches
key on fixed-size digests. Catalog publication is rate-limited per owner.
Inbox signatures prove integrity, not reputation, and owner review gates every
merge.

**Recovery and data loss.** Signed raw bytes are the source of truth, and
snapshots are disposable (TM-019). Account key rotation requires the old key
(`forkmesh-rotate-v1`). Recovering from a lost or stolen key currently relies
on account credentials and the procedures in [portable
identities](../portable-identities.md). There is no normative, independently
verifiable recovery protocol yet (TM-018).

## Review

A security reviewer changes a threat's status only by editing `threats.json`
and this table together. The reviewer cites the requirement or test that closes
it, or records `acceptance` with reviewer, date, and rationale. The 2026-07
security audit is the origin of TM-004 and TM-014. This register does not
record any acceptance until a named reviewer signs one.

pages.markdown:
# Getting started with ForkMesh

## Install

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

To build from source, clone `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` and run
`./desktop/run.sh` (Qt 6.4+, CMake 3.16+, OpenSSL headers, Git, a C++17
compiler). See the [desktop app guide](qt-client.md) and the
[installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).

### Opening ForkMesh again on Linux

The installer puts the program at `~/.local/bin/forkmesh` and starts it once.
After you close it:

- Open your applications menu (on GNOME press the Super key, on KDE click the
  launcher) and search for **ForkMesh**. ForkMesh adds itself there the first
  time it runs. To keep it handy, right-click its icon in the dock and choose
  **Pin to Dash** or **Add to Favorites**.
- Or open a terminal and type `forkmesh`. If the terminal says the command is
  not found, type `~/.local/bin/forkmesh` instead.

## Accounts and instances

- **One account everywhere.** The website, the desktop app and the phone apps
  use the same ForkMesh account. There is no separate desktop password: sign
  in with the email and password that work on the website.
- **Your username** is the name on your ForkMesh profile (it appears as
  `@name`), not your email. The desktop may suggest one when you first sign in;
  change it if it is not yours. If you get it wrong, the desktop tells you
  which username your email belongs to.
- **An instance** is the ForkMesh server that holds your account.
  `forkmesh.com` is the main one; leave the instance as it is unless someone
  gave you a different address. Choosing **Continue** on the sign-in screen
  only signs you in: it does not create an account or an instance. To create
  an account, use **Create account**, which opens the website.
- **The eye button** in the password box shows what you typed.
- **Too many wrong passwords** pause sign-in for a short time. The message
  says how long to wait; your password has not changed, so use the same one
  after the pause.

## First run

1. Launch ForkMesh. A local Ed25519 node identity is created; no server URL is needed.
2. Optionally sign in from **Settings** for a portable public username.
3. Open **Chat**, pick a conversation, and press Enter to send.
4. In **Repos**, choose **New repository**, **Add local repo**, or **Fork**.
   Public repositories appear in the catalog; private ones stay hidden unless shared.

To keep a safe copy of a repository you already have on GitHub, follow
[Back up a GitHub repository](back-up-a-github-repository.md).

## Make a change

Use normal Git (`git switch -c`, `git commit`, `git push`) or the desktop:
**Code → Branches → New branch**, edit, then **Code → Changes → Commit & push**.
For another owner's project, fork it and use **Pulls → New pull request**; the
relay queues the signed pull request while the owner is offline.

## Where data lives

```text
~/projects/forkmesh/   src/ data/ cache/
~/projects/<project>/  data/ cache/
```

`data/core/` holds the node's private identity key, settings (`config/`),
`ssh/`, `state/` and `logs/`; each plugin keeps its data in `data/<plugin>/`.
Export the identity from **Settings → Data** before moving machines. `FORKMESH_HOME` or `FORKMESH_PROJECTS_DIR`
moves the layout. Uninstalling removes only the program unless `--purge` is
given.

## Phones and the watch

Get ForkMesh for iPhone and iPad on the App Store (the Apple Watch app comes
with it) or the Android APK from the downloads page. Sign in with the same
account; see [ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

## Your own instance

To run ForkMesh under your own name on your own server, open
[forkmesh.com/start](https://forkmesh.com/start), or hand the job to a coding
agent. See [Start your own instance](start-your-own-instance.md),
[Self-hosting](self-hosting.md) and [Working with coding agents](coding-agents.md).
How the hosted service runs is on [Architecture and availability](architecture.md).

Next: [the desktop app](qt-client.md) or the [documentation index](README.md).

pages.title: ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement
pages.description: ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh product promise: proof and measurement

> ForkMesh lets developers collaborate on, mirror, and preserve source-code repositories across independent hosts—without relying on any single hosting provider.

## Four-step proof

Use a disposable public repository; never delete the source. How mirrors serve
clones is on [Mirroring](mirroring.md); what still depends on the hosted service
is on [Architecture and availability](architecture.md).

### 1. Collaborate

Create a signed issue, discussion or pull request.

### 2. Add an independent mirror

Mirror it on another node until it is online, integrity `ok` and at the same commit.

### 3. Take the source mirror offline

Stop `forkmesh-mirror-node` on the source host.

### 4. Clone again

`git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` must succeed at the same commit.

## Expected failures and recovery

**No eligible mirror**, a stale or integrity-mismatched mirror, or
**All serving hosts offline** make the clone fail cleanly; a
**Private repository** is outside this proof. Rollback is explicit: restart
`forkmesh-mirror-node` and wait for fresh signed health.

## Measurement and closure gate

Consented analytics count only `home-proof-opened`, `proof-clone-copied` and
`repository-clone-copied`. In every five-person cohort of maintainers,
contributors, and operators, each reader must restate the promise. A cohort passes
at 4/5 or better. Do not mark this gate complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.

## Linked automated evidence

`app/tests/test_installer_release.py`, `app/tests/test_mirror_serving.py`,
`app/tests/test_https_mirror_routing_integration.py`,
`app/tests/test_mirror_service_recovery.py`, `app/tests/test_product_promise.py`,
`app/tests/test_first_party_analytics.py`.

A capability in one column does not imply the other. - Other columns describe a category of tool. A cell that names a product quotes that product's documentation, listed under *Primary sources* with its check date. - **By definition** marks a statement that follows from what the category is. **No claim made** means no primary source supports a category-wide statement. ## How the claims stay honest The block below is generated from the ledger; if they disagree, the ledger wins. `python3 tools/category_comparisons.py check` fails when a matrix cell is missing or lacks evidence, a category claim lacks a dated primary source, any claim is older than the review cadence, copy overclaims ("unlimited", "guaranteed"), a next-step UTM value is not allowlisted, or the block is out of date (run `render`). `report` prints freshness measures. Wrong claims are fixed in the ledger with a `corrections` entry; unverifiable claims become **No claim made**. ## Review status Reviewed **2026-09-14** by ForkMesh maintainers reviewing issue #509. The next review is due **2026-12-13**, every 90 days; after that date the check fails until every claim is verified again. ## At a glance | Option | What it is | Consider it instead of ForkMesh when | | --- | --- | --- | | ForkMesh protocol and self-hosted software | The MIT-licensed protocol, mirror node, gateways, and desktop app, run on hosts you or your community operate. | — | | ForkMesh hosted service | The forkmesh.com and app.forkmesh.com relay, accounts, public index, and website that ForkMesh operates. | — | | Centralized Git hosting | One company runs Git hosting, issues, pull requests, and related services for you, for example GitHub. | You need anonymous pushes, or pushes that land on a read mirror. ForkMesh takes pushes only from an authenticated account, over SSH or HTTPS, and streams them to one write endpoint.
You need a contractual uptime SLO, a support response time, or a managed private workspace today. None of these is sold yet.
Your team depends on GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, or GitKraken being certified. They are not yet.

pages.title: Terminology and voice guide
pages.description: ForkMesh keeps standard Git forge words and explains its network ideas in place. The contract is terminology.json; tools/terminology_lint.py checks primary surfaces against it.…
pages.markdown:
# Terminology and voice guide

ForkMesh keeps standard Git forge words and explains its network ideas in
place. The contract is [`terminology.json`](terminology.json);
`tools/terminology_lint.py` checks primary surfaces against it.
Other pages are listed in the [docs index](README.md).

## Approved glossary

| Say | Meaning | Instead of |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **repository** | A Git repository with its issues, pull requests and releases. | project |
| **branch** | A named line of commits. | |
| **fork** | Your own copy of a repository. | |
| **pull request** | A proposal to merge commits, with discussion and reviews. | merge request, patch |
| **review** | Approval, change request or comments on a pull request. | peer approval |
| **mirror** | A synced full copy on another host that can serve clones. | peer, seed node, mesh node |
| **seed** | The first push that fills a new mirror. | seeder |
| **trusted maintainer** | A person whose signed actions every mirror accepts. | delegate |
| **desktop app** | The ForkMesh desktop application. | Qt client |

## Protocol terms and plain explanations

| Protocol term | Plain explanation for primary surfaces |
| --- | --- |
| node | A running copy of ForkMesh that signs and syncs for an account. |
| relay | The web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. |
| refs attestation | The signed branch and tag list a mirror must match. |
| signed repository proof | A host's signature over the refs it serves. |
| commit DAG | Commit history. |
| CRDT / fold | How signed events merge into one state without conflicts. |
| lease | A short claim that stops two hosts doing the same work. |
| outbox | Signed events waiting for delivery. |
| opaque replica | An encrypted copy a host stores but cannot read. |
| federation | Sharing activity with ActivityPub servers. |

## Rules

- Lead with the Git task; explain a network idea once, where it appears.
- `discouragedTerms` marks each term **replace** or **explain**. Exceptions go in
  `allowances` (with a `reason`) or a `terminology: allow=<term-id>` comment.
- Run `python3 tools/terminology_lint.py` (add `--extended` or `--json`).

## Compatibility aliases

One pull request lives at `/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pull/12` (its sections at
`/pull/12/files`, `/pull/12/commits`, `/pull/12/checks`) and the list at
`/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pulls`, the split GitHub uses, so a pull request link copied
from GitHub works after swapping the host. Other familiar forge URLs
(`/pulls/12`, `/pull-requests/12`, `/merge_requests/12`, `/-/issues/5`)
redirect with 308, keeping the rest of the path and the query. Routes, JSON fields, event kinds, config keys and flags are never renamed for wording; aliases are never removed. **Rollback.** Revert the copy change; aliases stay.

## Measurement

`--json --extended` reports `discouragedTermCount` (zero on primary surfaces).
Alias usage comes from Cloudflare zone analytics. Support vocabulary is sampled
monthly. For every five-person cohort of maintainers, contributors, and operators, test core tasks without a glossary. A cohort passes at 4/5 or better. Do not mark this gate complete with blank, synthetic, or inferred results.
Evidence: `app/tests/test_terminology_contract.py`.

pages.title: ForkMesh free-protocol / paid-services contract
pages.description: Contract version 1. The machine-readable source is /business-model.json; the public entitlement matrix and homepage pricing render the same boundary.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh free-protocol / paid-services contract

Contract version 1. The machine-readable source is
[`/business-model.json`](../www/public/business-model.json); the public entitlement
matrix and homepage pricing render the same boundary.

## The durable boundary

ForkMesh sells work and infrastructure, not permission to participate in the
protocol. The protocol, reference software and self-hosting unit are
MIT-licensed and need no account or payment. Public reading and cloning,
standard Git data, signed `.forkmesh` records, independent operation and
protocol governance can never become paid entitlements. Paid services operate
replaceable roles (hosting, administration, indexing, replicas, recovery,
runners, support) and give ForkMesh no authority over protocol objects.

Tokens, rewards, tips and bounties are optional and never affect identity,
permissions, ranking, moderation or governance
(`tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false`); see
[incentive independence](incentive-independence.md).

## Initial plans

| Plan | Price and status | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol + self-hosted | $0; available | Full MIT rights; the operator supplies capacity and support. |
| Hosted Free | $0; public preview | Best-effort public reads, clones, relay and index. No reserved capacity, SLO or support time. |
| Supporter membership | $5/member/month | Funds infrastructure; no extra capability or authority. |
| Pro membership | $10/member/month | Published Pro workflows within safety and capacity limits; not unlimited. |
| Managed services | Research preview; not for sale | Metered hosting, replicas, recovery, runners and support; checkout disabled until research, cost, security, portability and recovery gates pass. |

No paid plan may be `unlimited` for a variable-cost service. Usage units map to
cost drivers (member-month, replica GiB-month, egress GiB, runner minute,
support hour, request counts); unknown cost stays unknown, never zero.

## Portability commitments

Repository data stays Git objects and refs; collaboration data stays signed
`.forkmesh` records. Export is free at any time, including before
cancellation. A managed plan cannot be sold until a drill exports a managed
project, imports it into a clean self-hosted deployment, compares object IDs
and signatures, and restores from the same export.

## Support boundary

Community support covers documentation, discussions and reproducible issues;
free use and memberships carry no response time. A paid support order must
state platform, channel, hours, response target, exclusions and included human
time. Preservation orders use a
[repository availability contract](availability-contract.md), backed only by
demonstrated capacity (`app/tests/test_availability_contract.py`).

## No data sale

ForkMesh does not sell personal data, repository data, collaboration data,
telemetry, or derived profiles, and does not use them to sell advertising.
Optional analytics is off by default and consent-based. First-party ads are
placed by surface, never by viewer (the `advertising` block of the contract).

## Acquisition and paid adoption model

Public projects are the acquisition loop and stay free: anonymous read or
clone, signed contribution or mirror, a qualified service need, a bounded trial
with export available, and a paid proposal only when cost supports the target
margin. The funnel reports aggregate public projects reaching proof, qualified
service conversations, trials, paid customers, trial-to-paid conversion,
revenue, service cost and gross margin, without identifying readers.

## Unit-economics model and instrumentation

```text
gross profit = recognized service revenue - service cost
gross margin = gross profit / recognized service revenue
```

The admin usage report emits a `unitEconomics` projection from provider
analytics; `tools/unit_economics.py` combines it with invoice-backed costs.
Exports carry no raw account, repository, path or IP data. Provider analytics
unavailability is a failed sample, not a zero-cost day.

Managed pricing stays a hypothesis until the
[pricing-interview register](research/pricing-interviews.md) holds qualifying
interviews. Rollout and recovery steps:
[business-model rollout](operations/business-model-rollout.md). Contract test:
`app/tests/test_business_model_contract.py`.

pages.title: Incentive independence
pages.description: Repository access, identity, contribution, governance, and essential network participation work fully without a token, blockchain, reward system, or speculative asset.
pages.markdown:
# Incentive independence

Repository access, identity, contribution, governance, and essential network participation work fully without a token, blockchain, reward system, or speculative asset.

Optional incentives (tips, bounties, reward pool, microjobs, hackathon prizes,
memberships) are **adapters**. An adapter may read canonical state; canonical
state never reads an adapter. Requirements:
`conformance/incentives/v1/requirements.json`.

## Architecture

Canonical state is Git data and signed refs pins, accounts and keys, signed
`.forkmesh` collaboration records, organizations and roles, discovery, and
governance. Adapters include `solana.py`, `reward_policy.py`, `ledger.py`,
`microjobs.py`, `hackathon.py` and `patreon.py` with their own tables.

1. Canonical modules never import an adapter.
2. Hooks from canonical writes to adapters are best effort and cannot fail the write.
3. No foreign key points into an adapter table.
4. Identity, authorization, ranking, moderation and governance never read
   wallets, balances, tokens, tips or payment history.

## Commercial commitment

`/business-model.json` publishes `tokenOrBlockchainRequired: false` and
`incentivesAffectIdentityPermissionsRankingModerationOrGovernance: false`.

## Protocol governance

Collaboration authority comes only from the repository policy document's keys.
Changing that requires a new protocol version.

## Payment and no-payment paths

Every incentive has a no-payment path; conventional payment is preferred over
crypto. Grants follow [public-interest funding](funding/README.md).

## Disabled deployment

With no adapter configured, signup, keys, repositories, clone, collaboration
records, organizations, discovery and marketplace approval all work.
Unconfigured adapters answer explicitly (for example HTTP 503
`patreon_oauth_not_configured`) and never block a canonical response.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

A failed or removed adapter pauses payouts only: unset its configuration. A
coupling regression fails the `incentive-independence` quality gate; revert it.

## Telemetry and measures

- Essential no-incentive journey pass rate
- Adapter coupling violations (target zero)
- User comprehension: a cohort must answer that no wallet or token is needed

## Linked automated evidence

- `app/tests/test_incentive_independence.py`
- `app/tests/test_marketplace_governance.py`
- `app/tests/test_non_custodial_surfaces.py`

Last run 2026-09-14. | **supported** — Source-attested ref pins gate routing; the suite also injects bad refs and damaged packs. Last run 2026-09-14. | **supported** — Candidates must share the accepted ref digest; corruption fixtures must fail fsck. Last run 2026-09-14. | `git -C worktree fsck --full --strict` | | Rollback and recovery | **supported** — A verified pre-force bundle restores the exact previous ref over authorized SSH. Last run 2026-09-14. | **local** — Recovery is prepared locally and published with an authenticated HTTPS push or over SSH. Last run 2026-09-14. | **local** — A recovered owner ref is served only after mirrors refresh and attest the new state. Last run 2026-09-14. | `git clone recovery.bundle recovered` | ## Evidence runs | Client | Git | Platform | Protocol | Probe transport | Result | Finished | Evidence | Reproduce | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Debian system Git | 2.47.3 | Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 x86_64 | v2 | http | **pass** 15/15 | 2026-09-14 | [report](/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/df83f9aadd86159a.json) | `git checkout c792b91e35e78b54871d6814d77d8fcfb7621591 && python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 --transport http --client-label 'Debian system Git' --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json` | | Debian system Git | 2.47.3 | Linux 6.12.107+deb13-amd64 x86_64 | v0 | http | **pass** 15/15 | 2026-09-14 | [report](/docs/git-compatibility/evidence/f80323565e1c9af0.json) | `git checkout c792b91e35e78b54871d6814d77d8fcfb7621591 && python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 --transport http --client-label 'Debian system Git' --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json` | ## Tested clients | Client | Platform | Version | State | Last tested | Evidence | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | ForkMesh Qt desktop | Linux, macOS, Windows | current main | **tested** | 2026-08-20 | `desktop/tests/test_mesh_e2e.cpp` | | GitHub Desktop | macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | | Sourcetree | macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | | GitKraken Desktop | Linux, macOS, Windows | not yet recorded | **pending** | not yet tested | `desktop-client-validation` | ## Known limitations ### HTTPS pushes need a credential and are not probed by this suite - Applies to: relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: A push to the stable HTTPS URL without a credential gets HTTP 401 push_unauthorized with a Basic challenge before ForkMesh reads the push body. With a credential, the relay checks that the account may write the repository and streams the push to one endpoint that accepts receive-pack; for a repository the core nodes host, that is the core that last took a push, else the first live core in rendezvous order. Read mirrors never take writes. - Reproduce: `git push https://app.forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git HEAD` - Action: When Git asks, enter your ForkMesh account name or email and either your account password (when two-factor authentication is off) or the push credential from Settings, SSH keys, Push code over HTTPS. On the core nodes the default and protected branches only fast-forward, other branches may be force-pushed by accounts that may write them, new tags are allowed, and a push never deletes a branch. - Recovery: A refused push changes no remote ref or object. Check the account name and the password or credential, then retry the same push; HTTP 403 push_forbidden means the account may not push to this repository. The Git errors page lists every message. - Last tested: 2026-10-24 · not applicable (source contract tests) · app/tests/test_git_http.py::test_receive_pack_fails_closed_without_consuming_request_body, app/tests/test_hosted_repositories.py::test_account_name_or_email_and_password_push ### Repository-controlled server hooks are disabled - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: Client-side hooks in a checkout run normally. Gateways set core.hooksPath to the null device so pushed repository configuration cannot execute code on a mirror. - Reproduce: `git -C worktree commit -m 'exercise local hook'` - Action: Keep developer hooks local; put shared required checks in reviewed ForkMesh Actions or another CI system. - Recovery: A rejected local hook leaves the index and remote unchanged; fix or intentionally bypass the local hook according to project policy. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 hooks probe ### A response cannot change mirrors mid-stream - Applies to: mirror-failover. - Expected result: ForkMesh retries another eligible mirror only before response bytes are committed. An interrupted pack fails as a normal Git transport error. - Reproduce: `git fetch --prune origin` - Action: Retry the fetch; Git reuses valid local objects and ForkMesh may select another matching mirror for the new request. - Recovery: Run git fsck --full --strict if the client or disk reported corruption. Do not delete the existing clone before collecting diagnostics. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 mirror-failover and integrity probes ### Partial clone requires Git protocol v2 - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: A protocol-v0 filtered clone may receive the initial commits and trees, but its first lazy blob fetch is rejected as an unadvertised-object request so hidden ForkMesh objects remain inaccessible. - Reproduce: `git -c protocol.version=0 clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Use Git 2.34 or newer and retry with -c protocol.version=2, or omit --filter for a full clone. - Recovery: Remove the incomplete disposable clone, or keep it for diagnostics and clone into a new directory with protocol v2; no remote ref or object was changed. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 protocol-v0 rejection and protocol-v2 partial-clone probes ### Submodules are separate repositories - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: The superproject clone succeeds, then Git names the exact submodule whose independent URL is unavailable or unauthorized. - Reproduce: `git clone --recurse-submodules '{clone_url}' worktree` - Action: Confirm every .gitmodules URL uses a published public HTTPS route or an SSH route your key may read, then run git submodule update --init --recursive. - Recovery: The superproject and any completed submodules remain valid; Git resumes the missing child without recloning successful repositories. - Last tested: 2026-08-20 · Git 2.47.3 · forkmesh-stock-git v1 submodules probe ### Third-party desktop UI certification is not complete - Applies to: direct, relay, mirror-failover. - Expected result: GitHub Desktop, Sourcetree, and GitKraken are not release-supported rows until their exact application and bundled-Git versions produce a retained report. - Reproduce: `python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --git /path/to/the/client/bundled/git --client-label 'CLIENT VERSION'` - Action: Use a tested Git CLI or ForkMesh Qt build, or run the versioned probe with the desktop application's bundled Git before relying on it. - Recovery: The probe uses disposable repositories and makes no production write. Attach its JSON report when requesting a new supported row. - Last tested: not yet tested · not applicable · No support claim is published without retained evidence. ## Run the suite ```sh python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate python3 tools/git_conformance.py render --check python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 0 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py run --protocol-version 2 \ --output artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py attest \ artifacts/git-conformance-v0.json artifacts/git-conformance-v2.json python3 tools/git_conformance.py gate ``` Use `--git /path/to/git --client-label 'client version'` to exercise a desktop application's bundled, unmodified Git. Reports contain operation status, elapsed milliseconds, exact client/platform versions, generalized request counts, and test object IDs. They exclude temporary paths, URLs, repository contents, credentials, and client addresses.

pages.description: The Qt client is a workspace application: chat and repository UI, local Git data, signed collaboration records, actions, and coding agents. It does not serve repositories or…
pages.markdown:
# Qt desktop client

The Qt client is a workspace application: chat and repository UI, local Git
data, signed collaboration records, actions, and coding agents. It does not
serve repositories or publish the catalog; the Go mirror service does that.

## Install a release

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash
```

The installer verifies signed release metadata and the artifact checksum and
never compiles as a fallback. Native `.exe`, `.dmg`, and `.AppImage` packages
are on the [desktop downloads](https://forkmesh.com/desktop) page.

## Build and run from source

Requirements: Qt 6.4+ (Widgets, Network, SVG, Concurrent; D-Bus on Linux),
CMake 3.16+, a C++17 compiler, OpenSSL 3.0+ with headers, Python 3, and Git.
Private mirrors and the Password Vault need OpenSSL 3.5; on older systems pass
`-DFORKMESH_BUNDLED_OPENSSL=ON` (fetches and verifies a pinned OpenSSL) or
`-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR=...`. Optional: `libnghttp3` for the HTTP/3 log-feed client,
Qt 6 Multimedia for in-app video playback, and Qt 6 WebEngine
(`qt6-webengine-dev`) for the Browser tab and YouTube inside the app.

```sh
sudo apt install build-essential cmake git libssl-dev openssl \
  qt6-base-dev qt6-svg-dev qt6-base-dev-tools pkg-config \
  qt6-webengine-dev                                         # Debian/Ubuntu
brew install cmake git openssl@3 qt                         # macOS
```

From the repository root:

```sh
./desktop/run.sh           # incremental Release build and launch
./desktop/run.sh test      # build and run the critical contracts
./desktop/run.sh clean     # delete desktop/build
./desktop/run.sh rebuild   # clean, build, and launch
```

Manual CMake (prefer Ninja; its job pool caps concurrent heavy units):

```sh
cmake -S desktop -B desktop/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DFORKMESH_BUILD_TESTS=ON
cmake --build desktop/build --parallel 12
ctest --test-dir desktop/build --output-on-failure
```

On macOS add `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="$(brew --prefix qt)"` and
`-DOPENSSL_ROOT_DIR="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)"`. `ccache`, `ninja`, and
`mold` speed up rebuilds. In-app *Rebuild & restart* builds `RelWithDebInfo`,
re-runs a pass if sources changed mid-build, and installs only a build of an
unchanged tree. Developer notes:
[docs/desktop/build-and-test.md](desktop/build-and-test.md).

Qt 6.4 is the floor. Guard newer APIs with
`#if QT_VERSION >= QT_VERSION_CHECK(6, 5, 0)` and verify with
`tools/qt64-build-check.sh [ubuntu-24.04]`, which builds against each
distribution's own Qt in a private sysroot.

Never run ForkMesh as root.

## KVM-isolated coding workspace

On Linux, coding agents can run in a Lima QEMU/KVM guest while the UI stays on
the host. Only the launch directory (mounted at the same path), the Git metadata
it needs, and a temporary agent-worktree root are shared; the home directory,
sockets, SSH agent, and unrelated environment are not. It needs Lima 2.0+,
QEMU, and `/dev/kvm`; there is no software-emulation fallback.

Launch ForkMesh from the narrowest directory holding your repositories (the
home directory is refused), enable **Settings → General → KVM workspace**,
choose **Prepare / start VM**, sign in to agents in **Open VM shell**, then
restart. Toggling the mode requires a restart; repositories outside the launch
directory are rejected while it is active.

## First run and navigation

A first launch creates the node identity, connects to the default relay, and
syncs the ForkMesh project. The left rail holds the main areas: Chat, Repos,
Code, Issues/Pulls/Actions, Agents, Network, Team, Pings, Health, Settings,
and others. Add a project with **Repos → Add local repo**; contribute elsewhere
with **Repos → Fork**.

**Network → Hosts** can create managed Vultr mirrors and optionally size the
fleet automatically to a target healthy count. Only instances this client
created are ever destroyed; an unreachable catalog makes no change.

### Team and teammate run modes

**Team** loads teammate definitions from `.forkmesh/teammates/`. Each teammate
runs on demand, on a bounded cron cadence, on repository events, or in
**Continual** mode, and only while the desktop is open. A continual teammate
runs one bounded cycle, then waits at a decision card (Yes/No, or three
options) before the next; **Stop work** pauses it. Permission mode, repository
grants, concurrency limits, and any VM boundary apply to every cycle. A Git
worktree separates branches but is not a sandbox.

### Multiple relay instances

The relay selector holds any number of named relay instances, each with its
own remembered account. The active relay is a security boundary: catalogs,
account requests, bearer capabilities, channel membership, chat history, and
queued agent work are scoped to its local instance id and exact origin.
Switching clears active credentials first; chat never fails over to another
relay. Bearer tokens are never written to `QSettings`. Each repository record
belongs to the relay it was added under and is only synced with that relay.
Private channels and direct messages keep their device-to-device layer; see
[Chat encryption and integrations](security/sealed-chat.md).

### Connectors

Discord and Sentry connectors are Market packages. Discord uses a bot token
(never a user token) and the server's permissions; Sentry reads unresolved
issues read-only with an `org:read`/`project:read` token. Tokens live in
device-local package settings, never in logs, arguments, or chat. Removing the
package clears its token and cached data.

## Create a pull request

Within your own repository: create a branch under **Code → Branches**, commit
in **Code → Changes**, then select the branch and click **Create PR**. ForkMesh
records the commit series and a signed binary-safe patch. Agents work the same
way in isolated worktrees under `.worktrees/` in the project.

For another owner's repository: **Fork** it, commit a feature branch, open
**Pulls → New pull request**, set the target node, base, and head, and submit.
The signed patch is delivered to the owner's inbox; the relay holds it until
the owner is online. See [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Run a managed mirror

Do not use the desktop binary as a repository server; run the Go mirror daemon
per the [headless mirror runbook](operations/headless-mirror.md#refresh-and-publication).

## Logs and diagnostics

- The footer CPU/RAM/stall indicator shows UI-stall details.
- **Network diagnostics** shows connections and recent endpoint results;
  per-request logging is opt-in in Settings.
- **Settings → Data** shows the data, preferences, mirror, and cache
  directories for the current OS.

Diagnostic journals (default layout):

```text
~/projects/forkmesh/data/core/logs/diagnostics/actions.jsonl   action lifecycle journal
~/projects/forkmesh/data/core/logs/diagnostics/stalls.log      UI freezes longer than 500 ms
```

Each `actions.jsonl` record names `source`, `function`, `routine`, `cwd`,
`queued_ms`, and an `outcome`. The data directory also holds `network_log.txt`
and crash records. Details:
[docs/desktop/diagnostics.md](desktop/diagnostics.md).

When reporting a problem include `forkmesh --version`, OS and display server,
the triggering action, and a log excerpt with secrets and private content
removed.

## Common fixes

- **CMake cannot find Qt6:** install the Qt development packages; on macOS
  pass `CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH`.
- **Qt platform plugin error:** launch from a graphical session.
- **Stale CMake cache after moving the checkout:** `./desktop/run.sh clean`.
- **Repository actions are read-only:** fork it or add its local working tree.
- **Backup:** **Settings → Data → Export configuration**; **Control → Deploy →
  Export complete system…** writes clear-text secrets, so protect it.

Back to [Getting started](getting-started.md) or the
[documentation index](README.md).
