pages.description: A capability is present on a surface when the surface implements it or offers a safe deep link to its canonical interface. The contract is capability-matrix.json: every row names…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh surface capability matrix

A capability is present on a surface when the surface implements it or offers a
safe deep link to its canonical interface. The contract is
[`capability-matrix.json`](capability-matrix.json): every row names a canonical
path and a non-missing mode for the app server (the `worker` column),
dashboard/Web, World and Qt, and CI validates it. The phone and watch apps are tracked in
[PARITY.md](native/PARITY.md).
How the surfaces connect is on [Architecture and availability](architecture.md).

Owner-device secrets never leave the device: Cloudflare tokens, repository
decryption keys, mirror process control, wallet signing keys, SSH private keys,
agent-provider credentials, and microphone audio. Web and World show authorized
state and link to the local flow. The app server supplies authenticated APIs,
policy, encrypted envelopes, and public-safe projections; an API entry does
not imply custody or plaintext access. Raw SSH terminates only at the
node-side forced-command gateway.

pages.title: Installation support matrix
pages.description: The machine-readable matrix is install-support-matrix.json; CI checks that every supported artifact is in the latest signed release.
pages.markdown:
# Installation support matrix

The machine-readable matrix is
[`install-support-matrix.json`](install-support-matrix.json); CI checks that
every supported artifact is in the latest signed release.

**Supported** artifacts are in the Ed25519-signed release manifest, SHA-256
verified and tested; **Preview** is packaged but not fully published;
**Source-only** builds with `FORKMESH_FROM_SOURCE=1`; **Planned** is not
installable.

The iPhone and iPad app is on the
[App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735), and the Apple
Watch app installs with it. Apple signs and delivers it, so it is never in the
signed release manifest and stays listed as Preview here.

## Profiles

| Profile | Tier | Artifact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `linux-desktop-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-linux-x86_64`, `.AppImage` |
| `linux-cli-headless-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-linux-x86_64` |
| `linux-server-mirror-node-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64` |
| `windows-desktop-x86_64` | Supported | `forkmesh-windows-x86_64-setup.exe` |
| `android-universal` | Supported | `forkmesh-android-universal.apk` |
| `macos-desktop-arm64` | Preview | `forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg` |
| `macos-desktop-x86_64` | Preview | `forkmesh-macos-x86_64.dmg` |
| `linux-desktop-arm64` | Preview | `forkmesh-linux-arm64.AppImage` |
| `linux-arm-small-device` | Source-only | none |
| `ios` | Preview (on the App Store) | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735), with the watch app inside |
| `oci-container` | Planned | none |
| `cluster` | Planned | none |

## Lifecycle

| Action | Command |
| --- | --- |
| Install or upgrade | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh \| bash` |
| Roll back | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh \| FORKMESH_RELEASE=candidate-<version> bash` |
| Uninstall, keeping data | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/uninstall.sh \| bash` |
| Uninstall and erase all data | `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/uninstall.sh \| bash -s -- --purge --yes` |

Each install verifies the manifest signature, its binding of `SHASUMS256.txt`
and the artifact digest before replacing the binary. Upgrade, rollback and
uninstall touch only program files; user data in
`~/projects/forkmesh/{data,config,ssh,state,logs}` (and `/var/lib/forkmesh`
for a mirror node) is removed only by `--purge` or a confirmed desktop
uninstall. Back up the identity key first: see
[Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md).

pages.title: Portable identities and recovery
pages.description: Keys, the recovery kit and authenticators stay with the user; ForkMesh stores only public authority state. Never send keys or kits to support. Key types and signatures are…
pages.markdown:
# Portable identities and recovery

Keys, the recovery kit and authenticators stay with the user; ForkMesh stores
only public authority state. Never send keys or kits to support.
Key types and signatures are explained on
[Encryption and signatures](encryption.md).

## Enroll and revoke authenticators

Use a passkey for sign-in plus a hardware key and a second device. Revoking a
device kills its key and sessions; revoked keys only verify old signatures.
Delegates get scoped, expiring authority.

## Recovery drills

Practise each before relying on an identity: lost device, compromised device
(revoke first), key rotation (old key revoked atomically), social recovery
(threshold of contacts, who never hold the key) and organization delegation
(minimal scope, expiry).

## Portable encrypted export

The kit is JSON of type `forkmesh.portable-identity`, `schemaVersion` 1:
PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (600000 iterations, 16-byte salt) and AES-256-GCM (12-byte
IV, tag appended, associated data `forkmesh.portable-identity/v1`) over at most
128 KiB of plaintext, all base64url without padding. Passkey and hardware-key
secrets are never exported. Web, iOS, Android and desktop share the format.

## External-account proofs

Signed short-lived challenges with `private`, `members` or `public` visibility;
revocable, and shown unverified once revoked or expired.

pages.title: Portable social signals
pages.description: Suite 1.0.0 · Vectors: conformance/social-signals/v1/vectors.json · Implementations: tools/social_signals.py (Python), app/public/social-signals.js (JavaScript).
pages.markdown:
# Portable social signals

Suite `1.0.0` · Vectors: `conformance/social-signals/v1/vectors.json` ·
Implementations: `tools/social_signals.py` (Python), `app/public/social-signals.js`
(JavaScript).

Stars, watches, bookmarks, follows, recommendations, usage endorsements,
security reviews and mirroring commitments are signed records the user owns.
They can be exported, imported, merged and revoked, and any implementation can
verify them. This page is normative for requirements `FM-SOC-*`; it reuses the
protocol's canonical JSON and strict Ed25519 rules
([encoding](protocol/encoding-and-identifiers.md),
[signatures](protocol/signatures-and-authentication.md)).

Status: records, bundles, merge, verification, recommendations and the CLI ship.
Client screens, a hosted import/export endpoint and telemetry: Not yet. Hosted
stars and follows are still unsigned per-account rows.

## Tiers

| Kind | Tier | Scope | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `star`, `watch`, `bookmark`, `recommendation`, `follow` | interest | `{}` | `[]` |
| `usage-endorsement` | attestation | `environment`, `version`, `since` | 1–16 links |
| `security-review` | attestation | `revision`, `method`, `findings` | 1–16 links |
| `mirror-commitment` | attestation | `https` `endpoint`, `protocols`; `expiresAt` required | 1–16 links |

- **FM-SOC-001** `tier` is fixed by `kind` (`tier_mismatch`).
- **FM-SOC-002** Interest records carry no scope or evidence
  (`interest_claims_scope`); attestations need evidence (`evidence_required`),
  each item exactly `{label, uri, sha256}`.
- **FM-SOC-003** Attestations are displayed with category, scope and evidence
  count (`describe`), never merged with stars. Evidence is the signer's claim.

## Record format

Schema `forkmesh-social-signal-v1` with keys `schema, kind, tier, signer,
subject, issuedAt, expiresAt, visibility, scope, evidence, note, signalId,
signature`.

- **FM-SOC-004** Exactly these keys; subjects are protocol repository
  identifiers or, for `follow`, `urn:forkmesh:identity:ed25519:<key>` other than
  the signer (`self_follow`); millisecond timestamps; `note` ≤ 1024 bytes.
- **FM-SOC-005** Signing bytes are `"forkmesh-social-signal-v1\n"` + canonical
  JSON without `signalId`/`signature`; `signalId` is `sha256:` of those bytes;
  strings are NFC-normalized.
- **FM-SOC-006** Verification order ends with `signal_id_mismatch`,
  `invalid_signature` and `issued_in_future` (more than five minutes ahead); the
  first failure code is reported.
- **FM-SOC-007** Signed `visibility`: `public`, `followers` or `private`.
  Exports enforce it; records are signed, not encrypted.

## Revocation

- **FM-SOC-008** Schema `forkmesh-social-revocation-v1`, prefix
  `"forkmesh-social-revocation-v1\n"`, reason `withdrawn`, `superseded`,
  `compromised` or `mistaken`. Only the record's signer can revoke; otherwise
  status `signer_mismatch` and no effect. A revocation arriving first is
  `pending` until its record arrives.
- **FM-SOC-009** Revocation is final; sign a new record instead.

## Export, import, and merge

Bundle: `{"schema": "forkmesh-social-signal-bundle-v1", "exportedAt", "signals", "revocations"}`.

- **FM-SOC-010** Each record is validated independently; invalid ones are
  reported in `{accepted, duplicate, rejected}` and skipped. Only a bad envelope
  or more than 10,000 records rejects the bundle.
- **FM-SOC-011** The store is the union keyed by ID, so merge order does not
  matter. State digest: `sha256` over `"forkmesh-social-signal-state-v1\n"` +
  canonical sorted ID lists.
- **FM-SOC-012** Status precedence: `revoked`, `superseded` (newer record, same
  signer, kind and subject), `expired`, `active`.
- **FM-SOC-013** Export audience `public`, `followers` or `self`; revocations
  travel with their targets.

## Recommendations

- **FM-SOC-014** Local controls `{viewer, enabled, asOf, limit, mutedSigners,
  mutedSubjects}`, never exported; `enabled: false` computes nothing.
- **FM-SOC-015** Only signers the viewer actively follows count (no
  transitivity); mutes apply at once.
- **FM-SOC-016** Weights: `star` 1, `watch` 1, `recommendation` 2,
  `mirror-commitment` 2, `usage-endorsement` 3, `security-review` 3. One signer
  adds at most their highest weight per subject.
- **FM-SOC-017** Each result lists score, supporters and every contributing
  record, plus counts of what was excluded and why.

## Command line

```sh
python3 tools/social_signals.py keygen --out ~/.forkmesh/social.seed
python3 tools/social_signals.py sign --seed-file ~/.forkmesh/social.seed star.json > signed.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py revoke --seed-file ~/.forkmesh/social.seed sha256:<signalId> --reason withdrawn
python3 tools/social_signals.py merge a.json b.json --audience public --output public.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py verify public.json
python3 tools/social_signals.py recommend public.json --viewer <key> [--disable]
python3 tools/social_signals.py gate
```

`gate` checks the committed vectors, runs both implementations against them and
a cross-implementation round trip (quality gate `social-signal-portability`).
Any rule change regenerates vectors (`vectors --write`), updates both
implementations and bumps the suite version.

## Failure and recovery

| Situation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Tampered or malformed record in a bundle | Rejected with its code; the rest imports |
| Revocation before its record | `pending` until the record arrives |
| Revocation by another signer | `signer_mismatch`, no effect |
| Compromised key | Revoke with `compromised`, rotate identity ([portable identities](portable-identities.md)), re-sign |
| Lapsed mirror commitment | `expired`; sign a new one |
| Two services disagree | Compare state digests and merge both bundles |

pages.markdown:
# Empty repositories created from the web

Create an empty repository from **Repositories → New** and push with plain
`git` to `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<name>`. When git asks, enter your
account name or email and your account password (if two-factor authentication
is off), or the push credential shown.
The credential is a
keyed MAC over account,
repository, session and a seven-day expiry; it is not stored, dies with the
session, and every push re-checks permissions. After each push ForkMesh records
the attestation (the signed list of branch and tag commits) that reads route
against.
Where hosted repositories live is on
[Architecture and availability](architecture.md).

Packs are bounded by the gateway's `limits.receiveMaxInputBytes` (git's
`receive.maxInputSize`). Where core nodes host
repositories (`HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES`) the form also offers private
repositories, initial files and imports, up to 10 repositories of 200 MB per
account.

## Contributing without write access

Step by step, with the commands: [Contribute with git only](contributing-with-git.md).

The usual way: open the repository, choose **Forks → Fork this repository**,
create a push credential for your fork (Settings → SSH keys → Push code over
HTTPS, `<you>/<name>`), push any branch to it, and choose **Contribute: Open
pull request** on your fork. A fork shares the original's history, so it is
created at once whatever the repository's size.

On a repository the operator opened to contributors, anyone signed in with a
verified email address can also push a branch and open a pull request without
a fork:

1. **Settings → SSH keys → Push code over HTTPS**: enter `<owner>/<name>` and
   choose **Create push credential**.
2. Push a branch named `pr/<your-account>/<topic>`:
   `git push https://<host>/<owner>/<name>.git pr/<your-account>/<topic>`.
   When Git asks, use your account name or email with your account password
   (if two-factor authentication is off), or the credential.
3. Open the pull request from that branch on the repository's **Pull
   requests** tab.

Every other ref is refused (Git prints `[remote rejected]` with the reason),
and a contributor keeps at most 32 branches there. You may force-push your own
`pr/<your-account>/` branches to update a pull request after a rebase or
amend; use `git push --force-with-lease`, and if it is refused because the
branch moved on the server, run `git pull --rebase` first. The previous tip is
kept, and the pull request shows "force-pushed from … to …" with a compare
link. Ordinary pushes to the branch update the pull request too ("pushed N
commits").
Contributors cannot delete branches, even their own: when the limit is
reached, a maintainer deletes merged ones. Only new objects are sent, so a
large repository costs no more than the change.

## Operator notes

Production hosts repositories on the core nodes listed in
`HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES`: a push goes to the core that took the last push, else
the first live core by rendezvous hash, and the others replicate from it
([core-hosted repositories](operations/core-hosted-repositories.md)). Without core hosting the
fallback is `HOSTED_GIT_WRITE_NODE`, a node with `writableRepositoryRoot` and
`"writableOwners": ["*"]`. With neither, the API answers
`hosted_git_unavailable`.
See [direct-https-mirror-gateway.md](operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md).
Endpoints are `POST /api/hosted-repositories` and
`POST /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential`; records are marked
`source: "hosted-web"` until a signed publication from the owner's node takes
over.

Contributor pushes are off unless `HOSTED_GIT_CONTRIBUTOR_PUSH` lists
repositories: `owner/name`, `owner/*` or `*`, separated by spaces or commas
(an organization alias or its backing node both match). Only public
repositories qualify, and only active user accounts with a verified email.
The relay (the app on the core nodes) signs `pushPrefix=refs/heads/pr/<account>/` (and
`rewrite=` with the same prefix, which lets the contributor force-push only
there) into the receive-pack capability; the gateway refuses refs outside it, so both
must be updated together (an older gateway refuses the field, failing closed).
Contributor pushes never queue Actions runs.

There is no per-account byte quota or push rate limit on this path: each push
may be up to the gateway's `limits.receiveMaxInputBytes`, and pushes are
unlimited. Listing `*` lets any verified account store data in every public
repository, so prefer naming repositories or owners.

pages.title: External repository imports and resumable migrations
pages.description: Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with preservation-first crisis onboarding.
pages.markdown:
# External repository imports and resumable migrations

Racing a shutdown, a takedown, a lost account, or censorship? Start with
[preservation-first crisis onboarding](crisis-preservation.md).

An import copies a project's issues, pull requests and their history once. It
does not copy the code and is not kept up to date, so it is not a backup; to
keep a copy of the code, see [Back up a GitHub repository](back-up-a-github-repository.md).

## Setup

On **Repositories**, choose **New repository**, select **GitHub / GitLab /
Codeberg**, paste the URL (a gitea.com URL works there too), and select
**Start resumable import**. A read-scoped
provider token is optional for public repositories and required for private
ones. Tokens are used per request and never stored, logged, or returned, so a
private import asks for one again on **Continue import**.

Imports live apart from the live catalog: `/api/repositories` lists published
ForkMesh repositories, `/api/repository-imports` lists external metadata entries
and stubs. An external entry is never routed or called mirrored until a node
hosts it (see [Ending the provider dependency](#ending-the-provider-dependency)).

## API

```http
POST /api/repository-imports                     # metadata entry or stub (mode: import | stub)
POST /api/repository-imports/discover            # expand a GitLab group or a Codeberg or Gitea profile, max 200 public repos
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations          # durable job, 202 with a mig_… id
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/resume
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/objects?type=reviews&limit=100
GET  /api/repository-imports/migration-metrics   # setupP50Ms, setupP95Ms, transfer, retries
DELETE /api/repository-imports/{id}
```

Only canonical `github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`, and `gitea.com`
HTTPS URLs are accepted. Codeberg (Forgejo) and gitea.com share one adapter,
because both serve Gitea's `/api/v1`; other Gitea or Forgejo instances are
not accepted, so the import cannot be pointed at an arbitrary host. `targetOwner` is the caller or an organization they administer.
Each `/resume` call advances one provider page and returns the next checkpoint;
clients repeat it until `completed`, `429`, or an explicit error. Setup time
(form to accepted job) and transfer time are measured separately; the setup
gate is p50 at most 180,000 ms.

Every adapter emits the same object families: `git_refs`, `issues`,
`pull_requests` (GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests), `reviews`,
`releases`, `documentation`, `labels`, `users`, and `collaboration_history`.
Each object keeps the original provider payload plus a common projection.
Credential-shaped fields are redacted and counted. Git objects travel through
the normal bare-mirror path; wikis, workflow logs, and artifact bytes are
reported as out of scope. Provider rate limits are honored: the job becomes
`rate_limited` and resumes on the same page.

## Idempotence, checkpoints, and signed completion

Object identity is `SHA-256(object family + preserved source id)`. Objects are
upserted before the checkpoint advances, so a crash can repeat work but never
duplicate it. An object must be absent from two consecutive complete scans
before it is pruned. On completion the sorted `(objectType, sourceKey,
payloadHash)` tuples are hashed and signed; run numbers and timestamps are
excluded, so an unchanged source yields the same state hash on every rerun.

## Failure, abandonment, and rollback

- Retry a `paused`, `failed`, or `rate_limited` job with `/resume`.
- `POST …/{id}/abandon` stops work but keeps objects; resume with `{"recover": true}`.
- `POST …/{id}/rollback` removes the job, its objects, and its telemetry. It
  keeps the external listing and never touches the source forge.
- A missing optional stream goes to `report.skipped`. A required page the
  provider will not serve pauses the job; resume with `{"deferFailure": true}`
  to continue and leave that work listed as retryable.
- A single record that cannot be stored is counted as failed; the rest of its
  page is imported.

## Migration reports

```http
GET  /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/report[?sequence=N]
POST /api/repository-imports/migrations/{id}/retry
```

Every import ends with a signed `forkmesh-repository-migration-report-export-v1`
report (owner-only, `no-store`), issued on completion, abandonment, and each
retry. Sections: `summary`, `reconciliation.rows`, `refs`, `artifacts`,
`checksums`, `retries`, `failures`, `externalDependencies`, `verification`,
`remediation`.

Each provider record lands in exactly one class: `imported`, `skipped`,
`failed`, `external`, or `unclassified`. Any `unclassified` record makes the
outcome `unreconciled`. Outcomes are `verified`, `completed_with_failures`,
`completed_with_unmeasured_sources`, `unreconciled`, and `abandoned`.

The report hash is signed with the relay's Ed25519 router key (published as
`routerPublicKey` on `GET /api/mirrors/https`) over
`forkmesh-repository-migration-report-v1\n<reportHash>`, or HMAC when no key is
configured. Reports chain through `sequence` and `supersedes`. `/retry` queues
only failed pages and deferred streams (`409 no_failed_work` if none).

`tools/verify_migration_report.py` checks a report without ForkMesh code:
hash, signature, reconciliation arithmetic, chain, and, with `--objects`, every
payload hash. Exit 0 verified, 1 failed check, 2 unreadable input.

```bash
python3 tools/verify_migration_report.py report.json \
  --objects objects.json --public-key "$ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY"
```

Tests: `app/tests/test_repository_migration.py`,
`app/tests/test_repository_migration_report.py`.

## Visibility and statuses

Anonymous listings filter private entries before decryption; a private id
returns the same `404` whether absent or forbidden. Statuses:
`external_repository`, `stub_only`, `mirror_requested`, `partially_mirrored`,
`actively_mirrored`, `mirror_unavailable`, `archived`. The mirrored states
require a matching catalog record; `actively_mirrored` also needs a live host
heartbeat.

## Ending the provider dependency

Public imports become ForkMesh-hosted repositories:

1. `tools/hosted_repository_sync.py` runs on mirror nodes from
   `forkmesh-hosted-repository-sync.timer` (every 30 minutes), reads the public
   import listing, and keeps a `git clone --mirror` of each eligible entry
   under `/srv/forkmesh-git/imports/<node>/<name>.git`.
2. The node publishes a signed catalog record, so the gateway serves the copy
   with no provider in the path.
3. The relay links that record to the import entry, which becomes
   `actively_mirrored` and routes `/<targetOwner>/<name>` to the hosting node.

Only canonical public provider URLs without credentials qualify. Private and
archived imports are never hosted. A node caps its imports root at 20 GiB and a
first clone at 10 minutes; over budget an entry is deferred. Deleting the
import removes the hosted copy on the next run; nothing is deleted at the
provider.

## Mirror volunteers, invitations, and logos

- `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/mirror-volunteers` needs a mirror node the
  caller owns (`eligible_owned_mirror_node_required` otherwise).
- `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/invitations` is limited to
  provider-verified administrators, needs a durable provenance record
  (`public_for_invitations`, `prior_consent`, or `owner_supplied`) and
  `confirm: true`, is rate limited, and stores only masked addresses and blind
  indexes. Every message carries opt-out and abuse-report links.
- Each entry gets a locally generated SVG logo (`aiGenerated: false`).
  `POST /api/repository-imports/{id}/logo-suggestions` accepts PNG, JPEG, or
  WebP for owner approval.

pages.markdown:
# Admin dashboard (`/product-analysis`)

An internal, read-only dashboard at `https://app.forkmesh.com/product-analysis`
for account, signup-origin, mirror, and clone counts. It has no public version.
Other pages are listed in the [docs index](README.md).

## Access

| Secret | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_USER` | Login username. |
| `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS` | Login password and session-cookie key material. |

- With either secret unset the route returns the ordinary 404 (a signed-in
  `is_admin` account is still admitted).
- Unauthenticated `GET` shows only a sign-in form, `noindex`. Unknown paths,
  methods, views, and actions return 404.
- Login sets `forkmesh_product_analysis` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict,
  12 hours). Rotating the password ends every session.
- Failed logins share the account-login rate limit (`429` with `Retry-After`).
- No JavaScript; CSP `default-src 'none'`; `no-store`. Rendered inside the
  shared admin shell (`app/src/admin_shell.py`).

## Sections

All windows are UTC (last 30 days, previous 30 days, 90-day and 30-day daily
charts). Five tabs:

- **Overview**: total accounts, accounts with a mirror, activation (first
  mirror within 7 days of signup), returning accounts, mirrors created,
  repositories cloned and anonymous clones (from `product_clone_daily`), and
  all-time clones (`mirror_serve_counters`).
- **Signup sources**: accounts and mirror creators per origin.
- **Users**: sortable, paginated, read-only list with last activity.
- **Repositories**: catalog records with mirror count, size, clones, and
  `hostedSince`.
- **Acquisition**: pending; served without building a report
  (`VIEWS_WITHOUT_REPORT`).

## Signup origin

`users.signup_origin` is `job_flow`, `referral`, `organic`, or `unknown`,
stamped at signup by `_record_signup_origin`. Rules (`v1`): a referral
attribution or referrer marker gives `referral`; a signup inside
`PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_JOB_FLOW_WINDOWS` (none configured) gives `job_flow`; a
captured marker without referrer gives `organic`; everything else is `unknown`.
Migration `0175_product_analysis.sql` backfills the referral rule; the app
backfills the encrypted rules once, guarded by `schema_meta` key
`product_analysis_signup_origin_backfill:v1`.

## Data correctness and placement

Every source table is read with keyset pagination (`scan_table`) and checked
against `COUNT(*)`; a mismatch renders an error for the affected figures only.
Requests run in their own app ingress shard (an emulated Durable Object on
the core nodes) because a report decrypts every account and repository row.

## Operations

- Rotate the password on the fleet: edit `PRODUCT_ANALYSIS_PASS` in
  `secrets.env`, then run `python3 tools/next_vault.py sync --execute`
  ([operations](operations/README.md)).
- Disable the route by deleting either secret.
- Each public HTTPS clone does one best-effort `product_clone_daily` upsert.
- Down migration: `app/migrations/down/0175_product_analysis.sql`.

pages.description: tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py is a standard-library coding agent with pluggable model providers: Cloudflare Workers AI, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible local server. The…
pages.markdown:
# Cloudflare Workers AI coding agent

`tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py` is a standard-library coding agent with
pluggable model providers: Cloudflare Workers AI, Ollama, or any
OpenAI-compatible local server. The desktop embeds it; how agents fit into
ForkMesh is on [Working with coding agents](coding-agents.md).

## Architecture

The loop (`Agent`, `Conversation`, `Memory`, `Session`, `PromptBuilder`) is
separate from transport (`CloudflareProvider`, `OllamaProvider`,
`LocalLlamaProvider`) and from repository tools (`ToolRegistry`, `FileEditor`,
`GitManager`, `SearchEngine`, `CommandExecutor`). Tools include `read_file`,
`write_file`, `replace_text`, `apply_patch`, `undo_edit`, `grep`,
`execute_command`, `git_*`, `run_tests` and `lint_project`. Tool arguments are
coerced to schema, tool results are bounded, and repeated or stalled turns end
the run.

## Desktop

Choosing **Cloudflare AI** creates an isolated worktree and sends each turn
straight to Cloudflare's `/ai/v1/chat/completions` with the account ID and API
token saved in Settings (`CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`);
tools run only locally, and no turn passes through the relay. Models come from
Cloudflare's `/ai/models/search`, with a built-in list when that is
unreachable. **Local Llama** uses an Ollama server at
`127.0.0.1:11434`; when `GET /api/version` answers, the native `/api/chat`
route is used, which sizes `num_ctx`, controls thinking, and keeps the model loaded.

## Command line

```bash
export FORKMESH_AGENT_PROVIDER=cloudflare   # or local-llama
export FORKMESH_AGENT_ACCOUNT_ID=… FORKMESH_AGENT_API_TOKEN=…
export FORKMESH_AGENT_MODEL='@cf/google/gemma-4-26b-a4b-it'
python3 tools/forkmesh_coding_agent.py issue.md
```

Other `FORKMESH_AGENT_*` settings: `ENDPOINT`, `TEMPERATURE` (0.2),
`MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (2000), `CONTEXT_WINDOW` (32000), `TIMEOUT` (600),
`STREAMING`, `RETRY_COUNT` (4), `MAX_TURNS` (120), `SESSION_PATH`,
`TEST_COMMAND`, `LINT_COMMAND`, `PREVIEW_EDITS`, `TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT`,
`THINKING`, `KEEP_ALIVE`, `LOCAL_API` (`ollama` or `openai`),
`SHOW_REASONING`.

## Safety

Paths are repository-relative with no `..` or symlink escapes; commands have
closed stdin, bounded output and a timeout; global Git config writes are
isolated; nothing is pushed automatically. Tests:
`app/tests/test_coding_agent.py`, `app/tests/test_local_agent.py`. After
editing the tool, run `python3 tools/sync_coding_agent_header.py`.

pages.markdown:
# Reading and cloning without an account

Public projects are readable without an account. The website never redirects
to sign-up or log-in to read; it asks you to sign in only when you change
something.
Clones also work from any mirror when the hosted service is unreachable; see
[Mirroring](mirroring.md).

## What works without an account

Repository overview, code, branches, commits, issues, pull requests and
reviews, discussions, releases and their manifests, mirrors
(`/owner/repo/mirrors`), public profiles (`/@name`), and
`git clone https://forkmesh.com/owner/repo`. Other forges' URL shapes redirect
to the readable page. See [Git compatibility](git-compatibility.md).

## Where you are asked to sign in

Starring, forking, writing issues, pulls, comments or reviews, changing issue
state, copying an agent prompt, linking a desktop node, and account pages send
you to `/login?next=<page>`. So does a write rejected with `401`, and nothing
else.

## Not yet available

A passkey-backed **browser identity** for signing contributions, and handing it
to a full node, are not yet available. See
[Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md).

## Evidence

`app/browser_tests/tests/anonymous-public-reading.spec.js` and
`app/tests/test_anonymous_public_reading.py` check the rule.

pages.description: Weekly reporting template. Definitions live only in the metric dictionary; monthly KPIs go in the monthly outcome review.
pages.markdown:
# Activation-to-revenue weekly scorecard

Weekly reporting template. Definitions live only in the [metric
dictionary](outcome-metrics.json); monthly KPIs go in the [monthly outcome
review](outcome-review.md).

## Reporting contract

- Report the last complete Monday–Sunday week in UTC.
- Read every source to exhaustion. A page size of 100 is a transport limit, never a population limit.
- If source and collected totals do not reconcile, write `UNKNOWN`; never show the partial first page.
- Keep acquisition cohorts, anonymous clone totals and accounting periods separate.
- A missing input is a blocker, not a zero.

```text
Week: YYYY-MM-DD through YYYY-MM-DD UTC
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Pagination audit: pages collected=<n>; provider/source rows=<n>; all continuations exhausted=true|false
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
Decision: <one sentence>
```

| Stage | Metric id | This week | Prior week | WoW | Coverage/confidence |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |

## Reconciliation checklist

1. `python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary`, then `review --input week.json`.
2. Run `cd app && pytest -q tests/test_attribution.py -k 'report_returns_all_250_rows_not_the_page_size or page_past_100_rows or count_mismatch_raises'`.
3. Reconcile anonymous clones to daily snapshots. Never add `clone_url_copied` to that total.
4. `python3 tools/unit_economics.py validate-contract` and `python3 tools/unit_economics.py report --input period.json`.
5. Do not include raw email, account, repository, path, IP, customer or support identifiers.

pages.description: ForkMesh runs on the web, the desktop, iPhone and iPad, Apple Watch and Android. Every app signs in to the same account and instance, so a change made on one shows up on the…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh apps

ForkMesh runs on the web, the desktop, iPhone and iPad, Apple Watch and
Android. Every app signs in to the same account and instance, so a change
made on one shows up on the others. Downloads are at
[forkmesh.com/#downloads](https://forkmesh.com/#downloads); the platforms
and their release status are in the
[installation support matrix](install-support-matrix.md).

| App | Get it | What it is for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Web | [app.forkmesh.com](https://app.forkmesh.com) or your own instance | Repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, the dashboard and the admin console |
| Desktop (Linux, Windows, macOS) | The install script in [Getting started](getting-started.md), or the installers on the downloads page | The full node: mirrors repositories, runs coding agents in their own worktrees, runs Actions, hosts and agents |
| iPhone and iPad | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735) | A mobile node: browse, edit and commit, run and steer agents, chat and calls, review diffs, Siri, widgets |
| Apple Watch | Installs with the iPhone app | Follow, steer and hear your agents from your wrist |
| Android | Signed APK, `forkmesh-android-universal.apk`, from the downloads page | The iPhone app's features and look ([Android guide](mobile/android.md)) |
| Chrome and Chromium browsers | The **Browser extension** page of the dashboard | Fill Password Vault logins, link mail to the CRM, update Marketing channels and mirror a repository in one click ([browser extension](browser-extension.md)) |

## Desktop

The desktop app is a ForkMesh node. It creates its own Ed25519 identity on
first run, mirrors repositories, runs agents in isolated worktrees with live
transcripts and diffs, and turns their work into pull requests. See
[Getting started](getting-started.md) and the
[desktop app guide](qt-client.md).

## iPhone and iPad

The phone is a node too: it holds its own key and has its own Git engine, so
it can clone and commit without the desktop. You can start, steer, stop and
merge agents running on your desktop or on cloud runners, review their diffs
file by file, chat (direct messages are end-to-end encrypted) and make calls,
and use the Market's phone tools. Start with
[getting started on a phone](mobile/getting-started.md); every phone guide is
on the [phone apps](mobile/README.md) page, including
[privacy and security](mobile/privacy-and-security.md),
[Siri](mobile/siri.md), [Apple Health](mobile/apple-health.md),
[editing files](mobile/mobile-file-editing.md) and
[agent access](mobile/mobile-agent-access.md).

## Apple Watch

The watch app works through your iPhone, which holds your session and keys:
see the agent list and a live view, Stop, Continue and Retry, send a prompt by
dictation, review diffs, hear each agent as sound and haptics, and start an
agent with Siri. Everything it does is on the [Apple Watch](mobile/apple-watch.md)
page.

## Android

The Android app is built from the same design as the iPhone app (the same
Liquid Glass theme) and talks to the same endpoints, so the server cannot
tell them apart. Since 2026-10-28 every phone change ships in both apps in the
same pull request; the few differences kept on purpose, such as a background
connection in place of push, are on the [Android](mobile/android.md) page. It
is distributed as a signed APK from the downloads page.

## Browser extension

The ForkMesh extension for Chrome serves the Password Vault, the CRM and
Marketing from one sign-in, and mirrors a GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg or Gitea
repository to your account from its page. Install it from the dashboard's
**Browser extension** page; see the [browser extension](browser-extension.md)
guide.

Developer documentation for the native apps is in
[docs/native/README.md](native/README.md).

pages.title: Repository availability contracts
pages.description: A repository availability contract states how many verified copies, operators, and regions hold a repository, which transports and refs they serve, how often that is checked, how…
pages.markdown:
# Repository availability contracts

A repository availability contract states how many verified copies, operators,
and regions hold a repository, which transports and refs they serve, how often
that is checked, how fast incidents are answered, and what is credited on a
miss. Each period yields a `forkmesh-availability-contract-report-v1` report
computed only from an evidence bundle, so anyone can recompute and verify it.
Managed checkout stays disabled until the [business model](business-model.md)
gates pass.

## Evidence bundle

Schema `forkmesh-availability-contract-evidence-v1`: `contract` (terms,
remedies, exclusions, fee), `observations` (`/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`
payloads, scored by the [availability proof](availability-proof.md)), `drills`
(restore drill records), `responses` (incident acknowledgements), and
`capacity` (`community` or `contracted` per node).

## Contract terms

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `copies` | Verified copies required in every slot. |
| `operators` | Distinct operators holding the same verified state (at least 2). |
| `regions` | Distinct regions among verified copies. |
| `uptimeBps` | Share of slots that must meet every check. |
| `verificationIntervalMs` | Slot length; at most 10,000 slots per period. |
| `transports` | `router`, `directHttps`, `smartHttp`, each needing a verified copy. |
| `refCoverage` | Copies must carry every branch. |
| `artifactCoverage` | Copies must carry every release artifact. |
| `recoveryTimeObjectiveMs` | Longest incident and slowest restore drill allowed. |
| `drillIntervalMs` | Oldest allowed drill at period end. |
| `incidentResponseMs` | Longest time to acknowledge an incident. |
| `failureTolerance` | Operators, and separately regions, that may fail at once (0 to 2). |
| `maxExcludedBps` | Share of slots exclusions may remove. |

Malformed terms stop evaluation with a closed error code; there is no partial
report.

## Verification slots

A slot misses on any failed check; a slot without evidence is a miss.

| Check | The slot misses when |
| --- | --- |
| `unverified` | No observation. |
| `quorum_below_contract` | Too few operators held the same verified state. |
| `copies_below_contract` | Too few verified copies. |
| `regions_below_contract` | Too few regions. |
| `transport_missing` | A contracted transport had no verified copy. |
| `ref_coverage_incomplete` | Too few copies carried every branch. |
| `artifact_coverage_incomplete` | Too few copies carried every artifact. |

Availability is `met slots * 10000 // counted slots`, rounding in the
customer's favor.

## Exclusions

Kinds `scheduled-maintenance`, `customer-requested`, and `legal-hold` remove
whole slots when announced before they start and within `maxExcludedBps`.
Rejections: `unknown_kind`, `announced_late`, `over_budget`.

## Incidents and drills

Consecutive missed slots form one incident, measured in whole slots. Response
states: `ok`, `late`, `missing`, `pending`. The latest restore drill per node
decides its state: `ok`, `drill_missing`, `drill_stale`,
`drill_beyond_objective`. See
[node backup and recovery](operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md).

## SLOs and remedies

SLOs: `availability`, `recovery`, `incident-response`, `restore-drills`. The
period is `met` only when all four are met. Every miss is listed, even when its
SLO holds:

| Miss | SLO |
| --- | --- |
| `availability_window` | `availability` |
| `recovery_objective_exceeded` | `recovery` |
| `response_late` | `incident-response` |
| `response_missing` | `incident-response` |
| `drill_missing` | `restore-drills` |
| `drill_stale` | `restore-drills` |
| `drill_beyond_objective` | `restore-drills` |

Credits come from `remedies`: one `availabilityTiers` credit for missed
availability, fixed credits per recovery, response, and drill miss, capped at
`maxCreditBps`. Money is integer micro-USD.

## Demonstrated capacity and admission

A node is demonstrated when it verified in at least `uptimeBps` of slots and
its latest drill is `ok`. Undeclared capacity counts as community. A contract
is admissible only when demonstrated capacity meets the terms; otherwise
`admission.reasons` lists `no_evidence`, `copies_not_demonstrated`,
`operators_not_demonstrated`, `regions_not_demonstrated`, or
`failure_simulation_failed`.

The failure simulation removes every combination of `failureTolerance`
operators, then regions, from the latest observation and recomputes the
quorum; a surviving node's drill must fit the recovery objective.

## Correlated-risk disclosures

Disclosures do not change the outcome.

### `community_capacity_relied_on`

Contracted capacity alone does not reach the operator quorum.

### `contracted_single_operator`

One operator runs every contracted copy.

### `operator_concentration`

One operator runs more than half of the demonstrated copies.

### `region_concentration`

More than half of the demonstrated copies share one region or none.

### `no_failure_headroom`

Losing any one operator breaks the quorum.

### `capacity_not_demonstrated`

A declared contracted node lacks continuous probes or a qualifying drill.

## Privacy

Reports show opaque operator numbers only, never accounts, endpoints, mirror
URLs, drill paths, or keys.

## Signed reports and tooling

A `forkmesh-availability-contract-signed-report-v1` document holds `report`,
`reportHash` (`sha256:` over canonical JSON), and an Ed25519 signature over
`forkmesh-availability-contract-report-v1\n<reportHash>`.

```sh
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py explain bundle.json
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py sign bundle.json --private-key seed.txt > signed.json
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py verify bundle.json signed.json --public-key <key>
tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py fixture
```

`verify` recomputes the report and rejects edits to the report or evidence.
Exit codes: `explain` 0 met, 3 otherwise; `verify`/`fixture` 0 match, 1
mismatch; 2 for bad input. Model and fixture live in
`conformance/availability-contract/v1/`; tests in
`app/tests/test_availability_contract.py`. Reports are produced offline; drill
records are not signed.

pages.markdown:
# Availability proof and repository risk

The `forkmesh-availability-proof-v1` report says whether a repository is
preserved, how independently, and what is at risk. It is computed from the
public mirrors payload, so anyone can recompute it.
How copies are made and served is on [Mirroring](mirroring.md); what a block or
takedown can and cannot stop is on
[Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md).

## Evidence

Inputs come only from `GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`: signed endpoint
receipts (`endpointFresh`, `endpointHealthy`, `endpointIntegrity`,
`checkedAt`), direct clone probes (`directVerified`, `directCheckedAt`,
`directRefsSha256`), integrity gate verdicts (`integrity`, `behind`, `status`,
`lastSeen`), operator and region, and coverage (`branchCount`,
`artifactCount`). A receipt counts for 10 minutes; a passing probe for 24 hours.

## Copy classes and quorum

Each copy gets the first matching class: `failing`, `verified`, `declared`,
`stale`, `observed`. Reason codes: `integrity_rejected`, `abuse_blocked`,
`probe_failed`, `offline`, `behind`, `evidence_expired`, `awaiting_receipt`,
`never_observed`, `limited_replica`. A copy whose `replicaScope` is not `full`
is `observed` with `limited_replica` (see
[Offline and low-bandwidth sync](offline-sync.md)) and never counts toward quorum.

Proof is `quorum` when at least 2 distinct operators hold the same verified
state, `partial` with any verified copy, otherwise `none`. When probe digests
disagree, only the digest backed by the most operators counts. The risk score
is the sum of applicable weights, capped at 100: `critical` from 60, `high`
from 30, `moderate` from 10, else `low`.

## Risk codes

### `no_verified_copy`
Weight 50, critical. No copy has fresh signed evidence. **Remediation:** ask a node to mirror the repository, or [run a mirror node](operations/).

### `quorum_not_met`
Weight 25, high. Fewer than 2 operators hold the same verified state. **Remediation:** ask another operator to mirror it.

### `state_disagreement`
Weight 20, high. Verified copies returned different refs digests. **Remediation:** rerun the direct URL check; a divergent mirror re-syncs.

### `single_operator`
Weight 10, medium. All verified copies share one operator. **Remediation:** ask a different operator to mirror it.

### `failing_copy`
Weight 10, medium. A copy failed integrity, abuse checks or its clone probe. **Remediation:** re-sync the mirror and recheck it.

### `source_offline`
Weight 10, medium. The working-copy source is offline. **Remediation:** start the node that holds the working copy.

### `no_direct_clone_url`
Weight 10, medium. No verified copy passed a direct clone probe in 24 hours. **Remediation:** register a direct mirror URL and check it.

### `partial_ref_coverage`
Weight 10, medium. Too few verified copies carry every branch. **Remediation:** re-sync every branch.

### `stale_copy`
Weight 5, low. A copy is offline, behind or expired. **Remediation:** bring it back online.

### `partial_artifact_coverage`
Weight 5, low. Too few verified copies carry every release artifact. **Remediation:** re-sync release artifacts.

### `single_region`
Weight 5, low. All verified copies declare the same region. **Remediation:** ask a node in another region to mirror it.

### `declared_only_copy`
Weight 3, low. A catalog record exists but nothing has observed it. **Remediation:** check the endpoint is registered and reachable.

## Privacy and tooling

Operators appear only as opaque numbers; endpoint addresses and probe reasons
are never shown. The report is the `availability` field of the mirrors API
(`app/src/availability_proof.py`). `tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py
verify|explain|fixture` recomputes it. The model and fixture live in
`conformance/availability-proof/v1/`.

pages.markdown:
# Back up a GitHub repository

This guide is for keeping a private, safe copy of a repository that lives on
GitHub, for example a website you share with a friend, without changing
anything on GitHub. You need two commands in a terminal; everything else
happens in the ForkMesh desktop app.
How ForkMesh copies and serves repositories is on [Mirroring](mirroring.md).

## What you need first

- **Permission to view the repository on GitHub.** If you can open its files
  on github.com, that is enough. You do not need permission to push, and you
  do not need a new branch: a backup only reads.
- **A ForkMesh account** and the desktop app, signed in. See
  [Getting started](getting-started.md); the desktop uses the same email and
  password as the website.
- **Git** on your computer. On Debian or Ubuntu: `sudo apt install git`.

## The words, in plain terms

| Word | What it means | Does it change GitHub? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| View | Look at the files on github.com | No |
| Clone | Make a copy of the repository on your computer | No |
| Pull | Bring the newest changes from GitHub into that copy | No |
| Commit | Save a change you made, on your computer only | No |
| Push | Send your saved changes to GitHub | **Yes**, and it can change the live website |
| Mirror | ForkMesh's copy of a repository, kept on the ForkMesh network | No |

A backup uses only **clone** and **pull**. ForkMesh never pushes anything to
GitHub for you.

On the ForkMesh website, **Import from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg** copies a
project's issues and pull requests once. It does not copy the code and is
not kept up to date, so it is not a backup. **Clone URL** on the website
copies a public repository once. A private repository is backed up from the
desktop app, as below.

## 1. Copy the repository to your computer

Open a terminal and run (put in your friend's GitHub name and the repository
name from its github.com address):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git ~/Backups/REPOSITORY
```

For a private repository Git asks for a username and a password. Type your
GitHub username, and for the password paste a **GitHub access token**, not
your GitHub password (GitHub no longer accepts passwords here). To make one,
on github.com open **Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens**:

- If the repository belongs to you or to an organization you are in, choose a
  **fine-grained token**, limit it to that one repository, and set
  **Contents** to **Read-only**. It cannot change anything.
- If the repository belongs to a friend's personal account, GitHub does not
  let fine-grained tokens reach it; use a **classic token** with the `repo`
  scope and an expiry date. That token can also write, so keep it private.
  Git uses it only on your computer; ForkMesh never sees it.

## 2. Add it to ForkMesh as a private repository

1. In the desktop app open **Repos** and choose **Import folder…**.
2. Pick the folder you just cloned (`~/Backups/REPOSITORY`).
3. ForkMesh asks **Import REPOSITORY?**. Choose **Private**.

**Private** means the copy is encrypted before it leaves your computer, is
hidden from public browsing and cloning, and only you (and people you share it
with) can read it. Do not choose **Public**: that lists it for anyone.

## 3. Keep it up to date

While the desktop app is open, ForkMesh checks the folder about once a minute
and copies anything new to the ForkMesh network (change how often under
**Settings → Mirror sync**). ForkMesh does not fetch from GitHub by itself yet, so bring in your
friend's newest changes by pulling them into the folder:

```sh
git -C ~/Backups/REPOSITORY pull
```

ForkMesh then copies them within the next sync. Pull as often as you want a
fresh backup, for example once a week.

## 4. Check the backup

Open the repository in **Repos** and look at its settings: it shows
**Managed mirror enabled** and **Last sync** with a time. A recent time means
the ForkMesh copy matches the folder on your computer.

## Things that will not happen

- Nothing is changed on GitHub or on your live website: clone and pull only
  read. Avoid the **Push** button and `git push` until you mean to change the
  website.
- Nothing becomes public unless you choose **Public**.
- Removing the repository from ForkMesh does not delete it from GitHub.

Back to [Getting started](getting-started.md) or the
[documentation index](README.md).

pages.description: The ForkMesh extension for Chrome brings your Password Vault, your organization's CRM and Marketing, and one-click repository mirroring into the browser, all behind one sign-in.…
pages.markdown:
# Browser extension

The ForkMesh extension for Chrome brings your Password Vault, your
organization's CRM and Marketing, and one-click repository mirroring into the
browser, all behind one sign-in. It acts only when you press a button, on the
sites listed below, and reads nothing else.

Part of the [ForkMesh apps](apps.md). How it is built and released:
[browser extension internals](marketplace/browser-extension.md).

## At a glance

| | Feature | Works on | Needs | What reaches ForkMesh |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🔑 | [Password Vault](#password-vault) | Any https site, from the toolbar popup | Your vault (per account) | Ciphertext only |
| 📇 | [CRM](#crm) | Gmail, Zoho Mail, Mastodon | The `crm` package in your organization | Message ids, subject, addresses, date; never the body |
| 📥 | [Zoho Mail inbox tools](#zoho-mail-inbox-tools) | Zoho Mail | Nothing, not even a sign-in | Nothing |
| 📣 | [Marketing](#marketing) | X, Reddit, Google results, any channel you configure | The `marketing` package in your organization | The counts a channel page shows |
| 📦 | [Repositories](#repositories) | GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea | A ForkMesh account | The repository's address, when you press Mirror |
| 💬 | [Discourse forums](#discourse-forums) | Any Discourse forum | A ForkMesh account | The forum's address, when you press Mirror |

Requirements: Chrome 137 or newer, or a Chromium browser of the same age (for
native X25519 and Ed25519). The current version is shown on the
**Browser extension** page of the dashboard (`/dashboard/extension`).

## How it works

```text
  ┌──────────────────────────── your browser ─────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                                       │
  │   toolbar popup · side panel            page readers                  │
  │   (you press a button)                  Gmail, Zoho Mail, Mastodon,   │
  │            │                            X, Reddit, Discourse          │
  │            ▼                                     │                    │
  │   ┌─────────────────────────────────┐            │                    │
  │   │ service worker                  │◄───────────┘                    │
  │   │  session token (local storage)  │   readers only look; they never │
  │   │  vault keys (memory only)       │   click, post or send to sites  │
  │   └───────────────┬─────────────────┘                                 │
  └───────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                      │ HTTPS · Authorization: Bearer · browser cookies never sent
                      ▼
       your ForkMesh server: /api/vault · /api/crm · /api/marketing
                             /api/repository-imports
```

Every request to ForkMesh goes from the extension's background service worker
with the session token it received when you signed in. Website cookies are
never used, so being signed in to ForkMesh in a tab does not sign the
extension in, and the reverse.

## Install

The extension is installed from the dashboard, not from the Chrome Web Store.

1. Open **Browser extension** in the ForkMesh dashboard
   (`/dashboard/extension`), click **Download vX.Y.Z** and unzip it. You get
   a folder named `browser-extension`.
2. Click **Open chrome://extensions**, turn on **Developer mode**, press
   **Load unpacked** and pick that `browser-extension` folder.
3. Pin the ForkMesh icon to the toolbar, click it and sign in with your
   ForkMesh account (password, and your authenticator code if you use one).
4. For the CRM and Marketing, pick the organization the extension works for.
   The vault and repositories need no organization.

```text
  dashboard ──► Download ──► unzip ──► chrome://extensions ──► Load unpacked
                                         (Developer mode on)        │
                                                                    ▼
                         ForkMesh icon ──► Sign in ──► pick organization
```

**Self-hosted ForkMesh.** Expand **Self-hosted ForkMesh** on the sign-in form
and enter your server's address; Chrome asks once for access to it.

**Updating.** The dashboard page says when the installed copy is older than
the current one. Unzip the new download over the same folder and press
**Reload** on the extension's card in `chrome://extensions`. Keeping the same
folder keeps the same extension id, so you stay signed in.

**Signing out.** **Sign out** in the popup ends the session on the server,
forgets the token and locks the vault.

## Password Vault

Create your vault on ForkMesh first (**Vault** in the dashboard), then use it
from the toolbar popup on any https site:

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Unlock** | Opens the vault with your master password, stretched with Argon2id inside the extension and never sent |
| **Fill** | Types the saved username and password into the page you are on |
| **User** / **Pass** | Copies one field |
| **Save this page's login** | Offers to save what you typed on this page |
| **Generate password** | Copies a new 24-character password |
| **Lock** | Locks at once; the vault also locks after 15 idle minutes, on sign-out and when the browser closes |

Why it is safe to use:

- 🚫 **No standing access.** There is no content script on the open web and no
  access to all sites; a page is touched only after you press a button.
- 🎯 **Exact site match.** A login fills only when the tab's host is exactly
  the saved host (`www.` aside), over https, in the top frame. The check runs
  in the background worker, not in the page.
- 🧠 **Keys in memory only.** The unlocked keys live in the background worker
  and Chrome's session storage, which content scripts cannot read and which
  is cleared when the browser closes.
- 🔒 **Ciphertext on the server.** The vault sends only encrypted items,
  wrapped keys and signed shares to ForkMesh; the extension carries its own
  copy of the vault's cryptography rather than loading it from the server.

## CRM

The CRM half links the conversations you have open to contacts in your
organization's ForkMesh CRM. It works in Gmail (`mail.google.com`), Zoho Mail
(`mail.zoho.com`, `.eu`, `.in`, `.com.au`, `.jp`, `mail.zohocloud.ca`) and any
Mastodon instance you add.

**An email.** A compact **CRM header** above the message names the other party
and offers **Look up**; nothing is asked of ForkMesh until you press it. Look
up shows the record: name, pipeline and stage, owner, last email, linked
emails, company, title, deal value, next step and tags. The **FM** button (or
the toolbar popup) opens the panel, prefilled from the message:

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Add to pipeline** | Picks a flow and stage, creates the contact if needed and links the email |
| **Link only** | Records the message without changing the pipeline |
| **Link to an existing contact…** | Files the message under another record; the address joins that record, so the next message is found by itself |
| **Last contacted** | Sets the date on the record |
| **Unlink** | Removes the link |

Records are matched by address, Mastodon handle, LinkedIn, GitHub or X
profile, phone, or by name when the address or company supports it. A name
that contradicts the record or fits two records never matches on its own, and
the panel says how a record was found.

**Mail you send.** With **Track emails I send** on (the default), a message you
send from Gmail or Zoho Mail is linked to the first recipient that already has
a record, people outside your domain first, and moves **Last contacted**. Gmail
sends are linked after its 10-second undo window. No contact is created for a
send to unknown people.

**Mastodon.** Add each instance under **Mastodon instances** in the popup, or
press **Record this toot in the CRM** on one you have not added; Chrome asks
for that site once. With **Add people I mention on Mastodon** on (the
default), opening one of your own posts on its permalink links everyone it
mentions to the CRM, up to ten people, creating contacts for new ones.
Timelines, profiles and other people's posts send nothing.

**Save this page to a contact** adds a dated line with the page's title and
address to a contact's notes.

## Zoho Mail inbox tools

Two strips sit above Zoho Mail's message list. They need no sign-in and send
nothing anywhere; everything lasts until the tab is reloaded.

- **Sort** by **Sender**, **Subject** (ignoring `Re:` and `Fwd:`) or
  **Date**; click again to reverse.
- **Search** as you type: every word must match the subject or the sender;
  `from:acme` and `subject:invoice` narrow it, `"two words"` keeps a phrase.
- **Group by sender** puts the biggest senders first and lets you pick one.
- **Select**, **Mark read**, **Archive** and **Delete** act on exactly the
  messages shown. The extension ticks Zoho's own checkboxes, checks Zoho
  selected that exact set, then presses Zoho's own button. **Delete** asks
  first and moves to Trash; permanent delete is never pressed.

## Marketing

For organizations using the Marketing package, the extension reads the
numbers that channel pages show, so the Marketing dashboard stays current
without anyone copying figures by hand. It reads only when asked and never
posts, clicks or sends anything to the channel sites.

| Feature | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| **Update** on a channel | Opens the channel's saved page in a new tab, reads its counts, sends them to Marketing, closes the tab. The first time, Chrome asks for that one site; **Allow channel sites** grants all of them at once. Discord is never opened in a tab; Marketing asks Discord's public API instead. |
| **Side panel** | Lists, per site, the pages that feed Marketing, marks those read in the last 12 hours and suggests the next one to update. The toolbar badge counts the unread pages. |
| **X profile stats** | On your tracked X profile, **Sync now** records followers, following, posts and the counts of posts on screen. **Update X stats from this page** keeps sending changes until you stop it. |
| **Connect X for posting** | Started from Marketing by an owner or admin: a guide card walks X's developer console and reads the four keys, which go once to Marketing to be checked with X. Signing in, accepting X's terms and buying credits stay with you. |
| **Reddit desk** | Reads the watched subreddits, searches, threads and rules pages you open, and your own accounts' posts and views. Nothing reaches the desk until you press **Send to Reddit desk**, except fresh numbers for threads already in the log. **Walk the watch list** visits up to 24 pages in one tab at a reader's pace, scrolling only. |

## Repositories

Open the popup on any page of a repository on `github.com`, `gitlab.com`,
`codeberg.org` or `gitea.com`. A card shows its size, stars, forks and open
issues, its language, licence and default branch, when it last changed, and
whether it is already on ForkMesh.

**Mirror to my ForkMesh account** lists the repository under your account;
the mirror nodes copy its Git history on their next pass (about every 30
minutes), and **Open on ForkMesh** takes you to it. A repository someone else
already listed is not listed twice. Private repositories get no card, because
the provider's public API does not show them: import them from
**Repositories** on ForkMesh with a read token
([repository imports](repository-imports.md)).

Nothing runs inside GitHub or GitLab: the popup reads only the tab's address,
and details come from the provider's public API without your provider
sign-in.

## Discourse forums

On any Discourse forum the popup shows **Mirror this forum**. It opens your
ForkMesh server's mirror setup with the forum's address filled in: on an
instance where you are an admin it sets up the mirror; elsewhere it explains
how to start an instance of your own. The extension reads only the page's
generator tag and site name, and only when you open the popup.

## Permissions

| Chrome permission | Why the extension needs it |
| --- | --- |
| `storage` | Keeps your session token, organization and settings |
| `activeTab`, `scripting` | Fills a login or reads a page only in the tab where you pressed a button |
| `alarms` | Locks the vault after 15 idle minutes; runs the optional hourly Reddit thread update |
| `sidePanel` | Shows the Marketing refresh panel |
| `tabs` | Reads the current tab's address for the repository card and the side panel; the address stays in the browser |
| ForkMesh sites | Talks to app.forkmesh.com and forkmesh.com |
| Reddit | Lets the Reddit desk read the pages it is asked to |
| Optional: other https sites | Asked for one site at a time: your self-hosted server, a Mastodon instance, a Marketing channel |

The extension also reads pages on Gmail, Zoho Mail, X, X's developer console
and Zoho's API console, each for the feature named above.

## What leaves the browser

| Feature | Sent to ForkMesh | Never sent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vault | Encrypted items, wrapped keys, signed shares | Master password, keys, decrypted logins |
| CRM | Message and thread ids, subject, addresses or handles, direction, date, the details shown in the panel, the chosen flow and stage | The email body (read only to prefill the panel) |
| Marketing | A channel's counts, title, description, image and up to five recent posts; Reddit desk fields; X keys once | Anything to X, Reddit or the channel sites |
| Repositories | The derived import id when you open the popup; the address when you press Mirror | Your provider sign-in |
| Zoho Mail tools | Nothing | Everything |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome says **Missing 'manifest_version' key** | You picked the wrong folder. Pick the unzipped `browser-extension` folder, or from a checkout `marketplace/packages/browser-extension/content/extension` |
| The dashboard says the extension is out of date | Unzip the new download over the same folder and press **Reload** on its card |
| You were asked to sign in again after updating | The new copy went to a different folder, which Chrome treats as a new extension; sign in once |
| Chrome refuses to load it | Update Chrome to 137 or newer |
| CRM buttons do nothing | Pick an organization in the popup; the `crm` package must be installed there |
| A repository's size shows "–" | GitLab tells only a project's members its size |
| The repository card says the provider is rate-limiting | GitHub allows 60 public requests an hour per address; Mirror still works, because the server reads the provider itself |
| A Marketing update asks for a site | Allow it once, or press **Allow channel sites** to grant all channels |

## Related

[ForkMesh apps](apps.md) ·
[Repository imports](repository-imports.md) ·
[Encryption and signatures](encryption.md) ·
[Browser extension internals](marketplace/browser-extension.md) ·
[Documentation index](README.md)

pages.title: Voice and video calls
pages.description: You can call anyone you have a direct message with, or everyone in a private channel at once. Calls work on the web at /chat, on iPhone and on Android. The desktop app has no…
pages.markdown:
# Voice and video calls

You can call anyone you have a direct message with, or everyone in a private
channel at once. Calls work on the web at `/chat`, on iPhone and on Android.
The desktop app has no call engine of its own: its call buttons open the call
in your browser and ask before anything rings.
How calls are encrypted is on
[Encryption and signatures](encryption.md#end-to-end-encrypted-chat-and-calls).

## Start a call

1. Open the direct message and press the phone button (voice) or the camera
   button (video) in the header.
2. A pre-call check opens first. You see your camera, can pick a face,
   background or voice filter, and can press **Record a 10-second test clip**
   to hear exactly what the other person will get.
3. Press **Start voice call** or **Start video call**. Only now does it ring.

The other person's phone rings on any screen. An iPhone shows the system call
screen, even when it is locked or ForkMesh is closed, and even with
notifications turned off. The push notification never names the caller; the
app shows the name once it has opened the encrypted invite. A call nobody
answers leaves a "Missed audio call" or "Missed video call" line in the
conversation. A declined call leaves nothing, and the caller sees "Call
declined" or "Busy" with the reason.

## During a call

- **Back to chat** shrinks the call into a small window with Mute, Hang up
  and Open. Drag it anywhere; tap it or press Open to make it large again.
  The web remembers where you left it.
- Until the other person's video arrives, or while their camera is off, you
  see your own camera and their name instead of a black screen.
- On iPhone, video calls play through the loudspeaker, like FaceTime. Voice
  calls use the earpiece. The ring/silent switch does not mute a call.
- On iPhone, app sounds, speech and dictation leave your microphone alone
  while a call runs. During someone else's call (a phone call, Signal,
  FaceTime) ForkMesh stays quiet too.

## When the connection drops

A call reconnects by itself after a network drop, or when the other person's
audio goes silent while the connection still looks fine. The call says
"Reconnecting…" meanwhile. If it is not back within 30 seconds it ends with
"Call lost". A call that never connects ends after 30 seconds with "Could not
connect". If your microphone is unplugged or interrupted, the call opens it
again and says "Microphone reconnected".

One-to-one media goes straight between the two devices, with no relay server
in between. Two people who are both behind strict networks (some mobile
carriers and office firewalls) may not be able to connect at all.

## Call quality and Diagnose

Every call shows a small pill with four signal bars, a voice waveform (you up,
the other side down) and the round trip time. Four bars is a good connection,
one a poor one. Click the pill to open charts of your voice, the network and,
on video calls, the video in and out.

Next to it, **Diagnose** is grey while it measures, green while the call is
fine, and red when
it finds a lasting problem: high latency, lost packets, jitter, video held
back by bandwidth or by your device, a low frame rate, or a slow face filter.
Press it to see each problem, why it matters and the fixes in order. **Copy
prompt** gives you a ready question for an AI assistant; paste its `LESSON:`
line back and the next prompt starts from it. Fixes that worked on your
device move up the list. Nothing is sent anywhere: the report stays on your
device.

Voice is sent at up to 128 kbps with protection against lost packets, and when
the network is tight the call keeps your voice and lowers the picture first.

## Group calls

In a private channel, the same buttons start a group call for up to 16 people.
Members who are not in it see "A call is in progress here" with a Join button.
Public channels have no group calls, because their messages are readable by
the server. On the web, stay on the channel during the call: if you switch to
another one, people who join meanwhile see a blank tile for you until you
come back.

## Verification codes

Group calls on ForkMesh's newer call engine (on iPhone, and on the web in
browsers that support it) show four emoji with their names and "Or compare
numbers: 123 456". Read them aloud with everyone and press **They match** or
**They don't match**. The code changes when someone joins, and the panel says
who is not verified yet. If the codes differ, someone may be listening in:
leave the call and tell the others another way. A tile warns you when a
person's video cannot be confirmed as theirs or fails a check. Scanning a QR
code instead, and remembering verified people between calls, are not built
yet.

## What is encrypted

- **One-to-one calls.** The messages that set up the call are sealed with
  chat encryption, so the relay sees only ciphertext and stores none of it.
  Audio and video are encrypted and go directly between the two devices. The
  relay learns that a call is ringing in a conversation and when, not whether
  it is voice or video.
- **Group calls.** Each sender encrypts every audio and video frame on their
  device. ForkMesh's call server forwards the frames without being able to
  decrypt them. On the newer engine the keys use post-quantum key exchange and
  each sender signs their media, so nobody in the call can fake someone
  else's picture.
- Face, background and voice filters run on your device.

See [Chat encryption and integrations](security/sealed-chat.md) for how chat
itself is sealed, and [Safety numbers and trusted devices](chat-safety-numbers.md)
for checking who you are talking to.

## On Android

Android has one-to-one calls with the pre-call check and the quality pill.
Group calls, automatic reconnecting, the small call window, the Diagnose
button and the loudspeaker change arrive on iPhone first and are still being
ported. See [ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

pages.markdown:
# Safety numbers and trusted devices

Direct messages are end-to-end encrypted to each device of the two people in
the conversation. Every browser, phone and desktop you sign in on has its own
chat key. A safety number lets you check that nobody else's key has slipped
into the conversation, and new devices wait for your approval before they get
anything.
How chat keys and signatures fit together is on
[Encryption and signatures](encryption.md#end-to-end-encrypted-chat-and-calls).

Approvals and safety numbers are for direct messages. Channels accept every
correctly signed device on their own; see
[Chat encryption and integrations](security/sealed-chat.md).

## What a safety number is

A safety number is 60 digits in 12 groups of five, plus a QR code. You and the
other person see the same number, and it covers every approved device on both
sides. To find it:

- **Web.** Press the lock button ("End-to-end") in the conversation header.
  The Chat encryption panel shows the number under **Safety number**.
- **iPhone.** Open the conversation's details and tap **Safety number**. It
  shows the digits, your QR code and **Scan their code**.
- **Android.** Open **Safety number** from the conversation's menu.

Compare the digits in person or over a call you trust, or scan the other
phone's code. Then press **Mark as verified**. A scan tells you whether it
matched, or whether you scanned the wrong code.

## When it changes

The number changes whenever the set of approved devices changes: someone
approves a new phone or browser, or a device gets a new key. The change clears
"verified", and the conversation says "Your safety number with Alex changed".
If nobody you know added a device, compare the number again before you share
anything sensitive: a key nobody expected can mean someone is trying to read
along.

## New devices wait for you

In a direct message, the first device you see for a person is trusted. Every
further device for that person, including a new device of your own, waits.
It gets nothing sealed to it and its messages are held, unseen, until you
decide. The conversation shows "A new device for Alex wants to join this chat.
Check the safety number, then approve or block." and a banner with
**Safety number**, **Approve** and **Block**.

- **Approve** lets it receive new messages and opens the ones it sent while it
  waited (the most recent ones, if it sent many).
- **Block** keeps it out.
- A new device reads only messages sealed after it was approved, never the
  older history.

When several devices are waiting at once, for example after someone signs in
on a new phone and a new browser, the iPhone shows one banner for all of them
("2 new devices for Alex want to join this chat"), and Approve and Block act
on all of them. The web shows one device at a time and says how many are
waiting. On Android the single banner is still being ported.

## Reinstalling on iPhone

Your iPhone keeps a projects folder, by default in iCloud Drive, that survives
deleting the app. It holds your identity key, encrypted with your passphrase.
When you reinstall ForkMesh and press **Restore**, the app rebuilds your chat
key from that identity key. Your safety numbers stay the same, the people you
chat with see no new device, and a conversation you had verified stays
verified.

- This works only when the folder outlives the app. If the folder sits inside
  the app (On My iPhone › ForkMesh), it is deleted with the app, and ForkMesh
  warns you at every launch with "Keep your ForkMesh data safe" until you move
  it.
- If your iPhone set up chat before this was added (October 2026), it keeps
  its older chat key until the next reinstall. That one reinstall changes your
  safety numbers once; after it they survive.
- Restoring the key does not unlock old messages: the keys that opened them
  are not part of it.
- On Android, keeping the chat key through a reinstall is still being
  ported.

Related: [Voice and video calls](calls.md) has verification codes for group
calls, and [Portable identities and recovery](portable-identities.md) covers
your identity key.
