pages.markdown:
# Mirror and deploy a Cloudflare Worker with ForkMesh

You already have a Cloudflare Worker and a GitHub repository for it. This guide
makes ForkMesh a signed mirror of that repository and the place your Worker is
deployed from. Each push to the default branch deploys automatically. You can
also deploy, watch the log, approve and roll back from your phone.

Your Cloudflare token stays on your own ForkMesh desktop. It never goes to
GitHub, the ForkMesh relay or a shared runner. More guides are in the
[docs index](README.md).

## How it fits together

```text
GitHub push ──► GitHub Actions bridge ──► ForkMesh (ssh.forkmesh.com)
                                              │
                                              ▼
                     your ForkMesh desktop  (label: cloudflare-deploy)
                     .forkmesh/deploy-cloudflare.yml
                                              │  wrangler deploy
                                              ▼
                                     Cloudflare Workers

ForkMesh phone app ──► desktop (LAN or relay): Run · Re-run · Approve · Roll back
```

| Piece | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/forkmesh-github-sync.yml` | Copies branches and tags between GitHub and ForkMesh on every push and every 15 minutes, fast-forward only ([Connecting to GitHub](forge-sync.md#connecting-a-repository-to-github)) |
| `.forkmesh/deploy-cloudflare.yml` | Runs on your desktop when the default branch moves, or when you start it by hand |
| `.forkmesh/rollback-cloudflare.yml` | Started by hand: rolls the Worker back to its previous version |
| `.forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py` | Checks the setup, runs Wrangler and reports the deployed URL and version |
| `.forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.json` | Worker folder, Wrangler environment, branch and variable names |

## Before you start

On the computer that will deploy (your ForkMesh desktop):

- the ForkMesh desktop, signed in to your account. Desktop Actions run on
  **Linux** only. They need `bwrap` (bubblewrap), a systemd user session, and
  a desktop that is not running as root.
- **Node.js 22 or newer** and **npm**, installed system-wide; current Wrangler
  needs Node.js 22. Many distributions still ship an older `nodejs`, so
  check `node --version`; [NodeSource](https://github.com/nodesource/distributions)
  packages install into `/usr`. Runs see `/usr` but not your home folder, so a
  Node.js installed with `nvm` is not found.
- `python3` and `git`.

You also need:

- a **Cloudflare API token**. In the Cloudflare dashboard, open *My Profile →
  API Tokens → Create Token* and use the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template.
  Limit it to the account and zones the Worker uses.
- your **Cloudflare account ID**: 32 hexadecimal characters, shown in the
  dashboard's Workers overview.
- admin rights on the GitHub repository, and the `gh` command-line tool
  (optional, but it makes setting secrets easier).
- a ForkMesh repository with the same name. Create an empty one under
  **Repositories → New** on [app.forkmesh.com](https://app.forkmesh.com).
- the ForkMesh tools:

```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh ~/forkmesh-tools
```

## Step 1: connect the repository

Run `connect` in a checkout of your Worker's GitHub repository. It writes the
deploy files above and the GitHub sync files, and adds `github` and `forkmesh`
remotes:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/OWNER/NAME && cd NAME
python3 ~/forkmesh-tools/tools/cloudflare_worker_deploy.py connect \
  --github OWNER/NAME \
  --bridge-key-out ~/forkmesh-bridge.pem
```

Add these options as needed:

| Option | Use it when |
| --- | --- |
| `--worker-dir worker` | `wrangler.toml` / `wrangler.json(c)` is not at the repository root |
| `--env production` | you deploy a Wrangler environment (`[env.production]`) |
| `--branch release` | you deploy from a branch other than `main` |
| `--manual-only` | you only want deploys you start yourself, never on push |
| `--needs .forkmesh/ci.yml` | a ForkMesh test workflow must pass first |
| `--forkmesh OWNER/NAME` | the ForkMesh repository has a different owner or name |
| `--runs-on LABEL` | you want a desktop label other than `cloudflare-deploy` |
| `--token-variable NAME`, `--account-variable NAME` | different Workers deploy to different Cloudflare accounts |
| `--replace-vars` | Wrangler may delete dashboard variables that are missing from your config (by default they are kept, with `--keep-vars`) |
| `--no-rollback` | you do not want the roll-back workflow |

`connect` prints a JSON summary. Its `nextSteps` list is a checklist of the
remaining steps, and `existingGitHubDeploys` lists GitHub workflows that
already deploy this Worker. Running `connect` again is safe: it only rewrites
files whose content changed.

## Step 2: let GitHub push to ForkMesh

The bridge workflow pushes to ForkMesh over SSH. Give it its own key:

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C forkmesh-sync -f ~/forkmesh-sync
```

1. Add `~/forkmesh-sync.pub` to your ForkMesh account under
   **Settings → SSH keys** (`/dashboard/settings/ssh-keys`). The key acts with
   your account's write access.
2. Store the secrets in GitHub:

```bash
gh secret set FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY --repo OWNER/NAME < ~/forkmesh-bridge.pem
gh secret set FORKMESH_SYNC_SSH_KEY --repo OWNER/NAME < ~/forkmesh-sync
gh variable set FORKMESH_SYNC_REMOTE --repo OWNER/NAME \
  --body ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/OWNER/NAME.git
```

To pin the server's identity, also set the `FORKMESH_SYNC_KNOWN_HOSTS`
variable to this line:

```text
@cert-authority ssh.forkmesh.com,*.forkmesh.com ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAII5OvM7x8w4o1auHqYiSObIWHaVdAy4tT8dxLOai76Vs
```

## Step 3: prepare your desktop

1. **Add the repository.** In the desktop, open **Repositories** and clone
   `OWNER/NAME` from ForkMesh. The desktop now holds a mirror of the
   repository and receives each commit the bridge pushes.
2. **Label the desktop.** Under **Settings → Profile → Node labels**, add
   `cloudflare-deploy`. Only a node with this label runs the deploy. Mirrors
   and shared runners hold no secrets and skip it.
3. **Add the secrets.** Under **Settings → Secrets**, add:

| Name | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` | the API token from *Before you start* |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` | your 32-character account ID |
| `FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK` | `1` |

   A run receives only the variables its workflow names, and their values are
   masked in logs. `FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK` gives every Actions run on
   this desktop network access, because Wrangler needs to reach Cloudflare.
4. **Turn on Actions for the repository.** In the repository's **Actions** tab,
   tick **Run actions on push**. Then read [Keep the token safe](#keep-the-token-safe)
   before you decide on **Automatically approve runs**.

## Step 4: turn off the old deploy

If GitHub or Cloudflare also deploys this Worker, each push deploys twice and
the last deploy wins. Before your first ForkMesh deploy:

- disable or delete the GitHub workflows listed in `existingGitHubDeploys`
  (`cloudflare/wrangler-action` or `wrangler deploy` steps);
- if the Worker uses **Workers Builds** (Cloudflare's own Git integration),
  disconnect the repository under *Worker → Settings → Build* in the Cloudflare
  dashboard.

Keep your GitHub test workflows: they still run on GitHub.

## Step 5: commit and deploy

```bash
git add .forkmesh .github/workflows/forkmesh-github-sync.yml
git commit -m "Mirror to ForkMesh and deploy the Worker from it"
git push origin HEAD
```

The bridge copies the commit to ForkMesh within a minute or two, and your
desktop starts **Deploy Cloudflare Worker**. If you turned off
**Automatically approve runs**, the run waits until you approve it in the
desktop's Actions tab or from your phone. A successful run ends with a line
like:

```text
::cloudflare-deploy:: ok worker=shop version=1b2c3d4e-… url=https://shop.example.workers.dev
```

The first step, `check --online`, stops the run before anything is deployed if
the token, account ID, Node.js or network is wrong. See
[Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting).

## Deploy from your phone

Install the ForkMesh app for iPhone or Android and sign in to the same account
as your desktop. The app finds your desktop with no pairing code: on the same
Wi-Fi it connects directly, and away from home it goes through the end-to-end
encrypted relay ([Encryption](encryption.md)). Open the app once on the same
network as your desktop; if the connection away from home is refused, do that
again. See [Mobile access](mobile/mobile-agent-access.md).

Open the repository, then **Actions**:

| You want to | In the app |
| --- | --- |
| Deploy now | **Deploy Cloudflare Worker → Run**, branch `main` |
| Undo a bad deploy | **Roll back Cloudflare Worker → Run** |
| Let a held run start | open the run, **Approve** (or **Reject**) |
| Retry a failed deploy | open the run, **Re-run** |
| Stop a deploy | open the run, **Stop** |
| See what happened | open the run: steps and live log, ending with the URL and version |

Things to know:

- Your desktop must be switched on, signed in and online. A re-run you ask
  for while it is offline is queued and starts when the desktop reconnects.
- You can also ship from GitHub's mobile app: merge a pull request into the
  default branch, and the bridge and your desktop deploy it.
- The website on a phone lists the workflows and the runs that mirrors report.
  It cannot start or approve a run on your desktop; use the app for that.
- This guide is in the app too, under **Docs**.

## Keep the token safe

Anyone who can change `.forkmesh/` workflows on the default branch can make a
run read `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`. With the bridge, that includes everyone with
write access on GitHub. The desktop approves a workflow's exact content, so:

- untick **Automatically approve runs** for this repository if other people can
  push to it. Every changed workflow then waits until you approve it, which you
  can do from your phone;
- give the token only the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** permissions, for the one
  account and zone it needs;
- revoke and replace the token in Cloudflare if a run you did not expect ever
  reads it, then update **Settings → Secrets**.

Pull requests never run this workflow: it has no `pull_request` trigger, and the
bridge fetches pull request code only as data and never runs it.

## Several Workers or environments

- **Staging and production:** connect with `--env production` and keep the
  default deploy for `main`. To deploy staging from another branch, use a
  second checkout or repository; one repository holds one deploy
  configuration.
- **Monorepo:** use `--worker-dir` for the Worker you deploy from this
  repository.
- **Two Cloudflare accounts:** save the tokens under different names
  (`SHOP_CF_TOKEN`, `SHOP_CF_ACCOUNT`) and pass `--token-variable` and
  `--account-variable`.

## Moving off GitHub

To drop GitHub completely, import the repository (**Repositories → New →
GitHub**, see [Repository imports](repository-imports.md)) or push your
history to an empty ForkMesh repository. Then run `connect` without
`--github`. Pushes to ForkMesh's default branch deploy the same way.

## Troubleshooting

| The log says | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| `bubblewrap (bwrap) is required` / `no configured ForkMesh Actions sandbox` | Run the deploy on a Linux desktop with `bubblewrap` installed |
| `Node.js is not installed on this node` / `Node.js 20 is too old` | Install system-wide Node.js 22+ (for example from NodeSource); a Node.js from `nvm` is not visible to runs |
| `… GiB of virtual address space` | Update the ForkMesh desktop; Wrangler reserves a large sparse address range |
| `Cloudflare's API is unreachable` | Add `FORKMESH_ACTIONS_ALLOW_NETWORK` = `1` under **Settings → Secrets** |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is empty` / `not a 32-character account ID` | Add or correct the secret under **Settings → Secrets** (names are case-sensitive) |
| `Cloudflare rejected the API token` | Create a new token from the **Edit Cloudflare Workers** template |
| `pins account_id … different account` | Your `wrangler.toml` names another account: fix `account_id` or the secret |
| `no wrangler.jsonc, wrangler.json, wrangler.toml` | Run `connect` again with `--worker-dir` |
| `skipped refs/heads/… is not refs/heads/main` | Expected: only the configured branch deploys |
| The run never starts | Check the `cloudflare-deploy` node label, **Run actions on push**, and whether the run is waiting for approval |
| GitHub commits never reach ForkMesh | Open the **ForkMesh GitHub sync** run on GitHub; check `FORKMESH_SYNC_REMOTE`, the SSH key, and that the ForkMesh repository exists |
| Two deploys per push | Turn off the GitHub or Workers Builds deploy (Step 4) |

## Command reference

`cloudflare_worker_deploy.py` is also copied into your repository as
`.forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py`:

```bash
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py check            # config, Wrangler file, Node.js
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py check --online   # plus token, account and Worker
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py deploy --dry-run # build without uploading
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py deploy
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py rollback [--version VERSION_ID]
python3 .forkmesh/cloudflare-deploy.py render-workflow
```

`deploy` and `rollback` read `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`
from the environment, so you can also run them by hand from a terminal. Exit
codes: `0` success or skipped, `1` the deploy failed, `2` setup error, `75`
Cloudflare unreachable. Wrangler output is masked so the token never appears.

pages.markdown:
# How the codebase fits together

The developer entry page. ForkMesh keeps Git data on hosts people run
themselves; the app on the core nodes handles accounts, routing and
collaboration metadata. The public overview, including what is still a single
dependency, is [docs/architecture.md](architecture.md); the
index of developer docs is [README.md](README.md).

```text
        browsers · phones (iOS, Android) · desktop nodes · mirrors
                              │
     DNS round robin (app.forkmesh.com, world.forkmesh.com), no proxy
                              ▼
   core nodes n3 · n4 · n5 (equal; WireGuard mesh between them):
   Caddy · app (Python on CPython) · rqlite · Go daemon (Git gateway)
         ▲                 ▲                        ▲
 signed HTTP,       node events (WebSocket)    outbound job leases
 WebSockets               │                         │
   desktop node      mirror daemon             runners (agent jobs)
   (Qt, desktop/)    (Go, server/)
         └── both hold bare Git repositories and serve clones ──┘
```

## Parts

| Part | Code | Runs on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop node | `desktop/` (Qt 6, C++) | Linux, Windows, macOS |
| Mirror daemon and gateway | `server/` (Go), `tools/mirror_gateway.py` | headless mirrors, core nodes, runners |
| App | `app/` (Python, run on CPython by `app/host/`) | the core nodes ([served stack](operations/served-stack.md)) |
| Website | `www/` (static site and docs) | forkmesh.com ([www/README.md](www/README.md)) |
| World | `world/` (three.js client; backend in the app) | world.forkmesh.com |
| Native apps | `native/ios/`, `native/android/` | phones |
| Marketplace packages | `marketplace/` | inside the desktop, app, World and mobile hosts |
| Fleet tooling | `deploy/`, `tools/next_*.py` | operator box ([fleet tooling](operations/fleet-tooling.md)) |
| Releases | `tools/package/`, release tooling | build hosts ([release/README.md](release/README.md)) |
| Contracts | `conformance/` | CI and independent implementations ([conformance/README.md](conformance/README.md)) |

## How they talk

- **Identity.** Every node has an Ed25519 key and signs its requests; users
  have accounts with web sessions.
- **Desktop ↔ app.** HTTP API plus an account event WebSocket that pushes
  topics instead of polling; chat rides WebSockets into room objects, which
  `app/host/` places on one core by rendezvous hash
  ([app/cron-and-durable-objects.md](app/cron-and-durable-objects.md)).
- **Mirror ↔ app.** The daemon publishes a catalog record and endpoint lease
  per repository, holds a signed node-event WebSocket, materialises
  web-submitted issues and pulls into Git, and runs merges, agent jobs and
  Actions.
- **Desktop ↔ mirror.** The desktop installs and updates mirror hosts over SSH
  and pushes to them with Git.
- **Clones.** `git clone https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>` reaches a
  core, which redirects or proxies to a mirror whose signed health is fresh
  and whose refs match the signed pin
  ([docs/mirroring.md](mirroring.md)). The app stores no
  packfiles except for repositories hosted on the cores
  ([core-hosted repositories](operations/core-hosted-repositories.md)).
- **Collaboration records.** Issues, pulls, discussions, reviews and releases
  are signed files under `.forkmesh/` in the repository, so they travel with
  every clone.
- **Phones** are access clients over the same API and sockets; they do not
  mirror Git.
- **Agents.** Agent jobs run on desktops, mirrors or the untrusted runner tier,
  which holds only per-job grants ([runners](operations/runners.md)).
- **Packages.** Hosts expose generic sockets; packages contribute pages, API
  handlers and World modules without core code naming them.

## Where data lives

- Desktop: `~/projects/forkmesh/{data,config,cache,state,logs,ssh}` with the
  checkout in `src/`.
- Mirror: the daemon's config, identity key and bare repositories.
- Cores: rqlite (payloads encrypted under `DATA_KEY`, HMAC blind indexes),
  node-local caches, and room-object storage in rqlite. Secrets are sealed in
  the vault ([vault](operations/vault.md)); every layer is summarised in
  [docs/encryption.md](encryption.md).

Trust boundaries: [security/README.md](security/README.md) and the
[threat model](protocol/threat-model.md). The normative protocol
for independent implementations is the
[protocol suite](protocol/README.md). Running your own:
[docs/self-hosting.md](self-hosting.md).

pages.markdown:
# Working with coding agents

ForkMesh publishes one guide written for coding agents such as Claude Code:
[app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md).
Hand it to your agent and it can start your own ForkMesh instance for you,
work on ForkMesh repositories, and open pull requests the way the ForkMesh
team does.

## What the guide covers

- **Starting an instance.** What your server needs, writing the settings
  file for the [start page](https://forkmesh.com/start), or running
  `install-instance.sh` over SSH yourself, and what to do once it is up.
- **Working on a repository.** Cloning, branching, pushing to a hosted
  repository, and small commits with one scope each.
- **Opening pull requests.** From the desktop app, the MCP server's
  `open_pr_from_branch`, or the signed HTTP API, and the rules that keep a
  pull request easy to accept: small, independent of the others, built on
  the current `main`, and confirmed on the server before it is called live.
- **Ground rules.** Ask before anything hard to undo, never print secrets,
  never delete ForkMesh data folders.

## Use it in one message

Copy this into Claude Code (the start page has a Copy button for it):

```text
Read https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md and help me start my own ForkMesh instance. Ask me for anything you need first.
```

The agent asks for your server address, domain, admin account and repository
owner, writes the settings file, and tells you when to upload it on the start
page. Your SSH password or key and your admin password stay out of the file:
you type them into the page yourself, so the agent never sees them. It asks
before it runs anything on your server.

## Keep it in your repository without committing it

To have every session read the guide, save it next to your code and tell Git
to ignore it only in your clone:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md -o FORKMESH.md
echo FORKMESH.md >> .git/info/exclude
```

`.git/info/exclude` is a per-clone `.gitignore` that is never committed, so
the file stays yours. Add `FORKMESH.md` to `.gitignore` instead when the
whole team should ignore it. Then point your agent at it: add `@FORKMESH.md`
to an ignored `CLAUDE.md`, or start a session with "read FORKMESH.md".

Re-download it now and then; the guide changes as ForkMesh does.

## Connect the ForkMesh MCP server

The ForkMesh source ships an MCP server, `tools/forkmesh_mcp_server.py`,
and lists it in `.mcp.json`, so Claude Code opened in a ForkMesh checkout
finds it. Reading code, issues and notes needs no token. Writing (issues,
notes, pull requests) needs a device-local token from **Desktop → Settings →
MCP**. No MCP tool gives a shell, arbitrary file access, pushes or
administration.

## Related

- [Start your own instance](start-your-own-instance.md)
- [Start from a settings file](start-config.md)
- [Contributing](../CONTRIBUTING.md), including the pull request workflow
- [Contribute with git only](contributing-with-git.md)

pages.markdown:
# Contribute with git only

You can contribute to a public repository on ForkMesh with plain `git` and a
browser. You do not need the desktop app. The steps match GitHub: fork, push a
branch to your fork, open a pull request.

The examples use `app.forkmesh.com`. On a self-hosted instance, use that
instance's address instead, for example `git.example.org`.

## 1. Fork the repository

Sign in with a verified email address, open the repository and click **Fork**
next to **Star** at the top of the page. ForkMesh creates `<you>/<repo>` in
your account. Your fork shares the original repository's history, so it is
ready at once, whatever the repository's size.

If you already have a fork, **Fork** opens it. The arrow next to **Fork** lists
everyone's forks.

## 2. Clone and add your fork as a remote

```bash
git clone https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
cd <repo>
git remote add fork https://app.forkmesh.com/<you>/<repo>.git
```

`origin` stays the original repository, so `git pull` keeps you up to date.

## 3. Push a branch

```bash
git checkout -b my-change
git commit -am "Describe the change"
git push fork my-change
```

When git asks for a username and password, enter your ForkMesh account name or
email and your account password. A push credential from **Settings → SSH keys
→ Push code over HTTPS** also works as the password.

After the push, git prints the page to open:

```
remote: Open a pull request for 'my-change' by visiting:
remote:      https://app.forkmesh.com/<you>/<repo>/compare/main...my-change
```

## 4. Open the pull request

Open that link, write a title and a description, and click **Create pull
request**. The pull request goes to the original repository. Your browser signs
it, so the maintainer can check it came from your account. If the original is
a read-only mirror of a repository hosted elsewhere, the pull request is
opened on your fork instead, and the page says so.

A pull request opened from a branch of the same repository follows that
branch: push more commits (or force-push a rebase) and the pull request shows
them, with "pushed N commits" in its timeline. A pull request from a fork
records your branch as it was when you opened it. After you push more commits
to your fork, open the pull request and click **Update pull request**: it sends
your branch's current state as a new revision, and the comments and reviews
stay. Only the pull request's author can update it this way.

## Without a fork

Some repositories let contributors push straight to them. There, push a branch
named `pr/<your-account>/<topic>` to the original repository and open the pull
request from the link git prints. See
[Contributing without write access](hosted-repositories.md#contributing-without-write-access).

## Good to know

- You can fork any public repository, whether it is hosted on ForkMesh's
  servers or published from someone's own node (like `forkmesh/forkmesh`). If
  you have a linked managed mirror, a fork of a node-published repository is
  made on your mirror instead.
- You can force-push your own branches after a rebase, amend or squash, which
  updates an open pull request. Use `git push --force-with-lease`: it refuses
  when the branch has commits you have not fetched (say, after **Update
  branch** on the pull request). If that happens, run `git pull --rebase` and
  push again. The default branch and protected branches only move forward,
  and the previous tip of a force-pushed branch is kept, so reviews of older
  commits still resolve.
- A pull request sent from your own copy as a patch series has no branch
  here to force-push: send the new commits with **Update pull request** on
  its page, which signs a revision of the same pull request.
- A push never deletes a branch. Delete branches on the fork's **Branches**
  page.
- Forks have their own per-account limit, separate from the repositories you
  create.
- If git says `Authentication failed`, check the account name or email and the
  password. [Git errors](git-errors.md) lists every message ForkMesh sends.

pages.markdown:
# Preservation-first crisis onboarding

For a project that could disappear soon. A plan
(`forkmesh-crisis-preservation-plan-v1`) orders the work to fit the time and
access left; an assessment (`forkmesh-crisis-preservation-assessment-v1`) and a
drill (`forkmesh-crisis-preservation-drill-v1`) report what is actually safe.
One pure reference implementation backs the API, CLI, and fixture. How copies
spread is on [Mirroring](mirroring.md); what survives a block is on
[Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md).

## Start here

```sh
curl -s 'https://app.forkmesh.com/api/preservation/crisis-plan?scenario=urgent_takedown&minutes=45'
tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py plan urgent_takedown --minutes 45
```

Work through `steps` in order: a [resumable import](repository-imports.md), a
pushed local clone, a [portable identity](portable-identities.md) export, or a
mirror request. Read `tradeoffs` first; an urgent plan that leaves anything out
sets `acknowledgementRequired`. Afterwards, assess the migration report and the
mirrors payload:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py assess request.json \
  --report report.json --availability mirrors.json
```

## Scenarios

Request fields: `scenario`, optional `minutes` (1 to 525,600), `access`
(`owner`, `read`, `public`, `none`), `sizeMb`, `issues`, `releases`,
`assetsMb`, `private`, `localClone`. Missing sizes use defaults listed in
`assumed`.

### `planned_shutdown`

Known end date, account still controlled. Window 30 days, access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`.
Drill budget: **120 minutes**.

### `urgent_takedown`

Removal could happen any moment; always urgent. Window 1 hour, access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`.
Drill budget: **30 minutes**.

### `lost_account`

Provider account lost; access capped at `public`. Window 1 day. Private data is
only preservable from a `localClone`.
Priority: `refs`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`.
Drill budget: **60 minutes**.

### `censorship`

Blocked in a region or by the provider. Window 4 hours, access `public`.
Independent operators in different regions matter most; see the
[availability proof](availability-proof.md).
Priority: `refs`, `trusted_mirrors`, `identity_proofs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `artifacts`, `issues`.
Drill budget: **60 minutes**.

### `provider_eol`

Provider or product discontinued. Window 7 days, access `owner`.
Priority: `refs`, `releases`, `documentation`, `issues`, `artifacts`, `identity_proofs`, `trusted_mirrors`.
Drill budget: **120 minutes**.

## How a plan is built

The plan walks the priority order and includes each category whose
conservative estimate fits the remaining time. The import copies issues,
releases, and documentation in a fixed phase order, so a deferred import
category defers every later one. A plan is urgent for `urgent_takedown` or a
window of 240 minutes or less. `refs` is always included, flagged when it
exceeds the window.

## Reasons

### `time_budget`

Higher-priority data uses the available time.

### `requires_token`

The source is private and the current access cannot read it.

### `source_unreachable`

The source is gone (`access: none`) and no local clone holds the data.

### `import_order`

An earlier import phase did not fit, so this one will not be reached.

### `needs_refs`

Mirrors can only be requested once `refs` is preserved.

### `over_budget`

`refs` is required but its estimate exceeds the window.

## Coverage states

Only evidence can make a category `preserved` or `empty`; without evidence the
plan decision maps to `missing`, `skipped`, or `unavailable`.

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `preserved` | Evidence proves a complete copy. |
| `empty` | Evidence proves the source has none. |
| `partial` | Evidence proves only some of it. |
| `failed` | The attempt produced nothing usable. |
| `missing` | Planned, no evidence yet. |
| `skipped` | Deferred by the plan. |
| `unavailable` | Out of reach with the access available. |

`refs` needs an availability proof with a verified copy carrying every branch;
a migration report alone is `partial`. `trusted_mirrors` needs a `quorum`
proof. Report rows are recomputed, not trusted. `status` is `preserved`,
`partial` (a verified usable mirror exists), or `at_risk`.

## Risks to understand

### `ownership`

A copy does not transfer ownership; keep license and attribution.

### `legal`

Each node operator answers legal requests for their own node. See the
[node operator policy](operations/node-operator-policy.md).

### `secrets`

A mirror copies every committed secret; rotate them first. See
[secret scanning](security/secret-scanning.md).

### `verification`

Only a reconciled, signed migration report and an availability proof count.

### `external_dependencies`

Artifact bytes, wikis, CI logs, and registries are not imported; the report
lists them under `externalDependencies`.

### `emergency_contacts`

Report compromised accounts or keys to **security@forkmesh.com**.

## Getting help without lock-in

| Route | Who | Payment | Available |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `self_serve` | You, with an import and your own mirror node | No | Yes |
| `community_mirror` | Independent operators via the Mirrors tab | No | Yes |
| `managed_recovery` | Paid verified recovery | Yes | No |

Every route exits through `git clone --mirror`, the signed report, and the
identity kit. See the [business model](business-model.md).

## Drills

A drill records `startedAt` and `verifiedAt` (ms) plus evidence, and passes
within its scenario's drill budget with no failures:

```sh
tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py drill drill.json
```

| Failure | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_timing` | Timestamps missing or reversed. |
| `over_time_budget` | Took longer than the budget. |
| `no_migration_report` | No readable report. |
| `migration_report_unreconciled` | Report incomplete or rows do not add up. |
| `no_verified_mirror` | No verified copy carries every branch. |

## API and conformance

`GET /api/preservation/crisis-plan` returns the
`forkmesh-crisis-preservation-catalog-v1` catalog, or a plan when `scenario` is
given. It is public, cached five minutes, stores nothing, and returns `400` with
a closed code on bad input. Assessments and drills run locally only. CLI exit
codes: 0 success, 3 at risk or failed, 2 unreadable input. Migration metrics
are under [migration reports](repository-imports.md#migration-reports).

Model and fixture: `conformance/crisis-preservation/v1/` (`model.json`,
`fixture-input.json`, `generate_fixture.py --check`). Tests:
`app/tests/test_crisis_preservation.py`.

pages.markdown:
# Stable repository identity and dependency workflows

Builds that depend on Git sources must install the same bytes when the hosting
provider changes or the origin disappears. Contract:
`conformance/dependencies/v1/contract.json`; reference rules:
`app/src/stable_repository.py`; probe: `tools/dependency_conformance.py`.
Stock clients need no ForkMesh tooling.

## Identity and pinning

| Concept | Value | Changes when moved? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Logical identity | `urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:<64 hex>` (FM-ID-001 over `git-root-commit:<root>` from the signed catalog record) | No |
| Pinned content | Full 40- or 64-hex commit ID | No |
| Routes | `https://HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY[.git]`, `ssh://git@HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git` | Yes |

Hosts, owners, aliases, names and URLs are routing hints only. A record with no
root commit has no identity (empty string). The
[repository index](repository-index.md) returns `identity` on every result.

A pin is identity plus full commit ID. The resolver rejects branches, tags and
short IDs (`mutable_pin`), malformed identities (`identity_invalid`) and refs
outside `refs/heads/` or `refs/tags/` (`ref_invalid`).

## Switching providers without editing a lock

Write manifests and locks against one logical base URL and point it at the
active provider:

```sh
git config --global url."https://ACTIVE-PROVIDER/".insteadOf "https://LOGICAL-HOST/"
```

All recipes run Git underneath, so locks stay byte-identical; rollback restores
the previous line. `LOGICAL_URL` is `https://LOGICAL-HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git`.

### Git

`git clone LOGICAL_URL dep && git -C dep checkout --detach COMMIT` (evidence:
`git rev-parse HEAD`).

### Git submodule

`git submodule add LOGICAL_URL deps/dep`, then check out `COMMIT` (evidence: the
gitlink in the superproject tree).

### pip

`dependency @ git+LOGICAL_URL@COMMIT` (evidence: `vcs_info.commit_id` in
`direct_url.json`).

### npm

`"dependency": "git+LOGICAL_URL#COMMIT"` (evidence: `resolved` in
`package-lock.json`).

### Go modules

`GOPROXY=direct GOPRIVATE=LOGICAL-HOST go get LOGICAL-HOST/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git@COMMIT`
(evidence: `go.sum` hashes; a moved tag fails with a checksum mismatch).

### Cargo

`dependency = { git = "LOGICAL_URL", rev = "COMMIT" }` with
`CARGO_NET_GIT_FETCH_WITH_CLI=true` (evidence: `source` line in `Cargo.lock`).

## Fallback

The relay checks candidate hosts in declared order before sending any bytes. A
route is skipped as `unreachable`, `identity_mismatch`, `state_unverified`
(refs do not hash to a signed state), `commit_missing` or `ref_moved`.
Resolution status:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `resolved` | The first route proved the content. |
| `failed_over` | A later route proved it; skipped routes are listed with reasons. |
| `unavailable` | No route proved it; nothing is served. |
| `rejected` | The pin itself is unusable. |

There is never a silent fallback to unverified or mutable content.

## Scenarios

`tools/dependency_conformance.py run` builds loopback providers (origin, mirror,
tampered copy, retagged copy) and runs every client through:

| Scenario | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| `install` | Installs the pinned commit. |
| `provider-switch` | Installs via `insteadOf`; lock identical. |
| `origin-lost` | `failed_over` to the mirror; lock identical. |
| `unverified-fallback` | Refused with `state_unverified`. |
| `missing-commit` | Fails with `commit_missing`. |
| `moved-tag` | Fails with `ref_moved`. |
| `rollback-recovery` | `resolved` again; lock identical. |

The report (`forkmesh-dependency-conformance-report-v1`) summary carries
`resolutionSuccess`, `resolutionAttempts`, `failoverSuccess`,
`failoverAttempts`, `reproducibleLocks`, `lockChecks`, `verificationFailures`,
`unexpectedResults` (must be 0) and `unavailableClients`. Reports contain no
paths, loopback URLs, contents, credentials or addresses.

```sh
python3 tools/dependency_conformance.py validate
python3 tools/dependency_conformance.py run --output report.json [--clients git,pip --require git,pip]
```

`run` exits 0 on success, 1 on an unexpected result or missing required client,
2 when it cannot run. It only reads: pushes (over SSH, or over HTTPS with an
account credential) are out of scope, and only public repositories and direct
Git installs are covered.

pages.title: DJ Studio jams
pages.description: Video Mix DJ Studio mixes two YouTube decks with turntables, a crossfader, cues, loops, tempo and sampler pads. Install it once from the Market and it follows your account to…
pages.markdown:
# DJ Studio jams

Video Mix DJ Studio mixes two YouTube decks with turntables, a crossfader,
cues, loops, tempo and sampler pads. Install it once from the Market and it
follows your account to your phone, desktop and the web dashboard. On iPhone
and Android it is a full-screen native studio, and there you can start a
**jam**: friends join, share both decks and the queue, and each phone plays
the music itself.

## The queue

The row of small video thumbnails in the middle of the studio is the queue.

- **Add a song.** Press **+**: the loader opens with **Queue** chosen, and the
  search result you pick goes to the queue instead of a deck. On iPhone you
  can also share a YouTube link to ForkMesh from the share sheet.
- **Plays at once when idle.** If nothing is playing, a song you add does not
  wait: it loads and starts straight away, on the deck the crossfader favours
  (or on the empty deck, so a song you cued is not replaced). Adding a
  playlist or tag plays its first song this way and queues the rest.
- **Hold for a menu.** Tap or hold a thumbnail for Load on Deck A, Load on
  Deck B, Tags and Playlists… and Remove from Queue. Loading a song takes it
  off the queue.
- **Drag onto a deck.** Move your finger across the queue (sideways in
  landscape, up or down in portrait) and the thumbnail lifts at once. Drop it
  on a platter to load it there; drop it anywhere else to put it back. Moving
  along the queue still scrolls it.
- **AUTOMIX** takes the next song from the queue when it mixes.

Outside a jam the queue is kept on your phone.

## Start a jam

1. Press the people button at the top of the queue and choose **Start a Jam
   Session**. The decks carry on as they are.
2. Invite ForkMesh users by name; names are suggested as you type.
3. They get a ping, and a red dot on the people button the next time they
   open the studio. Once they join, the jam is shared.

## In a jam

- **One queue for everyone.** Anyone in the jam can add or remove songs. Each
  thumbnail shows who added it and when: just the time for today, the date
  and time before that, in your phone's time zone. The menu says it in full,
  for example "Added by bob on Oct 23, 2026 at 9:41 PM". Songs queued before
  this was added show no time.
- **Shared decks.** Every load, start, pause, stop, seek, tempo change and
  scratch is shared, and the other phones follow within a second or two.
  Nothing is streamed between phones: each one plays its own copy from
  YouTube. Your deck volume stays your own.
- **People.** Everyone has a round icon. Green means in the studio, blue with
  headphones listening in the background, grey not listening, a moon not
  heard from for a while, dashed still invited. The host has a crown.
- **Motion and reactions.** Icons move when people dance with their phone.
  Turn this off with **Share My Phone's Motion** in the jam sheet; no location
  is ever sent. The smiley button sends one of 30 silent reactions that play
  over everyone's studio.
- **Leaving.** The host can remove people or end the jam for everyone; anyone
  else can leave. Your phone remembers the jam and rejoins it when you open
  the studio again.

Limits: up to 32 people in a jam, 100 songs in its queue, and 20 jams you
host. Playlists stay on your phone; only the songs you queue from them are
shared. Removing the package, or deleting your account, ends the jams you
host.

## On Android

Android has the studio and jams. The newest queue changes (hold for a menu,
drag on first touch, play at once when idle, and who added each song and
when) arrive on iPhone first and are still being ported. See
[ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

pages.title: External dependency and observability map
pages.description: Every outside service a ForkMesh surface can contact: what it observes, how long it keeps data, its jurisdiction, which copy is canonical, and what still works without it. The…
pages.markdown:
# External dependency and observability map

Every outside service a ForkMesh surface can contact: what it observes, how long
it keeps data, its jurisdiction, which copy is canonical, and what still works
without it. The source of truth is
[`conformance/external-dependencies/v1/manifest.json`](../conformance/external-dependencies/v1/manifest.json);
[`tools/external_dependency_inventory.py`](../tools/external_dependency_inventory.py)
`render` writes the block below from it. If the page and the JSON disagree, the
JSON wins. How the hosted service is built and where it runs is on
[Architecture and availability](architecture.md); the [docs index](README.md)
lists related pages.

## How the map stays complete

`python3 tools/external_dependency_inventory.py check` fails when production
source names an unclassified outside host, a link-only host is loaded as a
resource, a deploy secret or `env` credential has no dependency, a database
table that stores a provider identifier is undocumented, a dependency has
neither a failure drill nor a recorded gap, or the generated block is stale.
`report` prints the result as JSON. The `external-dependency-map` quality gate
runs the check on Linux, macOS and Windows. Hosts that exist only in dashboard
settings, DNS or secret values are listed as `configuredHosts`.

Components: `app-server` and `world-server` are the Python app and World
server on the self-hosted core nodes; `app-browser`, `www-browser` and
`world-browser` are visitors' browsers.

| Label | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Mandatory for the hosted service | The hosted service stops without it; a self-host runs its own instance or uses the mirror node. |
| Degrades one feature | One feature stops or shows a named unavailable state. |
| Optional, off unless enabled | Nothing is contacted until a user or operator turns it on. |
| Operator tooling only | Only deploy, provisioning, or maintenance commands contact it. |
| Build and release only | Only builds and CI contact it. |

## Self-hosting and offline use

The Go mirror node (`server/`) uses only the standard library and serves Git
without any service on this page, apart from a TLS certificate authority and,
optionally, a DNS provider API. Clone, fetch, push to a mirror, signed
collaboration records and local desktop work continue when every hosted
dependency is unreachable; the [product-promise drill](product-promise.md)
proves this for clone. Every optional service stays off until its secret is
set. See [Self-hosting](self-hosting.md) and [Mirroring](mirroring.md).

<!-- external-dependency-map:begin -->

<!-- Generated by tools/external_dependency_inventory.py render; edit the manifest, not this block. -->

## Summary

| Service | Kind | Needed | Components | Observes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Cloudflare DNS, the forkmesh.com website Worker, DNS over HTTPS, and Web Analytics](#cloudflare) | hosting, dns, certificates, cdn-edge, telemetry | Mandatory for the hosted service | app-server, app-browser, www-browser, world-server, world-browser, mirror-node, desktop, operator-tools | Requests to forkmesh.com and www.forkmesh.com end at the forkmesh-www Worker: client IP address, TLS SNI, headers including User-Agent, request path, and timing. The Worker serves the homepage, blog, docs, and static pages and passes app paths on to app.forkmesh.com. app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com are unproxied DNS records that point at the core nodes, so Cloudflare answers the DNS lookups for them but never sees their requests. Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS receives mirror hostnames and profile domains being verified. The content security policy also allows the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon, which is a zone setting rather than repository code. |
| [ACME certificate authorities for direct-HTTPS mirrors](#acme-certificate-authority) | certificates | Degrades one feature | mirror-node | The mirror's public hostname and the host's IP address during certificate issuance and renewal. Issued certificates are published in public Certificate Transparency logs. |
| [GitHub source and release downloads](#github-downloads) | forge-api, package-registry | Degrades one feature | desktop, installer, mirror-node, operator-tools, ci | The downloading host's IP address and the release or repository requested: desktop self-update clones of forkmesh/forkmesh when no source checkout exists, the age binary for the macOS installer, the pinned cloudflared release, and build toolchains. |
| [GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, and Gitea APIs for imports, GitHub sync and repository mirrors](#forge-apis) | forge-api | Optional, off unless enabled | app-server, desktop, operator-tools, ci | The owner and repository being imported, the app's egress IP, and a user-supplied access token when the user provides one. The GitHub sync workflow reads and writes issues, discussions, and pull requests of the connected repository. A repository mirror set up in repository settings sends the owner's stored access token with every API call and Git push, and the forge sees the mirrored branches, tags, issues, comments, discussions and releases. The relay's GitHub Actions watcher reads the public workflow runs, jobs and annotations of forkmesh/forkmesh every 5 minutes, with an optional read-only GITHUB_ACTIONS_WATCH_TOKEN. |
| [Internet Archive public repository backups](#internet-archive) | hosting | Optional, off unless enabled | app-server | The public repository identifier, the ForkMesh app's egress IP, the repository's public Git bundle, and the Internet Archive access key supplied by the repository owner. The owner-provided secret is sent only to the Internet Archive S3 endpoint and is stored encrypted by ForkMesh. |
| [GitHub Actions hosted runners](#github-actions) | hosted-runner | Build and release only | ci | The full public repository source, test output, and uploaded evidence artifacts for every run on ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, and windows-latest. Workflows check out with persist-credentials: false. |
| [Package registries and distribution mirrors](#package-registries) | package-registry | Build and release only | ci, operator-tools | The build host's IP address and the exact package names and versions requested. |

## Services in detail

<a id="cloudflare"></a>

### Cloudflare DNS, the forkmesh.com website Worker, DNS over HTTPS, and Web Analytics

- **Needed:** Mandatory for the hosted service
- **Kind:** hosting, dns, certificates, cdn-edge, telemetry
- **Components:** app-server, app-browser, www-browser, world-server, world-browser, mirror-node, desktop, operator-tools
- **Hosts:** `api.cloudflare.com`, `www.cloudflare.com`, `cloudflare-dns.com`, `static.cloudflareinsights.com`, `cloudflare.com`
- **Credentials:** `USAGE_ANALYTICS_API_TOKEN`, `WORKERS_OBSERVABILITY_ACCOUNT_ID`, `WORKERS_OBSERVABILITY_API_TOKEN`, `WORKERS_OBSERVABILITY_SERVICE`
- **Observes:** Requests to forkmesh.com and www.forkmesh.com end at the forkmesh-www Worker: client IP address, TLS SNI, headers including User-Agent, request path, and timing. The Worker serves the homepage, blog, docs, and static pages and passes app paths on to app.forkmesh.com. app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com are unproxied DNS records that point at the core nodes, so Cloudflare answers the DNS lookups for them but never sees their requests. Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS receives mirror hostnames and profile domains being verified. The content security policy also allows the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon, which is a zone setting rather than repository code.
- **Retention:** Workers observability on forkmesh-www, the only ForkMesh Worker, samples 5% of logs and traces every request, kept for the Cloudflare plan's retention. Edge caches expire by their Cache-Control lifetimes. Relay data on the core nodes is covered by the relay data retention page.
- **Jurisdiction:** Cloudflare, Inc. (United States) on a global edge network.
- **Canonical data:** Canonical only for the DNS records of ForkMesh domains. Accounts, sessions, keys, organizations, the catalog, and inboxes live on the core nodes (see Vultr); the website's pages are built from www/ in Git.
- **When it is gone:** forkmesh.com and www.forkmesh.com stop, along with the app paths reached through them. When cached DNS answers expire (the app and world records have a 60-second TTL), app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com stop resolving, so new visitors cannot reach the dashboard, API, or Git over HTTPS even though the core nodes keep running. Mirrors reached by their own hostnames keep serving Git clone and fetch; desktops keep local Git, signed records, and direct mirror access. DNS-over-HTTPS checks of mirrors and profile domains report unavailable rather than rejected.
- **Recovery:** Service resumes when Cloudflare recovers. No data is lost: it lives on the core nodes, which keep running.
- **Alternative:** Clone from any independent mirror node's direct HTTPS or SSH URL. A self-hosted instance runs the same app on its own server behind Caddy and needs no Cloudflare account; putting Cloudflare in front of it is optional.
- **Failure drills:** `app/tests/test_https_mirror_health_leases.py::test_cloudflare_dns_check_distinguishes_unavailable_from_rejected`, `app/tests/test_availability_proof.py::test_source_host_outage_does_not_remove_a_mirror_quorum`
- **Known gap:** Every ForkMesh domain uses Cloudflare DNS with no second provider, so a Cloudflare DNS outage takes app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com offline even while the core nodes are healthy.
- **Evidence:** `www/worker.js`, `www/wrangler.production.toml`, `docs/operations/served-stack.md`, `app/src/app_runtime.py`, `app/src/usage_reporting.py`, `app/src/entry.py`

<a id="acme-certificate-authority"></a>

### ACME certificate authorities for direct-HTTPS mirrors

- **Needed:** Degrades one feature
- **Kind:** certificates
- **Components:** mirror-node
- **Hosts:** `acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org`, `acme.zerossl.com`, `acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org`
- **Observes:** The mirror's public hostname and the host's IP address during certificate issuance and renewal. Issued certificates are published in public Certificate Transparency logs.
- **Retention:** Certificate Transparency entries are permanent and public.
- **Jurisdiction:** Caddy's default issuers, Let's Encrypt (ISRG, United States) and ZeroSSL, unless the operator configures another ACME issuer.
- **Canonical data:** None. The certificate is a cache the proxy renews.
- **When it is gone:** Existing certificates keep serving until they expire, so clones continue. New direct-HTTPS mirrors cannot obtain a certificate, and a mirror whose renewal keeps failing stops serving HTTPS at expiry; its SSH gateway and other mirrors are unaffected.
- **Recovery:** Caddy retries renewal automatically; the operator can switch ACME issuer or use the Cloudflare Tunnel mode.
- **Alternative:** Self-host operators may point Caddy at any ACME issuer or their own certificate, or run the mirror node in Cloudflare Tunnel mode.
- **Known gap:** No automated drill simulates ACME issuance failure or certificate expiry on a direct-HTTPS mirror.
- **Evidence:** `tools/direct_https_bootstrap.py`, `docs/operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md`

<a id="github-downloads"></a>

### GitHub source and release downloads

- **Needed:** Degrades one feature
- **Kind:** forge-api, package-registry
- **Components:** desktop, installer, mirror-node, operator-tools, ci
- **Hosts:** `github.com`
- **Observes:** The downloading host's IP address and the release or repository requested: desktop self-update clones of forkmesh/forkmesh when no source checkout exists, the age binary for the macOS installer, the pinned cloudflared release, and build toolchains.
- **Retention:** Set by GitHub's access-log terms; ForkMesh does not configure it.
- **Jurisdiction:** GitHub, Inc. (Microsoft, United States).
- **Canonical data:** None. ForkMesh's canonical source is served by ForkMesh mirrors; GitHub holds a synchronized copy.
- **When it is gone:** Desktop self-update without a local checkout, first-time macOS installs that need age, cloudflared installation, and toolchain bootstraps fail with a download error. Running desktops, mirrors, and the hosted service are unaffected.
- **Recovery:** Retry after GitHub recovers, or install the same pinned artifact from a ForkMesh release mirror.
- **Alternative:** Update from a local source checkout or a ForkMesh mirror clone; self-host operators can preinstall age and cloudflared from their distribution.
- **Known gap:** No drill runs the desktop updater or install.sh with github.com unreachable.
- **Evidence:** `tools/cloudflared_install.py`, `www/public/install.sh`, `desktop/src/MainWindowSetup.cpp`

<a id="forge-apis"></a>

### GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, and Gitea APIs for imports, GitHub sync and repository mirrors

- **Needed:** Optional, off unless enabled
- **Kind:** forge-api
- **Components:** app-server, desktop, operator-tools, ci
- **Hosts:** `api.github.com`, `gitlab.com`, `codeberg.org`, `gitea.com`, `user-images.githubusercontent.com`
- **Credentials:** `GITHUB_ACTIONS_WATCH_TOKEN`
- **Observes:** The owner and repository being imported, the app's egress IP, and a user-supplied access token when the user provides one. The GitHub sync workflow reads and writes issues, discussions, and pull requests of the connected repository. A repository mirror set up in repository settings sends the owner's stored access token with every API call and Git push, and the forge sees the mirrored branches, tags, issues, comments, discussions and releases. The relay's GitHub Actions watcher reads the public workflow runs, jobs and annotations of forkmesh/forkmesh every 5 minutes, with an optional read-only GITHUB_ACTIONS_WATCH_TOKEN.
- **Retention:** Set by each forge's API log terms. ForkMesh never stores user-supplied import tokens. A mirror's access token is stored encrypted until the owner disconnects the mirror.
- **Jurisdiction:** GitHub, Inc. (United States); GitLab Inc. (United States); Codeberg e.V. (Germany); CommitGo, Inc. (United States) for gitea.com.
- **Canonical data:** The forge is canonical for its own repository until import; after import the ForkMesh repository and its signed records are canonical, and the stored external id only links the two.
- **When it is gone:** New imports, scheduled GitHub sync and repository mirrors fail with a named provider error; mirror items stay queued and retry. The GitHub Actions watcher sends no pings until GitHub answers again. Imported repositories, clones, and collaboration keep working.
- **Recovery:** Retry the import; the sync workflow resumes on its next schedule and is idempotent.
- **Alternative:** Push the repository directly to a ForkMesh mirror with stock Git; no forge API is needed.

- **Retention:** Set by Vultr for the instances and their disks. Data on the cores is kept as the relay data retention page describes. Nightly rqlite backups are pulled off Vultr to the operator box, encrypted with age, and kept as 7 daily and 4 weekly copies. ForkMesh does not store a user's own Vultr key.
- **Jurisdiction:** Vultr (The Constant Company, United States); the fleet runs in the ewr region (New Jersey).
- **Canonical data:** The core nodes are canonical for hosted accounts, sessions, device and SSH public keys, organization membership, the catalog, pull and issue inboxes, routing health, and repositories hosted on the cores. The data is in rqlite, replicated across the three cores; the app's D1-shaped database layer and Durable Object emulation run on top of it. Not canonical for repositories published from users' own nodes, which live on those nodes, mirrors, and desktops, or for signed .forkmesh records, which live in Git. For a user's mirror host, Vultr is canonical for the virtual machine only.
- **When it is gone:** One core can fail: rqlite keeps quorum with the other two, and the operator box's DNS health loop takes the failed core out of the app and world records after three failed probes. Losing the region or the account stops app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com (dashboard, API, accounts, chat, catalog, and Git over HTTPS) and the runner's Actions and agent runs; the forkmesh.com pages on Cloudflare keep serving. Independent mirrors keep serving Git clone and fetch, and desktops keep local Git, signed records, and direct mirror access. One-click mirror host creation fails at that step; existing user hosts keep running.
- **Recovery:** A failed core rejoins or is replaced from deploy/fleet.toml with tools/next_fleet.py. After data loss, decrypt the newest verified nightly backup with tools/next_backup.py restore and load it through the rqlite leader's /db/load. Retry a failed mirror host provisioning.
- **Alternative:** A self-hosted instance runs the same app on any Linux server it owns, and the mirror node installs on any Linux host with install.sh. Moving the hosted service to another provider means provisioning new cores and restoring a backup; the fleet tools only create Vultr instances.
- **Failure drills:** `deploy/tests/test_next_dns.py::test_production_failover_removes_from_both_names_and_readds`, `app/tests/test_d1_transient_errors.py::test_router_answers_503_degraded_instead_of_re_raising`, `app/host/tests_unit/test_autoscale.py::test_boot_timeout_destroys_a_node_that_never_joined`
- **Known gap:** All three cores and the runner are in one Vultr region, and no drill covers losing the region or the account.
- **Evidence:** `deploy/fleet.toml`, `docs/operations/runbook.md`, `tools/next_fleet.py`, `tools/next_backup.py`, `app/host/forkmesh_host/vultr_guard.py`, `app/host/forkmesh_host/d1_rqlite.py`, `app/host/forkmesh_host/durable.py`, `desktop/src/MainWindowChat.cpp`

<a id="repository-webhook-endpoints"></a>

### Repository webhook endpoints owners register

- **Needed:** Optional, off unless enabled
- **Kind:** hosted-runner
- **Components:** app-server
- **Hosts:** `api.codemagic.io`
- **Observes:** Each registered endpoint receives one signed JSON event per subscribed repository change: the repository's owner and name, its public URLs, the moved refs (branch, before/after commit, refs digest), merged pull numbers and the merging account, released tags and their notes, plus the relay's outbound IP address. Only public repositories emit events. api.codemagic.io is the one endpoint ForkMesh itself registers, for its own repository's mobile builds.
- **Retention:** Set by each endpoint operator. ForkMesh keeps the encrypted destination and signing secret until the owner deletes the webhook, queued deliveries until they settle, and the newest 20 delivery outcomes per endpoint.
- **Jurisdiction:** Wherever the endpoint the repository owner chose operates; Codemagic is Nevercode OU (Estonia).
- **Canonical data:** None. Every event repeats state that is canonical in Git and the catalog.
- **When it is gone:** Deliveries retry with capped backoff and are dropped after 6 attempts; the Settings tab shows the failure. Pushes, merges, and releases are unaffected because delivery is queued out of band.
- **Recovery:** Send a test delivery from the repository's Settings tab once the endpoint is back, or push again.
- **Alternative:** Delete the webhook and poll the public catalog with tools/forkmesh_integration.py watch instead; nothing in ForkMesh depends on an endpoint answering.
- **Failure drills:** `app/tests/test_repository_webhooks.py::test_a_failing_endpoint_is_retried_then_given_up_on`, `app/tests/test_repository_webhooks.py::test_a_gone_endpoint_stops_immediately_and_a_transport_error_retries`

pages.title: Fediverse digests, mentions and replies
pages.description: How public repositories talk to the fediverse: outbound daily digests, inbound mentions that an owner can turn into issues, and threaded Lemmy or Mastodon replies on issues, pull…
pages.markdown:
# Fediverse digests, mentions and replies

How public repositories talk to the fediverse: outbound daily digests,
inbound mentions that an owner can turn into issues, and threaded Lemmy or
Mastodon replies on issues, pull requests and discussions. Actors, handles and
signatures are in [ActivityPub federation](design/activitypub-federation.md).
Private repositories never federate.

## Daily digests

Public repository events (issues, pulls, discussions, commits, releases) are not
posted one by one. Each becomes a small record (category, title, public link
without query string, UTC time, scope) in an encrypted, bounded queue. Private
repositories are never queued, and a queue is dropped when its repository turns
private or federation off.

A scope posts at most one automated digest per 24 hours, after a 24-hour first
wait. Empty queues post nothing; a digest holds at most 12 updates from a queue
of at most 80. The scheduled job handles at most 12 scopes per run and delivers
through the ActivityPub outbox with backoff. Posts start with "ForkMesh
automated daily update".

The repository **Post updates** switch enables the digest and previews its
text. `"manual": true` on `ap-publish` keeps immediate owner announcements.

```text
GET  /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fediverse-digest
GET  /api/orgs/{org}/fediverse
POST /api/orgs/{org}/fediverse   {"enabled": true|false}
```

The repository endpoint is owner-only, `no-store`, and `404` for private
repositories. The organization switch only suppresses: a repository owner's
`federate` and `broadcastEvents` settings stay authoritative.

## Mention review

World lists an inbound ActivityPub Note only after HTTP-signature verification,
when it addresses a published public repository actor and the ActivityStreams
Public collection. Private or missing repositories are rejected before a
record is written; instance blocks and the repository's `federate` and
`acceptComments` controls apply.

Mentions never create issues automatically. States:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `review` | Available for owner review |
| `pending` | The owner confirmed a draft and the encrypted owner inbox accepted it |
| `created` | The owner node committed the issue and returned its number in a signed acknowledgement |

An item stays pending until the owner node confirms the committed issue
number.

Redeliveries are deduplicated by a blind index of the remote Note id. The
public feed exposes only a random id, sanitized author/post fields, repository
name, and generalized progress.

Follow-up consent is off by default. With consent, one idempotent public reply
with the issue link is queued only after owner-node confirmation.

API: `GET /api/world/fediverse-mentions`, and
`POST /api/world/fediverse-mentions/{id}/preview|create|moderate|materialized`.
The desktop inbox acknowledgement carries
`materialized={review-id}:{real-issue-number}` entries.

## Threaded replies (Lemmy-compatible)

ForkMesh accepts public ActivityPub replies (Lemmy or Mastodon `Create` of a
`Note`, `Page` or `Article`) to public federated issues, pull requests and
discussions, including replies to other verified remote replies.

### Trust boundary

Remote replies are stored encrypted in `ap_comments`
(`forkmesh-federated-thread-v1`), never in `.forkmesh` records or any signed
event stream. An HTTP signature authenticates the remote actor but does not make the reply a ForkMesh native event;
projections carry `federated: true` and `nativeEvent: false`.

A remote object cannot select a ForkMesh context: a top-level reply inherits the
context of the `/ap/o/{id}` object it targets, a nested reply that of its
stored parent, and unresolved targets are discarded.

### Lifecycle

- `Create` is idempotent per remote `id`.
- `Update` replaces the body only when the author matches; marked `edited`.
- `Delete` leaves a `tombstoned` placeholder; `Remove` (same instance only)
  leaves `moderated`.
- `Undo(Remove)` waits for redelivery instead of restoring cached content.

Blocked instances (and their subdomains) are rejected before verification and
hidden on read. Private repository threads never federate.

### Client API

```text
GET /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fedi-comments?kind={issue|pull|discussion}&number={n}
```

Clients render bodies as plain text, accept only HTTPS backlinks, cap nesting
depth, label edited and removed records, and never parse them as native
events. Fixtures are in `app/tests/fixtures/activitypub/lemmy/`.

pages.title: Subscribing by feed or email
pages.description: Every public repository's issues can be followed without an account, without JavaScript and without loading anything from another site: as Atom feeds, by email through a…
pages.markdown:
# Subscribing by feed or email

Every public repository's issues can be followed without an account, without
JavaScript and without loading anything from another site: as Atom feeds, by
email through a feed-to-mail tool, or on the plain "lite" pages.
Reading without an account is covered in
[Reading and cloning without an account](accountless-reading.md).

## Feeds

Replace `<host>/<owner>/<repo>` with the repository's address, for example
`https://forum.example.org/example/forum`.

| Feed | Address |
| --- | --- |
| New threads | `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/issues.atom` |
| New threads and every new comment | `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/activity.atom` |
| One thread and its comments | `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>.atom` |
| New threads with one label | `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/labels/<label>.atom` |

A label with a space is written with `%20`, for example
`labels/reading%20group.atom`. Feeds hold the newest 50 entries; add
`?limit=200` for up to 200. Comments carry the Atom threading extension
(RFC 4685), so feed readers and mail tools show them as replies to their
thread. The issue list and every issue page also announce their feeds, so
pasting the page address into a feed reader finds them.

## By email with rss2email

[rss2email](https://github.com/rss2email/rss2email) turns each new entry into
an email. Install it (`pip install rss2email` or your system's package), then:

```
r2e new you@example.org
r2e add forum-activity https://forum.example.org/example/forum/activity.atom
r2e run --no-send
r2e run
```

`r2e run --no-send` once marks what is already there as read, so the first
real run mails only new threads and comments. Run `r2e run` from cron (for
example every 30 minutes) to keep receiving them. To follow fewer messages,
subscribe to new threads only, or to one label:

```
r2e add forum-threads https://forum.example.org/example/forum/issues.atom
r2e add forum-iran https://forum.example.org/example/forum/labels/Iran.atom
```

Each mail's subject is the thread title (`Re:` and the author for a comment)
and its body is the post. Images that are not stored on the instance appear
as links, so opening a mail never contacts another site.

## The lite view

`https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/lite` lists the threads, 50 to a page, newest
first (`?sort=active` for the most recently active, `?label=Iran` for one
label). `https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>/lite/issues/<number>` shows a whole
thread on one page. The pages are plain HTML with no scripts and no outside
fonts or images, made for slow or filtered connections such as DNS tunnels;
a thread list page is under 30 KB. `https://<host>/lite` lists the
instance's public repositories. Every normal page links to its lite version
for readers without JavaScript, and the sidebar has a "Lite" link.
