pages.description: A repository page shows an About box on the right: description, website and links. Any folder can have its own About box too, so a monorepo with one project per folder shows each…
pages.markdown:
# Folder About boxes

A repository page shows an **About** box on the right: description, website
and links. Any folder can have its own About box too, so a monorepo with one
project per folder shows each project's name, logo, description, website,
links and topics when you open its folder.
Other repository features are listed in the [docs index](README.md).

## Add an About box to a folder

Commit `.forkmesh/info.json` inside the folder: the same file the repository
uses for its own About at its root.

```
bolt-c/
  .forkmesh/info.json
  logo.svg
  README.md
  src/
```

`bolt-c/.forkmesh/info.json`:

```json
{
  "name": "Bolt-C",
  "about": "Track and monitor GitHub pull request readiness.",
  "website": "https://leaf.example.net/",
  "links": [
    {"label": "Source", "url": "https://code.example.org/Bolt/Bolt-C"},
    {"label": "Contributing", "url": "https://code.example.org/Bolt/Bolt/blob/main/bolt-c/CONTRIBUTING.md"}
  ],
  "topics": ["security", "github", "cloudflare-workers"]
}
```

Every field is optional; an empty object (`{}`) is enough to turn the box on.

| Field | Meaning | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Title of the box | 80 characters; defaults to the folder name |
| `about` | One-paragraph description (`description` is accepted too) | 240 characters |
| `website` | Project website (`homepage` is accepted too) | `http` or `https` only, 240 characters |
| `links` | List of `{"label", "url"}` rows | up to 8; `url` must be `http`/`https`, 400 characters; `label` 60 characters, defaults to the address's host |
| `topics` | List of topic words (`tags` is accepted too) | up to 20; lowercased, spaces become `-`, letters, digits and `-` only, 50 characters each |

Text is shown as plain text: HTML and Markdown are not interpreted. Links
with any other scheme (`javascript:`, `data:`, `ftp:`), with a user name or
password in the address, or with spaces are dropped. A field of the wrong
type is ignored. A file that is not valid JSON, or larger than 64 KB, still
shows the box, but with only the fallbacks below.

## Logo

Put `logo.svg` or `logo.png` in the folder itself (not in `.forkmesh/`). If
both exist, the SVG is used. The logo appears at the top of the folder's About
box and next to the folder path above the file list.

- Up to 512 KB.
- A PNG must be a real PNG file.
- An SVG must start with an `<svg>` element (an XML declaration, comments or a
  doctype may come first) and may not declare entities.
- The logo is always shown as an image, never inlined into the page, so
  scripts inside an SVG never run.

## Fallbacks from the folder's README

When the About file has no `about`, the description is the first paragraph of
prose in the folder's `README.md` (also `readme.md`, `Readme.md`,
`README.markdown`, `README.txt` or `README`). Headings, HTML blocks, images,
badges, code blocks, lists and lines like `**Live Site:** ...` are skipped;
links keep their text. It is cut to 240 characters.

When the About file has no `website`, a README line such as
`**Live Site:** https://...`, `**Website:** ...` or `**Homepage:** ...`
supplies it.

## Monorepos with project addresses

On an instance whose administrator set up project addresses (one address per
folder, such as `/Bolt/Bolt-C`), every folder in that project table gets an
About box without committing an About file: its name comes from the table, and
the description, website and logo come from the README and logo files above.
A committed `.forkmesh/info.json` still wins for every field it sets. The web
page looks for a folder About when the folder contains a `.forkmesh` folder,
`logo.svg` or `logo.png`, so a project folder needs one of them.

## Contributor roster

The repository page's Contributors section counts git author names, so bots
are left out but one person with several commit names still counts more than
once, and there are no pictures. To show your own list, commit
`.forkmesh/contributors/contributors.json` at the repository root:

```json
{
  "count": 2,
  "contributors": [
    {"slug": "alice", "name": "Alice", "commits": 120, "profile": "https://example.com/@alice"},
    {"slug": "bob", "name": "Bob", "commits": 40}
  ]
}
```

and a square picture for each person at `.forkmesh/contributors/<slug>.png`.
The page shows `count`, the eight people with the most `commits` (name and
commit count on hover, a link to `profile` when it is an `https://` address,
initials when there is no picture), and a "+N" link to the file.

## What stays the same

Folders without an About file (and not in a project table) are unchanged.
Inside a folder that has an About, the folder's box takes the right-hand
column. Private repositories show folder About boxes and logos only to people
who can read the repository.

pages.title: Forge sync
pages.description: Keeps a ForkMesh repository in step with a repository on another forge. Two tools share the job: tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py moves branches and tags between GitHub and…
pages.markdown:
# Forge sync Keeps a ForkMesh repository in step with a repository on another forge. Two tools share the job: `tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py` moves branches and tags between GitHub and ForkMesh and imports GitHub records one way, and `tools/forge_sync.py` keeps ForkMesh issues and comments (fields, labels, assignees, state, edits, comment deletions) in step two ways with GitHub (`github` adapter) or Gitea, Forgejo and Codeberg (`gitea` adapter). Why a second copy matters is on [Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md); one-off imports are on [Repository imports](repository-imports.md). ## Connecting a repository to GitHub A GitHub Actions workflow syncs a ForkMesh repository with GitHub on events and every 15 minutes. Refs move both ways by fast-forward only (never forced or deleted; diverged branches are reported). Issues, discussions and pull requests import one way into `.forkmesh` records; two-way issues use the issue sync below. ```bash python3 tools/github_forkmesh_bridge.py connect --github OWNER/NAME --forkmesh OWNER/NAME --key-out KEY.pem ``` `connect` writes `.forkmesh/github-sync.json`, `.forkmesh/github-bridge.py` and `.github/workflows/forkmesh-github-sync.yml`. Set secrets `FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY` and `FORKMESH_SYNC_SSH_KEY` and variable `FORKMESH_SYNC_REMOTE` (optionally `FORKMESH_SYNC_KNOWN_HOSTS`). - Imported events are signed by the bridge key with `authorName` `github:LOGIN`. - GitHub numbers are kept unless taken; event ids derive from GitHub ids, so reruns are idempotent. - ForkMesh-side edits survive. - Pull request code is fetched as data and never executed (payloads over 8 MiB skipped). Subcommands `git-sync`, `export` and `run --dry-run` run pieces by hand; tests are `app/tests/test_github_forkmesh_bridge.py`. To also deploy a Cloudflare Worker from the mirror, see [Mirror and deploy a Cloudflare Worker](cloudflare-workers.md). ## Two-way issue sync ```bash python3 tools/forge_sync.py connect --provider gitea --repository octo/app \ --base-url https://git.example.org --slo-minutes 15 FORKMESH_FORGE_TOKEN=… FORKMESH_BRIDGE_SIGNING_KEY="$(cat sync-key.pem)" \ python3 tools/forge_sync.py sync --report sync-report.json python3 tools/forge_sync.py status python3 tools/forge_sync.py resolve --issue 12 --field body --take forkmesh python3 tools/forge_sync.py pause --reason "maintenance"; python3 tools/forge_sync.py resume ``` `connect` writes the ledger `.forkmesh/forge-sync.json`; commit it after each pass. `sync --avatars` and `--attachments` also copy pictures and files into the repository ([Avatars](#avatars), [Attachments](#attachments)). Exit codes: `0` converged, `1` conflicts, `2` configuration error, `75` retryable provider failure. A paused connection sends no requests. ## Merge rules - The ledger stores a digest of each field and comment as last agreed. A change on one side is copied over; differing changes on both sides become a conflict, and nothing is written until it is resolved. - `sourceOfTruth` sets a per-field rule: `manual` (default), `forkmesh` or `provider`. Discarded values are kept in ledger `history`. - Synced records carry a `forkmesh-forge-sync:v1` marker, so echoes and lost ledgers never create duplicates. Issues are never deleted. ## Mirror mode `connect --mirror` makes a one-way, read-only copy of a provider's issues, for a project whose home stays on the forge. `--two-way` switches back. The ledger stores `"mode": "mirror"`; a ledger without `mode` is two-way. - Every issue is imported, open and closed, with every comment, label, assignee and state, in full and in any script. The only cap is the git node's 16 MiB per-issue record limit (`maxIssueRecordBytes`). Text is stored in the canonical form every ForkMesh client signs: `\n` line endings, leading and trailing blank lines trimmed, titles trimmed. - The provider wins every field. A ForkMesh edit to a mirrored title, body, state, labels, assignees or comment is replaced on the next pass, without a conflict. Comments deleted on the provider are deleted in ForkMesh (signed `delete` events). - Nothing is written to the provider. The engine wraps the adapter so any write method raises before a request is made; a read-only token is enough. - ForkMesh-only comments and issues stay in ForkMesh. - A `forkmesh-forge-sync` marker in a provider record is ignored, so a forged marker cannot claim and overwrite a ForkMesh-only issue or comment. ## Where the ledger lives The ledger defaults to `.forkmesh/forge-sync.json`. `--ledger PATH` (or `FORKMESH_FORGE_LEDGER`) keeps it elsewhere, for example on the sync server, so the repository carries only the records. It is about 3 KB per issue (1.7 MB for a 609-issue forum) and its timestamps change every pass. Each pass also writes the small public `.forkmesh/forge-source.json` (`forkmesh-forge-source-v1`: `provider`, `repository`, `baseUrl`, `issueUrl` with a `{number}` placeholder, and `renumbered`, the issues whose ForkMesh number differs from the provider's): all a reader needs to link an issue to its original. A mirror that wants its own provider sync builds a fresh ledger on its first pass. ## Identities Imported records are signed by the sync key and credited as `:`. The web dashboard shows a `github:` author as `@`, linked to `https://github.com/` in a new tab (`forgeIdentity` in `app/public/dashboard/js/02-helpers.js`), with the picture stored in the repository ([Avatars](#avatars)) or the initial. List rows show plain `@` text (`userNameHtml`, server `user_name_html`). A page never loads anything from GitHub, because readers of a mirror may be on networks where GitHub is blocked or watched ([Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md)). The ledger `identities` map links provider logins to ForkMesh accounts for assignees only; ambiguous links are ignored. ## Avatars With `--avatars`, a pass copies each provider author's picture into the repository so the reader's browser never contacts the provider. Without it, `.forkmesh/contributors` is left alone and authors show initials. - **Who.** Every issue and comment author the pass reads, plus every `:` author already in the records. The ledger `avatars` map keeps `login`, the API's `avatar_url`, `fetchedAt`, `fetchedUrl`, `failed`. - **Where from.** The API's `avatar_url` (`RemoteIssue.author_avatar` / `RemoteComment.author_avatar`) at 96 px (`&s=96` on GitHub), else `https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/?s=96`. Only `https` on the provider's picture host (`avatars.githubusercontent.com`, or the Gitea `baseUrl` host); a redirect elsewhere is refused. At most 1 MiB, 10 s and 100 pictures per pass. The token is never sent. - **Stored as** `.forkmesh/contributors/-.png`. With Pillow the picture is re-encoded as a 96x96 PNG; without it, PNG or JPEG bytes are kept as they are (`` decodes by content) and anything else is dropped. - **Refresh.** Only when the file is missing, the URL changed, or it is 30 days old (`AVATAR_REFRESH_MS`); a failed fetch waits a day (`AVATAR_RETRY_MS`). An unchanged pass writes nothing. - **Roster.** `.forkmesh/contributors/contributors.json` gets one row per person (`slug`, `name`, `github` or `login`, `profile` for GitHub, `avatar`), sorted by login, in the [contributor roster](folder-about.md#contributor-roster) schema. Rows whose slug does not start with `-` are kept first, with the file's own `count`; invalid JSON is left alone. Pages draw the stored picture for a `github:` author (`issueActorAvatarHtml` / `avatar_html`) from the repository's raw URL when the issue index lists the person in `forgeAvatars`. ## Attachments On a `github` connection, `sync --attachments` copies the images and files that issue titles, bodies and comments embed from GitHub into the repository (`tools/forge_attachments.py`). A picture loaded from GitHub would tell a watching network which thread a mirror reader is on. Without `--attachments`, or with `FORKMESH_FORGE_ATTACHMENTS=off`, nothing is copied. - **Addresses.** `https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/`, `https://github.com/user-attachments/files//`, `https://github.com///assets//`, `https://github.com///files//`, `https://user-images.githubusercontent.com//`, `https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com//?jwt=…` and `https://objects.githubusercontent.com/github-production-repository-file-5c1aeb/…`, found in Markdown images and links, ``, `` or as bare addresses (`SOURCE_RE`; `&` reads as `&`, trailing `.,:;!?` are not part of the address). Every event's `title` and `body` is read, earlier versions included. Images on other hosts are not copied. - **Hosts.** Only `https`, no port or user name, on `github.com` (the paths above), the three `*.githubusercontent.com` hosts, and the two S3 buckets GitHub redirects to (`github-production-user-asset-6210df.s3.amazonaws.com`, `github-production-repository-file-5c1aeb.s3.amazonaws.com`). A redirect leaving that list is refused before it is requested. No token is sent (it would follow the redirect to S3); public attachments need none. - **Expired links.** A `private-user-images` JWT lives five minutes. After that, the picture is fetched from `user-images.githubusercontent.com//`, then `github.com/user-attachments/assets/` (the uuid is in the file name). An `objects.githubusercontent.com` address with an expired signature is fetched as `github.com/user-attachments/files//`, the name taken from `response-content-disposition`. All of these answer without a token. - **Kept types.** Checked by first bytes: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG, PDF, ZIP, gzip, 7z, xz, bzip2, MP4/QuickTime, WebM, pcap, pcapng, and UTF-8 text with a text extension (`.txt`, `.log`, `.csv`, `.json`, `.c`, …; stored as `.txt`). Anything else (an HTML login page, an executable) is dropped. At most 25 MiB a file (`MAX_BYTES`) and 30 s a request. Files are stored by content as `.forkmesh/attachments/.`. SVG is served by the raw route as a download (`raw_spec`) and drawn through `data-repo-svg-src`, never inline. - **Index.** `.forkmesh/attachments/index.json`: `{"schema": "forkmesh-attachments-v1", "files": {"
": {"path", "type", "bytes"}}, "unavailable": {"
": {"reason", "tries", "nextTry"}}}`, sorted, written only on change. Each issue with a copied file also gets `.forkmesh/attachments/issues/.json` (`forkmesh-attachments-issue-v1`), which the issue page reads. Signed issue records are never changed, and nothing is deleted. - **Retries.** An unfetchable file is listed under `unavailable` and retried after 1, 2, 4, … days, at most every 30 days; a too-large or unkept file waits 30 days. A rate limit (`429`, or `403` with `Retry-After`) waits once if `Retry-After` is at most 60 s, otherwise the pass stops copying; neither marks the file unavailable. - **Budget.** One request at a time, 0.5 s apart, newest issues first; at most `--attachment-files` (300) downloads, `--attachment-megabytes` (256) and 300 s per pass. The repository keeps at most 1 GiB of copies (`TOTAL_BYTES`, summed from `index.json`); past that a pass stops with `stopped: "total"`. Copies stay in Git history for good, so without the cap anyone who can comment upstream could grow every clone by 256 MB a pass. A 611-issue forum with about 5,900 comments needed roughly 110-120 MB. Pages draw a copied file from the repository's raw URL, and an uncopied GitHub attachment as a link, never an `` ([repo-views.md](app/repo-views.md#issue-page-first-view)). ## Rate limits and status A rate limit (`429`, or `403` with an exhausted quota) waits for `Retry-After`; other failures back off exponentially, and a stopped pass keeps its progress. Reports (`forkmesh-forge-sync-report-v1`, see [synchronization status](sync-status.md)) give lag against the SLO (default 15 minutes), convergence and conflict rates, and retries. They never contain tokens.

pages.title: Git errors when cloning, pulling, or pushing
pages.description: ForkMesh serves Git over HTTPS at https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>. Clones and pulls are often redirected to a mirror, so a warning: redirecting to ... line is normal.…
pages.markdown:
# Git errors when cloning, pulling, or pushing

ForkMesh serves Git over HTTPS at `https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<repo>`.
Clones and pulls are often redirected to a mirror, so a
`warning: redirecting to ...` line is normal. Errors ForkMesh explains are
printed on `remote:` lines with a link to this page; connection failures show
only Git's own message, usually with a `curl` error.

## Messages from ForkMesh

| `remote:` message | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ForkMesh could not reach a mirror of this repository just now. | No mirror that holds the repository answered in time. | Try again in a minute. The repository's **Mirrors** page (`/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`) shows which mirrors are up. |
| This ForkMesh mirror could not read the repository just now. | The mirror you were sent to failed while reading the repository. | Try again; the next attempt may use another mirror. |
| ForkMesh has no public repository at this address. | The owner or repository name is wrong, or the repository is private. | Check the spelling in `git remote -v`. Private repositories need their owner's credential. |
| This ForkMesh mirror has no public repository at this address. | Same as above, answered by the mirror itself. | Same as above. |
| Pushing over HTTPS needs your ForkMesh account name or email and your password, or the repository's push credential. | The push had no credential, or a wrong one, or the account cannot push here. | Use your account name or email as the username and your account password, or the push credential, as the password. See [Hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md). |
| This repository is private. Sign in with your ForkMesh account name or email and your password, or the repository's credential. | The repository is private and the credential was missing or wrong, or your account cannot read it. | Sign in with an account that can read the repository, or use the credential its owner gave you. |
| ForkMesh could not reach the node that accepts pushes for this repository. | The node that writes this repository did not answer. | Try again in a minute. Your commits are still local and safe. |
| Use Git protocol version 0, 1, or 2. | Your Git sent a protocol version ForkMesh does not speak. | Remove `protocol.version` from your Git configuration, or set it to `2`. |

## Errors from your own Git client

These come from Git and curl on your computer; ForkMesh never saw the request.

| Git prints | What happened | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Error in the HTTP2 framing layer`, `HTTP/2 stream … was not closed cleanly`, `curl 16`, `curl 92` | The HTTP/2 connection broke partway through. VPNs, proxies, antivirus that inspects HTTPS, and unstable mobile or Wi-Fi links cause most of these. | Run the command again. If it keeps failing, use HTTP/1.1 for this repository: `git config http.version HTTP/1.1`. Add `--global` to use it everywhere. |
| `RPC failed; curl 18 transfer closed with outstanding read data remaining`, `curl 56`, `early EOF`, `unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet` | The connection dropped while Git was downloading. | Run the command again. If it fails at the same point every time, include a trace in your report (below). |
| `Could not resolve host`, `Failed to connect`, `Connection timed out`, `Connection refused` | Your computer could not reach ForkMesh at all. | Check your network, DNS, and any VPN or proxy. |
| `SSL certificate problem` | Something between you and ForkMesh is presenting another certificate, or your clock is wrong. | Check the system clock, and any proxy or antivirus that intercepts HTTPS. |

## Reporting a problem

Open an issue on
[forkmesh/forkmesh](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh/issues) with
`git --version`, `curl --version`, the time of failure with time zone, and a
trace (check it for secrets before posting):

```bash
GIT_TRACE_CURL=1 GIT_TRACE_CURL_NO_DATA=1 git pull origin main 2>&1 | tail -60
```

## How the messages are produced

For developers. Git shows a server's explanation only for a failed `info/refs`
GET and only when the body is `text/plain`, printing each line as `remote: …`.
A failed `git-upload-pack` or `git-receive-pack` POST shows nothing from the
body, and transport failures carry no body at all.

| Part | Where | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| App | `_git_error_as_text` (`app/src/entry.py`) | Wraps the `info/refs` routes (upload-pack public and private, receive-pack). A JSON error of status 400 or more becomes one sentence plus `Help: https://forkmesh.com/docs/git-errors/`. The status and `cache-control`, `retry-after`, `www-authenticate`, `x-forkmesh-expected-degraded` and `x-forkmesh-served-by` are kept (`WWW-Authenticate` must survive or git never prompts for credentials). A `message` or `hint` in the JSON wins over the table in `GIT_ERROR_MESSAGES`. Other routes and POSTs still answer JSON. |
| Node gateway | `dispatch_error_response` (`tools/mirror_gateway.py`) | The same for the public `/<owner>/<repo>.git/info/refs` route. Restricted and missing repositories get the same 404 text. |
| Desktop | `forkmesh::gitrefusal::explainFailure` (`desktop/src/GitRefusal.cpp`) | Shows the server's `remote:` sentence, or a plain sentence for transport failures, instead of raw stderr (the log keeps the raw text). HTTP/2 breaks count as transient. |
| Transports | `tools/forkmesh_transports.py` | Treats HTTP/2 breaks as route failures and tries the next route. |
| Installer | `www/public/install.sh` | Names HTTP/2 breaks and dropped downloads. |

pages.title: Hackathon
pages.description: How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works. Anything worth money is gated on the referral ledger, every reward is a fixed threshold, there are no random draws, and sharing earns…
pages.markdown:
# Hackathon

How a ForkMesh hackathon campaign works. Anything worth money is gated on the
referral ledger, every reward is a fixed threshold, there are no random draws,
and sharing earns nothing.
Other pages are listed in the [docs index](README.md).

| Area | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Policy (points, missions, rewards, judging, config validation) | `app/src/hackathon.py` |
| Routes, storage, admin page | `app/src/hackathon_runtime.py` |
| Share cards | `app/src/og_card.py` (`render_hackathon_card`) |
| Participant HQ | `app/public/dashboard/partials/views/hackathon.html` |
| Public pages | `www/public/hackathon/leaderboard.html`, `www/public/hackathon/projects.html` |
| Schema | `app/migrations/0182_hackathon.sql` |

## What /hackathon shows

`/hackathon` and `/hackathon/rules` are the current campaign's pages; they are
static templates in `www/templates/pages/`. When a campaign ends, its pages
move under `/hackathon/archive/<slug>` with an "Archived" banner, and
`/hackathon/archive` lists every finished one.

| Campaign | Dates (UTC) | Pages |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plugin Race | 19 Oct – 18 Dec 2026 | `/hackathon`, `/hackathon/rules`; engine in [docs/app/plugin-race.md](app/plugin-race.md) |
| September Revenue Contest | 15 Sep – 15 Oct 2026 | `/hackathon/archive/revenue-contest-2026`, `/hackathon/archive/revenue-contest-2026-rules`; continued as the [affiliate program](app/affiliates.md) |

The archive pages are routed to the website by `WWW_HACKATHON_ARCHIVE_PAGES` in
`app/src/static_routes.py`; add a new archive slug there. The Plugin Race
does not use the points engine below, because its finish line is marketplace
ratings.

## Lifecycle

A campaign is a `hackathons` row keyed by slug with status `draft`,
`registration`, `live`, `judging`, or `closed`. A `draft` campaign 404s on
every participant page and API, so unfinished campaigns can ship safely. Only an
administrator advances status.

## Points

`hackathon_points` is append-only with primary key
`(hackathon_slug, account_bi, kind, ref)`, which prevents double payment. Kinds:
`joined`, `verified`, `referral_joined`, `referral_qualified`, `first_mirror`,
`pull_accepted`, `submission`, `referral_post`. No kind is client-reportable.

A referral is *joined* when the invitee verifies email and *qualified* when the
referral ledger credits it. Anything of value reads qualified.

## Rewards

Missions and milestones award `pro_months`, `supporter_months`, a `badge`, or
nothing; cash follows judged tracks only. Grants are claimed once in
`hackathon_reward_grants` and projected into `role_grants` with
`scope_type='promotion'`, stacking months.

## Teams, submissions, and judging

A squad is an invite tree; a team (up to five) submits one project per track.
Submissions must name a public repository first hosted in the campaign window;
doubtful ones are flagged for review, not rejected. Only `valid` projects are
public. Judges score 1 to 5 on four criteria; finalizing ranks each track and
grants the prize table once.

Challenge links fix their target when sent, need a strictly higher score, and
pay no points. Share presses are measured, never paid, and nothing is sent on
anyone's behalf.

## Administration and privacy

`/admin/hackathon` and `/api/admin/hackathon` require a live `is_admin`
session. Public reads are cached and bounded. No contacts are collected;
public pages show only public usernames.

pages.title: Integration contract (v1)
pages.description: A versioned contract for tools that migrate, automate, discover, deploy, analyze, or moderate repositories without scraping a UI: HTTP resources, a forkmesh-event-v1 event…
pages.markdown:
# Integration contract (v1)

A versioned contract for tools that migrate, automate, discover, deploy,
analyze, or moderate repositories without scraping a UI: HTTP resources, a
`forkmesh-event-v1` event stream, command-line output, and signed webhooks.
[`conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json`](../conformance/integrations/v1/contract.json)
is the source of truth; if this page disagrees, the JSON wins. The client,
contract runner, watcher, webhook sender, and offline fixture are one
standard-library file,
[`tools/forkmesh_integration.py`](../tools/forkmesh_integration.py). The
[docs index](README.md) lists related guides; how the hosted service runs is on
[Architecture and availability](architecture.md).

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py discover --target hosted
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py contract --target self-hosted --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8791
python3 tools/forkmesh_integration.py contract --target hosted --fixture next   # offline
```

`contract` prints a `forkmesh-integration-contract-report-v1` report (status
codes, fields, headers, attempts, latency, service version; no credentials).

## Services and authentication

| Service | Default base URL | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hosted` | `https://app.forkmesh.com` | The hosted application API |
| `self-hosted` | `http://127.0.0.1:8791` | The `forkmesh-mirror-node` loopback control API |

Each resource names one scheme: `anonymous` (public, may be cached),
`loopback-operator` (socket access is the authorization; never publish the
port), `catalog-view-token` (owner-signed `forkmesh-catalog-view-v1` `viewer`,
`ts`, `sig`; adds private repositories, `no-store` with a weak `ETag`),
`account-bearer` (`Authorization: Bearer …`, never in a URL),
`webhook-capability-url` (the 256-bit token in the URL is the credential), and
`webhook-hmac` (see [Signatures](#signatures)).

## HTTP resources

| Service | Method and path | Required fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hosted | `GET /api/version` | `ok`, `rev`, `worker`, `version`, `now` |
| hosted | `GET /api/openapi.json` | `openapi`, `info`, `paths` |
| hosted | `GET /api/metrics/endpoints` | `ok`, `endpoints[].method`, `endpoints[].template` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories` | `ok`, `repositories[].owner`, `.name`, `.visibility` |
| hosted | `GET /api/repositories/search` (beta) | `ok`, `total`, `results[].owner`, `.name`, `.clone` |
| hosted | `GET /api/status` | `ok`, `now`, `systems[].id`, `systems[].status` |
| hosted | `GET /api/mirrors/https` | `ok`, `protocol`, `registration` |
| hosted | `POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` | inbound webhook, `202 {"ok", "messageId"}` |
| self-hosted | `GET /healthz` | `ok`, `node` |
| self-hosted | `GET /readyz` (200 or 503) | `ok`, `ready`, `version` |
| self-hosted | `GET /v1/status` | `ok`, `ready`, `node`, `version`, `uptimeSeconds`, `repositories`, `lastSyncOk`, `syncCount` |
| self-hosted | `POST /v1/control/sync` | `202 {"ok", "queued"}` |

Only these routes are stable; others discovered via OpenAPI may change.

## Pagination

Collections are bounded: `GET /api/repositories` returns at most 200 records,
newest `updatedAt` first. Time feeds resume with `since` = previous `latestTs`
(deduplicate the boundary). `GET /api/repositories/search` is keyset-paged:
pass `nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`. See
[Searchable repository index](repository-index.md).

## Filtering

Only search filters server-side (`q`, `view`, `language`, `topic`, `owner`,
`cloneable`). Otherwise filter client-side on documented fields.

## Idempotency

`GET`/`HEAD` are safe to repeat. `POST /v1/control/sync` is idempotent
(`"queued": false` while pending). Inbound chat webhook POSTs are not
deduplicated. Every outbound event has a stable `id` to use as the idempotency
key.

## Ordering and the event stream

```json
{"schema":"forkmesh-event-v1","id":"4c1f…","type":"repository.changed",
 "subject":"owner/name","sequence":7,"digest":"9a0e…","occurredAt":1789347378245,
 "source":"https://app.forkmesh.com","data":{"owner":"owner","name":"name"}}
```

| Type | Service | Subject | Producer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repository.changed`, `repository.removed` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | `watch` |
| `repository.push`, `branch.push` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `pull.merged`, `release.published` | hosted | lowercase `owner/name` | relay |
| `mirror.node.changed` | self-hosted | `node:<name>` | `watch` |
| `mirror.repository.changed`, `mirror.repository.removed` | self-hosted | the daemon's repository key | `watch` |

Delivery is at-least-once, `sequence` increases by one per subject (no global
order), and every `changed` event carries full current `data`. `EventLedger`
in the tool applies the consumer rules: ignore seen ids and stale sequences,
buffer gaps, emit `resync` after `gapTimeoutSeconds` (120), and accept the
first event per subject as the baseline.

## Webhooks

`deliver` posts events as canonical JSON with these headers: `ForkMesh-Webhook-Id`
(event id), `ForkMesh-Webhook-Timestamp` (Unix seconds per attempt),
`ForkMesh-Webhook-Signature` (`v1=<hex>`, comma-separated during rotation),
`ForkMesh-Webhook-Attempt`, `ForkMesh-Event-Type`. `2xx` acknowledges, `410`
stops, retryable statuses retry, anything else goes to the dead-letter file
(replay with `deliver --input dead.ndjson`).

### Signatures

```text
signature = "v1=" + hex(HMAC-SHA256(secret, "forkmesh-webhook-v1\n" + timestamp + "\n" + id + "\n" + raw_body))
```

```python
msg = b"forkmesh-webhook-v1\n%d\n%s\n" % (ts, headers["ForkMesh-Webhook-Id"].encode()) + body
```

Reject timestamps more than 300 seconds off and deduplicate by id.

### Repository webhooks

Owners register public `https` endpoints in repository **Settings**
(`POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/webhooks`); the relay generates the secret and
shows it once. Events: `repository.push` (any ref moved), `branch.push`
(default branch moved), `pull.merged`, `release.published`. Only public
repositories emit them; deliveries are queued out of band and stop after 6
attempts. `sequence` is per endpoint.

### Inbound chat webhooks

`POST /api/chat/webhooks/{token}` with `{"text": "…"}` posts to a public
channel (`202`). Errors: 400 `empty_webhook`, 404 `not_found`, 405
`method_not_allowed`, 409 `public_channel_required`.

## Retries

Retry idempotent requests on transport errors and `408`, `425`, `429`, `500`,
`502`, `503`, `504`: at most 6 attempts, exponential backoff from 0.5 s capped
at 30 s with jitter; `Retry-After` or `retryAfterMs` overrides. Non-idempotent
requests retry only on `429`.

## Rate limits

Throttled requests answer `429` with `Retry-After`. Hosted public reads are
cached (catalog 30 s). `watch` polls no faster than 30 s hosted, 5 s
self-hosted.

## Errors

Hosted errors are `{"error":"<snake_case>"}`; the daemon answers
`{"ok":false,"error":"<message>"}`. Branch on status class, then code. New
codes are additive.

## Command-line output

Each stdout line is one JSON object (`"schema":"forkmesh-cli-v1"`, or events
for `watch`); diagnostics go to stderr. Commands: `validate`, `discover`,
`contract`, `watch`, `deliver`, `fixture`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | success |
| 1 | contract failure or undeliverable events |
| 2 | usage or configuration error |
| 3 | unsupported service version skew |

`forkmesh-mirror-node` flags: `-config`, `-init`, `-check`, `-public-key`,
`-set-version`, `-register-link-code`, `-version`; exit `0` or `1`.

## Deprecation

Deprecated entries are marked `"stability": "deprecated"` and listed with
`announced`, `sunset` (at least 180 days later), and `replacement`. Removal
needs contract v2.

## Version skew

Within v1 services only add; consumers must ignore unknown fields. A version
below `serviceMinimum` is `unsupported` (exit 3); unparseable versions are
`unknown`. The fixture serves `previous`, `current`, `next`, `broken`, and
`unsupported` profiles.

## Examples

Examples in `conformance/integrations/v1/examples/` use only this contract:
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/discovery_catalog.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/migration_export.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/webhook_moderation.py`,
`conformance/integrations/v1/examples/deployment_gate.py`.

## Contract tests and telemetry

`app/tests/test_integration_contract.py` checks every entry against the
serving source, runs the contract against the fixture for both services and
every profile, and runs every example. Each report's `telemetry` block records
requests, retries, transport errors, status classes, and latency.

# Launch

Launch readiness for ForkMesh: the evidence gate before a public launch, the
clean-machine install proof behind it, the incident plan rehearsal, and the
GitHub outage campaign kit. Each page records measured evidence, not plans
presented as facts.

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Y Combinator News launch readiness](y-combinator-news-readiness.md) | The launch verdict, required evidence ledger, launch gates and incident plan |
| [Clean-machine install evidence](clean-machine-evidence.md) | The harness that installs the signed `latest` release on clean machines and records each step |
| [Launch incident tabletop](incident-tabletop-2026-09-16.md) | A desk walk-through of the incident plan and its findings |
| [GitHub outage survival kit](github-outage-survival-kit.md) | An unpublished video script, post thread and mirror bounty for getting repositories mirrored before an outage |

Core pages: [architecture](../architecture.md), [mirroring](../mirroring.md),

pages.title: Clean-machine install evidence
pages.description: Part of Launch.
pages.markdown:
# Clean-machine install evidence

Part of [Launch](README.md).

The clean-machine harness tests whatever the signed `latest` manifest
publishes and stamps every step with the tag and `checksums_sha256` it
verified. Pin a release with `FORKMESH_EXPECTED_TAG` /
`FORKMESH_EXPECTED_CHECKSUMS_SHA256` (Actions variables `CLEAN_MACHINE_TAG` /
`CLEAN_MACHINE_CHECKSUMS`). Evidence classes follow the
[launch readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md). A step passes only
when a dated transcript line shows it.

Release measured on this page: tag `v1.5.0`, `checksums_sha256`
`61872afbc33560807e531bf9e650141d9424c5e2c9f417d72b24decd1167fb9f`
([checks](#v150-release-checks)). The earlier
[v1.2.7 checks](#v127-release-checks) are kept below for history.

## Status

| Acceptance step | Linux x86_64 | Windows x86_64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` binding | **Measured fact** | Same manifest |
| Blob hash of the downloaded asset | **Measured fact** | **Measured fact** |
| Authenticode signature | Not applicable | **Measured fact** (pinned signer) |
| SmartScreen dialog text | Not applicable | **Missing proof** |
| Installer run on a fresh machine | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| First launch and node identity creation | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Provider CLI discovery | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Continual cycle stops at the human decision card | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| **Stop work** pauses the loop | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| Uninstall (default keeps data) | **Missing proof** | **Missing proof** |
| `--purge` prompt text | **Missing proof** | No purge option |

### Why the steps do not run on a production host

`uninstall.sh` stops every process named `forkmesh` and `install.sh` stops
managed daemons, so `tools/clean_machine_transcript.sh run` refuses to start
when a ForkMesh process or ForkMesh data already exists. Fresh-machine steps
run only in a disposable VM.

## Harness

`tools/clean_machine_transcript.sh verify` clones `.forkmesh/releases/latest`,
takes the Ed25519 key from the live `install.sh`, verifies the manifest
signature, checks that `sha256(SHASUMS256.txt)` equals `checksums_sha256`, and
prints the asset hashes. The installer itself prints no verification lines on
success, so the harness records them before installing and compares the
installed binary with `blob_sha256` afterwards.

`run` executes, in order: machine header, release verification, provider CLIs,
`curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install.sh | bash`, installed-binary hash,
node identity files, default `uninstall.sh` with a listing of kept data,
`--purge` answered `no`, `--purge` without a terminal, and `--purge --yes`.
Between install and uninstall it stops at operator checkpoints for first
launch, provider discovery, the decision card and **Stop work**; an empty
answer is logged as `NOT OBSERVED`. Use a throwaway account, because first
launch announces the node to the network.

The **Clean-machine VM evidence** Action (`.forkmesh/clean-machine-vm.yml`,
driver `tools/clean_machine_vm.py`) boots a disposable Debian VM under QEMU,
runs the harness inside it, and keeps per-step screenshots, a video, the
transcript, the serial log and `summary.json`. A host-side observer OCRs the
framebuffer at each step and matches phrases from
`tools/clean_machine_expectations.json`; the verdict is `observed`,
`not-observed` or `unchecked`, and only `observed` passes. GUI steps that need
a person stay `not-observed` in unattended runs.

Purge prompt, quoted from `www/public/uninstall.sh`:

```text
This removes ForkMesh and ALL of its data from this computer:
  • the forkmesh binary and installed source
  • settings, the node identity key (the account cannot be recovered)
  • every mirrored repository, and all chat history
  • the desktop launcher, icons, and login-autostart entry

Type DELETE to continue:
```

Without a terminal it prints `Refusing to erase ForkMesh data without
confirmation. Re-run with --yes (or set FORKMESH_ASSUME_YES=1): …`.

## Windows

The installer is Authenticode-signed with a self-issued certificate. Against
public roots verification fails ("self-signed certificate"); pinned to the
release certificate it passes, with a DigiCert RFC 3161 timestamp:

```text
$ openssl x509 -in signer.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256
sha256 Fingerprint=06:E0:93:EA:D7:0B:BD:A1:0B:4C:B6:0A:AE:B2:2C:8C:52:AA:ED:07:6E:21:F4:05:6E:45:2D:38:D1:BE:45:73
$ osslsigncode verify -in setup.exe -CAfile signer.pem
Signature verification: ok
```

That fingerprint equals `DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SIGNER_SHA256` in
`tools/forkmesh-release-host.py`. SmartScreen therefore warns on first run.

The NSIS installer (`tools/package/forkmesh.nsi`) installs per user into
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ForkMesh`; its uninstaller removes that directory, shortcuts,
the uninstall key and the `forkmesh:` URL handler, with no purge option. The
node identity key lives under Roaming `%APPDATA%\ForkMesh\ForkMesh` and
settings in the registry, so both should survive uninstall.

Fresh-VM procedure: `Get-FileHash` and `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` on the
setup executable, record the SmartScreen dialog text, install and launch,
list both data directories, run provider discovery, one continual cycle and
**Stop work**, uninstall, and list the directories again.

## macOS

The DMG is universal (`x86_64` and `arm64`), ad-hoc signed and not notarized,
so Gatekeeper blocks first launch until the user opens it with right-click →
**Open**. A fresh-Mac transcript must record the Gatekeeper dialog,
`codesign --verify --deep --strict`, first launch and removal.

## v1.2.7 release checks

Each blob is served from
`https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/releases/blob/sha256/<hash>`;
every hash and size below equals its manifest entry.

```text
57533adabf28889641ae8b383bce060b95476a2ff209fa8623f72da77670c5f2    111213600  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64          forkmesh-linux-x86_64
f5caed0e686e0ef66cb429c88f7702c5f355a177757182cca90cef45ec860c8c     13159125  ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, Go, static  forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64
57cda708a4098a666f9b7b95b56b2d361790bcf40438249ad782ac27b950d901     80290024  PE32 executable (GUI), Nullsoft Installer     forkmesh-windows-x86_64-setup.exe
6d6e3cb5fdfdc4c2978c4c5f37cc1b9fddfa22095d756d5e739c34efeb6ee7cf    173041477  zlib-compressed DMG holding an APFS volume    forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg
```

`forkmesh-macos-x86_64.dmg` has the same `blob_sha256` and size as
`forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg`. Every fresh-VM step in the status table is still
**Missing proof** for this release.

## v1.5.0 release checks

Measured 2026-10-31 from the same blob route. `release.json`,
`release.json.sig` and `SHASUMS256.txt` served at
`https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/raw?path=.forkmesh/releases/latest/…&ref=main`
(the `/desktop` page's manifest URL) are byte-identical to the repository
copies; the signature verifies with the key in `install.sh`, and
`sha256(SHASUMS256.txt)` equals `checksums_sha256`. Every hash and size below
equals its manifest entry.

```text
9ca90fe0dc5f26f97abaa3fd26b4d898a652fe3868ab32e53e5393fc99358ebf    142611552  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64          forkmesh-linux-x86_64
c4da0b5801fb0ca75deae158c61ac12b386ef7e9eb61ca87c5394a143f9c6378     14076218  ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64, static     forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64
7889aad7fd55d490d603ffe75603b50a0da1099fed7bf218b14ec317e29efbd6     96940752  PE32 executable (GUI)                         forkmesh-windows-x86_64-setup.exe
8991bcc9e47c807b1ef5fd0d16ab2c643b050013ba3dc90736ed5c448d2f6040    214746483  zlib-compressed DMG                           forkmesh-macos-arm64.dmg
```

The setup executable's Authenticode signer is `CN=ForkMesh, O=ForkMesh`, SHA-256
fingerprint `06:E0:93:EA:D7:0B:BD:A1:0B:4C:B6:0A:AE:B2:2C:8C:52:AA:ED:07:6E:21:F4:05:6E:45:2D:38:D1:BE:45:73`
(the pinned `DEFAULT_WINDOWS_SIGNER_SHA256`), timestamped by DigiCert; Windows
reports the chain as ending in an untrusted root, as expected for the
self-issued certificate. The two macOS assets again share one digest.
Every fresh-VM step in the status table is still **Missing proof** for this
release.

pages.markdown:
# GitHub outage survival kit

Part of [Launch](README.md).

A launch kit, not yet published: a 60-second video script, a post thread and a
$5 mirror bounty. The goal is to get repositories mirrored on ForkMesh
**before** a GitHub outage, so cloning and shipping continue during one.
Recording, posting, opening the bounty and paying claims are human actions.
Success is measured by valid bounty claims, not views or reposts. What keeps
working when a provider is down is described in [mirroring](../mirroring.md) and
[censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md).

## Claim boundaries

| Copy may say | Copy must not say |
| --- | --- |
| Creating a ForkMesh repository is one click; moving the code is one `git push` ([hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md)) | That the switch is automatic |
| A public GitHub import is refreshed about every 30 minutes and served without the provider ([repository imports](../repository-imports.md#ending-the-provider-dependency)) | That private imports are hosted, or that the copy is real-time |
| `git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` is served by a healthy eligible mirror ([product promise](../product-promise.md)) | Uptime or speed guarantees |
| One `insteadOf` line repoints pinned Git dependencies ([dependency workflows](../dependency-workflows.md#switching-providers-without-editing-a-lock)) | That every dependency is already on ForkMesh |
| Set up before the outage; new imports need the provider's API | That you can import from GitHub while it is down |

Never mock GitHub or an incident in progress.

## 1. Sixty-second video

Use a disposable repository and account, keep the push credential off camera,
and label the staged outage on screen.

| Time | Picture | Narration | On-screen caption |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0:00–0:06 | Title card on a dark background | "GitHub is down. Your commits are still on your laptop. Here's how to keep shipping." | Staged demo: origin unreachable |
| 0:06–0:14 | Terminal: `git push origin main` fails with a connection error | "Your push fails, and your teammates can't clone." | `git push` fails |
| 0:14–0:26 | Browser: app.forkmesh.com → **Repositories → New** → the **Empty repository** source is already selected → type a name → click **Create empty repository** | "On ForkMesh, create an empty repository. That's the one click." | One click: **Create empty repository** |
| 0:26–0:40 | Terminal: `git remote add forkmesh https://app.forkmesh.com/you/app` then `git push -u forkmesh main`; username prompt shown, password blurred | "Add it as a remote and push. Every branch and commit you have is now on ForkMesh." | One push |
| 0:40–0:52 | Second terminal, different directory: `git clone https://forkmesh.com/you/app`, then `git rev-parse HEAD` next to the same command in the first terminal; the hashes match | "A teammate clones from forkmesh.com and gets the exact same commit." | Same commit, no GitHub |
| 0:52–1:00 | End card: kit URL and the bounty line | "Do it before the next outage. Mirror one repo, post proof, and we'll send you five dollars." | forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit · $5 bounty, terms apply |

## 2. Thread

X counts each link as 23 characters; `www/tests` checks every post against the
280-character limit.

<!-- outage-thread:start -->

```text
GitHub will go down again. Your commits are safe on your laptop, but your team, CI, and installs aren't.

3 ways to keep shipping when it happens. Set them up before the outage.
```

```text
1. Push every commit to two places.

Create an empty ForkMesh repo and add your SSH key, then:

git remote set-url --add --push origin git@github.com:you/app.git
git remote set-url --add --push origin ssh://git@ssh.forkmesh.com/you/app.git

Now one git push updates both.
```

```text
2. Import the repo and let a host keep a copy.

app.forkmesh.com: Repositories, New, GitHub, paste the URL, Start resumable import.

For a public repo, ForkMesh hosts clone it and refresh it about every 30 minutes, so it still clones when GitHub can't.
```

```text
3. Keep builds installing. Pin git dependencies to full commit IDs, then point your mirrored org at ForkMesh with one line:

git config --global url."https://forkmesh.com/acme/".insteadOf "https://github.com/acme/"

Lock files don't change. The commit ID is the content.
```

```text
Already down? New imports need GitHub's API, so they wait. But your local clone can go to an empty ForkMesh repo right now: one click, one push.

60 seconds: [video]
```

```text
Try it for $5: mirror one of your public repos on ForkMesh, clone it from forkmesh.com, and post proof. Say it's for the bounty.

Terms: https://forkmesh.com/docs/launch/github-outage-survival-kit/
```

<!-- outage-thread:end -->

Way 3 only works for dependencies mirrored on ForkMesh under the same owner and
name. A private repository import is never hosted; point people at way 1.

## 3. The $5 mirror bounty

Mirror one of your public GitHub repositories on ForkMesh, clone it from its
`forkmesh.com` URL, and post proof on X. The first valid claims get $5 each
until the budget runs out.

Eligibility:

1. One claim per person and per ForkMesh account; no bulk, seeded or bot
   accounts; staff and contractors excluded.
2. The repository is public, owned or maintained by the claimant on GitHub,
   existed before the campaign, and is not a fork of `forkmesh/forkmesh`.
3. It is on ForkMesh as a fully hosted import or as a pushed empty repository.
4. The post is public, still up at review, includes the
   `https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY` URL and the clone output, and
   discloses the payment.

We never pay for likes, reposts, follows, or replies, and a claim never has to
ask anyone for them.

Reviewer checklist, from a clean machine with no ForkMesh credential:

```sh
git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY bounty-check
git -C bounty-check fetch -q https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY HEAD
git -C bounty-check merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD FETCH_HEAD && echo "commit is on GitHub"
curl -s https://app.forkmesh.com/api/repo/OWNER/REPOSITORY/mirrors
```

Approve only when the clone succeeds, `HEAD` is on GitHub's default branch,
the mirrors payload lists an online mirror, and every eligibility rule holds.
Payout details are exchanged privately, never in public comments. The bounty
has no effect on identity, permissions, ranking or moderation
([incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md)).

## Outage-day plan

1. Act only on an open GitHub status incident affecting Git operations.
2. Confirm a fresh clone of `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` works and
   ForkMesh status is healthy; otherwise post nothing.
3. Quote-post the pinned thread once.
4. Within a week, publish the claim count, verified clones and what failed.

# Launch incident tabletop — 2026-09-16

Part of [Launch](README.md).

A desk walk-through of the incident plan in the
[launch readiness packet](y-combinator-news-readiness.md#incident-plan). Data
custody answers come from [relay data retention and deletion](../relay-data-retention.md).

## Record

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Date | 2026-09-16 |
| Kind | Desk tabletop; no fault injected, no production control used |
| Scenario | A measured clone outage replayed minute by minute, then every other row of the incident plan |
| Incident lead | ForkMesh account `forkmesh`, the fleet operator account that holds every mirror-side control |
| Thread voice | The human launch owner, in their own words |

## Relay rate limits

Each limit is a constant in `app/src/entry.py`; changing one needs a relay
release, and counters reset only when their window rolls over.

| Limit | Constant and value | Answer when exceeded |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Account creation per source IP | `SIGNUP_MAX_PER_IP = 5` per hour | 429 `rate_limited` with `Retry-After` |
| Failed sign-ins | `LOGIN_MAX_FAILS = 10` in 15 minutes, then a 15-minute lock | Sign-in refused |
| Password reset | `PASSWORD_RESET_ACCOUNT_WINDOW_LIMIT = 5` per account per day; `PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTER_WINDOW_LIMIT = 10` per requester per hour | Same `{"ok": true}`, no email |
| Assistant prompts | `AI_ASK_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 60` per account per hour | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Browser error reports | `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_PER_CLIENT = 8`, `CLIENT_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 120` per minute | Not stored |
| Desktop error reports | `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_PER_OWNER = 6`, `DESKTOP_ERROR_RATE_GLOBAL = 60` per minute | Not stored |
| Chat frames per socket | `ROOM_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per 10 seconds | Frame dropped |
| Node event channel | `NODE_EVENT_MSG_MAX_PER_WINDOW = 20` per 10 seconds | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Catalog writes per owner | `CATALOG_WRITE_COOLDOWN_MS = 500` | 429 `rate_limited` |
| Security reports | `MAX_SECURITY_REPORTS = 1000` stored | Oldest beyond the cap dropped |

Mirror limits: `LARGE_REQUEST_BODY_SLOTS` in `tools/mirror_gateway.py` (2
large push bodies in flight) and the SSH gateway's session, process and
upload-pack deadline limits.

## Reset and recovery controls

| Control | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Signed admin `POST /api/mirrors/admission-override` (`ttlSeconds` default 1800, max 21600, audited) | Readmits mirrors that are up but locked out by the refs pin window; useless when mirrors are down |
| `systemctl restart forkmesh-mirror-node`, then `/readyz` | One node at a time |
| Reinstall the prior binary ([rolling migration](../operations/mirror-node.md#rolling-migration)) | After a release that coincides with onset |
| `GET /v1/status` on a node | Read-only diagnosis |

Missing controls: no rate limit on anonymous Git or public API reads, no
read-only or maintenance mode, and no way to post a public incident.

## Row 1: clone fails on every mirror

| Time (UTC) | Inject | Decision and control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 18:28:08 | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` fails with 503 | Declare an incident, stop the demo, say clone is down; no retry loop |
| +1 min | Relay or mirrors? | Read the serving list from `/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors` and probe each mirror's `/health` directly |
| +1 min | Status page shows every system operational | Quote timestamped probe results, not the status page |
| +2 min | Why did every mirror fail at once? | Check each node's journal and `/v1/status` for a fleet-wide gateway reload or roll |
| +2 min | Use the admission override? | No: the mirrors are down, not held out |
| 18:30:41 | Clone succeeds again | Resume only after `ls-remote` matches from two networks a minute apart, a depth-1 clone succeeds, and the availability proof verifies |
| After | Write-up | Record onset, first failed probe, recovery and cause-or-unknown; never edit history to look green |

The outage deleted or exposed no data.

## Rows 2–8

| Incident | First control |
| --- | --- |
| Status green while the Git path fails | Independent `ls-remote` and clone probes with timestamps |
| Install, checksum or signature failure | Stop recommending the installer; capture OS, manifest and asset hashes and the exact error |
| Platform questions (macOS, SmartScreen) | Link the signed manifest and the support matrix |
| Security report | Private channel only; preserve evidence; scope affected releases |
| Heavy traffic or abuse | Relay limits above; protect control endpoints first |
| Wrong claim found live | Correct the surface and link the evidence |
| What is stored and how to delete it | Link the retention table and its known gaps |

## Findings

| ID | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| T1 | One person holds every control; no second responder |
| T2 | No probe script or probe host outside the fleet |
| T3 | No public status history or incident record |
| T4 | No rate limit for anonymous Git or public API reads |
| T5 | No maintenance or read-only mode (the cores now go read-only when two of three are down, see [architecture](../architecture.md)) |
| T6 | No change freeze on `main` during a launch window, although each refs change reloads every mirror gateway |
| T7 | Changing a limit needs a release; counters cannot be reset |

The next exercise repeats row 1 on the current core nodes with two responders
and a prepared probe script against a disposable repository.
