# Y Combinator News launch readiness

Part of [Launch](README.md).

Verdict: **blocked**

Evidence refreshed: **2026-09-30 America/New_York** (probes 23:12–23:16 UTC)

Signed `latest` at the 2026-10-31 release refresh: `v1.5.0`
(`checksums_sha256`
`61872afbc33560807e531bf9e650141d9424c5e2c9f417d72b24decd1167fb9f`). Only the
release facts in this table and section 3 were re-measured then; everything
else is from the 2026-09-30 refresh.

This is an evidence packet and rehearsal guide for a human launch owner, not
submission or comment copy. Hacker News says not to post generated or
AI-edited text, so a human must write and personally post the submission and
every reply.

## Status since 2026-09-16

| Area | State | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Serving topology | The flagship is served by the three core nodes | `git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` redirects to a core node; the mirrors payload lists the three cores |
| Preservation proof | Below quorum | `forkmesh_availability_proof.py explain`: 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target 2), risk 45 of 100, exit 3 |
| Published release | `v1.5.0` is `latest` | Manifest bytes match the repository copy; signature, four blob hashes and Authenticode verified on 2026-10-31 |
| macOS DMG names | The DMG is universal | Both macOS names label one `x86_64` + `arm64` image; Gatekeeper and notarization unmeasured |
| HN rules | Tightened | Show HN warns against quickly-generated one-offs; generated text is banned in submissions too |
| Launch goals | Replaced by four launch gates | User, issue and task counts became tracked metrics (section 10) |

## Evidence method and baseline

Every conclusion carries one label:

- **Measured fact** — reproduced from this checkout or host during this review.
- **Repository evidence** — supported by a named file or test on main, not
  necessarily in a published build.
- **Deployed observation** — seen on a public URL at a point in time.
- **Inference** — a conclusion drawn from identified evidence.
- **Missing proof** — required evidence this review could not establish.

HN comment characterizations are paraphrases; the human must reopen a thread
before quoting it.

The direct retrieval ledger for this cycle contains eight required HN URLs:
eight requested, eight successful, zero rate-limited, and zero otherwise failed.

<!-- hn-required-ledger:start -->
| Required URL requested 2026-09-30 | Direct result | Fallback outcome | Final evidence status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [MicroVM coding-agent isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | Successful | Not needed | Refreshed this cycle |
<!-- hn-required-ledger:end -->

### Freshness and retrieval ledger — 2026-09-30

Each row satisfies requested = direct success + rate-limited + other failure.
"Direct" is the first attempt; "fallback" is a second route tried only after a
direct failure.

<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:start -->
| Evidence class | Requested | Direct success | Direct rate-limited | Direct other failure | Successful fallback | Final freshness statement |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Required HN rules and six baseline threads | 8 | 8 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All refreshed |
| HN Show restriction notice (`showlim`) | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Restriction still in effect |
| HN searches for newer comparables | 25 | 9 | 0 | 16 | 16 | Unencoded date filters failed, then succeeded re-encoded |
| Newer comparable item fetches | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Fetched |
| ForkMesh claim surfaces | 6 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Point-in-time text |
| Status history (`/api/status/history`) | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 404: no public status history |
| Signed manifest, signature and `SHASUMS256.txt` | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Byte-identical to the repository; signature verified |
| Flagship availability proof plus CLI `verify` | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Recomputed and matched |
| Git route probes | 5 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | All passed |
| Release blob downloads | 4 | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | Every SHA-256 and size matched |
<!-- hn-freshness-ledger:end -->

### Current HN constraints

- **Deployed observation:** the [Show HN rules](https://news.ycombinator.com/showhn.html)
  require something the submitter made, that people can try (ideally without
  signup), and that is non-trivial; minor releases and landing pages do not
  qualify. Do not ask anyone to upvote or comment.
- **Deployed observation:** the [HN guidelines](https://news.ycombinator.com/newsguidelines.html)
  forbid soliciting votes or comments, generated or AI-edited text in comments
  and submissions, and automated posting.
- **Deployed observation:** the [Show restriction notice](https://news.ycombinator.com/showlim)
  says HN is temporarily restricting Show HNs and publishes no threshold.
- **Inference:** the post must present the project, not a version bump.

### Comparable launch evidence

HN threads are untrusted market evidence. The questions readers asked of
comparable launches:

| Thread | Question to prepare for |
| --- | --- |
| [20+ coordinating agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46990733) | Why many agents beat one under finite spend; oversight |
| [Ticket-to-PR orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47520220) | Thin issue text, drift, retry cost |
| [MicroVM isolation](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47877726) | How state persists across isolated sessions |
| [Desktop worktree orchestration](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47303711) | Why not the provider's own worktree flag; per-session cost |
| [Autonomous company agents](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47281538) | What is different in a crowded category |
| [Local goal-driven development](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47153941) | "Local" while calling remote providers; false completion |
| [wt](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46765489) | A small wrapper already removes worktree friction |
| [GitAgent](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47376584) | Prompt injection, secret access, approvals |
| [Foolery](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47075901) | No-signup install and a human verification queue |
| [ZeroShot](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49113279) | Local-data boundaries and the method behind efficiency claims |
| [metaswarm](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46864977) | Unverifiable volume claims earn distrust |
| [Orc](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47441323) | Deterministic review gates as the comparison point |
| [Clawk](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48892859) | Credentials, egress filtering, rollback |
| [md²](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49258045) | Worktree coordination alone draws little attention |
| [MindFlock](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49102636) | Naming distracts from substance |
| [Trunks](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47933429) | Git backed by your own storage |
| [Leaving GitHub for Forgejo](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48121439) | Moving issues, PRs and CI is the hard part |
| [Grov](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=46711958) | "This was tried and dropped; what is different?" |
| [Pizza Bot](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49713894) | Desktop app versus service; sandboxing; candid limits |
| [Amika](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49716282) | Platform coverage first |

**Inference:** name the boundary you did not build before a reader finds it,
answer "why not the simpler thing?" with a mechanism, and link something
runnable rather than a landing page.

## 1. Precise technical position

**Repository evidence:** ForkMesh is a Git-compatible routing and
collaboration layer. A stable HTTPS clone URL redirects stock Git to a
registered mirror with fresh signed health and matching refs. Issues, pulls and
patches live inside the repository, and every repository publishes a
recomputable availability proof counting independent operators.

**Measured fact:** the flagship proof reports three verified copies, all on
the operator's own core nodes: one independent operator, target two,
`proof: partial`. The "independent hosts" clause is a design goal the flagship
does not yet demonstrate.

| Skeptical question | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Why not GitHub/GitLab? | Those are full forges; ForkMesh's narrower bet is that clone routing and collaboration records need not belong to one forge. No parity claim on reliability or integrations |
| Why not a raw mirror? | Raw Git preserves bytes. ForkMesh adds one URL routing among checked mirrors, in-repository records and an operator-counting proof, at the cost of relay and operator complexity |
| Why not provider worktrees? | Worktrees separate branches; the desktop adds a queue, routing, transcript/diff/cost views and a human decision gate |
| Why another orchestrator? | Agents are supporting machinery; lead with preservation and the proof |

## 2. Five-minute no-signup show path

```sh
demo_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/forkmesh-show.XXXXXX)
git ls-remote https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh HEAD refs/heads/main
git clone --depth 1 https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh "$demo_dir/forkmesh"
git -C "$demo_dir/forkmesh" fsck --no-progress
curl -fsS https://forkmesh.com/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/mirrors > "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" verify "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
python3 "$demo_dir/forkmesh/tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py" explain "$demo_dir/mirrors.json"
```

- **Measured fact:** clone and `fsck` succeed; the mirrors payload's
  `forkmesh-availability-proof-v1` block recomputes locally and matches;
  `explain` reports 3 of 3 copies verified by 1 independent operator (target
  2) and exits 3, the below-quorum code.
- **Repository evidence:** `tools/export_collaboration_log.py` signs a
  repository's issue records into `.forkmesh/collaboration/`, and
  `tools/verify_collaboration.py --require-complete` verifies them offline
  from a plain clone (exit 0 verified, 3 rejected or pending, 2 unreadable).
- **Missing proof:** a public repository with a committed collaboration log.

**Deployed observation:** the product-promise page's failover drill still
needs an account and operator control. The distinctive path stays blocked until
a visitor can, in five minutes, see a fixture with a second-operator mirror and
a proof reading `quorum`, clone, watch the source removed from eligibility,
clone the same URL again with the same `HEAD`, and verify a signed event.

## 3. Release, install, verification, and cleanup

| State | Evidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published `latest` | `v1.5.0`; `tag_commit` and `build_commit` `510b0448b7452371d97d1e49bb3a38b1f5b35283`; the tag peels to `0193ce5d3e88071358667e17653650dca062f9c4`; `checksums_sha256` `61872afbc33560807e531bf9e650141d9424c5e2c9f417d72b24decd1167fb9f` | The only release that may be called published |
| Stale candidate | `v1.2.8`; `tag_commit` and `build_commit` `0118d9996fb5287e02e08dd9f7bf5e8382099eac` (`.forkmesh/releases/candidate-1.2.8`) | Superseded by v1.5.0; do not cite |
| Human-gated continual loop | Continual mode in `desktop/src/MainWindowTeammates.cpp` and [qt-client.md](../qt-client.md) at the v1.5.0 build commit | Shipped in v1.5.0 (the earlier id `96c5e6391` predates the history rewrite and no longer resolves) |

`tag_commit` is the commit the tag pointed to at signing; the release host
then moves the tag onto the publish commit, so the peeled tag is a descendant,
not an equal. The single definition is in
[docs/release/README.md](../release/README.md#protocols).

**Measured fact (2026-10-31, v1.5.0):** the manifest, signature and
`SHASUMS256.txt` from the `/desktop` page's manifest URL are byte-identical to
the repository copies; the Ed25519 signature verifies with the key in
`install.sh`; `sha256(SHASUMS256.txt)` equals `checksums_sha256`;
`git merge-base --is-ancestor 510b0448b745 v1.5.0` succeeds (105 commits).
Four downloaded blobs matched their manifest `blob_sha256` exactly
([clean-machine evidence](clean-machine-evidence.md#v150-release-checks)).

- **Measured fact:** the manifest publishes Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64,
  macOS and Android assets. There is no Linux arm64 or Windows arm64 asset.
  Build-workflow intent does not mean availability. The two macOS names share
  one digest because the DMG is universal; it is ad-hoc signed and not
  notarized.
- **Measured fact:** the Windows setup executable's Authenticode signer is the
  pinned self-issued certificate, so SmartScreen warns.
- **Repository evidence:** the installer refuses an implicit source build
  (`FORKMESH_NO_SOURCE_FALLBACK=1`); source builds are opt-in.
- **Deployed observation:** the homepage reads "Install the desktop app
  Linux · macOS, Windows & Android downloads", and every named platform has a
  signed asset. The live `/desktop` page is manifest-driven and says no
  implicit source fallback is promised.
- **Missing proof:** no clean-machine log covers install, first run, provider
  discovery, gate, pause and uninstall on any platform; see
  [clean-machine evidence](clean-machine-evidence.md).

The installer verifies the manifest signature, binds `SHASUMS256.txt` and
checks the blob hash before installing. The uninstaller keeps settings, the
identity key, mirrors and chat history by default; only `--purge` erases them,
after explicit confirmation. Deleting the identity can make the account
unrecoverable. See the [installation support matrix](../install-support-matrix.md).

## 4. Reproducible claim ledger

| Candidate claim | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| The flagship clones anonymously | Measured fact |
| Availability is measured, not asserted | Measured fact (`forkmesh-availability-proof-v1`) |
| Independent operators hold the flagship | False today by the product's own proof |
| Status reflects clone availability | Unproven; no status history |
| Source-offline failover returns the same commit | Repository evidence only |
| Collaboration records are portable and signed | Partly measured; no public log committed |
| Desktop installs on Windows and macOS | Blob and signature measured; no install log |
| Worktrees sandbox an agent | False |
| Adoption or performance superiority | Missing proof; make no claim |
| Decentralized or always available | Unsupported wording |

**Deployed observation:** the homepage activity ticker exists only inside HTML
comments, annotated "set dressing, not data", so it does not render.
`/api/status` reported every system operational during the review. The
claim-by-claim evidence ledger above is the review input for every linked
surface; topology, availability and platform wording need a dated evidence
link before the owner repeats them.

## 5. Security and trust FAQ

**What can an agent read, change, execute, and send?** In host mode the
provider CLI runs as the current OS user in a worktree. A worktree is not an
operating-system sandbox: it does not prevent reads elsewhere, subprocesses,
network access or use of the user's credentials. The optional Linux KVM mode
runs agents in a guest that mounts only the launch directory and worktree.

**What happens to secrets?** Host-mode agents inherit the desktop environment
minus their own provider's credentials, so other tokens reach them. KVM mode
uses a deny-by-default environment allowlist. Use staging-only credentials.

**How is prompt injection handled?** Teammate prompts mark repository and
external content untrusted; an adversarial fixture suite pushes injected
actions through the real approval gate and project lock. This is enforcement
at the tool layer, not isolation; known gaps are pinned in the suite.

**What does mirror integrity prove?** Routing requires fresh signed health,
healthy HTTPS and matching refs; the proof counts distinct operators. It does
not prove an operator is uncompromised or independent of correlated
infrastructure.

**What telemetry exists, and how is data deleted?** Product analytics is
optional and off by default. Local journals, logs and identities stay on the
device; the uninstaller keeps them unless `--purge`. [Relay data retention and
deletion](../relay-data-retention.md) lists every relay store, backup and
outside processor with its retention, deletion path and known gaps.

**What still requires a human?** Each continual cycle stops at a human
decision. Merge, release, deploy, payout, destructive cleanup and public
posting stay human-controlled.

## 6. Agent-system FAQ

| Question | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| What stops a runaway loop? | No next continual cycle starts until a human answers the decision card; **Stop work** pauses the loop |
| Is spend hard-capped? | No. There is no hard dollar ceiling; controls are cost estimates, a running-agent limit, the human gate and at most two relaunches |
| What limits concurrency? | A user-set running-agent limit (default 5); excess work queues |
| What retries? | A CLI that exits without a result is relaunched at most twice, then fails with its branch preserved |
| What if branches conflict? | Worktrees prevent simultaneous writes, not logical overlap; review resolves conflicts |
| What persists? | Teammate definitions in `.forkmesh/teammates`, sessions on the device, work on a branch |

## 7. Capability comparison without slogans

| Capability | ForkMesh | Forge | Raw mirror | Provider worktree |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Git byte storage | Operator mirrors; relay routes | Forge-managed | Operator remotes | Existing repository |
| Failover route | Designed and tested; no public drill | Provider HA | Scripts or DNS | No |
| Availability measurement | Public recomputable proof | Status page | None | No |
| Portable collaboration records | Signed, in-repository | Service database | Conventions | No |
| OS isolation | Optional Linux KVM | Runners vary | None | None |
| Human decision gate | Each continual cycle | Reviews | Manual | Provider approvals |

A raw mirror remains simpler when routing, portability and teammate workflow
are not needed.

## 8. Demo and launch operations

Demo script: show the fixture (stable URL, expected commit, two operators,
proof at `quorum`); shallow-clone and show `HEAD` with the redirect line
visible; recompute the proof; verify one signed event; remove the source from
eligibility; clone again and compare; restore. If a step fails, stop and use
the incident plan. Every frame needs a timestamp and commit; never splice runs.

### Incident plan

| Incident | Immediate action |
| --- | --- |
| Clone fails on every mirror | Say clone is down; stop the demo; probe each core node directly; record onset and recovery |
| Status green while Git fails | Use timestamped independent probes |
| Install, checksum or signature failure | Stop recommending the installer; capture hashes and the exact error |
| macOS or SmartScreen questions | State the signing status; link the manifest and support matrix |
| Security report | Private channel only |
| Heavy traffic or abuse | Use the relay limits; protect control endpoints |
| Wrong claim found live | Correct the surface and link evidence |

The [incident tabletop](incident-tabletop-2026-09-16.md) walked this plan,
listed the exact controls, and recorded the gaps: no rate limit on anonymous
Git reads, no public incident record, and one person holding every control.

## 9. HN compliance gate

- The submitter must personally attest they built the project and can discuss
  it, and confirm their account can post a Show HN.
- The link must be the runnable project, not a waitlist or announcement.
- The core demo needs no signup, payment or credential.
- Nobody may be asked to submit, upvote, comment, or coordinate engagement.
- A human writes and posts every submission and comment.

## 10. Verdict and ordered blockers

Verdict: **blocked**. "Dry-run ready" needs a full rehearsal with the released
artifact and a visitor-runnable fixture whose proof reads `quorum`. "Ready"
also requires all four launch gates below.

<!-- launch-gates:start -->
| Gate | Acceptance evidence | State 2026-09-30 | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Second independent operator | `availability.proof == "quorum"` for `forkmesh/forkmesh` and `explain` exits 0, with the second copy on infrastructure and an account the current operator does not control | Not met: 3 copies, 1 operator | Mirror operations |
| Launch blockers closed | Every P0 row below closed with its evidence | Not met | Row owners |
| Try-it path verified | Dated show-path transcript from a clean environment plus one fresh Linux install, in launch week | Not met | Quality; launch owner |
| Human staffed and eligible | Poster confirms eligibility and authorship and names 24-hour thread and incident cover | Not met | Launch owner |
<!-- launch-gates:end -->

A second operator runs the headless mirror node (`install.sh` in direct-HTTPS
mode, see [mirror node](../operations/mirror-node.md)) under their own account,
links it within the link-code window, and carries every ref the cores carry.

### Tracked metrics

Re-measured every cycle; none gates the launch.

<!-- launch-goal-targets:start -->
| Target | Measure | Baseline 2026-09-30 | Gap | Evidence class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Users | NodeInfo `usage.users.total` at `/nodeinfo/2.1` | 235 | Not a gate | Deployed observation |
| Open issues | Files under `.forkmesh/issues/open/` on `main` | 6, all readiness blockers | Only P0 issues gate | Repository evidence |
| Open tasks | Organization tasks in `/api/tasks` not `done` | 81 | Not a gate | Deployed observation |
| Ecosystem listings | Published projects at `/api/ecosystem` | 471 | Third-party listings, never evidence of users or adoption | Deployed observation |
<!-- launch-goal-targets:end -->

NodeInfo counts every account row, including unverified ones; quote which
count you mean.

| Priority | Blocker | Acceptance evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Flagship below trusted quorum | Public proof reads `quorum` with two independent operators |
| P0 | No visitor-runnable failover proof or public collaboration log | Disposable public fixture; same `HEAD` before and after source removal; committed log passing `verify_collaboration.py --require-complete` |
| P0 | Show HN eligibility unknown; no thread cover | Human confirms eligibility and names cover |
| P1 | No clean-machine install log | Retained transcripts with hashes, first run, gate, Stop work, uninstall and dialog text |
| P1 | No status history or external Git-path probe log | 24-hour external probe log matched by status samples |
| P1 | Host-mode agents inherit secrets; no egress policy; no hard dollar cap | Environment allowlist for host launches, or quote the known gaps |
| P1 | Incident response rehearsed only on paper | Git-path rate limit; tabletop repeated with two responders |
| P2 | Page metadata says "decentralized" while the proof shows one operator | Remove the keyword or reach `quorum` |

The highest-leverage step is the first P0: a second independent operator turns
the product's own proof from "high risk" to `quorum`.

pages.markdown:
# Mentions and username suggestions

You never have to type a ForkMesh username from memory. Wherever you mention
someone or enter a username, ForkMesh suggests matching accounts as you type,
and every name and `@mention` you see opens that person's profile.

## @mentions

Type `@` and the first letters of a name. A short list of matching people
appears at the cursor:

- **Chat** (the `/chat` page and the dashboard chat panel): people in the
  room and the chat directory first, then anyone on ForkMesh.
- **Issues, pull requests, discussions and releases**: people already on that
  issue or pull request first (author, commenters, assignees, reviewers), then
  the repository's contributors, then anyone on ForkMesh.

Use the arrow keys and Enter or Tab to pick a name, or tap it on a phone.
Escape closes the list.

Mentioning someone in an issue or pull request pings them and subscribes them
to the thread. They can press **Unsubscribe** on the issue to stop hearing
about it, and a later mention does not subscribe them again.

Text that looks like a mention is left alone inside code, inside links and
web addresses (`https://x.social/@bob`), and in email addresses.

## Username fields

On the web, these fields suggest accounts as you type:

| Where | Field |
| --- | --- |
| Chat, channel settings, Members | The invite field; people already in the channel are not suggested |
| Chat, New channel | The members list: separate names with commas, and each name you add is left out of the next suggestions |
| Repository settings, Collaborators | The collaborator name; current collaborators are not suggested |
| Security advisory | The credit and collaborator name |

Your own name is never suggested. Prefix matches come first, then names that
contain what you typed. When the only suggestion is exactly what you typed,
the list hides so Enter submits the form.

The desktop app's invite dialogs search people too, and DJ Studio suggests
names when you invite people to a jam ([DJ Studio jams](dj-studio.md)). The
phone apps have no channel invite field.

## Profile links

Every account name and every `@mention` links to that person's profile at
`/@name`: in issues, pull requests, discussions, notes, tasks, chat, commit
lists, notification emails and more. In the phone apps a tap opens the
profile inside the app. The desktop app opens its own profile card when it
knows the person, and the web profile otherwise.

Some names stay plain text on purpose:

- bots, agents and system names such as Actions, runners and mirror nodes;
- Discord senders and fediverse authors, whose display names could match the
  wrong ForkMesh account;
- commit authors whose Git name is not a ForkMesh account;
- private profiles, accounts that do not exist, and names inside a row that
  is already a link.

Related: [Hosted repositories](hosted-repositories.md) and
[ForkMesh apps](apps.md).

pages.markdown:
# Mirror goals

A repository can set a goal of healthy copies kept elsewhere ("we want 10
healthy mirrors") and list the copies people run. This page explains the
**Mirrors** card for readers and maintainers, how to run a mirror, and how the
feature is built. How the ForkMesh mirror fleet works is on
[Mirroring](mirroring.md); why independent copies matter is on
[Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md).

An instance admin turns this on with the **Mirror goal** plugin (admin
console, Plugins). It is off until then.

A project that could be blocked or taken down survives if copies of it are
kept in many places. A repository page can show how many copies are running
and how healthy they are, in the **Mirrors** card at the bottom of the right
rail: "3 / 10 healthy" with a progress bar, then one row per copy with a
green, yellow or red dot.

- **This instance** and, for a repository synced from GitHub, Gitea or
  Forgejo, **the original** are always listed.
- **Mirrors people run** are added with **Add a mirror**. Anyone signed in can
  list a copy they run; it is checked about every 15 minutes.
- **Green** means the copy answered and has a commit this repository had in
  the last day. **Yellow** means it answered but is behind or different, or
  has not answered for a day. **Red** means it could not be reached twice in a
  row, or never. Grey means not checked yet, or an address that is listed but
  not checked (git://, ssh, .onion).

The goal is set by the repository's maintainers (the owner, an organization
maintainer or admin, or an instance administrator) with **Set target**. A goal
of 0 turns the count off.

Every repository has a page that explains all of this step by step, with the
live count: `https://<instance>/<owner>/<repository>/mirror` (for the
example forum, `https://forum.example.org/example/forum/mirror`).
While a repository is below its goal, its home page, issue list, lite pages
and feeds ask readers to help and link there.

## Run a mirror

```sh
git clone --mirror https://<instance>/<owner>/<repository>.git
cd <repository>.git && git update-server-info
```

Refresh it every 15 minutes, for example with cron:

```
*/15 * * * * cd /srv/<repository>.git && git remote update --prune && git update-server-info
```

Serve the folder over HTTPS with any web server (Git's "dumb HTTP" needs only
static files), or push it to another forge, then list its `https://` address
with **Add a mirror**. A repository synced with [forge sync](forge-sync.md)
keeps its issues in `.forkmesh/issues`, so the clone carries the whole forum,
not only the code. To serve it with issues, pull requests and a web page,
[start your own ForkMesh instance](https://forkmesh.com/start) and import the
clone.

Checking a mirror reads only its list of branches (`info/refs`); nothing is
loaded from it in visitors' browsers.

## How it is built

It is the `mirror-quota` instance plugin, `OPT_IN`: off on an instance until
an admin turns it on under Plugins, and off on forkmesh.com unless
`FORKMESH_CORE_PLUGINS` names it. While it is off there is no card, no
`/<owner>/<repo>/mirror` page, no call for mirrors on the feeds, lite pages or
issue list, the cron phase does nothing, and `/api/repo/<o>/<r>/mirror-quota`
answers 404 (`plugin_on`, from `instance_features.enabled_ids`).

The example instance `forum.example.org` mirrors `github.com/example/forum`
into `example/forum` with [forge sync](forge-sync.md) and asks for 10 mirrors
so the forum survives a takedown of either site. The issues are committed
under `.forkmesh/issues`, so a plain `git clone --mirror` carries the whole
forum.

Code: `app/src/mirror_quota.py` (API, health rules, cron job),
`app/public/dashboard/js/09-mirror-quota.js` (card and dialog),
`app/host/forkmesh_host/repo_ssr_mirrors.py` (the same card in the first
view). Tests: `app/tests/test_mirror_quota.py`,
`app/tests/host/test_repo_ssr_mirrors.py`.

### What is counted

These are not the ForkMesh mirror fleet
([mirroring](mirroring.md)). The Mirrors tab and the "Direct
access" list (`GET /api/repo/<o>/<r>/mirrors`) are ForkMesh nodes that serve
the repository with signed proofs and are routed to; on an instance they are
hidden because one node serves everything
([instances](operations/instances.md#dashboard-on-an-instance)). The quota counts
plain git copies anywhere, which the instance never routes to: it only checks
that they answer and are current.

The card's rows:

- **This instance**, built in and always green while it serves the page.
- **The original**, built in, when the repository carries
  `.forkmesh/forge-source.json` (`forkmesh-forge-source-v1`, written by
  `tools/forge_sync.py`): "GitHub (original)" for `provider: github`
  (`https://github.com/<repository>`), "<host> (original)" for Gitea or
  Forgejo (`baseUrl`). The file is read from the repository's own raw route at
  most every six hours; a failed read keeps the last answer and is retried
  after 30 minutes, and a missing file removes the row.
- **Registered mirrors**, stored in the database.

"healthy" is the number of green rows, built-in rows included, so
"3 / 10 healthy" with the instance and GitHub green means one external copy is
healthy.

### Storage

Migration `0283_repo_mirror_quota.sql`:

- `repo_mirror_quota` (`repo_bi` = the repository's `key_bi`, `target`,
  `next_check_at`, `updated_at`, `data`). `data` is encrypted (`encrypt_row`)
  and holds the storing owner and name, the repository's default-branch heads
  of the last 24 hours (`heads`: commit, first and last seen, at most 200),
  the parsed forge source and its last check. A row exists once a goal is set
  or a mirror is added.
- `repo_mirror_registry` (`repo_bi`, `mirror_id`, `added_by_bi`,
  `created_at`, `next_check_at`, `data`). `mirror_id` is the first 16 hex
  digits of SHA-256 of host plus lowercase path without `.git`, so the https,
  git:// and ssh forms of one copy are one row. `data` is encrypted: `url`,
  `host`, `scheme`, `checkable`, `label`, `kind`, `addedBy` and `check`
  (`lastCheck {at, ok, headCommit, error, latencyMs}`, `lastOkAt`,
  `lastOkHead`, `failures`, `checks`).

Both tables are in `_REPO_SCOPED_TABLES` (purged with the repository) and in
`tools/next_rekey.py` (`BI_COLUMNS`, `CIPHER_COLUMNS`); see
[rekey](operations/rekey.md).

### API

`/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirror-quota`, routed from the
`REPO_API_PREFIX_RE` block in `app/src/app_runtime.py` after the organization
alias rewrite. Public repositories only: a private or unknown repository
answers 404 to every method.

- `GET` → `{ok, target, healthy, total, registered, max, maxTarget, cloneUrl,
  mirrors: [{id, label, kind, url, host, builtin, status, statusLabel,
  lastCheck, addedBy, addedAt, checkable}]}`. Anonymous answers are
  `public, max-age=30, stale-while-revalidate=60`; a signed-in request also
  gets `viewer {signedIn, name, canSetTarget, canAdd}` and per-row
  `canRemove`, and is `private, no-store`. Both vary on `authorization,
  cookie`.
- `PUT {target}` sets the goal, 0 to 100 (0 turns it off). Maintainers only.
- `POST {url, label?, kind?}` adds a mirror. Any signed-in account. 201 with
  the new payload and `added`.
- `DELETE {id}` (or `?id=`) removes one. The account that added it, or a
  maintainer.

Mutations use `_account_session_record`, so a cookie session also needs an
allowed `Origin` (the App's CSRF rule) and a verified email. A maintainer is
the owner of the storing node (`_account_owns_node`), an account with
`maintain` or `admin` on the linked organization repository
(`_org_linked_repo_permission`), or an instance administrator (`_is_admin`).

**Addresses.** `https://host[:port]/path`, `git://host[:port]/path`,
`ssh://[user@]host[:port]/path` or `user@host:path`, at most 300 printable
ASCII characters, a dotted DNS name (no IP literal, no `localhost`, `.local`,
`.internal`, `.lan`, `.home.arpa`, `.test`, `.example`, ...), path characters
`A-Za-z0-9._~-` and `/`, no query, no fragment, no password, and no user name
on https. The instance's own host is refused (`same_instance`), and so is the
original's address. Only https addresses are checked; git://, ssh and
`.onion` / `.i2p` addresses are listed with status `unknown` ("Not checked").
`kind` is inferred from the host (`github.com`, `gitlab.com` or `gitlab.*`,
`codeberg.org`, `forkmesh.com` and its subdomains, `git` for git:// and ssh);
a `kind` sent by the client is used only when the host says nothing.

**Limits.** 100 mirrors per repository, 3 adds per account per minute and 10
per day (counted on `added_by_bi, created_at`; 429 with `Retry-After: 60`).

### Health checks

Cron phase `mirror-quota` runs at minute 3 of every five
(`_cron_due_phases`, `CRON_PHASE_CATALOG`):

1. Up to 4 due `repo_mirror_quota` rows: the repository's catalog record
   gives the current default-branch commit, which is added to `heads`; the
   forge source is reread when six hours old, and the original is checked
   when its jittered 15-minute slot is due. The row is due again in five
   minutes.
2. Up to 6 due `repo_mirror_registry` rows, oldest first, each checked and
   then due again in 15 minutes plus up to 3 minutes of jitter.

The run stops starting checks after 15 seconds and each check gets 10: the
cron tick's 35-second budget (`CRON_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`) is shared with the
other phases. At six checks every five minutes, 18 mirrors keep a 15-minute
cadence; more are checked less often, oldest first. A new mirror is first due
within the 3-minute jitter, so deleting and re-adding a mirror never jumps the
queue, and one account lists at most 3 mirrors of a repository
(`MAX_MIRRORS_PER_ACCOUNT`) so a few accounts cannot take every check slot.
"Healthy" means only that the mirror advertises the current head commit; a
server that replays the ref listing without the objects behind it passes.

The body of a check has its own deadline (`BODY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 10 s from
the first read, checked on every chunk), because the fetch timeout covers only
the headers and a mirror sending one byte at a time would hold the cron tick.

**One check** is `git ls-remote` without git: `GET <url>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`
through the App's `fetch`, so the host's egress guard applies (public
addresses only, every redirect hop re-checked, `*.forkmesh.com` refused
except this instance's own domain). The body is read through a stream reader
and dropped past 4 MiB. Smart-HTTP pkt-lines and the dumb-HTTP `info/refs`
format (`<sha>\t<ref>`) are both parsed; the head is `refs/heads/<default
branch>`, else `HEAD` (or its `symref`).

**Status.**

| Status | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| green | last check reached it and its head is a commit this repository's default branch had in the last 24 hours |
| yellow | reachable but the head is another commit or the branch is missing, or the last success is older than 24 hours |
| red | never reached, or two failed checks in a row |
| unknown | not checked yet, or not checkable |

Status is worked out when the API is read, from the stored check and the
stored heads, so it ages without a write. A single failed check keeps the
previous answer. The original is green when reachable; when the catalog
record carries `upstreamCommit` (the commit this copy last took from it) and
the original's head has differed from it for 24 hours, it is yellow ("Our
copy is behind").

### Overall status

The card's heading dot and progress bar are coloured by `status` in the API
answer (`overall_status` in `app/src/mirror_quota.py`, `mirrorQuotaOverall` in
the dashboard, `overall_status` in `repo_ssr_mirrors.py`): green when the
healthy count reaches the goal, yellow when it reaches at least half of it, red
below half (2 of 10 is red). Every green row counts, including "This instance"
and the original on GitHub, which is one of the mirrors. With no goal the card
is green when anything is healthy.

### Card

`renderRepoMirrorQuotaCard(data, viewer, helpHref)` draws, under a hairline
like the rail's other sections:

- "Mirrors" and "N / goal healthy" (or "N healthy" without a goal), then a
  slim progress bar filled in `success` green when there is a goal.
- Below its goal (a goal set and the overall status not green), a muted line
  "Needs N more mirrors · How to help →" linking to `/<o>/<r>/mirror`
  (`repoMirrorHelpHref`; `repo_ssr_mirrors.card_html(..., help_href)` in the
  first view, from `repo_ssr._about_rail`), the how-to-help page described in
  [feeds-and-lite.md](app/feeds-and-lite.md#asking-for-mirrors).
- One row per copy: a status dot (`bg-success`, `bg-attention`,
  `bg-destructive`, `bg-muted-foreground/40`) with `role="img"` and the word
  (Healthy, Behind, Unreachable, Not checked) as its label, the name as a
  `primary` link for https addresses (new tab, `noopener noreferrer
  nofollow`), and a muted line with the host, the detail and "checked 5
  minutes ago". Nothing is loaded from the mirrors or the original: no
  favicons, no pictures.
- "Add a mirror" (neutral `fm-btn-sm`; the page's green button stays "Create
  fork"). The dialog explains why copies matter, gives
  `git clone --mirror <this repository>.git`, `git update-server-info` and a
  15-minute cron line, says the issues are in `.forkmesh/issues`, links
  `https://forkmesh.com/start` to start an instance, links "Read the full
  guide" to `/<o>/<r>/mirror`, and for a signed-in
  visitor has the address and name fields; a visitor is asked to sign in.
- Maintainers get a number field and "Set target" ("Set a mirror goal" when
  there is none). The adder or a maintainer gets "Remove" on a row, with a
  confirmation.

The card is hidden when there is no goal and no registered mirror, except
for maintainers, who see the goal field. Private repositories have no card.

**First view.** The host micro-caches anonymous `GET .../mirror-quota` like
`/about` (`MICRO_CACHE_RE` in `repo_ssr.py`, 15 s fresh, 5 min stale, a write
through the node drops it) and remembers the last anonymous answer
(`_quota_memo`, `cached_quota`, warmed like `/about`). When it has one, the
first view draws the card with `repo_ssr_mirrors.card_html` at the bottom of
the rail and seeds it as `mirrorQuota` in `forkmesh-repo-ssr`;
`repoMirrorQuotaSection` draws the same markup from that seed, so the rail
does not change when the dashboard takes over, and `loadRepoMirrorQuota`
(from `loadRepoAboutRail`) refreshes it. Without one, both draw an empty
hidden section. The parity test runs the dashboard functions under node and
compares them with the Python port; a markup change goes in both.

### Setting the goal for example/forum

As the instance administrator or an owner/maintainer of the `example`
organization, open `https://forum.example.org/example/forum`, find
"Set a mirror goal" at the bottom of the right rail, enter 10 and press
"Set target". From a shell with a session token:

```sh
curl -X PUT https://forum.example.org/api/repo/example/forum/mirror-quota \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FORKMESH_SESSION" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"target": 10}'
```

The first cron run after that (within five minutes) reads the forge source and
adds the "GitHub (original)" row.

pages.title: Offline and low-bandwidth sync
pages.description: tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py moves a repository over removable media or an unreliable, metered link. It exports refs (and with them the signed .forkmesh/ collaboration records)…
pages.markdown:
# Offline and low-bandwidth sync

`tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py` moves a repository over removable media or an
unreliable, metered link. It **exports** refs (and with them the signed
`.forkmesh/` collaboration records) to a directory signed with an Ed25519 key,
**fetches** that directory in verified, resumable chunks, **imports** it in one
ref transaction, and **rolls back** any import.
See also [Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md) and
[Mirroring](mirroring.md).

Formats: manifest `forkmesh-offline-media-v1` inside the signed envelope
`forkmesh-offline-media-signed-v1`; checkpoint
`forkmesh-offline-transfer-checkpoint-v1`; import journal
`forkmesh-offline-import-journal-v1`; replica advertisement
`forkmesh-replica-scope-v1`.

## Start here: carry a repository on a USB stick

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen ~/.forkmesh-offline.key   # prints the public key
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export ~/src/project /media/usb/export-1 --signing-key ~/.forkmesh-offline.key
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify /media/usb/export-1 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import /media/usb/export-1 ~/src/project --trusted-key <public key>
```

Share the public key over a trusted channel. A key that starts with `-` goes
after an equals sign: `--trusted-key=-Ab…`. `export --since <earlier export>`
writes an incremental export listing its `prerequisites` and `previousExport`;
import refuses it until the base has been imported.

## Fetch over a link that keeps dropping

```sh
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py fetch https://files.example.org/export-1/ ./incoming \
  --rate 64k --budget 20M --schedule 22:00-06:00 --trusted-key <public key>
tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py status ./incoming
```

The source is any static HTTP host that honours `Range`, or a local directory.
The signed manifest is fetched and verified once. Chunks resume from the first
missing byte and count only after their SHA-256 matches the manifest; a chunk
failing 3 times stops the fetch. The bundle is assembled only when every chunk
and the whole-file digest verify. Retries back off; `--retries N` failures
without progress pause with `link_down`; Ctrl-C pauses with `cancelled`;
`--budget` pauses with `budget_exhausted`; `--schedule` windows pause with
`outside_schedule` (`--wait` sleeps instead); `--restart` discards the
checkpoint. `status` reads only the local checkpoint and reports remaining
bytes and an ETA; `fetch --json` adds transfer counters.

## Limited exports

| Export option | Limitation code |
| --- | --- |
| `--metadata-only` | `metadata_only` |
| `--path PATH` | `path_filter` |
| `--defer-blobs-over SIZE` | `deferred_large_objects` |
| `--ref GLOB` | `branch_filter` |
| _(detected on import)_ | `missing_objects` |

The signed manifest advertises a replica scope of `full`, `filtered` or
`metadata-only`; `verify` recomputes it and fails an overclaiming export. Import
needs `--allow-limited` for a limited export and stores left-out contents as a
Git partial clone. `forkmesh_offline_sync.py replica REPO` prints what a
repository may advertise. The [availability proof](availability-proof.md)
treats any limited replica as `limited_replica` and never counts it toward a
quorum.

## Import, reconciliation, and rollback

Import verifies signature, trusted key, manifest, digests, scope, object format
and prerequisites before writing anything, then decides each ref:

| Decision | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `create` | Ref created. |
| `fast_forward` | Ref moved forward. |
| `unchanged` | Nothing. |
| `local_ahead` | Local kept. |
| `conflict` | Local kept; incoming saved under `refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/`. |
| `checked_out` | Local kept; incoming saved aside for `git merge --ff-only`. |

Refs are never deleted. All changes apply in one `git update-ref --stdin`
transaction after a journal is written to
`<git-dir>/forkmesh-offline/imports/<importId>.json`.
`forkmesh_offline_sync.py rollback REPO IMPORT_ID` reverses it only if every ref
still holds the imported value.

Signing is Ed25519 over `forkmesh-offline-media-v1\n` plus the canonical
manifest's SHA-256; verification is pure Python. Unpinned signers need
`--allow-unpinned`. `--telemetry FILE` appends one count-only
`forkmesh-offline-telemetry-v1` line per run, with no names, URLs, refs or keys.

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error or unreadable input. |
| `3` | Verification, integrity, or missing-object failure; nothing changed. |
| `4` | Paused with the checkpoint kept; re-run to resume. |
| `5` | Imported, with conflicts saved aside. |

Tests: `app/tests/test_offline_sync.py` (quality gate `offline-sync-conformance`).

pages.title: Monthly outcome review
pages.description: Roadmap decisions use the KPIs in the versioned outcome metric dictionary, which defines each metric's numerator, denominator, window, privacy class, consent, retention, minimum…
pages.markdown:
# Monthly outcome review

Roadmap decisions use the KPIs in the versioned
[outcome metric dictionary](outcome-metrics.json), which defines each metric's
numerator, denominator, window, privacy class, consent, retention, minimum cell
size, freshness, coverage, baseline, target and source. This page is the monthly
record template; the [weekly scorecard](activation-revenue-scorecard.md) covers
`weekly` metrics. Baselines stay `unmeasured` and targets `to-be-set` until a
recorded review adopts them.

## Privacy rules

Measurement must never become required surveillance.

- Product analytics is opt-in. Other KPIs use operational records, closed
  ledgers, synthetic probes or voluntary operator registrations.
- A self-hosted node never has to report anything. Such KPIs are `lower-bound`.
- Observation files carry counts and segment labels only; the review tool
  rejects identifier fields and any email or IPv4 value.
- Segments below `minimumCellSize` are suppressed; if only one is suppressed,
  the next smallest is suppressed too.
- Exports built only for a monthly KPI are deleted once the review is recorded.
- A record never quotes a person, repository, pull, ticket, or customer.

## Prepare the review

```sh
python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py validate-dictionary
python3 tools/outcome_metrics.py review --input /path/to/month.json
```

Collect each source to exhaustion and record source and collected totals:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-outcome-observations-v1",
  "dictionarySchema": "forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2",
  "dictionaryVersion": 2,
  "cadence": "monthly",
  "periodStart": "2026-09-01T00:00:00Z",
  "periodEnd": "2026-10-01T00:00:00Z",
  "generatedAt": "2026-10-03T09:00:00Z",
  "observations": [
    {
      "metric": "repository_availability",
      "numerator": 1293120,
      "denominator": 1296000,
      "sourceTotal": 30,
      "collectedTotal": 30,
      "continuationExhausted": true,
      "coverage": 1.0,
      "dataCutAt": "2026-10-01T01:00:00Z",
      "segments": [{ "label": "clone", "value": 646560 }]
    }
  ]
}
```

A metric without an observation is `UNKNOWN`, never zero. Data older than
`freshnessHours` is `stale`. Confidence:

| Confidence | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `high` | Reconciled, exhausted, fresh, coverage at least 0.95, full coverage class |
| `medium` | Reconciled and fresh, partial coverage or class |
| `low` | Reconciled but stale, or coverage below 0.5 (`PARTIAL`) |
| `unknown` | Missing, unreconciled, not exhausted, or cut early (`UNKNOWN`) |

Before circulating, reconcile billing metrics with
`python3 tools/unit_economics.py report`, operations metrics with the status
history, and attach the month's Git conformance report. A failed sample makes
the metric `UNKNOWN`.

## Copy for each month

Store records as `docs/strategy/outcome-reviews/YYYY-MM.md`, aggregates only.

```text
Month: YYYY-MM
Dictionary: forkmesh-outcome-metric-dictionary-v2 / version 2
Data cuts: hosted=<ts>; analytics=<ts>; finance=<ts>; synthetic=<ts>
Quality state: COMPLETE | PARTIAL | UNKNOWN
```

| Stage | Metric id | Value | Baseline | Target | Freshness | Confidence | Coverage |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Acquisition | `landing_activation` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `anonymous_clone` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `signup` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `first_mirror` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `managed_service_qualification` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `paid_conversion` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Revenue | `retention` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `feature_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `support_load` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `infrastructure_cost` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Sustainability | `gross_margin` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Activation | `successful_migration` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `first_contribution` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Community | `active_maintainers` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Product | `hosted_service_adoption` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `repository_availability` |  |  |  |  |  |  |
| Availability | `independent_mirror_nodes` |  |  |  |  |  |  |

```text
Decisions:
- <decision> — evidence: <metric ids> — revisit: YYYY-MM
Experiments:
- <hypothesis> — metric: <id> — guardrail: <id> — result: <pending|kept|reverted>
Roadmap changes:
- <milestone> — <added|reprioritized|dropped> — because: <metric ids>
```

Definitions change only between periods: update `outcome-metrics.json`,
increment `version`, and never rewrite earlier records. A missing or
unreconciled source makes the metric `UNKNOWN` for the period; never carry a
prior value forward or reconstruct history by hand.

Tests: `app/tests/test_outcome_metrics.py`.

pages.title: Relay data retention and deletion
pages.description: What the hosted relay behind forkmesh.com, app.forkmesh.com and world.forkmesh.com stores, how long, and what deletes it. Git objects in repositories published from desktops and…
pages.markdown:
# Relay data retention and deletion

What the hosted relay behind `forkmesh.com`, `app.forkmesh.com` and
`world.forkmesh.com` stores, how long, and what deletes it. Git objects in
repositories published from desktops and mirror nodes are not relay data and
the relay cannot delete them. "Until deleted" means no automatic limit;
**missing proof** marks a gap.

## Where the relay runs

The application code (`app/src/`) runs under `app/host/` on self-hosted core
nodes (`deploy/fleet.toml`); see [Architecture and availability](architecture.md).
The binding names come from `app/wrangler.toml`, and
`app/host/forkmesh_host/env.py` maps each to a local implementation on the
cores. The forkmesh.com website forwards visitor IP and country to the app in
a signed header.

## Live stores

| Store | Holds | Retention / deletion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| rqlite database (`DB`) | Accounts, catalog, inboxes, chat backlog, status, analytics, memberships, package data, durable-object storage; full copy on every core node | Per table below |
| KV `REPOSITORY_METADATA` | Cached repository-page JSON per node, not replicated or backed up | No expiry, no delete (**missing proof**) |
| `ForkMeshRoom`, `ForkMeshNoteRoom`, `ForkMeshWorld`, `ForkMeshOfficeRoom` | Sockets and live presence in memory | Socket lifetime |
| `ForkMeshNodes`, `ForkMeshCronWatchdog`, `ForkMeshCronRunner`, `ForkMeshDiscordGate` | Push sockets, commit targets, cron progress, rate buckets (`do_storage`, `do_alarms`) | Overwritten or expired |
| Queue `forkmesh-notification-email` | Wake-up naming a recipient, in memory | Until delivered (3 retries) |
| Response cache | Public responses, ≤ 8 MiB per node | `Cache-Control` lifetime |
| Hosted Git repositories | Full copy per node | Removal moves to `.trash`; emptied by hand only |

## Database tables (rqlite)

| Data family | Retention | Deletion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Accounts, devices, SSH keys, encryption keys | Until deleted; stale devices 60 days | Account delete |
| Sessions | Expired and revoked sessions pruned on login | Sign out; account delete |
| Repository catalog, health, inboxes, webhooks, provider mirrors, Internet Archive backups | Until deleted; outboxes until delivered or retries exhausted | Repository or account delete |
| Chat backlog (encrypted) | 7 days, ≤ 500 messages and 16 MiB per room; DMs removed on recipient ack | Sweep; message, room or account delete |
| Notifications | 90 days, ≤ 500 per recipient | Account delete |
| Email delivery records | 90 days | Expiry |
| Security audit log | 365 days | Expiry |
| Error and diagnostic logs | Newest 5,000 rows each | Row cap |
| Site analytics | 400 days; IP digest 24 hours | Privacy-page delete; daily sweep |
| Status history, cron ticks, presence, throttles | Hours to 30 days | Expiry |
| Account-scoped packages | Until deleted | Account delete runs each package's `purge_account_data` |
| Organization-scoped packages | Until deleted | Uninstall or organization delete (`app/src/plugin_data.py`) |
| Notes, calendar, app installs, reviews, push tokens, suppressions, IDS records, bug reports, ledger rows | Until deleted | **Missing proof:** account delete leaves them |

Account deletion (`_delete_account_namespace` in `app/src/entry.py`) removes the
account's repositories and repository-scoped rows, identity and session rows,
notifications, follows, referrals, stars, grants, ads, package rows and direct
conversations, then republishes the public catalog.

## Backups and copies

| Copy | Retention |
| --- | --- |
| Nightly encrypted rqlite backups (`tools/next_backup.py`) | Last 7 daily and 4 weekly; a restore resurrects deleted rows unless deletions are replayed |
| rqlite Raft log and snapshots | rqlite truncation defaults |
| Archives from the previous hosting stack | **Missing proof:** no retention or deletion step |
| Hosted repository `.trash` | Until emptied by hand |

## Logs

| Log | Retention |
| --- | --- |
| Core node journal (errors, request counts, statement text without values, mail delivery lines) | ≤ 64 MiB per node (`journald.conf`), rotated by size |
| Reverse-proxy access log (masked client addresses, no headers) | In the journal |
| Mail event spool | 3 days |
| forkmesh.com website Worker logs (5% sample) | Cloudflare plan default |

## Outside processors

The hosting provider (all stores), the DNS and website provider, recipients' mail
servers, optional error reporting (redacted), membership provider, AI providers
used by runner jobs, webhook receivers, food-data lookups (no account id), push
notification service (token and fixed alert only), chat bridge, ActivityPub
peers, and opt-in product analytics. Each keeps data under its own policy.
Details: [external dependency map](external-dependency-map.md).

## Known gaps

1. No user data export API.
2. Account deletion leaves the rows marked **missing proof** above.
3. `REPOSITORY_METADATA` entries never expire.
4. No step replays deletions after a backup restore.
5. Archives from the previous stack have no retention policy.
6. `.trash` is emptied only by hand.

Update this page with any change to bindings, `env.py`, backup retention, a
retention sweep, or `_delete_account_namespace`.

pages.title: Searchable public repository index
pages.description: The public index finds active projects that anyone can clone without an account. app/src/repository_index.py implements exactly this methodology.
pages.markdown:
# Searchable public repository index

The public index finds active projects that anyone can clone without an
account. `app/src/repository_index.py` implements exactly this methodology.

## Endpoint

`GET /api/repositories/search` (anonymous; public catalog data only; cacheable
30 s). Parameters: `q` (up to 8 words, all must match), `view`, `limit` (1–50,
default 20), `cursor`, `language`, `topic`, `owner`, `cloneable=1`. Errors are
`400` (`unknown_view`, `relevance_requires_query`, `invalid_limit`,
`invalid_cloneable`, `invalid_cursor`, `cursor_query_mismatch`) or
`503 catalog_unavailable`.

Each result has `identity` (the root-commit repository URN, see
[dependency workflows](dependency-workflows.md)), `clone` (a stock `git clone`
command), `maintainer` (key-signed catalog record), `availability`, and the
`ranking` inputs. Responses also give `total`, `facets`, `withheld`,
`freshness` and `budgets`.

## Budgets

Freshness 6 minutes (catalog snapshot age, reported per response); latency
250 ms for ranking a full catalog; page size 50 (larger limits are rejected).

## Determinism and pagination

The sort key always ends in the unique `owner/name`. `nextCursor` is a keyset
cursor bound to the query; walking all pages returns each match once, and it
is `null` on the last page.

## Views

- **relevance**: per-word integer scores for name, owner, topic, language and description.
- **updated**: latest head-commit time.
- **trending**: commits and merges over 4 weeks, each week capped at 50, plus
  5 points per independent mirror (at most 8 mirrors count).
- **new**: signed hosted-since time.
- **discussions**: open discussions, pull requests and issues, each capped at 500.

Trending and discussions skip records older than 14 days and zero scores.

## Anti-manipulation rules

Only signed public records appear; flagged, blocked or private ones are
withheld. Each repository is one result; only mirrors run by other accounts
count; identical heads collapse into `duplicates`; old records cannot be
replayed; heartbeats and self-reported traffic never rank; timestamps more
than 5 minutes in the future are ignored.
