pages.title: Managed-services pricing interview register
pages.description: Part of Research.
pages.markdown:
# Managed-services pricing interview register

Part of [Research](README.md).

This register is the evidence gate for the managed-services plan in
`www/public/business-model.json`. It contains no customer research as of
2026-08-20.
The plans themselves are on the [business model](../business-model.md) page.

## Current decision

- Validation state: **not validated**
- Qualifying decision-maker interviews: **0**
- Managed checkout: **disabled**
- Price shown publicly: **none**
- Next decision: retain the research preview until the minimum cohort passes

No issue comment, contributor offer, analytics event, support ticket,
competitor price, internal opinion, or synthetic response is a pricing
interview. This explicit zero is preferable to inventing demand.

## Hypotheses to test

These are hypotheses, not findings:

| Field | Initial hypothesis |
| --- | --- |
| Economic buyer | Engineering manager, platform lead, or maintainer who owns hosting/reliability toil |
| Budget owner | Engineering infrastructure, developer productivity, or support/operations budget |
| Candidate budget | Must be elicited; no band has been validated |
| Paid job 1 | Operate reliable mirrors and recovery without maintainer toil |
| Paid job 2 | Administer a team, policy, identity, and audit boundary |
| Paid job 3 | Provide accountable migration, incident, and priority support |
| Secondary jobs | Managed indexing/discovery and bounded hosted runners |

## Minimum validation rule

Run at least five qualifying interviews with people who control or directly
recommend a relevant budget, spanning at least three organizations and two
organization-size bands. A result may move to `validated` only when:

1. at least three respondents name the same buyer role and an existing budget
   owner or purchasing path;
2. at least three provide a credible current spend, approved range, or
   budget-comparison anchor rather than a hypothetical willingness-to-pay;
3. each of the published top three paid jobs is independently selected in at
   least three interviews, or the public ordering is revised to match the
   observed ranking; and
4. every contradictory result and every resulting plan, unit, allowance, price,
   support, or positioning revision is logged below.

The facilitator must not pitch a price before learning the current process,
failure cost, buyer, and budget. Interest without authority is demand context,
not buyer validation.

## Interview record template

Copy one record per real interview. Store detailed notes only in the consented
research location and link them; do not commit names, emails, private project
names, recordings, or confidential budgets to this public repository.

```text
Interview id: PI-YYYY-NNN
Date (UTC):
Facilitator:
Consented evidence link:
Respondent role:
Organization-size band: 1-10 / 11-50 / 51-250 / 251+
Decision authority: buyer / recommender / user-only
Current workaround and spend anchor:
Budget owner and purchasing path:
Highest-cost failure or toil:
Top paid jobs, ranked:
Acceptable unit and why:
Budget range or comparison anchor:
Objections / portability concern:
Would enter bounded trial now: yes / no, with condition
Public-contract revision required:
Qualified: yes / no, with reason
```

## Revision log

| Version | Date | Evidence | Revision | Validation effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Before 2026-08-20 | Legacy marketing and membership implementation | Mixed free software, $5 Supporter and $10 Pro memberships, hosted workflows, and custom enterprise copy without a portable entitlement matrix or cost gate. | Not validated |
| 1 | 2026-08-20 | Product contract #476 plus repository capability, privacy, billing, and infrastructure-usage audits; **not customer interviews** | Separated permanent protocol rights, Hosted Free, Pro membership, and managed-service hypotheses; named observable usage units; prohibited unlimited variable-cost plans; disabled managed checkout pending evidence. | Still not validated; buyer and budget remain hypotheses |

Future rows must cite the interview ids that caused the revision. A revision
with no customer evidence may improve clarity or safety but cannot advance the
validation state. When the minimum cohort qualifies, add only its non-identifying
`PI-YYYY-NNN` ids to `pricing-interviews.json`, record a new revision row, and
set `validatedRevision` to that row's version. Counts without those ids and a
new documented revision fail the automated contract.

pages.title: Start your own instance from a settings file
pages.description: The Start your own instance page can be filled from one zip holding a settings .json file and a logo. Examples: start-config.example.zip and start-config.example.json. The page…
pages.markdown:
# Start your own instance from a settings file

The [Start your own instance](https://app.forkmesh.com/start) page can be
filled from one zip holding a settings `.json` file and a logo. Examples:
[start-config.example.zip](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.zip)
and [start-config.example.json](https://app.forkmesh.com/start-config.example.json).
The page and installer are described in
[Start your own instance](start-your-own-instance.md); the overall picture is on
[Self-hosting](self-hosting.md).

## The zip

Exactly one `.json` file; the logo is the image named by `logo`, or the only
image. Logo: PNG, JPEG, WebP or SVG up to 200 KB; zip up to 1 MB; no password.
Hidden files and `__MACOSX` folders are skipped.

## Settings

Every key is optional; missing keys keep the form's value. Keys starting with
`_` or `$` are notes; unknown keys are listed and skipped.

`theme` is empty (or `default`) for the ForkMesh colours, the id of a ready
theme from the page's theme cards, a colour preset name (`crimson`), or an
object of `#rrggbb` colours per mode, as the page's colour editor builds it:
`{"dark": {"primary": "#f97316"}, "light": {"primary": "#ea580c"}}`.
Tokens you leave out keep the ForkMesh colour.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `projectName`, `theme`, `logo` | Name (up to 40 characters), optional theme, logo file name or data URL |
| `host`, `sshUser`, `port` | Server address, SSH user (default `root`), port (default `22`) |
| `sshPassword`, `sshPrivateKey`, `sshPassphrase` | Password, or a key as one JSON string with `\n` breaks |
| `hostKeyFingerprint` | Optional `SHA256:` fingerprint |
| `domain` | Optional; empty uses a free `sslip.io` address |
| `adminUsername`, `adminEmail`, `adminPassword` | Admin account; password at least 10 characters |
| `adminPath` | Private admin console address, like `/manage-x7k2q9`: `/` then 8 to 64 letters, numbers, `-` or `_`. Empty keeps the one the page made |
| `ownerType`, `ownerName` | `org` or `user`; organization name when `org` |
| `owners` | Up to 20 extra organization owners, each `{"username", "email", "password"}` |
| `mailProvider`, `mailApiKey`, `mailFrom` | `none`, `mailtrap`, `sendgrid` or `mailgun`; key; sender |
| `mailgunDomain`, `mailgunRegion` | Mailgun only; region `us` or `eu` |
| `ownWorld`, `listOnHomepage` | Booleans, default `true` |

## Admin console address

The page makes a fresh random `adminPath` (`/admin-` and 20 random letters
and numbers, from the browser's `crypto.getRandomValues`) every time it opens,
and every example zip or settings file it downloads carries a new one. The
instance serves its admin console only there; `/admin` answers "not found".
Save it with your password: ForkMesh does not store it, and the setup page
shows it only until you leave.

## Privacy

The file contains secrets. The page reads it in the browser only; just the
submitted settings reach ForkMesh, and secret fields are cleared once setup
starts. Delete the file afterwards.

pages.title: Start your own instance
pages.description: A ForkMesh instance is your own Git host on your own server, under your own name: repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, Actions and agents, with your logo, colours and…
pages.markdown:
# Start your own instance

A ForkMesh instance is your own Git host on your own server, under your own
name: repositories, pull requests, issues, chat, Actions and agents, with
your logo, colours and domain. Start one at
[forkmesh.com/start](https://forkmesh.com/start). No ForkMesh account is
needed, and it takes about fifteen minutes.
For every way to run ForkMesh yourself, including a mirror node only, see
[Self-hosting](self-hosting.md).

## What you need

- A fresh server with Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04, x86_64 or arm64, at least
  1 GB RAM and 6 GB free disk, with ports 80 and 443 free.
- SSH access as `root`, or as a user with passwordless `sudo`, by password
  or private key.
- Optional: a domain whose `A` record points at the server. Without one the
  instance gets a free `<ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io` address. A domain behind
  Cloudflare's proxy needs SSL/TLS mode Full (strict).
- Optional: a Mailtrap, SendGrid or Mailgun key, so the instance can send
  sign-up and password emails.

## Three ways to start

1. **Fill in the page.** Six short sections: name, logo and colour theme;
   your server; your address; your admin account and repository owner;
   email; and whether to list the instance on forkmesh.com and give it its
   own World.
2. **Upload a settings file.** Put every answer in one `.json` file, or a zip
   with the file and your logo, and upload it at the top of the page. See
   [Start from a settings file](start-config.md).
3. **Let your coding agent do it.** Copy the prompt from the page into
   Claude Code or another coding agent. It reads the
   [agent guide](https://app.forkmesh.com/forkmesh-agent.md), asks for your
   details and writes the settings file for you. See
   [Working with coding agents](coding-agents.md).

## What happens

ForkMesh connects to your server over SSH, checks the host key and runs the
installer. The page shows each step live: system check, packages, source,
build, configure, database, services, HTTPS, admin and repository. Your SSH
password or key is used once to connect and is never stored; secret fields
are cleared from the page once setup starts. If the connection drops, the
setup keeps running on the server.

When it is done:

- **Sign in within five minutes.** An instance started from the page that
  nobody signs in to removes itself, so an abandoned launch does not leave a
  server running.
- **Save your admin console address.** The page makes a private, random
  address such as `/admin-…`; `/admin` answers "not found". ForkMesh does
  not keep it, and the page shows it only until you leave.
- Your instance hosts its own copy of the platform source at
  `<owner>/forkmesh`.

## Running it yourself

If you would rather no secret passes through forkmesh.com, run the installer
on the server with the same settings file, without the SSH fields. The
installer also needs `domain` (use `<ip-with-dashes>.sslip.io` if you have
none), `publicAddress` (the server's public IP) and `adminPassword`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install-instance.sh -o install-instance.sh
sudo bash install-instance.sh --config forkmesh-instance.json
```

A manual install never removes itself. It joins the forkmesh.com directory
and the World only when you turn that on in the admin console, under
Platform → ForkMesh directory.

## After setup

- **Update** from the admin console (Platform → Update ForkMesh), or with
  `sudo bash install-instance.sh --update`. The new version builds beside
  the running one; data, secrets and the admin account are kept.
- **Update when a pull request is merged.** The console's Update page can
  rebuild the instance each time a pull request is merged into its own
  `<owner>/forkmesh` source. It refuses until that branch is protected, so
  only a change an owner or admin approved can deploy.
- **Branding.** The project name replaces "ForkMesh" across pages and email.
  Pick a ready theme or your own colours at setup; an admin can change the
  theme later under Settings → Instance theme. The "Powered by ForkMesh"
  badge is on by default.
- **Plugins.** Turn optional features on and off in the admin console,
  Platform → Plugins, without a reinstall. Examples: the copyable "fix this
  issue" prompt for coding agents and the Fediverse panels, both on by
  default.
- **Actions.** The installer adds a runner for repository workflows; an
  instance works without it if it fails.
- **Directory and World.** A listed instance appears on the forkmesh.com
  homepage and gets its own place in the ForkMesh World. Either can be
  switched off in the admin console.

Developer details (the API, installer steps, themes, plugins, white label and
limits) are in [docs/operations/instances.md](operations/instances.md).

pages.title: Synchronization status
pages.description: All clients describe synchronization with one model, forkmesh-sync-status-v1. Copies are made by mirrors; see Mirroring.
pages.markdown:
# Synchronization status

All clients describe synchronization with one model, `forkmesh-sync-status-v1`.
Copies are made by mirrors; see [Mirroring](mirroring.md).

| State | Current | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `queued`, `syncing` | no | Waiting or in flight |
| `verified` | yes | Every copy holds the latest signed state, confirmed within an hour |
| `degraded` | yes | Enough copies verified, some offline, behind or rejected |
| `stale` | no | No recent confirmation |
| `conflicted` | no | Copies disagree |
| `paused`, `external-only`, `failed` | no | Paused, only at an external provider, or rejected |

Nothing reports success without a verified copy, and conflict outranks success.
A status holds counts, timestamps and fixed wording only (`verifiedCopies`,
`trustedMirrors`, `lastConfirmedAt`, `lagMs`, `error`, `action`, `summary`), never
node names or raw errors.

Implementations: `app/src/sync_status.py` (API `syncStatus` on
`GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/mirrors`), `desktop/src/SyncStatusModel.h`,
`SyncStatus.swift`, `SyncStatus.kt`, `server/syncstatus.go` and
`tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py explain` (exit 0 current, 3 not, 2 unreadable).
All match `conformance/sync-status/v1/fixture.json`, generated from `model.json`
(`staleAfterMs` 1 hour, `syncDeadlineMs` 15 minutes).

pages.title: Transports and anonymity postures
pages.description: tools/forkmesh_transports.py decides how a device reaches repositories and what it may reveal. A profile lists the device's adapters and one posture; the tool plans a route for a…
pages.markdown:
# Transports and anonymity postures

`tools/forkmesh_transports.py` decides how a device reaches repositories and
what it may reveal. A profile lists the device's adapters and one posture; the
tool plans a route for a URL, runs Git over the first permitted route that
answers (never falling back to a forbidden one), traces the Git process for
leaks in private postures, probes routes, and chooses which local addresses may
be advertised.
The adversaries these postures answer are in the
[threat model](protocol/threat-model.md); see also
[Censorship resilience](censorship-resilience.md).

Formats: profile `forkmesh-transport-profile-v1`, plan
`forkmesh-transport-plan-v1`, health report `forkmesh-transport-health-v1`,
advertisement `forkmesh-transport-advertisement-v1`, telemetry
`forkmesh-transport-telemetry-v1`. Planner vectors:
`conformance/transports/v1/cases.json`.

```json
{"schema": "forkmesh-transport-profile-v1", "posture": "anonymous",
 "adapters": [{"id": "tor", "kind": "proxy", "network": "tor", "socks": "127.0.0.1:9050"}]}
```

## Adapters

| Kind | Carries | Name resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clearnet` | Direct internet connections | System resolver, `standard` posture only |
| `proxy` | SOCKS5; `network` is `tor`, `i2p` or `socks` | By the proxy (`socks5h`); proxy endpoint must be a literal `IP:port` |
| `overlay` | Addresses inside its `cidrs` (WireGuard, Yggdrasil and similar) | None; literal addresses or pinned `hosts` |
| `lan` | Loopback, private, link-local, unique-local | None, except multicast DNS for `.local` |

Adapter fields: `allowPlaintext`, `authenticatedNetwork` (overlay),
`isolateStreams` and `serviceAddress` (proxy), `budgets.latencyMs` (default
2000).

Profile errors, checked in order: `profile_schema`, `unknown_posture`,
`adapters_missing`, `adapter_id_invalid`, `adapter_id_duplicate`,
`unknown_adapter_kind`, `proxy_endpoint_not_literal`, `proxy_network_unknown`,
`overlay_cidr_invalid`, `overlay_cidr_global`, `pinned_host_invalid`,
`budget_invalid`, `posture_has_no_adapter`,
`anonymous_requires_anonymity_network`.

## Postures

| Posture | Adapters | Lookups | Direct fallback | Telemetry | Advertises |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `standard` | all (`lan`, `overlay`, `clearnet`, `proxy`) | system | yes | counts | public, overlay, LAN |
| `private` | `proxy` | by proxy | never | counts | service address only |
| `anonymous` | `proxy` on `tor` or `i2p` | by proxy | never | off | service address only |
| `overlay-only` | `overlay` | none | never | counts | overlay |
| `lan-only` | `lan` | none | never | counts | LAN |

Outside `standard`, Git runs with a scrubbed environment, no system or global
config, no credential helpers or redirects, and redacted logs; `git://` and
`ssh://` go through the tool's relay. A repository config that could reroute
traffic (`insteadOf`, proxies, `core.sshCommand`, includes) is refused with
`repository_config_overrides_route`.

## Route refusals

Per adapter, first match: `adapter_not_permitted`,
`proxy_network_not_permitted`, `destination_requires_anonymity_network`,
`onion_requires_tor`, `i2p_requires_i2p`, `local_destination_via_proxy`,
`destination_outside_overlay`, `destination_outside_lan`, `name_needs_dns`,
`plaintext_via_exit`, `peer_unauthenticated`. Plan-level: `invalid_url`,
`scheme_unsupported` (only `https`, `http`, `ssh`, `git`), `no_permitted_route`.

## States

| State | Label | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `exposed` | Exposed | The trace saw a `dns_query` or `direct_connection` outside the route; wins over all others |
| `unreachable` | Unreachable | No permitted route answered, or the transfer broke |
| `degraded` | Degraded | Reachable with a reason: `failed_over`, `slow`, `intermittent`, `unauthenticated_peer` |
| `anonymous` | Anonymous | `anonymous` posture, healthy, no leak |
| `protected` | Protected | `private`, `overlay-only` or `lan-only`, healthy, no leak |
| `direct` | Direct | `standard` posture, healthy |

Clients display the report's `label`, `tone` and `explanation` verbatim. Leak
tracing uses `strace` on Linux; elsewhere `leakTrace` is `unavailable` and only
the in-process guard applies.

## Commands

```sh
tools/forkmesh_transports.py validate PROFILE
tools/forkmesh_transports.py plan --profile PROFILE URL
tools/forkmesh_transports.py probe --profile PROFILE URL [--report FILE]
tools/forkmesh_transports.py git --profile PROFILE URL [--repo DIR] [--trace auto|required|off] -- clone @URL app
tools/forkmesh_transports.py status REPORT
tools/forkmesh_transports.py advertise --profile PROFILE --address IP...
```

Use `fetch --atomic` so a broken route leaves refs unchanged. Git's own
failures do not trigger failover.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `2` | Usage error, invalid profile, or required tracer missing. |
| `3` | Refused by policy before anything was sent. |
| `4` | Unreachable. |
| `5` | Exposed. |
| `6` | Git failed on a reachable route. |

Tests: `app/tests/test_transports.py` (quality gate `transport-conformance`).
Only Git traffic honours the profile so far.

pages.title: Trust lists
pages.description: A trust list is a signed list of keys its owner vouches for or warns about, each entry scoped to one role and one place (repo:, org: or community:). There is no global list…
pages.markdown:
# Trust lists

A trust list is a signed list of keys its owner vouches for or warns about, each
entry scoped to one role and one place (`repo:`, `org:` or `community:`). There
is no global list; following is local, private and optional, and nothing basic
(read, clone, sign in, push, recover) needs a list. Protocol:
[Scoped community trust lists](design/scoped-trust-lists.md).

Follows can only narrow a list. Included lists count inside the overlap of their
scopes, up to four deep. Disagreements show as conflict until a local override
(`trust`, `distrust`, `ignore`). Distrusted keys may sign an appeal. Lists
should name an offline recovery key; versions last at most 400 days. States are
Active, Recovered, Expired, Revoked, Conflicted and Missing.
`python3 tools/forkmesh_trust_lists.py drill` replays a key-compromise recovery.

Resolvers sharing one set of vectors: `app/src/trust_lists.py`,
`app/public/trust-lists.js`,
`native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/TrustLists.swift`,
`native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/security/TrustLists.kt`
and `desktop/src/TrustLists.cpp`.

pages.title: ForkMesh World community services
pages.description: The shared services of ForkMesh World: the event calendar, the Fediverse directory, shared media rooms, community-reviewed placements and the World song. World keeps this data in…
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh World community services

The shared services of ForkMesh World: the event calendar, the Fediverse
directory, shared media rooms, community-reviewed placements and the World
song. World keeps this data in the database and serves it over HTTPS; the
multiplayer socket carries only presence and movement. Empty or unavailable
data is shown as such, never as demo content. All mutations and denied
attempts write metadata-only entries to `sensitive_audit_log`. How World is
built is on the [World home page](world/README.md).

## UTC community events

`GET /api/world/events[/{id}]` is public and lists unexpired events.
Administrators use `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` (cancel). `startsAt` and
`endsAt` are ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`; events last at most seven days, start
at most two years ahead, and the catalog is capped at 500 rows.

## Fediverse directory

`GET /api/world/fediverse` returns `mastodon`, `lemmy`, `x` and `reddit`
arrays. Administrator writes require `publicOnly`, `consentConfirmed`,
`consentSource` (`instance-operator`, `public-api`, `user-approved`,
`moderator-reviewed`) and a `consentCheckedAt` within the last year. Origins
must be public HTTPS with no credentials, paths, IPs or custom ports.
Relationship entries are accepted only when `public` and `consent` are both
`true`; X and Reddit records are operator attestations with
`oauthVerifiedByForkMesh: false`. No raw IPs, emails or private graphs are
stored. Repository posts and replies are on
[Fediverse digests, mentions and replies](fediverse.md).

## Shared media spaces

`/api/world/media/spaces` and its `items`, `playback`, `stop`, `schedules` and
`roles` sub-routes require a session. The creator owns a space and may grant
moderators; owners and moderators manage playlists, schedules and playback.
The actor always comes from the session.

Playlist items are links to allowlisted provider pages (SomaFM, YouTube,
Vimeo, SoundCloud, Twitch, Internet Archive, PeerTube) with
`termsConfirmed`, `noRebroadcast` and `autoplay: false`; raw media files are
rejected. ForkMesh never fetches or rebroadcasts media, and shared playback
state only coordinates clients.

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Spaces per owner | 5 |
| Items per space | 100 |
| Schedules per space | 50, UTC, at most one year ahead and 24 hours long |
| Moderators per space | 20 |
| Removed items and finished schedules | Purged after 30 days |
| Idle spaces | Archived after 180 days, purged 90 days later by the hourly retention cron |

## Community-reviewed placements

Approval means disclosed public evidence met an instance's current criteria
for a limited period; it is not an endorsement and can be appealed, suspended,
or expire. Criteria are served by `GET /api/world/community-ads/criteria`.
Proposals disclose sponsor, ownership, product, data use, tracking, labor,
accessibility, and impact evidence, with at least two public HTTPS sources.

Voting is one eligible verified account per proposal (active, email-verified,
at least seven days old), never wallet-weighted. Conflicted voters may only
abstain. Approval needs quorum and two-thirds of non-abstaining votes; review
deadlines are at most 180 days.

Each instance is disabled by default and chooses placement contexts and a
public revenue purpose. Placements receive only a coarse page context such as
`town-square` or `repository`; targeting does not use profiles, device or
country data, search terms, wallets, or behavioral history. Responses carry
`tracking: none`. Member text ads are a separate system,
[ForkMesh Ads](operations/ad-network.md); a community placement takes
priority.

Receipts use the `community_ad_revenue` ledger class. They are not user funds,
rewards, or on-chain transfers; the app does not custody money.

## World song

The World entrance sign links to a first-party track published by the project
at <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EsQMZuS6lbE>; it opens in a new tab and no
audio file is bundled or served. All other World sounds are short effects
synthesized locally with the Web Audio API.

pages.title: ActivityPub federation (fediverse interop)
pages.description: The relay joins the ActivityPub network (Mastodon-compatible) with followable actors on its own domain. Digests, mention review and threaded replies are in Fediverse digests…
pages.markdown:
# ActivityPub federation (fediverse interop)

The relay joins the ActivityPub network (Mastodon-compatible) with followable
actors on its own domain. Digests, mention review and threaded replies are in
[Fediverse digests, mentions and replies](../fediverse.md).
Part of [Design decisions](README.md).

| Actor | Handle | Actor URL | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| User profile | `@alice@forkmesh.com` | `/ap/users/alice` | `Person` |
| Repository | `@owner.repo@forkmesh.com` | `/ap/repos/owner/repo` | `Group` |
| Service actor | `@forkmesh.com@forkmesh.com` | `/ap/actor` | `Application` |

User names never contain a dot, so `owner.repo` splits on the first dot.
Handles are lowercase. Only active public accounts and published public
repositories federate.

## What federates

**Outbound.** Verified signed-inbox submissions (issue, pull request and
discussion opens, comments and reviews) are posted as `Create(Note)` by the
repository actor and, when the author is a local account, by the user actor.
Releases and merges are announced through the owner-signed
`POST /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/ap-publish`. Inline `data:` images in a body
(up to 4) are re-served at `/ap/o/{uuid}/media/{n}` and attached as `Image`.

**Inbound.** `Follow` (auto-accepted), `Undo(Follow)`, `Create(Note)` replies
and mentions, and `Delete`. Remote replies are stored as federated comments
(`GET /api/repo/{owner}/{repo}/fedi-comments`) and kept outside the
Ed25519-signed event log, because they can never carry a ForkMesh author
signature.

**Mentions never create issues automatically.** A verified public Note that
mentions a repository actor becomes an encrypted review record. The owner can
edit and explicitly authorize it as an issue-inbox submission; the feed says
`created` only after the owner's node commits the issue. A backlink reply is
sent only with separate consent.

## Wire protocol

- RSA-2048 key per actor, published as `publicKeyPem` (`<actor>#main-key`);
  private keys encrypted at rest.
- draft-cavage HTTP signatures (`rsa-sha256`). Outbound signs
  `(request-target) host date digest content-type`. Inbound requires
  `(request-target)` and `digest`, checks the digest byte for byte, enforces a
  ±12 h date window and requires the `keyId` host to match the actor. Remote
  keys are cached for 24 h with one forced refresh on failure.
- Inbox actor binding (`ap_inbox_handler`): after the HTTP signature verifies,
  the key's actor (the document fetched from `keyId` without its fragment)
  must be the activity's `actor`, or a path under it (GoToSocial publishes
  `<actor>/main-key`), or the inbox answers 401 `actor_mismatch`. A `keyId`
  path with `.`/`..` segments or any percent-encoding is refused
  (`key_actor_mismatch`), because the fetch would normalise
  `victim/../attacker` while the prefix check still saw the victim. A key from
  the same server is not enough: on a shared instance one account could send
  Undo(Follow) or a self-Delete naming another and erase its follows. Lemmy
  moderators sign their own Remove, so Remove needs no exception.
- Discovery: `/.well-known/webfinger`, `/.well-known/nodeinfo` →
  `/nodeinfo/2.1`, and content negotiation on `/@name` and `/@owner.repo`.

The protocol core (documents, signing strings, digests, sanitization) is
`app/src/activitypub.py`, tested by `tests/test_activitypub.py`.

## Delivery

Each publish writes one `ap_outbox` row per destination inbox (shared inbox
preferred). A few are delivered inline; a periodic drain retries the rest with
exponential backoff (5 minutes to 24 hours, 8 attempts; 404/410 drop at once).
Actor keys are created lazily on first lookup.

## Profiles

- Instance and user actors fall back to the instance avatar and banner; a
  repository actor never uses instance branding.
- Repository owners can upload a logo and banner through
  `POST /api/repo/{o}/{r}/about`; otherwise the committed
  `.forkmesh/banner.png` and `logo.png` are used. The About description is the
  actor bio.
- Every actor publishes `PropertyValue` links (canonical page and relay)
  verified by a reciprocal `rel="me"` link.
- A repository actor's `url` is its `/@owner.repo` profile page.
- Saving a profile broadcasts `Update(actor)` to followers.
- Owners can list and delete federated posts (`POST /api/repo/{o}/{r}/ap-posts`);
  a delete sends `Delete(Tombstone)` to followers.

## Administration

Signed admin routes `GET /api/accounts/admin-ap` and
`POST /api/accounts/admin-ap-update` read state and switch federation:
`enable`/`disable` (while disabled every ActivityPub endpoint returns 404) and
`block`/`unblock` a domain, which rejects its activities and purges its
followers, cached actors and queued deliveries, subdomains included.
`PUBLIC_BASE_URL` sets the actor origin for self-hosted relays.

## Limitations

- Local users cannot follow remote accounts; inbound `Like`, `Announce` and
  `Update` are acknowledged and dropped.
- Follower collections expose `totalItems` only.

pages.markdown:
# Conflict-safe signed collaboration objects

Status: normative protocol version 1, part of the
[ForkMesh protocol suite](../protocol/README.md). Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1`. The machine-readable envelope schema is
[`collaboration-event-v1.schema.json`](../../www/public/docs/protocol/collaboration-event-v1.schema.json).
The dependency-free reference fold is `app/src/collaboration.py`; the independent
WebCrypto fold is `app/public/collaboration.js`. Part of
[Design decisions](README.md).

## Invariants

ForkMesh collaboration state is a deterministic projection of an immutable set
of signed events. A relay, mirror, or database may transport and index those
events, but is never authoritative for their meaning. Given the same policy and
event set, implementations MUST produce the same state when events are
permuted, duplicated, delayed, or replayed.

Implementations MUST retain each canonical raw envelope. Materialized fields,
search indexes, counts, and notification views are disposable caches. Invalid
input is retained only in a bounded quarantine/audit channel and MUST NOT enter
the state fold.

## Repository, object, and event identity

A repository identity is:

```text
urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:<sha256(
  "forkmesh-repository-identity-v1\n" || verified repository root
)>
```

The verified root is deployment-specific (for example a signed repository
manifest), but aliases and mutable URLs are not identities.

Every object's first event carries a random 16-byte `objectKey`, base64url
without padding. The object ID is:

```text
urn:forkmesh:collaboration:<family>:sha256:<sha256(
  "forkmesh-collaboration-object-v1\n" || canonical-json({
    repository, family, creator, objectKey, references
  })
)>
```

This binds the repository, family, creator, and immutable references before an
event is signed. For reactions, clients SHOULD derive `objectKey` from subject,
author, and normalized emoji to make one logical reaction idempotent. For
notifications, clients SHOULD derive it from recipient and causing event.

The event ID binds both the signed meaning and its deterministic Ed25519
signature:

```text
signingBytes = utf8("forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1\n") ||
               canonical-json(unsigned envelope)
eventId = "sha256:" || hex(sha256(signingBytes || 0x00 || rawSignature))
```

Ed25519 public keys are raw 32-byte keys and signatures are raw 64-byte values,
both base64url without padding. Schema/domain prefixes are frozen; changed
meaning requires a new version.

## Canonical encoding

The wire envelope is canonical JSON encoded as UTF-8 with no BOM or trailing
newline. Object keys are ASCII, sorted lexicographically; there is no
insignificant whitespace. Strings are NFC-normalized and lone surrogates are
forbidden. Values are objects, arrays, strings, booleans, null, or integers whose
magnitude is at most 2^53-1 (envelope counters are additionally
non-negative); floating point and duplicate object keys are forbidden. Arrays
whose semantics are sets (`parents`, `references`, observed IDs, and set
values) are sorted and duplicate-free. An envelope is at most 1 MiB and JSON
nesting is at most 32 levels, so malformed input cannot force unbounded parser
or canonicalizer work.

A receiver MUST parse with duplicate-key detection, reproduce the exact
canonical bytes, recompute `eventId`, and verify Ed25519 before considering
causality or authorization. Noncanonical encodings fail closed even if they
would parse to the same JSON value.

## Causality and replay defense

`parents` names the events observed when an author made an event. The Lamport
`clock` is zero without parents and otherwise exactly one plus the greatest
parent clock. `issuedAt` is display/audit time only and never decides a winner.

Each signing key allocates a repository-wide monotonically increasing
`sequence`. Gaps and concurrent slots from different keys are valid. Two
different events signed by one key in the same sequence slot are equivocation:
both are excluded and surfaced in audit telemetry. A sequence lower than or
equal to a same-author ancestor is a rollback and is rejected.

Missing-parent events remain pending, with their raw bytes retained. A child of
a rejected event is rejected; it cannot bypass validation by arriving first.
Duplicate event IDs are one logical event and only increment the replay metric.
Repository, object, policy, and schema binding prevents a valid signature from
being replayed into another context.

## References and policy

References are sorted `{relation, family, object}` triples. A comment has one
issue/PR/comment subject; a reaction has one issue/PR/comment/review subject; a
review has one PR subject; a moderation object has one non-notification,
non-moderation subject. References on every event for one object must exactly
match its first event, preventing later retargeting.

Every event binds the SHA-256 ID of a canonical repository policy document:

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1",
  "repository": "urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:…",
  "maintainers": ["<Ed25519 key>"],
  "moderators": ["<Ed25519 key>"],
  "notifiers": ["<Ed25519 key>"]
}
```

The repository trust root pins this document. Version 1 deliberately treats a
policy change as a new collaboration epoch; clients must retain the old epoch
and policy to verify history rather than re-authorizing old events under a new
role list.

| Family | Create | Later mutation / tombstone |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Issue, pull request | Any signed identity | Creator or maintainer |
| Comment, reaction | Any signed identity | Creator; moderation is a separate decision |
| Review | Any signed identity | Creator; maintainer may dismiss via tombstone |
| Label, milestone, board | Maintainer | Maintainer |
| Notification | Recipient or policy notifier | Recipient |
| Moderation decision/resolution | Moderator | Moderator; subject creator may appeal |

Unauthorized events remain auditable but never influence state. Renderers MUST
NOT infer moderator power from an author name, server origin, arrival channel,
or possession of a database row.

Authority comes only from the policy document's keys. Implementations MUST NOT
infer any role from asset ownership or transaction history, and MUST NOT
require a wallet, token, blockchain account, payment, reward, tip, or bounty to
create, fold, authorize, moderate, or govern a collaboration object. Incentive
adapters may read folded state, but folded state never reads them; see
[incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md). Changing this rule is a
breaking protocol change.

## Fold and conflict rules

All families use the same primitives, with family-specific fields and role
rules:

| Family | Scalar registers | Observed-remove sets | Required reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Issue | title, body, status, priority, dueAt | labels, assignees | — |
| Pull request | title, body, status, base, head, mergeCommit | labels, reviewers | — |
| Comment | body | — | subject |
| Label | name, color, description | subjects | — |
| Reaction | emoji (immutable) | — | subject |
| Review | state, body, revision (immutable) | — | pull request |
| Milestone | title, description, status, dueAt | subjects | — |
| Board | name, description, status | items | — |
| Notification | kind/recipient (immutable), status, message | — | optional subject |
| Moderation | decision, reasonCode, note | — | subject |

For a scalar field, discard a candidate only when another write causally
descends it. One remaining value is current. Concurrent candidates with equal
values coalesce; concurrent differing values produce an explicit `conflicts`
entry and no current value. A resolving event names every conflicting head as a
parent and therefore causally dominates them. Timestamp, lexical author order,
or arrival order never silently resolves ambiguity.

`add` gives each set value an `(eventId, value)` tag. `remove` names the exact
ancestor add events it observed. A concurrent add survives. Tombstones use the
same rule: `restore` removes only the ancestor tombstone IDs it names, so an
unobserved concurrent tombstone continues to hide the object. History is never
erased.

## Moderation lineage

The first `decide` event is moderator-signed and binds its subject. An `appeal`
must be signed by the subject creator, name an ancestor `decide`/`resolve` as
`predecessor`, and descend from it. A moderator `resolve` names both that
predecessor and appeal as ancestors. Skipped, cross-object, or forged lineage is
rejected.

Concurrent differing active decisions never pick a quiet winner: the subject
is visibly `quarantined` with `moderationConflict`. Equal decisions coalesce.
Resolved `hide`, `quarantine`, and `allow` project to hidden, quarantined, and
visible respectively; the signed decision and appeal history remains readable
to authorized audit tools.

## Storage, migration, and recovery

The portable log format is one canonical envelope per NDJSON line with LF
record separators. Export sorts unique raw records by their raw SHA-256 digest.
Import verifies every line and recomputes state; it does not trust an exported
snapshot or silently normalize CRLF records.

Legacy `forkmesh-issue-v1`, `forkmesh-pull-v1`, comment, label, reaction,
review, milestone, project/board, notification, and moderation records migrate
through an importer-signed `create`/`decide` event. That event binds the exact
legacy record digest and records `valid`, `invalid`, or `unavailable` legacy
signature status. It never claims the legacy author made a new signature. The
original bytes stay beside the new log until retention policy permits archival.

Roll back readers before writers: stop emitting v1, keep accepting and
preserving raw envelopes, and project the prior snapshot format read-only. Do
not down-convert or delete v1 events because that loses causality. Recovery is
to restore policy plus NDJSON, run the independent verifier, and compare the
state digest. Corrupt lines remain quarantined while valid independent objects
continue folding.

Use the verifier locally:

```bash
python3 tools/verify_collaboration.py \
  --policy repository-collaboration-policy.json \
  --require-complete collaboration.ndjson
```

`tools/export_collaboration_log.py export --repository IDENTITY --signing-key
SEED` performs this import for a checkout's `forkmesh-issue-v1` records. It
writes `.forkmesh/collaboration/policy.json` and `issues.ndjson`, which can be
committed so a visitor verifies them from a plain clone. The digest binds the
exact record file bytes, and each record's legacy status is `valid` only when
every legacy event signature in it verifies.

The exporter carries its own copy of `issue_event_content` from
`app/src/events.py`, because that module needs the Worker's js bridge and a
stdlib tool cannot import it; `app/tests/test_export_collaboration_log.py` pins
the two byte-for-byte. A legacy `open` event is signed before the issue has a
number, so its signature may bind either 0 or the assigned number; every other
event binds the number. Signing uses `cryptography` when installed and falls
back to pure-Python RFC 8032. A record that v1 cannot represent, such as a
title over the 512-byte limit, is skipped and named in the export summary
rather than truncated, so the log never misstates an issue.

## Threat, abuse, privacy, and telemetry

The main threats are forged authorship, replay across repositories, malicious
clock/timestamp choice, key equivocation, reference retargeting, unauthorized
moderation, deletion races, and a relay omitting events. Signatures and domain
binding address forgery/replay; DAG validation and explicit conflicts address
ordering; role policy and lineage address moderation; observed tombstones
address deletion races. Omission requires peer exchange/availability receipts
and cannot be solved by a fold over an incomplete set.

Raw events can contain private issue text, notification recipients, moderation
notes, and relationship metadata. Private logs stay inside the repository's
authorization/encryption boundary. Telemetry exports counts only:
`received`, `uniqueRaw`, `signatureValid`, `accepted`, `pending`, `rejected`,
`duplicateDeliveries`, `equivocations`, `conflicts`, rejection reason, and
accepted family. It MUST NOT export bodies, object IDs, public keys, refs, or
raw signatures.

## Automated evidence and supported runtimes

`app/tests/test_collaboration_protocol.py` supplies the signed convergence
corpus, randomized permutations/replays, byte mutation fuzzing, adversarial
authorization/signature/sequence cases, all-family legacy migration,
rollback/recovery, telemetry, and Python↔WebCrypto parity. The dedicated
`collaboration-conformance.yml` workflow runs it with Python 3.12 and Node 24 on
Linux, macOS, and Windows and retains JUnit evidence. The same focused suite is
part of the core quality gate.

No network service, wall clock, or database is required. This is intentional:
an implementation passes only by deriving state from retained signed bytes.

pages.markdown:
# Conformance suites

`conformance/<suite>/v1/` holds versioned, machine-readable contracts: test
vectors, fixtures, ledgers and retained evidence. Each suite is shared by the
implementations it binds (the Python app, the Go daemon, the desktop, mobile)
and backs one public page under `docs/`. A version directory is frozen
once published; a breaking change adds `v2` beside it. The code map below
lists every suite with the page it backs. The threat model these suites test
is [threat-model.md](../protocol/threat-model.md); the normative protocol
suite is [protocol/README.md](../protocol/README.md). Back to the
[documentation index](../README.md).

## Code map

| Suite | Contents | Checked or produced by | Public page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `availability-contract` | `model.json`, `fixture.json`, `generate_fixture.py` | `app/src/availability_contract.py`, `tools/forkmesh_availability_contract.py`; `app/tests/test_availability_contract.py` | [`docs/availability-contract.md`](../availability-contract.md) |
| `availability-proof` | `model.json`, `fixture.json`, `generate_fixture.py` | `app/src/availability_proof.py`, `tools/forkmesh_availability_proof.py`; `app/tests/test_availability_proof.py` | [`docs/availability-proof.md`](../availability-proof.md) |
| `category-comparisons` | `ledger.json` | `tools/category_comparisons.py`; `app/tests/test_category_comparisons.py` | [`docs/category-comparisons.md`](../category-comparisons.md) (generated) |
| `certification` | `program.json`, `implementations.json`, `results.json`, `adapters/`, `evidence/` | `tools/protocol_certification.py`; `app/tests/test_protocol_certification.py` | [`docs/protocol/certification.md`](../protocol/certification.md), [`docs/protocol/certification-registry.md`](../protocol/certification-registry.md) (generated) |
| `crisis-preservation` | `model.json`, `fixture-input.json`, `fixture.json`, `generate_fixture.py` | `app/src/crisis_preservation.py`, `tools/forkmesh_crisis_preservation.py`; `app/tests/test_crisis_preservation.py` | [`docs/crisis-preservation.md`](../crisis-preservation.md) |
| `dependencies` | `contract.json` | `tools/dependency_conformance.py`; `app/tests/test_dependency_workflows.py` | [`docs/dependency-workflows.md`](../dependency-workflows.md) |
| `disaster-recovery` | `runbook.json`, `exercises/`, `evidence/` | `tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py`; `app/tests/test_disaster_recovery.py` | [`docs/disaster-recovery/`](../disaster-recovery/) |
| `external-dependencies` | `manifest.json` | `tools/external_dependency_inventory.py`; `app/tests/test_external_dependency_map.py` | [`docs/external-dependency-map.md`](../external-dependency-map.md) |

| `governance` | `charter.json`, `participants.json`, `records/` | `tools/protocol_governance.py`; `app/tests/test_protocol_governance.py` | [`docs/governance/`](../governance/) |

| `integrations` | `contract.json`, `examples/` | `tools/forkmesh_integration.py`; `app/tests/test_integration_contract.py` | [`docs/integrations.md`](../integrations.md) |
| `protocol` | `manifest.json`, `threats.json`, `vectors/`, `generate_vectors.py`, `verify_suite.py` | `app/tests/test_protocol_suite.py`; clean-room `verify_suite.py` | [`docs/protocol/`](../protocol/) |
| `secrets` | `corpus.json`, `build_corpus.py` | `tools/secret_gate.py`; `app/tests/test_secret_gate.py` | [`docs/security/secret-scanning.md`](../security/secret-scanning.md) |
| `service-roles` | `manifest.json` | `tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py`; `app/tests/test_service_roles_contract.py` | [`docs/operations/service-roles.md`](../operations/service-roles.md) |
| `social-signals` | `vectors.json` | `tools/social_signals.py`; `app/tests/test_social_signals.py` | [`docs/social-signals.md`](../social-signals.md) |
| `sync-status` | `model.json`, `fixture.json`, `generate_fixture.py` | `app/src/sync_status.py`, `server/syncstatus.go`, `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/SyncStatus.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/api/SyncStatus.kt`, `tools/forkmesh_sync_status.py`; `app/tests/test_sync_status.py` | [`docs/sync-status.md`](../sync-status.md) |
| `transports` | `cases.json` | `tools/forkmesh_transports.py`; `app/tests/test_transports.py` | [`docs/transports.md`](../transports.md) |
| `trust-lists` | `vectors.json`, `generate_vectors.py` | `app/src/trust_lists.py`, `app/public/trust-lists.js`, `desktop/tests/test_trust_lists.cpp`, `native/ios/ForkMeshCore/Sources/FMAccount/TrustLists.swift`, `native/android/core/src/main/kotlin/com/forkmesh/nativeapp/security/TrustLists.kt`, `tools/forkmesh_trust_lists.py`; `app/tests/test_trust_lists.py` | [`docs/trust-lists.md`](../trust-lists.md), [`docs/design/scoped-trust-lists.md`](../design/scoped-trust-lists.md) |

## Architecture

A suite is data, not code. Implementations load the same fixture or vectors
and must produce the recorded outputs, so the app, the Go daemon, the desktop
and the mobile apps cannot drift apart silently. Generator scripts
(`generate_fixture.py`, `generate_vectors.py`, `build_corpus.py`) rebuild the
expected outputs or, with `--check`, fail when they are stale. Ledger suites
(`git`, `category-comparisons`, `governance`, `funding`, `certification`) are
rendered by their tool's `render` command into Markdown under `docs/`
(most also write JSON under `www/public/docs/`). Each suite's JSON shape is
defined by its generator or consuming tool. Suites are versioned by
directory; there is no other configuration.

## Build, run, test

```sh
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/verify_suite.py
python3 conformance/sync-status/v1/generate_fixture.py --help
python3 tools/git_conformance.py validate
python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_protocol_suite.py app/tests/test_secret_gate.py app/tests/test_transports.py
```

After changing a rendered ledger, run its tool's `render` command so the
generated page matches; the matching test fails otherwise. CI runs
`tools/git_conformance.py validate`, `render --check` and `run` from
`.forkmesh/ci.yml`.

## Notes

- `secrets/v1/corpus.json` contains synthetic secret-shaped strings only; its
  file names (for example `docs/security.md`) are fixture paths, not files in
  this repository. Likewise, paths such as `docs/notes.md` or `docs/guide.md`
  in tests are fixtures.
- `social-signals/v1/vectors.json` and `disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json`
  are covered by signatures or attested digests; rehosting tools never
  rewrite them (`FROZEN_FILES`), and a hand edit breaks verification.
- Public keys are URL-safe base64, so about one in 64 starts with `-`, and
  argparse reads `--trusted-key -Ab…` as a missing value (exit 2). The drills
  generate fresh keys each run and must pass them as `--trusted-key=KEY`
  (`test_offline_bootstrap_passes_keys_that_start_with_a_dash`).
- Suites that talk to themselves over loopback TCP (stock Git, integration
  contract) run in CI under `unshare -rn` with `lo` up, because a host
  application firewall can drop loopback connections and stall a run.
  Reproduce CI hangs locally the same way.

# Design decisions

Specifications for features that cross the protocol, the app and the clients.
Conflict-safe collaboration is normative and part of the
[protocol suite](../protocol/README.md); scoped trust lists are a candidate
protocol with shared vectors; the others record how a feature works and why.

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Conflict-safe collaboration](conflict-safe-collaboration.md) | Signed collaboration events, identifiers, causality, deterministic fold and conflict rules, moderation lineage |
| [Scoped trust lists](scoped-trust-lists.md) | Signed, scoped community trust lists: documents, verification order, revocation, appeals, merge rules |
| [Pull review threads](pull-review-threads.md) | Signed anchors that keep review threads on the right lines across patchsets and branches |
| [Release binary publishing](release-binary-publishing.md) | Signed release metadata in Git, payloads in a content-addressed store, verification order |
| [ActivityPub federation](activitypub-federation.md) | Followable fediverse actors, HTTP signatures, inbox actor binding, delivery |

Related core pages: [encryption and signatures](../encryption.md),
[mirroring and distribution](../mirroring.md) and the
[threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md). Back to the
[documentation index](../README.md).

pages.title: Encoding and identifiers
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Vectors: canonical-json.json, identifiers.json · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.markdown:
# Encoding and identifiers

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Vectors: `canonical-json.json`,
`identifiers.json` · Part of the [ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md)

## Canonical JSON

ForkMesh hashes and signs a deliberately small JSON subset. It is chosen so
that Python `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True,
separators=(",", ":"))` and ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` with sorted keys emit
identical bytes for every admitted value.

- **FM-ENC-001** MUST — A canonical document is UTF-8 without a byte-order
  mark, without insignificant whitespace, and without a trailing newline. A
  signed document's top level is an object. Object keys match
  `^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]{1,256}$` and appear in ascending code-point order.
- **FM-ENC-002** MUST — Values are objects, arrays, strings, `true`, `false`,
  `null`, or integers whose magnitude is at most 2^53−1. Integers are written
  in shortest decimal form: no fraction, exponent, leading zero, or negative
  zero. `NaN` and infinities are not JSON and are rejected. Individual fields
  can narrow the range further; envelope counters, for example, are
  non-negative.
- **FM-ENC-003** MUST — Strings are Unicode NFC and contain no unpaired
  surrogate. An encoder normalizes strings to NFC before hashing. Within a
  string, `"` and `\` are written `\"` and `\\`; U+0008, U+000C, U+000A,
  U+000D, and U+0009 use `\b \f \n \r \t`; all other code points below U+0020
  use `\u00XX` with lowercase hex. Every other code point, including U+007F,
  U+2028, U+2029, `/`, and characters outside the BMP, is written literally.
- **FM-ENC-004** MUST — A receiver parses with duplicate-key detection,
  re-encodes the parsed value under FM-ENC-001..003, and rejects the input
  unless the result is byte-for-byte identical. An alternate spelling of the
  same value — whitespace, escapes, key order, or a non-NFC string — is a
  different, invalid input, not an equivalent one.
- **FM-ENC-005** MUST — A signed document is at most 1 MiB (1,048,576 bytes)
  and non-empty. Nesting depth is at most 32, counting the top-level object as
  depth 0 and each nested array or object as one more.

Some integrity receipts use variants that differ from signed collaboration
documents. The portable session claim (FM-AUTH-003) and the catalog v2 record
hash (FM-AUTH-004) serialize with ASCII escaping: every code point above
U+007E is written as lowercase `\uXXXX`, using surrogate pairs outside the
BMP. Migration state receipts (FM-ID-006) use the literal form without NFC
normalization. Each variant is pinned by vectors.

Rejection codes, in the order a parser meets them: `invalid_event_size`,
`invalid_json`, `invalid_number`, `floating_point_forbidden`, `duplicate_key`,
`event_not_object`, `json_too_deep`, `invalid_key`, `unsafe_integer`,
`invalid_unicode`, `noncanonical_encoding`.

## Binary encodings

- **FM-ENC-006** MUST — Keys, signatures, and object keys are base64url
  (RFC 4648 §5) without padding. A decoder rejects padding, characters outside
  the alphabet, the wrong decoded length, and any spelling that does not
  re-encode identically. The last check catches non-zero unused trailing bits:
  two textual signatures for the same bytes would otherwise produce two
  distinct envelopes. Ed25519 public keys decode to 32 bytes, signatures to
  64, and collaboration object keys to 16.

Digest identifiers are written `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex digits,
except where a field is specified as bare hex.

## Canonical strings

Older signed actions sign newline-joined strings rather than JSON.

- **FM-ENC-007** MUST — A canonical string is the UTF-8 encoding of a frozen
  scheme prefix `forkmesh-<scheme>-v<N>`, then each field in the order the
  scheme lists, joined by a single LF (0x0A) with no trailing LF. Timestamps
  are decimal milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Senders write them without
  sign or leading zeros; verifiers sign-check the field text exactly as
  transmitted. Variable-length content is bound as a lowercase hex SHA-256
  field, never inline.

The scheme field lists live in [Signatures and
authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md#canonical-string-schemes).

## Identifiers

- **FM-ID-001** MUST — A repository identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:repository:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-repository-identity-v1\n" || NFC(verified root)))`.
  The verified root is established out of band, for example by a signed
  repository manifest. Display names, organization aliases, and URLs are
  routing hints, never identities.
- **FM-ID-002** MUST — A collaboration policy document has exactly the keys
  `schema` (`forkmesh-collaboration-policy-v1`), `repository`, `maintainers`,
  `moderators`, and `notifiers`. Each role is a sorted, duplicate-free list of
  32-byte base64url Ed25519 keys. Its identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(canonical JSON))`, with no domain prefix because
  the schema value is inside the hashed bytes. A document that is not already
  in this form is rejected, never repaired.
- **FM-ID-003** MUST — A collaboration object identity is
  `urn:forkmesh:collaboration:<family>:sha256:` followed by
  `hex(SHA-256("forkmesh-collaboration-object-v1\n" || canonical JSON of
  {repository, family, creator, objectKey, references}))`. `references` is
  the validated, sorted list of `{relation, family, object}` triples that the
  object's first event carries.
- **FM-ID-004** MUST — A collaboration event identity is
  `sha256:` + `hex(SHA-256(signingBytes || 0x00 || rawSignature))`. Here
  `signingBytes` is defined by FM-SIG-003 and `rawSignature` is the 64 decoded
  signature bytes. A receiver recomputes it and rejects a mismatch
  (`event_id_mismatch`).
- **FM-ID-005** MUST — A repository state digest is taken over the refs a node
  serves. From a protocol-v0 `upload-pack --advertise-refs` pkt-line stream,
  keep only `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`. Drop `HEAD`, peeled `^{}` lines,
  and every other namespace, including `refs/pull/` and `refs/forkmesh/`.
  Strip capabilities after the first NUL, and sort by refname in byte order.
  The canonical text joins `<object-id> <refname>` lines with LF and has no
  trailing LF. `stateHash` is its lowercase hex SHA-256; an empty
  advertisement hashes the empty string.
- **FM-ID-006** MUST — Migration identifiers are domain-separated SHA-256 over
  LF-joined parts: `hex(SHA-256(domain || "\n" || join("\n", parts)))`.
  A job is `mig_` followed by the first 24 hex digits for the domain
  `forkmesh-migration-job-v1`. An object key uses
  `forkmesh-migration-object-v1` with parts object type and source id. A
  state receipt is `sha256:` + hex SHA-256 of the literal-form canonical JSON
  (see above) of the state document.

pages.title: ForkMesh protocol suite
pages.description: Suite version: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Status: candidate — not yet stable; see Stable release gate.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh protocol suite

Suite version: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **candidate** — not yet stable; see
[Stable release gate](#stable-release-gate).

This suite is the normative description of ForkMesh wire behavior. An
independent implementation should be able to derive every identifier, produce
and verify every signature, and fold collaboration state from these documents
and their vectors without reading ForkMesh source. The hosted
[protocol reference](https://forkmesh.com/docs/protocol/) remains the
narrative guide to HTTP routes and deployment; where the two disagree, this
suite wins and the disagreement is a bug. Plain-language overviews are on
[Encryption and signatures](../encryption.md) and
[Architecture and availability](../architecture.md); other
[design decisions](../design/README.md) and the
[conformance suites](../conformance/README.md) sit beside this suite. Back to
the [documentation index](../README.md).

| Document | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Encoding and identifiers](encoding-and-identifiers.md) | Canonical JSON, base64url, canonical strings, repository/policy/object/event/refs/migration identifiers |
| [Signatures and authentication](signatures-and-authentication.md) | Strict Ed25519, domain separation, envelope verification order, request tokens, push authorization, portable sessions, catalog publication |
| [Relay, synchronization, and migration](relay-sync-and-migration.md) | Integrity-gated clone routing, NDJSON log exchange, deterministic folding, migration receipts, rollback |
| [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md) | Version identifiers, rejection of unknown versions, downgrade resistance, rollout order |
| [Conflict-safe collaboration](../design/conflict-safe-collaboration.md) | Collaboration event families, fold rules, moderation lineage |
| [Threat model](threat-model.md) | Trust boundaries, attackers, threat register, release blockers |
| [Certification program](certification.md) | Profiles, adapter protocol, detection classes, expiring badges, independence, governance, appeals, trademark use |
| [Certification registry](certification-registry.md) | Current badges and detection coverage (generated by `tools/protocol_certification.py render`) |

## Conformance language

The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are to be interpreted
as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in
a numbered requirement. A requirement is written as a bold identifier followed
by its level, in the form `**FM-AREA-NNN** MUST`. Identifiers are never reused;
a withdrawn requirement keeps its number with the text "Withdrawn".

Everything outside a numbered requirement is informative.

## Suite requirements

- **FM-SUITE-001** MUST — The documents, schemas, vectors, and threat register
  of one suite version are released together. The manifest
  (`conformance/protocol/v1/manifest.json`) records the SHA-256 of each file
  and maps every requirement to its evidence. A verifier MUST reject the suite
  when any digest, version string, requirement identifier, requirement level,
  vector citation, or threat severity/status disagrees.
- **FM-SUITE-002** MUST — An implementation that claims a vector set passes
  every case in it: valid cases produce exactly the listed values, and invalid
  cases are rejected.
- **FM-SUITE-003** SHOULD — A rejection reports the listed error code.
  Validity is normative; codes are the stable vocabulary for audit telemetry
  and interop debugging. An implementation's known code deviations are
  recorded in the manifest (`codeDeviations`) and tested for exact equality,
  so a new deviation fails like any other inconsistency.

## Vectors

Vector files live in `conformance/protocol/v1/vectors/`:

| File | Content | Implementations passing it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical-json.json` | Parse and encode cases, including every rejection class | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `identifiers.json` | Repository, policy, object, refs-state, and migration identifiers | reference Python, clean-room Python; JavaScript for repository/policy/object |
| `signatures.json` | RFC 8032 and strictness cases, canonical-string schemes, push-message normalization, freshness windows | reference Python, clean-room Python |
| `events.json` | Signed collaboration envelopes and each verification failure | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript, clean-room Python |
| `fold.json` | Folded NDJSON logs with state digests and telemetry | reference Python, WebCrypto JavaScript |
| `sessions.json` | Portable session tokens | reference Python, clean-room Python |

Byte-exact inputs are given as `rawHex`; `rawText` is informative. Keys and
signatures come from deterministic test identities and MUST NOT be used
outside tests.

Run the suite:

```bash
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/verify_suite.py          # clean-room verifier + consistency
python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py --check
python3 -m pytest -q app/tests/test_protocol_suite.py
```

`verify_suite.py` uses only the Python standard library and was written from
these documents. It does not yet fold collaboration logs, so `fold.json` is
evidenced by the two reference implementations only.

## Compatibility policy

Wire version identifiers and the suite version are separate:

- A **wire version identifier** (for example `forkmesh-collaboration-event-v1`
  or the `v1.` session-token prefix) names frozen bytes. Its meaning never
  changes; see [Version negotiation](version-negotiation.md).
- The **suite version** uses semantic versioning. A patch release fixes
  wording or adds vectors for existing behavior. A minor release adds
  requirements, vectors, or wire identifiers without changing what an existing
  conforming implementation accepts. A major release removes acceptance of a
  wire identifier; it is announced one minor release in advance and ships
  with a migration path.

## Change process

Changes are decided under the [governance charter](../governance/README.md).
Steps 1–5 are the technical part of a proposal record (`FMP-NNNN`). Review
windows, quorum, dissent, and appeals follow the charter.

1. Open an issue that names the requirement identifiers and threats affected.
2. Change the normative text, the reference implementations, and the
   generator expectations in one change. The generator compares every vector
   with an expectation written in `generate_vectors.py`, so a behavior change
   that is not also a documented expectation fails generation.
3. Update `threats.json` and the [threat model](threat-model.md) table
   together when a control or residual risk changes.
4. Regenerate: `python3 conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py`. This
   rewrites vectors and manifest digests; `--check` fails CI on anything stale.
5. Review requires one maintainer for informative or vector-only changes and a
   security reviewer for any requirement, wire identifier, or threat status
   change.

## Stable release gate

The suite may be marked `stable` only when no `critical` or `high` threat in
the register is `open`. Each must be `mitigated` by a numbered requirement or
`accepted` with a reviewer, date, and rationale. The verifier enforces this and
reports the current blockers as `stableReleaseBlockers`.

Before the umbrella epic can close, more evidence is needed:

- a clean-room collaboration fold;
- a second-language clean-room verifier;
- stock-Git clone interoperability against an independently written relay;
- the platform matrix.

The [certification program](certification.md) packages these vectors into
profiles any implementation can run through a language-neutral adapter. Its
closure gate is an independent implementation holding a current `core`
badge.

The [Git conformance suite](../operations/git-conformance.md) already covers
stock clients.

pages.description: Program version: 1.0.0 · Protocol suite: 1.0.0-rc.1 · Part of the ForkMesh protocol suite · Current badges: certification registry
pages.markdown:
# Protocol certification program

Program version: `1.0.0` · Protocol suite: `1.0.0-rc.1` · Part of the
[ForkMesh protocol suite](README.md) · Current badges:
[certification registry](certification-registry.md)

Independent clients, relays, indexes and providers prove compatibility by
running the published suite through a small adapter and publishing the report.
A badge says exactly one thing: *this implementation, at this version, passed
every case of this profile, against these vectors, within the last 90 days, on
these platforms*. Badges are derived from retained reports only.

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `conformance/certification/v1/program.json` | Profiles, detection classes, performance budgets, freshness window, closure gate |
| `conformance/certification/v1/implementations.json` | Registered implementations, adapter commands, profiles, platforms, independence review |
| `conformance/certification/v1/evidence/<run>.json` | Retained reports, named by content address |
| `conformance/certification/v1/results.json` | Index of retained reports |
| `tools/protocol_certification.py` | Harness, attestation, badge derivation, generated outputs |

Generated, never hand-edited: [certification-registry.md](certification-registry.md),
`/docs/certification/badges.json`, `/docs/certification/evidence/<run>.json`.

## Profiles

| Profile | For | Vector groups | Must detect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `core` | clients, relays, indexes, providers | canonical JSON; identifiers; Ed25519 strictness, canonical strings, git-push messages, freshness; signed events; portable sessions | malformed signatures, divergence, downgrade, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |
| `collaboration-fold` | clients and relays that fold collaboration logs | canonical JSON; identifiers; signed events; log folding | malformed signatures, divergence, replay, data loss, incompatible versions |

Every case is positive (exact value) or negative (rejected). Detection classes:

| Class | A failing implementation … |
| --- | --- |
| `malformed-signature` | accepts a non-canonical scalar, small-order key, tampered payload or alternate signature spelling |
| `divergence` | derives a different identifier or folded state from the same input |
| `downgrade` | verifies under an older version or another scheme |
| `replay` | accepts a stale request, expired or future session, or re-applies a redelivered event |
| `data-loss` | drops a ref, rounds an integer or discards a pending or rejected record |
| `incompatible-version` | parses an unknown or future version instead of rejecting it |

The clean-room adapter's `--fault` modes break one property at a time, and the
tests require each fault to fail its class. Each case must answer within
2,000 ms and a profile within 120 s. A rejection with a different stable error
code still passes and is recorded as a code deviation (FM-SUITE-003).

## Adapter protocol

`forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1` is newline-delimited JSON over the adapter's
stdin and stdout, run from the repository root.

1. Harness: `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","suite":"forkmesh-protocol","suiteVersion":"1.0.0-rc.1"}`.
2. Adapter: `{"type":"hello","protocol":"forkmesh-conformance-adapter-v1","implementation":{"name":"…","version":"…"},"suiteVersions":["1.0.0-rc.1"]}`.
   A protocol or suite-version mismatch records the run as `incompatible`.
3. Per case, harness: `{"type":"case","id":"<set>:<case>","operation":"…","input":{…}}`;
   adapter: `{"id":"…","valid":true,"value":…}`,
   `{"id":"…","valid":false,"error":"<code>"}` or `{"id":"…","unsupported":true}`.

A missing, late or mismatched response fails the case; an adapter that exits
or hangs fails every remaining case, and a report is still produced.

| Operation | Input | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canonical.parse` | `rawHex` | ignored |
| `canonical.encode` | `value` | canonical text |
| `identifier.repository` | `verifiedRoot` | repository identifier |
| `identifier.policy` | `policy` | policy identifier |
| `identifier.object` | `repository`, `family`, `creator`, `objectKey`, `references` | object identifier |
| `identifier.refs-state` | `advertisementHex` | `{"canonicalText","stateHash"}` |
| `identifier.migration` | `operation` and fields | identifier or hash |
| `signature.ed25519` | `publicKeyHex`, `messageHex`, `signatureHex` | ignored |
| `signature.canonical-string` | `messageText`, `publicKey`, `signature`, optional `scheme`/`fields`, `catalogV2Record` | ignored |
| `signature.git-push-message` | `owner`, `repo`, `method`, `ts`, `bodySha256` | message text |
| `request.freshness` | `ts`, `nowMs` | ignored |
| `event.verify` | `rawHex`, `policy`, `context` | event identifier |
| `session.parse` | `token`, `nowMs`, `routerPublicKey` | claim object |
| `log.fold` | `ndjson`, `policy` | `{"stateDigest","telemetry","rejectionReasons"}` |

Working adapters in Python and JavaScript are in
`conformance/certification/v1/adapters/`.

## Running and publishing

```sh
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py run --profile core \
  --implementation acme-relay --command "cargo run --release --bin fm-adapter" \
  --output artifacts/acme-relay-core.json
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py attest artifacts/*.json
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py validate
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py render --check
python3 tools/protocol_certification.py gate
```

`attest` retains passing and failing reports, and rejects reports that do not
match the registered implementation, profile, platform or adapter command, that
disagree with their own cases, trim the case list, or contain local paths or
loopback addresses. The newest report per implementation, profile and platform
wins. `gate` runs in the quality gates: it validates everything, checks
generated outputs and re-runs every in-repository adapter.

## Badges

A badge covers one implementation, one profile, and the platforms registered
for it. Each report binds the program version, a profile digest, the suite
version and every vector file's digest.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `revoked` | Withdrawn by a recorded governance decision |
| `unverified` | No retained run on some listed platform |
| `failing` | The newest run on some platform failed |
| `expired` | Vectors, suite, program or profile changed, or the oldest run is older than 90 days |
| `certified` | Every listed platform passed against the current suite within 90 days |

The hosted SVG at `/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>.svg`
checks expiry on every request, and
`/docs/certification/badges/<implementation>/<profile>` redirects to the
evidence. A badge may be cited as "passes the ForkMesh `<profile>` profile,
suite `<version>`" only while it is `certified` and only with the hosted image.

## Independence and governance

The program's closure gate needs a non-ForkMesh implementation with a current
`core` badge: source public outside ForkMesh repositories, written from the
documents and vectors without copying ForkMesh source, and reviewed by someone
who does not maintain it (recorded in the registry's `independence` block).
In-repository implementations are `independent: false`.

Decisions follow the [governance charter](../governance/README.md) and are
recorded in the [decision register](../governance/decision-register.md).
Registration is a pull request adding a registry entry and an attested report,
rerun by a reviewer who does not work on that implementation. Program changes
follow the suite's [change process](README.md#change-process): narrowing a
profile is a major version, adding cases is a minor version that expires
existing badges. Disputed vectors are fixed through the change process with no
per-implementation exemptions; refusals and revocations can be appealed within
30 days. A badge is revoked when its evidence cannot be reproduced, its
independence statement is false, or it is used outside its scope.

New cases, especially adversarial and version-skew inputs, are added to
`conformance/protocol/v1/generate_vectors.py` and listed under their class in
`program.json`.
