pages.markdown:
# Organization roles and the authorization matrix

Every organization request is decided by one deny-by-default table,
`app/src/organization_rbac.py`. A role holds a capability only when the matrix
names it; unknown roles, empty roles and unlisted capabilities are refused for
everyone, owners included. The tables below are generated from that module and
checked against it by `app/tests/test_organization_rbac.py`.
Part of [Security](README.md).

## Roles

Strongest first.

| Role | Purpose | Repository permission on linked repositories |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `owner` | Runs the organization. The only role that can dissolve it or grant and revoke `owner`/`admin`. | `admin` |
| `admin` | Administers members, teams, linked repositories, integrations and bot tokens. Cannot promote anyone to `owner`/`admin` or demote them. | `admin` |
| `maintainer` | Ships code: may queue agents and manage bots it links, administers nothing. | `maintain`, a team grant can raise it to `admin` |
| `member` | Collaborates. | `read`, a team grant can raise it to `admin` |
| `auditor` | Read-only observer: sees the roster, agent work and internal surfaces, never writes, pushes or votes. | `read`, a team grant cannot raise it |
| `guest` | Outside collaborator: sees the public profile and only the repositories a team grants, read-only. Not an insider for world floors, office chat channels, task boards or succession votes. | none, a team grant raises it to `read` at most |

## Capabilities

`read` capabilities never change organization state; no `write` row lists
`auditor` or `guest`.

| Capability | Kind | owner | admin | maintainer | member | auditor | guest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `organization.agents.queue` | write | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no |
| `organization.agents.read` | read | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| `organization.bots.link` | write | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no |
| `organization.bots.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.chat.channels` | write | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no |
| `organization.dissolve` | write | yes | no | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.fediverse.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.issues.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.members.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.pull_rules.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.read` | read | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `organization.repositories.import` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.repositories.link` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.roles.administer` | write | yes | no | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.roster.read` | read | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| `organization.settings.write` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.succession.approve` | write | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | no |
| `organization.tasks.administer` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.teams.manage` | write | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.world.private` | read | yes | yes | no | no | no | no |
| `organization.world.restricted` | read | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |

## Role administration

- An `owner` may assign or remove any role.
- An `admin` may manage `maintainer`, `member`, `auditor` and `guest`
  accounts, but cannot grant `owner`/`admin` or change an account holding one.
- Other roles assign nothing.
- The last `owner` can never be removed or demoted.

Denied writes are recorded in the sensitive-action audit log with a reason
(`insufficient_role`, `owner_role_required`, `last_owner`).

## Enforcement points

- Organization settings, members, teams, linked repositories, integrations,
  bot tokens and repository imports.
- `_org_permission`, used by the Git push gate and every repository-permission
  check: the role's baseline, raised by team grants up to the role's ceiling.
- A linked repository's Settings tab and every endpoint behind it (About,
  features, federation switches, webhooks, provider mirror, Actions secrets,
  logo review, delete) need repository permission `admin`, so `owner` and
  `admin` hold it and `maintainer` does not unless a team grants `admin`; the
  account that stores the repository keeps it too
  (`docs/app/repo-settings.md` in the source tree).
- World building access, office chat channels, task boards and succession
  votes, which enumerate the insider roles in SQL.
- Notes shared with the organization, organization package state
  (`/api/plugins/<org>` and the package list), installing or requesting an
  app for the organization, and slash commands from its app installs. These
  are insider surfaces too, so a guest gets none of them. An auditor reads an
  organization-shared note but never edits it, and cannot install apps.

Roles are stored as plain text in `org_members.role`; a build that does not
know a role treats it as no membership.

pages.title: Private repository confidentiality boundary
pages.description: The leakage and recovery contract for private repositories: what is protected, what at-rest inspection may reveal, how keys rotate and are revoked, and the evidence general…
pages.markdown:
# Private repository confidentiality boundary

The leakage and recovery contract for private repositories: what is protected,
what at-rest inspection may reveal, how keys rotate and are revoked, and the
evidence general availability needs. Part of [Security](README.md); the
encryption layers are on
[Encryption and signatures](../encryption.md#private-repositories).

## Protected data

Repository objects and refs, artifacts, repository and organization names,
device labels, discussions, issues, pull requests and reviews, agent prompts
and transcripts, notifications, security findings, media, and any search terms
or indexes derived from them.

Two confidentiality boundaries apply:

- **Repository objects** are sealed on an authorized device as
  `forkmesh.private-replica` ciphertext (fresh AES-256-GCM content key per
  update, wrapped to X25519 and ML-KEM-768 recipients). Storage and replication
  operators hold no recipient key and learn neither identity nor contents.
- **Relay collaboration rows** are AES-256-GCM encrypted under the instance
  `DATA_KEY`, with a separately derived HMAC blind index for equality lookups.
  Owner-agent payloads and private rooms add recipient encryption on top. An
  operator holding the live service and `DATA_KEY` is inside this boundary; a
  database, log or backup operator without it is not.

A missing recipient key never falls back to plaintext.

## Metadata envelope

At-rest inspection may reveal only random identifiers, keyed blind indexes,
counts, ciphertext sizes, coarse status values, timestamps, digests, key epochs,
algorithm and public-key identifiers, and a private flag. These leak existence,
activity volume and equality within one key lifetime, but never names, paths,
labels, message text, Git refs or object IDs. Public-mirror history tables hold
no rows for private repositories.

Plaintext still exists in authorized memory, exported working copies and
recipients' own copies; use disk encryption alongside ForkMesh keys.

## Key lifecycle

Each repository update or recipient change creates a new content key and
advances `keyEpoch` atomically. To revoke a device or collaborator: remove the
recipient, reseal to the fresh owner-signed recipient set, publish the new
epoch, and verify the removed key cannot open it and an older epoch cannot
overwrite it. Revocation cannot erase copies already held. Keep at least two
owner recipients; organizations may escrow a recipient key in their own KMS and
enroll only its public half.

## Backup and keyless inspection

Back up `.fm-private` files, the encrypted database export, configuration and
the identity recovery kit, never plaintext checkouts or the raw `DATA_KEY`
alongside ciphertext. Restore ciphertext and schema together.

```bash
python tools/audit_private_surfaces.py backup.sqlite3 \
  --replica-root /read-only/private-replicas \
  --output artifacts/private-surface-audit.json
```

The audit takes no key and checks column declarations, blind-index shape,
payload and replica framing, digests and epoch monotonicity. Exit `0` passes,
`1` is a confidentiality finding, `2` is an input failure; an undeclared column
or incomplete coverage fails closed.

## GA evidence

Commercial general availability requires, per release candidate: private-surface
CI on Linux, macOS and Windows; keyless inspection of primary, backup, log and
replica data; revocation, rotation and recovery drills including failure paths;
content-free telemetry; and an independent cryptographic and tenant-isolation
review. Any unresolved critical or high finding, plaintext finding or missing
review blocks GA.

pages.title: Secret scanning before replication
pages.description: A node copies every object it receives to mirrors, forks, clones and backups, so a pushed object cannot be recalled. The only remediation for a leaked credential is rotation; the…
pages.markdown:
# Secret scanning before replication

A node copies every object it receives to mirrors, forks, clones and backups,
so **a pushed object cannot be recalled**. The only remediation for a leaked
credential is rotation; the only prevention is stopping it before the first
remote receives it. Every boundary prints this warning with its findings.
Part of [Security](README.md); why a copy cannot be recalled is explained on
[Mirroring](../mirroring.md).

## Scanner contract

`tools/secret_gate.py` defines `forkmesh-secret-scan-v1` (standard library
only; `python3 tools/secret_gate.py contract` prints it):

- **Rules**: provider-prefixed token patterns (Git hosts, cloud providers, chat
  and payment services, AI APIs, package registries, PEM private keys) plus a
  generic password/token assignment rule, each with rotation guidance.
- **Placeholder filter**: the generic rule skips obvious placeholders
  (`example`, `changeme`, `${VAR}`, `{{ }}`).
- **Ignore marker**: `forkmesh-secret-scan:ignore-line` on a logical line skips
  it, unless the organization refuses markers.
- **Value-free findings**: rule, path, line, blob id and a fingerprint derived
  from rule, path and blob id, never from the value.

The desktop scanner carries the same patterns; `app/tests/test_secret_gate.py`
fails if they drift.

## Boundaries

| Boundary | Behaviour | Mechanism |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local commit | Blocks or warns on added lines | `secret_gate.py install-hooks` (pre-commit) |
| Local push | Blocks or warns on every outgoing object | `secret_gate.py install-hooks` (pre-push) |
| Desktop push and review diffs | Review dialog or banner per match | desktop `RepoSecurity` |
| Node receipt (HTTPS and SSH) | Refuses the push before storing anything | `secrets` in the [node operator policy](../operations/node-operator-policy.md) |
| Sync and mirror intake | Detects after replication, quarantines under `block` | `node_operator_policy.py enforce` |
| Public security report | Findings without values | `tools/security_scan.py` |

```sh
python3 tools/secret_gate.py install-hooks --repo . \
  --repository owner/app --org-policy ~/.config/forkmesh/secret-policy.json
```

The installer never overwrites a hook it did not write. It writes
`--org-policy` and `--repository` before the hook stage, because Git appends
the remote name and URL to a pre-push hook's arguments and argparse cannot
hand positionals that follow options to the stage's arguments; with the
options after the stage, every push failed with "unrecognized arguments".
Hooks installed in that older order keep working without reinstalling.

## Policy

With no policy every rule blocks. The organization policy file:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "mode": "block",
  "rules": {"generic-secret-assignment": "warn"},
  "customRules": [
    {"id": "custom-deploy-key", "title": "Deploy key",
     "pattern": "deploy_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{32}", "severity": "critical",
     "action": "block", "rotation": "Revoke it in the provider console."}
  ],
  "allowlist": [
    {"paths": ["tests/fixtures/fake/*"], "rules": ["*"],
     "reason": "synthetic credentials for parser tests"}
  ],
  "honorIgnoreMarkers": true,
  "allowRepositoryAllowlist": false,
  "allowRepositoryCustomRules": false,
  "overrides": {
    "allowedSignersPath": "/etc/forkmesh/secret-override-signers",
    "maxLifetimeDays": 90
  }
}
```

- `mode` and `rules` take `off`, `warn` or `block`.
- A repository's `.forkmesh/secret-scan.json` can only tighten rules; its
  allowlist and custom rules count only when the organization allows them.
  Deleting it in a push loosens nothing.
- Allowlist entries need a reason and cannot cover every path. Invalid or
  empty-matching patterns and unknown fields are refused.

## Signed overrides

A block is lifted only by an SSH-signed override naming exact fingerprints:

```sh
python3 tools/secret_gate.py sign-override --key ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 \
  --signer signer@example.com --repository owner/app --days 30 \
  --reason "synthetic token for a parser test" \
  --fingerprint <fingerprint> > .forkmesh/secret-overrides/parser.json
```

Signers are listed in OpenSSH allowed-signers format with
`namespaces="forkmesh-secret-override"`. An override is ignored if the
signature fails, it names another repository, it has expired or exceeds
`maxLifetimeDays`, or the policy has no `allowedSignersPath`. Accepted
overrides are written to the node audit log.

## Accuracy

`conformance/secrets/v1/corpus.json` (generated by `build_corpus.py`, all
credentials synthetic) is run by `python3 tools/secret_gate.py corpus` at every
boundary. Bounds: at most 15% false negatives and 10% false positives. Known
misses are JSON object keys, concatenated tokens and base64-wrapped keys.

## Response after replication

`python3 tools/secret_gate.py respond --report <scan.json>` prints the plan:

1. **Contain**: quarantine on nodes you operate, remove the value in a new
   commit, pause automation using it.
2. **Rotate** at the issuer and review its audit log.
3. **Notify** the owner and security contact with the value-free evidence.
4. **Residual risk**: existing copies keep the object; treat it as compromised.

## Telemetry and limits

Scan reports and `node_operator_policy.py status` count blocked, warned,
overridden, allowlisted and stored detections without values. Blobs over 1 MiB
and binary blobs are skipped and counted. Browser uploads and provider imports
are scanned only when they reach a node's `enforce`.

pages.markdown:
# Security

Security is ForkMesh's first priority. This page is the security home for users
and developers: it maps the trust boundaries, says where each key lives (by
name and path, never by value), and lists every security page and the code
that owns each mechanism. Algorithms and encryption layers are on
[Encryption and signatures](../encryption.md); who can attack what is in the
[threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md). Report a vulnerability as
[SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md) describes.

## Pages

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Private repository confidentiality](private-repository-confidentiality.md) | What a private repository leaks at rest, key epochs, revocation, keyless inspection, GA evidence |
| [Chat encryption and public integrations](sealed-chat.md) | Conversation policies, device keys, sealed messages, the DM ratchet, safety numbers, limits |
| [Organization roles](organization-roles.md) | The deny-by-default role and capability matrix |
| [Node link grants](node-link-grants.md) | Moving a node account to a new owner with consent from both sides |
| [Secret scanning](secret-scanning.md) | `forkmesh-secret-scan-v1`: stopping credentials before the first replica |
| [Hidden Unicode](hidden-unicode.md) | `forkmesh-hidden-unicode-v1`: invisible characters removed from every text field and request body |
| [Host-mode agent boundaries](agent-host-boundaries.md) | What a desktop coding agent can read, run and reach, proven by named checks |
| [World-to-desktop speech bridge](world-local-speech-bridge.md) | Local speech-to-text for a World page without sending audio anywhere |
| [Third-party dependencies](dependency-security-audit.md) | Every dependency we keep and why, and its risk score |
| [Sentinel](sentinel.md) | The security teammate that reviews changes between audits |
| [Findings register](findings.md) | Fixed findings with their guard tests, and open items already public |

Related core pages: [architecture](../architecture.md) (cores, DNS round robin,
runners, read-only mode), [mirroring](../mirroring.md) (signed mirror health and
release verification), [self-hosting](../self-hosting.md) and
[censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md) (what still depends on a
provider). Back to the [documentation index](../README.md).

## Trust boundaries

1. **The device** holds the node identity key, repository decryption keys,
   chat device keys, SSH keys, agent-provider logins and wallet keys; none
   leave it.
2. **The core nodes (relay)** run the app with rqlite and are reached by DNS
   round robin ([architecture](../architecture.md)). They store routing,
   authorization and collaboration metadata encrypted at rest under
   `DATA_KEY` with HMAC blind indexes. This protects a stolen database copy,
   not data from the operator. Cores run no agent or untrusted code.
3. **Git hosts** (core gateways and user mirrors) hold Git bytes and release
   blobs, publish signed health, and serve a clone only with a fresh
   account-bound signature and a repository proof matching an accepted
   revision.
4. **Runners** run agent jobs, hold no core secret, are not mesh peers, keep
   no repositories, and push only `refs/heads/agent/<session>` with a per-job
   grant ([runners](../operations/runners.md)).
5. **Third parties** are listed with what they observe in the
   [external dependency map](../external-dependency-map.md).
   Cloudflare hosts the DNS zone and the forkmesh.com homepage Worker
   (`www/worker.js`); it does not proxy app or world traffic.

## Where each key lives

| Key or secret | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Node identity key (Ed25519) | `<data>/identity/ed25519.pem` on the device |
| Chat device keys | browser storage wrapped by a non-extractable key, the desktop secure store, the iOS keychain, Android Keystore-wrapped storage ([chat encryption](sealed-chat.md#device-keys)) |
| Private repository recipient keys | authorized devices only; an organization may escrow one in its own KMS ([private repositories](private-repository-confidentiality.md#key-lifecycle)) |
| SSH keys | `<project>/ssh/`; the fleet key under `ssh/fleet/` |
| Tool secrets | `<project>/config/tools/secrets` |
| `DATA_KEY` | the operator box; on a core only in the app's memory while the node is unsealed ([vault](../operations/vault.md)) |
| Operator files | `~/projects/forkmesh/config/fleet/` (a link into `data/core/config/fleet/`): `DATA_KEY`, `secrets.env`, provider credentials, `ids-operator.key`; the backup decryption key is kept offline |
| DNS token | the operator box only |
| Bootstrap credentials | host-encrypted systemd credentials on each core |
| App secrets | named in `[app] secrets` and `optional_secrets` in `deploy/fleet.toml`, sealed in the vault |
| Release signing key | an Actions variable on the release host |
| Mobile and Windows signing material | `<data>/release/` on the release host |

Fleet hosts are never added to the desktop's saved hosts.

## Code map

| Mechanism | Code | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node identity | `desktop/src/ForkMeshIdentity.{h,cpp}`, `server/identity.go` | [portable identities](../portable-identities.md) |
| Signed events | `app/src/events.py`, `app/src/releases.py` | [signatures and authentication](../protocol/signatures-and-authentication.md) |
| Encryption at rest | `app/src/entry.py` (row sealing, blind indexes) | [encryption](../encryption.md#data-on-the-service) |
| Secrets vault and unseal | `app/host/forkmesh_host/vault.py`, `vault_crypto.py`, `tools/next_vault.py` | [vault](../operations/vault.md) |
| Key rotation | `tools/next_rekey.py` | [re-key](../operations/rekey.md) |
| Organization roles | `app/src/organization_rbac.py` | [organization roles](organization-roles.md) |
| Node ownership changes | `_account_link_grant` | [node link grants](node-link-grants.md) |
| Signup bot check | `app/src/turnstile.py` | [operations](../operations/README.md) |
| Front-door checks | `app/host/forkmesh_host/request_guard.py`, `request_policy.py` | [host](../host/README.md) |
| Edge-client header | `x-forkmesh-edge-client`, verified before the app sees the request | [edge client](../www/edge-client.md) |
| Outbound request guard | `app/host/forkmesh_host/egress.py` | [host](../host/README.md) |
| ActivityPub inbox | `ap_inbox_handler` | [ActivityPub federation](../design/activitypub-federation.md#wire-protocol) |
| Hidden Unicode in input | `app/src/hidden_unicode.py`, `www/public/safe-input.js`, `desktop/src/HiddenUnicodeGuard.{h,cpp}`, `HiddenUnicode.swift`, `HiddenUnicode.kt`, `conformance/hidden-unicode/v1` | [hidden Unicode](hidden-unicode.md) |
| Host intrusion detection | `deploy/core/ids.py`, `tools/next_ids.py` | [intrusion detection](../operations/intrusion-detection.md) |
| Node hardening | `deploy/core/render.py`, `deploy/core/certsync.py`, `tools/next_fleet.py` | [operations](../operations/README.md) |
| Runner isolation | `server/runner.go`, `sandbox.go`, `jobhome.go`, `runnergrant.go` | [runners](../operations/runners.md) |
| Encrypted backups | `tools/next_backup.py` (age) | [disaster recovery](../disaster-recovery/README.md) |
| Secret scanning | `tools/secret_gate.py`, `conformance/secrets/v1` | [secret scanning](secret-scanning.md) |
| Desktop outbound firewall | `desktop/src/BackoffNetworkAccessManager.{h,cpp}` | every external destination needs an Allow or Deny |
| Agent filesystem guard | `tools/forkmesh_agent_guard.py` | fail-closed allowlist |
| Agent host boundaries | `desktop/tests/test_agent_host_boundaries.cpp`, `conformance/agent-adversarial/` | [agent host boundaries](agent-host-boundaries.md) |
| MCP server | `tools/forkmesh_mcp_server.py` | reads Git objects only |
| Organization Discord OAuth | `_oauth_callback_browser_bound` in `app/src/organization_discord.py` | [below](#browser-bound-oauth-callbacks) |
| Security audit log | `sensitive_audit_log` | [below](#security-audit-log) |
| Releases | `www/public/install.sh`, release tooling | [releases](../release/README.md) |
| Destructive actions | guarded delete helpers | [destructive actions](../engineering/destructive-actions.md) |
| Vulnerability reports | `security_report_handler` in `app/src/entry.py` | [Sentinel](sentinel.md#reports-from-the-security-webhook) |
| Protocol threat register | `conformance/protocol/v1/threats.json` | [threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md) |

## Mechanisms

### Unseal

Each core has a unix socket for unsealing. `DATA_KEY` arrives on SSH stdin,
never as an argument, environment variable or file. Peers unseal each other
over the mesh; a restarted node comes back sealed until then
([vault](../operations/vault.md)). IDS changes use signed expected-change
manifests and signed quarantine records
([intrusion detection](../operations/intrusion-detection.md)).

### Edge-client header

`x-forkmesh-edge-client` is an HMAC-signed visitor address from the homepage
Worker, verified before the app sees the request; direct requests have
client-address headers replaced by the TCP peer
([edge client](../www/edge-client.md)).

### Browser-bound OAuth callbacks

The organization Discord OAuth callback must come from the browser that
started the connection. Each Connect sets its own transaction cookie,
`forkmesh_discord_oauth_<first 16 hex of the state>` (SameSite=Lax, path
`/api/integrations/discord/callback`, ten minutes), and the callback finishes
only when a cookie holds exactly the returned state
(`_oauth_callback_browser_bound` in `app/src/organization_discord.py`).
Without it an owner could send the authorize link to another server's admin
and bind that server to their organization; state and PKCE alone do not stop
that. The session cookie cannot be checked instead: it is SameSite=Strict and
is not sent on the redirect back from discord.com. Two tabs or two Connect
clicks both finish (one cookie each). A missing cookie or a different browser
gets `invalid_context`, and the World Discord panel says nothing was
connected.

### Security audit log

`sensitive_audit_log` keeps 365 days (`SECURITY_AUDIT_RETAIN_MS`, pruned by
the `sensitive-cleanup` cron). An agent run's status report
(`organization.task_agent_status`, `world/src/world_office_tasks.py`) writes an
audit row only when the run's status changes from the stored one; a repeated
report of the same status still updates the task but adds no row, because one
row per desktop status heartbeat fills the log on 1 GB nodes (19 MiB seen).

## Practice

- Keys only in memory or permission-restricted files; no plaintext exports of
  user data left on disk.
- Least-privilege credentials, scoped per tool and per provider.
- Treat every new outbound fetch as a possible server-side request forgery
  and route it through the egress guard.
- Validate input at trust boundaries; render user text as text, never HTML.
- Sign security-relevant records over canonical strings that bind their
  context (repository, node, time, nonce).
- Fail closed when a security dependency (key, challenge secret, signature)
  is missing.
- Roll node-file security changes before the app release that relies on them.

## Traps

- User-data wipes (`install.sh --uninstall/--reinstall/--purge`,
  `uninstall.sh --purge`) erase the identity key; agents must never run them.
- After hardening, the provider web console cannot log in as root; use the
  rescue image.
- `DATA_KEY` cannot be rotated in place; rotation is an offline re-key.
- Public chat channels are readable by the relay operator by design; private
  channels and direct messages are end-to-end encrypted, and the server still
  knows which two accounts a DM joins ([chat encryption](sealed-chat.md)).
- The content security policy still allows inline scripts; a strict policy
  needs nonces.
- `app/tests/test_no_banned_identifiers.py` guards against personal
  identifiers returning through branches cut from rewritten history; rebuild
  such branches on `main`. It also bans the owner's personal Reddit handle
  (words joined by `_` count as one word, so the handle matches as a whole).
  Docs and tests use the desk's accounts or the `ada_lovelace` placeholder.

## Build, run, test

```sh
python3 -m pytest app/tests/host deploy/tests
python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_secret_gate.py app/tests/test_crypto.py app/tests/test_browser_security_headers.py
python3 tools/security_scan.py --help
python3 tools/secret_gate.py --help
```

# Security findings register

Reviewed through: `fc80139d04` on 2026-10-28 (full-system sweep, two rounds; S-38 to S-83)

Sentinel ([sentinel.md](sentinel.md)) keeps this page: fixed findings with the
test that guards each fix, and open items that are already public. Unfixed
findings that are not public are tracked on the organization task board in
the `security` department and appear here only once their fix is on main.
Update the checkpoint line after each review. Part of
[Security](README.md).

Status words: **Fixed** means the fix is on main and the Guard test fails
without it, and the guard runs in a gate: the `security` suite of
`tools/run_critical_tests.py` (CI, the quality gate and the auto-deploy
must-pass set) holds the S-2, S-5 and C-H5 guards, the account TOTP gate and
the destructive-delete contract; the Go guards run with `go test` in
`server/` in the same gates.
**Fixed, unguarded** means no test guards it yet. **Partial** and **Open** are
used only for items already public. Add a finding as one row;
the last cell names the guard test (paths must exist).

pages.markdown:
# Sentinel, the security teammate

Sentinel (`.forkmesh/workflows/sentinel.json`) owns security between audits.
Its run playbook is `.forkmesh/shortcuts/review-security.md`, its standing
rules are the `.forkmesh/skills/security-review.skill` repository skill, and
the record it keeps is [findings.md](findings.md).
`app/tests/test_security_sentinel_teammate.py` pins the parts of the
definition that keep it safe. It exists because many changes cross trust
boundaries every day and no other teammate's lane reviews them. Part of
[Security](README.md); attacker model:
[threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md).

## Lanes

| Trigger | What Sentinel does |
| --- | --- |
| Scheduled weekday run | review every trust-boundary commit since the checkpoint, review unmerged branches about to land, re-run guard tests, sweep for secrets, check dependency advisories weekly, update the register |
| Mention, question or assignment | answer from evidence with path:line and who can reach the path; change nothing unless asked |
| Pre-merge review request | review one branch's diff against main and leave the verdict on its task or pull request |
| Security report task | confirm a report from the security webhook, fix it test first on its own branch, and open a pull request for review |

## Reports from the security webhook

`POST /api/security/report` (`security_report_handler` in `app/src/entry.py`)
is the private channel for people (the form at `/security-report` and
Desktop → Settings → Security) and for AI agents and scanners, which
[`AGENTS.md`](../../AGENTS.md), [`SECURITY.md`](../../SECURITY.md) and
`llms.txt` ask to report there right away, so a scan that finds a hole reaches
us at once instead of sitting in someone else's transcript.

Each valid report is stored encrypted and emailed to `SECURITY_EMAIL`, then:

- a private task is filed on the `OFFICE_MARKETING_ORG` organization's board
  in the `security` department, routed to an agent at priority 5, linking the
  flagship repository; and
- every platform admin gets a `security_alert` Ping linking that task. Ping
  settings and quiet hours cannot mute that kind ([intrusion detection](../operations/intrusion-detection.md)), so it rings
  like an intrusion alert. Resubmitting the same report reuses one Ping.

The endpoint is anonymous, so the report is hostile input. The task's details
wrap it in an "untrusted" block and tell the agent to treat it as evidence,
confirm it from code alone, never touch the fleet, write a failing test first,
open a pull request and never merge or deploy; a report that gives orders is
recorded as a prompt-injection finding. At most
`SECURITY_REPORT_TASKS_PER_HOUR` tasks are filed per hour, so a flood cannot
fill the board or the agents' queue. Each source (an IPv4 address or an IPv6
/64) may send `SECURITY_REPORTS_PER_SOURCE_PER_HOUR` reports an hour; past
that the endpoint answers 429 before anything is stored, emailed or pinged, so
one sender cannot spend the mail budget or ring the admins without limit.
Stored reports leave by age (`SECURITY_REPORT_RETAIN_MS`, a year). A source's
first report in `SECURITY_REPORT_KEPT_WINDOW_MS` (30 days) is kept; its others
are bulk. The pool is marked in the row's `ts` without a schema change: kept
rows have an even millisecond, bulk rows an odd one (the sealed body keeps the
exact time). When `MAX_SECURITY_REPORTS` are held, a new report evicts the
oldest bulk row; with no bulk row left it is still emailed and pinged but not
stored. A flood from one source only churns its own bulk reports, and no
flood can evict a kept report (evicting the oldest row let 100 IPv4 addresses
or one IPv6 /56 fill the table and drop every new report).
The agent working such a task does not call the webhook again (`AGENTS.md`),
which would loop.

## Checkpoint

The `Reviewed through` line at the top of [findings.md](findings.md) names the
main commit the last merged review covered. The next run reviews
`<checkpoint>..main` in bounded slices, oldest first. A review whose branch is
not merged leaves the checkpoint unchanged.

## Disclosure

The repository is public, so an unfixed exploitable finding never goes into a
public issue, chat, commit message or [findings.md](findings.md). It is filed
on the organization task board in the `security` department, readable only by
members. A finding moves into the register when its fix lands on main.
Outside reporters use [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md).

## A finding is fixed when a test guards it

A fix counts only when it is on main and a test fails without it; otherwise it
is "Fixed, unguarded", and adding the test is a valid unit of work. Every run
re-runs the guard tests, because a fixed boundary can silently come undone.

## What Sentinel never does

- Act on the live fleet (no SSH writes, rolls, deploys, rotations, `--execute`
  fleet commands, scans or login bursts) unless the operator asks for one
  named check.
- Print, commit or post a secret value.
- Do the operator's work (credential rotation, moving keys offline, disk
  encryption, provider account changes); it reports each item with its age and
  next action.
- Merge, rebase or push another teammate's branch, or deploy.

## Permissions

`read-repositories`, `modify-code` and `create-branches` (one fix per run on
its own branch), `review-prs`, `manage-issues`, and `external-tools` (to query
advisory databases). It does not monitor logs.

pages.markdown:
# Third-party dependencies and their security audit

Every third-party component ForkMesh uses, why it is kept, and how each one is
audited for risk: publisher, maintenance history, known advisories and a score.
The filterable report is at
**[the dependency audit report](/docs/dependency-audit/)**.
Part of [Security](README.md); signed releases are covered on
[Encryption and signatures](../encryption.md#software-distribution).

## Inventory

The Go mirror node (`server/`) and the app source (`app/pyproject.toml`) use
only their standard libraries; the third-party packages the cores need are
pinned in `app/host/requirements.txt` ([docs/host/README.md](../host/README.md));
the iOS packages resolve nothing remote, and the desktop links Qt, OpenSSL and
(optionally) libnghttp3 from the system.
`marketplace/packages/docs/data/dependencies.json` is the full inventory
(`marketplace/tools/docs_dependencies.py`).

Every manifest and vendored library was last reviewed on 2026-10-29 for
packages we could drop or replace with our own code.

## Removed

| Dependency | Where | Why it could go |
|---|---|---|
| `three` (npm) | `world/browser_tests` | No test imported it. The browser tests load the vendored `world/public/world/vendor/three-0.184.0` that World serves, and `app/tools/render_call_backgrounds.cjs` maps `three` to the same file with an import map. `world/tests/test_world_source_layout.py` keeps it out. |
| `watchfiles`, `python-dotenv` | `app/host/requirements.txt` | They came with `uvicorn[standard]`, for `--reload` and `--env-file`, which `forkmesh_host serve` never uses. `watchfiles` was a compiled Rust wheel on every core node. The host pins `uvicorn` plus the three extras it does use: `uvloop`, `httptools`, `websockets`. |
| `numpy` | `app/tools/call_video_metrics.py` | It only took means, medians, a 95th percentile, point distances and mean grey-level differences. `math`, `statistics` and Pillow's `ImageChops`/`ImageStat` give the same numbers (checked against the numpy version on random landmarks and frames). The tool needs only Pillow. |

## Kept

| Dependency | Why |
|---|---|
| `cryptography` | Ed25519, X25519, P-256, RSA, AES-GCM and HKDF in 28 source files (60 with tests); we do not write our own cryptography. |
| `httpx`, `httpcore`, `h2` | The host's outbound HTTP with the egress guard (`egress.py`); `h2` because APNs only speaks HTTP/2. |
| `uvicorn`, `uvloop`, `httptools`, `websockets` | The ASGI server, its event loop, its HTTP parser and the WebSocket protocol the rooms of the cores' Durable Object emulation (`durable.py`) and the mesh listener use. |
| `orjson` | The `JSON.stringify`/`JSON.parse` shim in `forkmesh_host/js.py` runs on every request; it falls back to `json` when missing, so it is a speed choice, not a hard need. |
| `Pillow` | PNG/WebP decode and encode for avatars and pull-request cards. |
| `PyYAML` | Tests and release tools read `codemagic.yaml` and workflow files. |
| `numpy` in `build_call_face_assets.py` | It is the array engine under our own TFLite interpreter; the arithmetic is the point of the tool. |
| `ctranslate2`, `sentencepiece`, `fontTools`, `pycairo`, `brotli` | Single offline tools (forge translation, icon font subsetting, logo rendering, deploy compression with a Node fallback). |
| Vendored `three` (World and code map) | The renderer. The two copies stay separate because an instance can run the app with the World plugin turned off. |
| Vendored `satellite-js` | SGP4 orbit propagation; a rewrite would need its own validation suite. |
| `esbuild`, `@playwright/test`, `typescript` | Build and test tools only. |
| Android: Compose, `activity-compose`, `kotlinx-coroutines-android` | The UI toolkit and the coroutine runtime. |
| Go: `golang.org/x/mobile` | `gomobile bind` for the phone build of the mirror node (`native/fmm`). |

## Next candidate

`www/public/assets/vendor/lucide-0.468.0.min.js` is 358 KB and carries every
Lucide icon. The dashboard uses about 200 literal names, but 264 places build
the name at run time (`data-lucide="${...}"`, `dataset.lucide`), so a
generated subset needs a list of every dynamic name first, and a test that
fails when a page asks for an icon the subset lacks. Until then a missing
icon would fail silently as a blank square.

## Audit method

Package metadata comes from each ecosystem's registry (npm, PyPI, go.dev,
Gradle/Maven plugin indexes) and advisories from the OSV database, queried per
package and exact pinned version. Toolchains (Go, Kotlin, Android Gradle
Plugin) are audited alongside libraries, since a stale toolchain can carry
standard-library advisories even when every package is current.

## Scoring rubric

Each package starts at 100 and loses points for risk signals.
Grades: A ≥ 90, B 80–89, C 70–79, D 60–69, F below 60.

| Signal | Deduction |
| --- | --- |
| Open advisory matching the pinned version | −40 |
| Advisory in the package's history, pinned version not affected | −5 |
| Discontinued or deprecated | −30 |
| No verified publisher | −15 |
| Verified community publisher | −5 |
| No release in more than 24 / 12 months | −20 / −10 |
| Pinned version over 18 months old and a major version behind | −5 |
| Registry quality score below threshold, or analysis pending | −10 / −5 |
| Ships native code (plugin or FFI) | −5 |
| npm: fewer than two maintainers | −10 |

## Acting on findings

1. Open advisories on a pinned version or toolchain are fixed first: upgrade,
   rebuild and redeploy the affected component.
2. Packages that hold keys or secrets are kept on current major versions.
3. Stale packages and toolchains are upgraded in batches with the full test
   suite for the affected platform.
4. New dependencies in any ecosystem (including Swift packages and native
   Android Gradle dependencies) are added to the next audit.

pages.description: The desktop client can expose its local speech-to-text engine to a World page without sending microphone audio anywhere. The browser is only a controller and transcript…
pages.markdown:
# World-to-desktop speech bridge

The desktop client can expose its local speech-to-text engine to a World page
without sending microphone audio anywhere. The browser is only a controller and
transcript recipient; capture and transcription stay in the desktop client. The
World currently ships no speech controls, and the desktop bridge is dormant
infrastructure.
Part of [Security](README.md).

## Pairing

1. The user enables voice control for one exact World origin in the desktop
   client.
2. The client listens on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and shows a short-lived
   pairing capability, storing only its SHA-256 digest.
3. The page sends the capability once as `Authorization: Bearer …` to
   `POST /v1/pair`, which consumes it and returns an origin-bound ten-minute
   session capability.

Capabilities never appear in URLs, cookies, server requests, analytics or
persistent browser storage. Revoking, closing the panel or quitting the client
invalidates them.

## Capture protocol

- `POST /v1/transcription/start`, stop and cancel each carry a single-use
  `X-ForkMesh-Request-Id`; replays are rejected.
- `GET /v1/transcription` returns status and transcript text.
- Text is inserted into a World composer only after the user confirms the
  destination (`chat`, `issue` or `note`).

There is no audio upload or download endpoint, and responses report
`audioRelayed: false`. Bodies are limited to 8 KiB and headers to 16 KiB, query
strings and transfer encodings are rejected, responses are `no-store`, and
transcript and error text is bounded and stripped of control characters. One
capture runs at a time.

## Origin boundary

The origin is matched exactly (no suffix, wildcard or `null` matching). CORS
echoes only that origin and never enables credentials. Both the listener and
each peer must be loopback. The bridge is never proxied by a server.

## Auditing

Audit events (issued, paired, started, stopped, cancelled, completed, failed,
revoked) are written without capability values, transcript contents, audio,
device names or browsing history.

pages.title: apt repository
pages.description: Part of Releases.
pages.markdown:
# apt repository

Part of [Releases](README.md).

Debian and Ubuntu users install and update the desktop app with apt:

```sh
sudo curl -fsSLo /usr/share/keyrings/forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc https://forkmesh.com/apt/forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc
sudo curl -fsSLo /etc/apt/sources.list.d/forkmesh.sources https://forkmesh.com/apt/forkmesh.sources
sudo apt update
sudo apt install forkmesh
```

After that, `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` installs each new release.
The package runs on the same systems as the Linux binary: Ubuntu 22.04 and
newer, Debian 12 and newer, x86_64. The build:
[Linux release baseline](linux-baseline.md).

## Code map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/package/deb.sh` | builds `forkmesh-linux-x86_64.deb` from the release binary and its CMake-installed resources |
| `tools/package/linux-baseline/build-forkmesh.sh` | runs `deb.sh` in the Debian 12 container after the AppImage |
| `tools/package/linux-baseline/smoke-test.sh` | `dpkg --dry-run -i` and the packaged binary's `--version` on Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and Debian 12 |
| `tools/package/apt/forkmesh.sources` | the apt source the package installs and the setup command downloads |
| `tools/package/apt/forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc` | the public apt signing key |
| `tools/forkmesh-apt-repo.py` | writes and signs `dists/`, verifies it; `init-key` creates the signing key |
| `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py` (`refresh_apt_repository`) | republishes the apt metadata each time `latest` is promoted |
| `.forkmesh/releases/apt/` | the committed, signed apt metadata |
| `app/src/releases.py` (`apt_redirect_target`), `app/src/app_runtime.py` | the `/apt/*` routes |

## Package

`deb.sh` installs `/usr/bin/forkmesh` (and `forkmesh-term` when the build
has it), the resource tree in `/usr/share/forkmesh` (the binary finds it at
`../share/forkmesh`, as in the AppImage), a launcher, the 512 px icon, the
public key in `/usr/share/keyrings/forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc` and the
source in `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/forkmesh.sources`. The source is a
conffile. A user who ran the setup commands already has byte-identical
copies of both files at those paths, so dpkg takes them over without a
prompt, and someone who installed the `.deb` by hand still gets updates.

`Depends` is worked out in the container: each `NEEDED` library of the binary
is mapped to its Debian 12 package with `dpkg -S`, and `libc6` gets the
newest `GLIBC_` symbol version the binary uses. The build fails if a library
maps to no package or to several. These package names are the same on
Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04, which the smoke test checks.

The package version is the release version, with `+<build>` added for a
rebuilt platform build (`--deploy-build linux`, [build numbers](README.md#build-numbers)).
Build 0 of 1.5.1 is `1.5.1`, build 2 is `1.5.1+2`, and dpkg orders
`1.5.1 < 1.5.1+2 < 1.5.2`. A rebuild with the same version would never reach
apt users, which is why the build number goes into the version.

The `.deb` is published into the candidate with the other Linux assets, but
it is not in `HOST_ASSETS` or the gate's required list: a missing `.deb`
never holds a release back. Its manifest entry is `os: linux,
arch: x86_64`, like the AppImage; the desktop updater takes the first
matching asset, and the manifest is sorted by name, so the bare binary still
comes first.

## Repository

The repository has one suite, `stable`, one component, `main`, and only the
newest package. Its metadata is committed under `.forkmesh/releases/apt/`:

```
dists/stable/Release
dists/stable/InRelease
dists/stable/Release.gpg
dists/stable/main/binary-amd64/Packages
forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc
forkmesh.sources
```

A package's `Filename` is `pool/sha256/<sha256>/forkmesh_<version>_<arch>.deb`.
The `.deb` bytes are never in git; they live in the release store like every
other asset.

The app answers `/apt/*` on `app.forkmesh.com` with a 302:

- `/apt/pool/sha256/<sha256>/<name>.deb` goes to
  `/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/releases/blob/sha256/<sha256>`, so downloads
  are counted and served from the mirrors as usual;
- the six metadata files go to
  `/api/repo/forkmesh/forkmesh/raw?path=.forkmesh/releases/apt/<file>&ref=main`;
- anything else is a 404. Instance-branded nodes do not answer `/apt`.

`apt` is in `CORE_RESERVED_ROUTE_PREFIXES`, so no account or organization can
take a name the route would hide. `forkmesh.com/apt/*` reaches the same routes
through the static site's `forkmesh-www` Worker, which 308s two-segment paths
to the app; the source
file names `app.forkmesh.com` directly so apt takes one redirect less.

apt verifies `InRelease` against the key named in `Signed-By`, and each file
against the hashes in `Release`, so the redirects and mirrors are not trusted.
Each file is read from `main` separately, so in the minute after a promotion
one request can reach a mirror that already has the new commit and the next
one a mirror that does not; apt then reports a hash mismatch for `Packages`,
and the next `apt update` succeeds.

## Signing key

The key is an OpenPGP Ed25519 signing key, separate from the Ed25519 release
key that signs `release.json`: apt reads only OpenPGP signatures. It was
created on the release host with

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh-apt-repo.py init-key \
  --signing-key ~/projects/forkmesh/data/core/release/apt-signing-key.asc
```

which refuses to replace an existing key and writes the public half to
`tools/package/apt/forkmesh-archive-keyring.asc`. The secret key is
`data/core/release/apt-signing-key.asc` (0600), next to the Android keystore
and Authenticode certificate; `FORKMESH_APT_SIGNING_KEY` overrides the path.
It must be backed up with them. If it is lost, every installed system fails
`apt update` until its owner downloads a new keyring.

`forkmesh-apt-repo.py publish` refuses to sign with a key that is not the
committed public key, signs with SHA-512 (the Sequoia `sqv` verifier in
Debian 13 and newer apt rejects SHA-1), and verifies the result with `gpgv`
before it returns.

## Release host

After the gate promotes a candidate and the promoted manifest verifies,
`publish_and_promote` calls `refresh_apt_repository`. When `latest` carries
`forkmesh-linux-x86_64.deb`, it reads the `.deb` from the local release store
by hash, runs `forkmesh-apt-repo.py publish` into the promotion worktree and
adds `.forkmesh/releases/apt` to the same metadata commit as `latest`, so apt
and the installer switch together when that commit reaches `main`. The blob
is seeded to the mirrors with the other assets before the merge.

- No `.deb` in `latest`: nothing changes.
- No signing key: logged, and the repository keeps its previous release.
- The `.deb` missing from the store, or signing or verification failing:
  the step fails and nothing is promoted.

The repository starts with the first release built after this change. Until
then `dists/` does not exist and `apt update` reports a 404 for the source.

## Tested

`app/tests/test_apt_repository.py` covers the package, the metadata and the
signatures. The whole path was checked end to end with a throwaway key: on
Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04 and Debian 12, `apt install` with the setup files in place
(no conffile prompt) and `apt upgrade` from `1.5.0+2` to `1.5.0+3`; Debian 13's
apt 3.0 (`sqv`) verified the same repository.

pages.title: Auto-deploy: main to the core nodes
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Auto-deploy: main to the core nodes

Part of [Operations](README.md).

A push to `main` that changes the served stack deploys it to the cores: the
same deploy an operator runs with `tools/next_deploy.py`, driven by a ForkMesh
Actions workflow and an agent on the operator box. `.forkmesh/deploy.yml` is
manual-only and refuses. `python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py pause <reason>` or
`disarm` stops it. Fleet map: [fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md); commands:
[runbook](runbook.md).

## Pieces

| Piece | Where | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workflow | `.forkmesh/deploy-nodes.yml` ("Deploy nodes") | queued by a push to `main` matching `on.push.paths`, or by *Run workflow*; pinned to the source node; only watches |
| Agent | `tools/next_autodeploy.py serve`, user unit `forkmesh-node-deploy.service`, installed copy in `~/projects/forkmesh/bin/node-deploy/` | decides, gates and deploys |
| Deploy tool | `tools/next_deploy.py` in a clean worktree pinned to the commit | build, upload, migrate, rolling restart |
| Alerts | `POST /api/accounts/admin-operator-alert` (`app/src/operator_alerts.py`) | admin-signed Pings and email |

**Why an agent outside the sandbox.** Workflow steps run sandboxed as
`nobody` with no access to fleet credentials, and must not get them. The
agent runs as the operator and reads fleet files in place. It trusts only
run metadata the desktop writes, writes its log into the run workspace with
`O_EXCL`/`O_NOFOLLOW`, and ends with `::node-deploy-result:: ok|fail <message>`.

The agent runs its installed copy, so a commit cannot change how it decides
before it has passed the gates of the agent already running; it then updates
itself to that commit (*Self-update*). `python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py
install` copies `tools/next_autodeploy.py`, `next_common.py`,
`forkmesh_paths.py`, `deploy/core/render.py` and `caddy_routes.py` into
`~/projects/forkmesh/bin/node-deploy/` and writes the unit. Everything else
(`next_deploy.py`, `next_fleet.py`, `next_dns.py`, the tests) runs from the
pinned worktree or the test archive of the commit being deployed.

## Where the agent finds runs

The desktop writes each run's `meta.json` under
`~/projects/forkmesh/data/actions/runs/`; its sandbox tree (the run's
`/workspace`, where the agent writes `node-deploy.log`) goes wherever
`ActionStore::sandboxDir()` puts it: `data/actions/sandbox/`, or
`<TMP mount>/ForkMesh/actions/sandbox/` when a disk labelled `TMP` is in use
([TMP disk](../desktop/tmp-disk.md)). `running_runs` scans both, finding the
TMP disk the way the desktop does (`/dev/disk/by-label/TMP` matched against
`/proc/self/mounts`), and keeps the newest `forkmesh-run-<id>-<ms>` per run.

An agent that sees no runs never deploys, so it cannot fix itself by
self-update: a stale installed copy needs `install` by hand. The workflow's
timeout therefore ends with a `FAILED: ... Fix: ...` line naming the
stale-copy case and the `install` command.

## Trigger

- **Only `main`** of the served repository, and only commits on the source
  checkout's `main`. Branch, pull-request and fork runs are refused. Merges
  made on the cores deploy once the source publisher brings them into the
  checkout.
- **Only served-stack paths** (`classify`):
  - *release paths* (`app/`, `office/`, `world/`, `www/public/`,
    `www/worker.js`, `www/wrangler.production.toml`, `deploy/`,
    `marketplace/packages/`, marketplace catalog files,
    `tools/rqlite_migrate.py`, `tools/next_*.py`) start an app release;
  - *roll paths* (`server/`, `deploy/core/`, `tools/mirror_gateway.py`, not
    Markdown) need a node roll. `deploy/core/` covers `render.py`,
    `caddy_routes.py` and `templates/`, so a Caddy change reaches the cores
    through the roll's `files` and `start` steps (`start` reloads Caddy).
  Tests never count. Changed paths are those of the whole push.
- The workflow's path filter is a prefilter generated by
  `python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py workflow-paths` and checked by
  `deploy/tests/test_next_autodeploy.py`.
- **Debounce:** deploy once `main` is quiet for a few seconds (10-minute cap);
  deploy the tip; every waiting run the deployed commit contains gets the
  result.
- **Pause after a deploy:** once a deploy has restarted the cores, the next
  one waits `DEPLOY_COOLDOWN_SECONDS` (5 minutes), so merges landing in that
  window ship as one deploy. A deploy that failed before restarting anything
  (gates 1 to 3) does not pause the next one, so a fix ships at once.
- Fast-forwarding `main` to a commit first pushed on a branch queues no main
  run; merge with `--no-ff` or run `deploy --commit <sha>`.

## Gates, in order

1. **Fast-forward only.** Read each core's running revision from
   `/api/version`, locate it (deploy manifest, the commit itself, or a served
   tree signature) and refuse a rollback unless the run is a manual rollback.
   If nothing served changed, end green. If no core answers at all, treat the
   operator box as offline and wait up to 30 minutes rather than blaming a
   node. If some cores answer and others give no HTTP answer, ask the silent
   ones again every 30 seconds for up to 5 minutes (a short loss of the
   operator box's own route looks the same). A core still silent after that,
   or one the DNS health loop holds or has taken out of DNS, is skipped
   (*Skipped cores*). A core in DNS that answers with an HTTP error fails the
   gate at once.
2. **Tests** from a clean `git archive` in a no-network sandbox with no home:
   a must-pass set (`app/tests/host/test_host_e2e.py`, `deploy/tests`, host
   shim, request guard, apps e2e, timer, desktop and operator-alert pings,
   the `security` suite of `tools/run_critical_tests.py` and the
   destructive-delete scanner), `go test ./...` in `server/`, plus *no new
   failures* in `app/tests/host` against the deployed commit (baseline
   cached). Must-pass entries may be files, folders or single test ids.
   Files run in parallel at low priority while the build and upload proceed.
   The Go tests run beside them in the same sandbox with the host's Go
   toolchain bound read-only (`GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, `GOPROXY=off`, a per-run
   `GOCACHE`). Go is found on the agent's `PATH`, then in `/usr/local/go`,
   `/usr/lib/go`, `~/go` or `~/.local/go`; without it every deploy fails here
   rather than skipping the Go tests.

   Go tests that fail are run once more after the Python files finish, alone
   (`-count=1 -p 1 -run` with only the failed top-level tests); the gate fails
   only if they fail again, and a test that passes its rerun is named in the
   log. Reason: the real-time call and QUIC tests (failover audio within
   500 ms, a multipath gap within one round trip, 70% of frames through
   impaired links, the anti-amplification allowance) miss by tens of
   milliseconds when twelve pytest workers, the build and the upload share
   the box. `TestThreePeopleHoldACallThroughImpairedLinks`,
   `TestAntiAmplificationLimit`, `TestMultipathPathFailureAudio` and
   `TestCoreDeathMovesTheCallToTheStandbyCore` also give their timing checks
   three attempts themselves ([server](../server/README.md)),
   which helps even before the agent has updated itself, since the Go tests
   come from the commit being deployed. A real regression fails both runs.
3. **Build** in a fresh detached worktree.
4. **Deploy:** upload, migrate, then a rolling restart one core at a time
   (the first chosen per release), each gated on `/readyz` (never ready while
   sealed) and the running revision before the next one restarts, with
   per-node rollback.
5. **Verify** on each node: `/readyz`, `/api/version`, the node name's
   `/readyz`, `/dashboard`, `/login`, and the World deploy marker, retrying up
   to 2 minutes.

## Skipped cores

One core down must not stop a fix from shipping, so gate 1 and `next_deploy`
skip cores that cannot take the release:

- **Which cores are skipped.** A core whose entry in `dns-health.json` is
  held (drained, a failed roll, joining) or out of DNS, without waiting for
  it; and a core in DNS that gives no HTTP answer at all after the 5-minute
  re-ask. An HTTP error from a core in DNS still fails the gate: the health
  loop takes it out of DNS within a few probes, and the next deploy skips
  it.
- **Never below a majority.** The cores that get the release must be a
  majority of `deploy/fleet.toml`'s cores and at least two
  (`next_common.deploy_quorum`: 2 of 3, 3 of 5); otherwise gate 1 fails and
  nothing is skipped.
- **Everything else is unchanged** for the cores that get it: the tests,
  the migration, one core at a time with the readiness and revision gate,
  IDS expectations, verification (of those cores only).
- **One decision per deploy.** The agent passes its list to every
  `next_deploy` step in `FMNEXT_DEPLOY_SKIP` (empty when it skips nothing),
  so `upload` and `restart` agree even if DNS changes meanwhile. A commit
  whose `next_deploy.py` predates skipping (a rollback) cannot skip, and the
  agent refuses rather than restart only some cores and stop at the down
  one. By hand, `next_deploy.py upload|restart|all` finds the same cores
  itself (DNS state, then an SSH probe), or takes `--skip nN`.
- **Recorded.** The log, the run result and an admin Ping (`deploy-skipped`)
  name the skipped cores and why; `deploy-manifest.json` gives the release
  `skipped`; `state.json` keeps `behind`: `nodes` (release missed) and `roll`
  (node roll missed). When a roll is needed it runs on the deployed cores
  only (`next_fleet.py roll nA nB`), and the skipped ones go into
  `behind.roll` so the advanced `lastRoll` does not lose them.
- **Catch-up.** Every 5 minutes (`CATCH_UP_SECONDS`) while `behind` is not
  empty, the idle agent takes the deploy lock (never waiting for it) and
  asks every core's `/api/version`. When the other cores agree on one
  revision and a behind core answers and is not held, it brings that core
  alone to that revision from the pinned worktree: `build` only if the
  tarball was pruned, `upload nN`, `restart nN`, then `next_fleet.py roll
  nN` if it missed a roll (unless `manual-roll`), then the usual
  verification of that core. A core that runs something that is not an
  ancestor of the others' release is left for a human. Success Pings
  (`core-caught-up`); a failure emails once per distinct error
  (`core-catch-up-failed`) and is tried again. `next_deploy restart nN`
  moves the core from `skipped` to `caughtUp` in the manifest.
- **The gap.** A core the health loop re-adds to DNS before its catch-up
  serves the previous release for up to 5 minutes, the same mix a rolling
  restart has (migrations already allow the old release on the new schema).
- `status` shows `wouldSkip` when gate 1 would skip a core now, and
  `state.behind`.

## Node rolls

After the release passes (or for a roll-only push), the agent runs
`python3 tools/next_fleet.py roll --execute` from the pinned worktree under
the deploy lock: one core at a time, drain, wait the DNS TTL plus 30 s
(`ROLL_DRAIN_MARGIN_SECONDS`, 90 s in all), install `daemon,files,start`,
check readyz, units and IDS, undrain, stop at the first failure. Roll paths
are counted since the last successful roll, so a skipped roll is caught up.
When `server/` changed, it then runs `roll-runners --idle-wait 0`, which
never restarts a runner with active job scopes; busy runners are retried every
10 minutes ([runners](runners.md)). Failures Ping and email and are kept
in `state.json` until `next_autodeploy.py ack-roll`. Create
`<fleet config>/autodeploy/manual-roll` to only report that a roll is needed.

By hand: `python3 tools/next_fleet.py roll [nN ...] [--mail] --execute`,
`roll-runners [rN ...] --execute`, then `ack-roll`.

## Self-update

Once idle, the agent compares its installed files with those of the last
commit whose deploy passed gate 2 and ended green (`state.json` `tested`,
written for `auto` and `manual` deploys, never for `rollback`). The
comparison is by git blob hash (`git hash-object` of each installed file
against `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`), never by mtime. If they differ:

1. **Only when idle:** no deploy running, no run queued, no runner-roll
   retry running, auto-deploy armed. A queued run is deployed first. While
   the update runs and restarts, the agent attaches no new run, so the
   restarted agent picks up every waiting run from the run folders.
2. **Once per set of files:** the hash of the commit's agent files is
   recorded in `state.json` `selfUpdate` before anything runs. The same files
   are never tried again; changed files on a later commit get one new attempt.
3. **Under the deploy lock** (`wait=0`; a busy lock retries a minute later).
4. **Stage and check:** in the pinned worktree at the commit, run
   `install --stage <cache>/node-deploy/agent-stage`, then
   `<stage>/next_autodeploy.py self-check`, which imports every module from
   the staged folder, builds the agent and its notifier as `serve` does, and
   prints `next_autodeploy self-check ok`. A failure stops here and nothing
   installed changes.
5. **Install:** copy the current files and unit into
   `bin/node-deploy.previous/`, run `install --no-restart` from the worktree,
   check the installed hashes match the commit, arm a watch
   (`systemd-run --user`, unit `forkmesh-node-deploy-watch-<hash>`, in 180 s,
   running the previous copy's `self-update-watch`), then
   `systemctl --user restart --no-block forkmesh-node-deploy.service`.
6. **Confirm:** the new agent's `serve` marks `selfUpdate` `ok`, records
   `state.json` `agent`, and Pings "Node deploy agent updated to <rev>".
7. **Failure:** a failed stage, check, install, watch or restart puts the
   previous files and unit back where they were already replaced, marks
   `selfUpdate` `failed`, logs `self-update: FAILED`, and Pings and emails
   "Node deploy agent update to <rev> failed". If the new agent has not
   confirmed after 180 s, the watch restores the previous copy, restarts the
   unit, and alerts the same way. Nothing is deleted.

After a failure, fix the agent on `main` (new files get a new attempt) or run
`install` by hand. `status` shows `selfUpdate` and `agent`.

`tools/forkmesh_paths.py` is not a served path, so a push that changes only
it starts no deploy; the agent takes it with the next green deploy.

## The website Worker

forkmesh.com is still the `forkmesh-www` Cloudflare Worker (`www/worker.js`).
After a good deploy the agent compares its `x-forkmesh-deploy-fingerprint`
with the hash of the target's `www/` tree and, if they differ, runs
`npx wrangler deploy --config wrangler.production.toml` from the pinned
worktree with Node 22 and credentials from `config/fleet/cloudflare.env`. The
node roll runs before the website step, so a website failure never skips a
roll.

## Safety

- **One deploy at a time:** `<fleet config>/deploy.lock` (`flock`) is taken by
  every `next_deploy --execute`, `next_fleet roll` and `install`, and by the
  agent (deploys, runner-roll retries and its self-update), which passes it to
  children as `FMNEXT_DEPLOY_LOCK_FD`.
- **Kill switch:** auto-deploy needs `autodeploy/armed` and no
  `autodeploy/paused` (`pause`, `resume`, `disarm`). Manual deploys still work.
- **Manual triggers:** `deploy --commit <sha|main> [--skip-tests]`,
  `rollback --rev <rev> [--run-tests]` (also the way past gate 1 after a
  history rewrite), *Run workflow*, the desktop's Deploy app button, and
  `next_deploy.py rollback nN --execute`.
- **Alerts:** every failed or refused deploy Pings admins; a second failure in
  a row also emails them.
- **Weak networks:** probes retry dropped connections; uploads resume a
  dropped scp.
- **rqlite tunnel:** `next_deploy.open_rqlite_tunnel` picks the first loopback
  address that accepts connections (`127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `127.0.0.2`) so a
  local firewall dropping one address does not block deploys; errors end with
  a concrete `Fix: …`.
- `python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py status` prints the switch, lock holder,
  last deploy and failure, pending rolls, live revisions, `wouldSkip` and
  `state.behind`.

## World deploy notice

`next_deploy.py` writes the `world_deploy_status` row (`deploying`, `ready`,
`failed`) for whole-fleet commands; the World client polls
`/api/world/deploy-status` and offers a refresh. Status alerts are suppressed
while deploying and for 5 minutes after.

## Files

| File | Written by |
| --- | --- |
| `<fleet config>/deploy.lock` | `next_deploy`, `next_fleet`, the agent |
| `<fleet config>/deploy-manifest.json` | `next_deploy` after a full-fleet restart (`skipped`), and a catch-up restart (`caughtUp`) |
| `<fleet config>/dns-health.json` | `next_dns.py` (read by gate 1 and `next_deploy` to skip cores out of DNS) |
| `<fleet config>/autodeploy/{armed,paused,manual-roll,state.json}` | `next_autodeploy.py` |
| `<fleet logs>/autodeploy/*.log` | the agent and manual runs |
| `~/projects/forkmesh/cache/node-deploy/` | test archives and venvs |
| `~/projects/forkmesh/worktrees/node-deploy` | the pinned build worktree |
| `~/projects/forkmesh/bin/node-deploy/` | the installed agent |
| `~/projects/forkmesh/bin/node-deploy.previous/` | the copy before the last self-update |

`<fleet config>` is `$FMNEXT_CONFIG_DIR` or `~/projects/forkmesh/config/fleet`;
`<fleet logs>` is `$FMNEXT_LOGS_DIR` or `~/projects/forkmesh/logs/fleet`.

## Install

```sh
python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py install
python3 tools/next_autodeploy.py status
```

The unit starts disarmed. After the first install the agent updates itself;
a copy older than self-update (2026-10-21) needs one `install` by hand. Gate
changes apply from the deploy after the one that brought them.
`install --stage <dir>` copies the files only; `install --no-restart`
installs without restarting the unit. If runs never report a result, compare
the installed copy with `tools/`.

## Restarts without 502s and 503s

A rollout must never take cores away from clients still using them (restarting
two of three cores together, or restarting a core seconds after its DNS drain,
gave users "HTTP 502" and `503 {"error":"sealed"}`). So:

- Restarts go one core at a time (`tools/next_deploy.py` `restart`); each
  must pass `/readyz` and report the new revision before the next starts.
- A roll waits out the DNS TTL plus 30 s after the drain, before the core
  restarts (`tools/next_fleet.py` `roll`).
- Caddy keeps a request waiting for the local App for up to
  `APP_UPSTREAM_TRY_SECONDS` (30 s, `deploy/core/render.py`), which covers an
  App restart. If the App is still unreachable, the shared names answer
  `{"error":"upstream_unavailable"}` with `Retry-After: 5` (the
  `upstream_errors` snippet). The status stays 502 or 504, because the
  forkmesh.com Worker falls back to the per-node names only on those
  (`www/worker.js` `APP_FALLBACK_STATUSES`). The Caddy install check allows
  `CADDY_INSTALL_MAX_TIME` (35 s) per request, so a fresh core's `/readyz`
  is not cut off while Caddy waits for the App.
- The Notes page retries a failed read 3 times (0.5, 1.5 and 4 s), as
  `fetchJson` already did, and shows "ForkMesh is restarting" rather than
  "HTTP 502".

Still exposed: a browser keeps reusing an HTTP/2 connection to a drained
core, so DNS does not move it. For those clients the 30 s Caddy wait and the
client retries hide the restart.

pages.title: Breakout authorization replica
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Breakout authorization replica

Part of [Operations](README.md).

Mirrors replicate repository data through Git and signed ledgers. Managing
repositories while the controller is unreachable also needs authorization
data, but copying account or session tables to every public host would make
each mirror a credential database. Instead each node holds a narrow, signed
authorization projection in SQLite, and browsers carry a controller-signed
portable session grant. This is how a mirror keeps working when the core nodes
are unreachable ([censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md),
[architecture](../architecture.md)); the dashboard side is in
[direct-HTTPS mirror gateway](direct-https-mirror-gateway.md#same-codebase-dashboard).

## Projection contents

Each monotonically numbered generation contains only: opaque account id and
public username; enabled device or passkey public keys and their capabilities;
public repository ids with owner/collaborator roles; key, account, and
repository revocation generations; and issue time, expiry, previous digest,
and Ed25519 signature.

It never contains email addresses, password hashes or reset state, TOTP seeds,
bearer or session tokens, private-message metadata, payment state, administrator
privileges, or encrypted account/repository rows. It is built by a dedicated
query, never a database export.

## Synchronization

A node refreshes after each controller authorization event and on the reconcile
interval. It verifies signature, schema, strictly increasing generation,
previous digest, size, and expiry, then applies one SQLite transaction. A bad
generation is discarded and the last good one stays. Peers exchange only
controller-signed generations. Repository content keeps syncing through Git and
event spools; this database only decides who may sign changes.

## Sessions

Each controller login also mints a signed portable session grant (opaque ids,
public username, issue/expiry, mirror-dashboard audience; no bearer token). It
travels in a separate HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict parent-domain cookie,
and mirrors verify it with the published router key. The grant lives at most
twelve hours, never outlives its controller session, and is cleared on logout
or session/device revocation. Tampering, ambiguous cookies, future grants,
expiry, and unknown keys fail closed. Custom-domain fleets set
`PORTABLE_SESSION_COOKIE_DOMAIN`.

Mirrors never accept password-only authentication: a password verifier on
every node would be offline attack material. Without a portable grant, an
enrolled device or passkey signs a node nonce bound to the origin and
authorization generation, creating a short-lived node-local session.

## Recovery

During an outage, authorized mutations land in local Git and signed spools.
On recovery the node reconciles revocations, forwards events idempotently,
fetches the newest generation, and reconciles refs. Billing, password reset,
account recovery, private data, and platform administration always fail
closed on a mirror.
