pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Business-model rollout and recovery

Part of [Operations](README.md).

This runbook publishes the free-protocol / paid-services boundary of the
[business model](../business-model.md) without giving the hosted operator
control over protocol participation.

## Owners and release gate

Name a product owner, infrastructure-cost owner, support owner, and privacy or
legal reviewer before enabling a managed checkout. Managed checkout stays
disabled while any gate in `www/public/business-model.json` is open.

```sh
python3 tools/unit_economics.py validate-contract
python3 tools/quality_gate.py run --profile core
python3 tools/unit_economics.py report --input /path/to/period.json
python3 tools/unit_economics.py launch-gate --input /path/to/period.json
```

A period file combines the admin usage report, invoice-backed costs, and
aggregate funnel counts. Never pass the launch gate with synthetic evidence or
zero-valued missing costs.

## Supported surfaces

- Contract page and pricing: current desktop and mobile browsers.
- Portable proof: standard Git plus the web app.
- Self-hosted desktop: macOS, Windows, and Linux release packages.
- Managed mirror evidence: the Linux headless mirror service.

Self-hosted deployments receive documentation and community support unless a
separate support order names the platform.

## Deployment

1. Validate the contract JSON, visible matrix, docs links, analytics allowlist,
   and unit-economics tests.
2. Confirm `/business-model.json`, `/docs/business-model`, `/#pricing`,
   `/privacy`, and `/terms` are served.
3. Confirm the managed plan says `research-preview-not-for-sale`, has no
   checkout control, and no variable-cost service says unlimited.
4. Deploy the site; deploy the app only when the admin usage projection changed.

## Failure paths

| Failure | Required behavior | Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract JSON malformed or drifts from the matrix | CI/deploy fails | Fix source and matrix together |
| Provider analytics unconfigured | Usage endpoint returns `analytics_unconfigured`; cost unknown | Restore the scoped token and retry |
| Provider analytics unavailable | Usage endpoint returns `analytics_unavailable`; never record zero | Retry later or reconcile the invoice |
| A cost source is missing | Period report incomplete; launch gate fails | Attach an attributable source |
| Export or restore differs | Trial stops | Restore the last verified copy, fix the exporter, repeat |
| Optional analytics denied | No product event is sent | Continue; consent is never a service condition |

## Rollback

The contract deployment changes no protocol object, repository, identity,
entitlement, or customer data. Roll the site back to the last reviewed asset
revision. Never roll back by deleting repositories or signed collaboration
records; a pricing rollback cannot revoke license rights or make an export paid.

## Recovery and portability drill

Before the first managed trial and each material format change: export a
disposable project from the managed service without a paid-only exporter,
import it into a clean self-hosted deployment with hosted routes disabled,
compare all Git refs, object ids, and signed `.forkmesh` records, collaborate
from the self-host, then restore the managed service from the same export. Any
mismatch blocks launch.

## Telemetry and privacy

The infrastructure projection is aggregate and holds only fixed unit ids and
quantities. Period files may hold aggregate funnel counts, revenue, and cost
labels, never account or repository names, paths, IP addresses, request ids,
provider customer ids, or interviewee identity. Pricing-page events use the
default-off first-party analytics controller and are sent only after explicit
consent; Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track disable them.

pages.title: Community reward pool
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Community reward pool

Part of [Operations](README.md).

The reward system is non-custodial. The server coordinates public Solana state
and unsigned transfer intents; it never creates, accepts, stores, or uses a
wallet private key. The desktop's local signer ([below](#local-signer)) is
the only component that signs an outgoing pool transaction.

## Custody boundaries

- Contributors sign direct transfers from their own wallets to the public pool
  address.
- The pool private key lives only in the instance owner's desktop client,
  inside its encrypted local vault. The client shows and validates every
  source, destination, amount, network, and expiry before the owner approves.
- The database stores only public addresses, Solana Pay references, eligibility
  snapshots, unsigned plans, transaction signatures, and status.
- The server fetches each finalized transaction and requires its System Program
  transfer list to match the approved intent exactly.
- Node operators supply only a public payout address.

User funds, pool funds, pending rewards, and completed transfers are separate
states. Contributions are voluntary community support, not investments.

## Configuration

```text
COMMUNITY_REWARD_NETWORK=mainnet-beta
COMMUNITY_REWARD_RPC_URL=https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com
COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS=<public address>   # or TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS
REWARD_SIGNER_ACCOUNT=<instance owner account>
REWARD_INTERVAL_MS=3600000
REWARD_JITTER_MAX_MS=2700000
REWARD_AMOUNT_LAMPORTS=100000
REWARD_MIN_UPTIME_MS=1800000
REWARD_MIN_CONTRIBUTION_UNITS=0
REWARD_HEALTH_FRESH_MS=600000
```

`COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS` wins when set; an invalid value fails closed
rather than falling back. The pool is exposed only when the network is known,
the RPC is credential-free HTTPS, `getGenesisHash` matches the cluster, and the
pool account exists. Devnet requires explicit development configuration.

## Contributions

`POST /api/rewards/contributions` with `action=prepare` returns a one-hour,
reference-bound Solana Pay URI:

- `trickle` leaves the contribution in the pool for randomized rounds;
- `instant_all_nodes` creates an equal unsigned plan for every eligible node,
  in batches of at most eight transfers.

Confirmation checks finality, the reference, destination, amount, replay, and
that it is an ordinary System transfer. No outgoing plan is created while
finality is unknown.

## Randomized mirror rewards

Each interval the server records a round with a reproducible jitter, freezes an
eligibility snapshot, and selects one node by SHA-256 modulo over a finalized
blockhash. The intent publishes the snapshot and its hash, rejection reasons,
entropy, algorithm, selected index, payee, amount, and expiry.

Eligibility requires a fresh signed heartbeat, a healthy direct HTTPS endpoint,
signed identity registration, an independently challenged refs proof matching
the integrity pin, a public payout address, minimum observed uptime, and the
optional contribution threshold. Federated relays must forward each node's
original signed registration and nonce-bound health message; relay approval is
a disclosed, revocable trust boundary. Identity, operator, device key, and
wallet are de-duplicated. These gates reduce Sybil risk but do not eliminate it.

## Pending walletless rewards

The instance owner can create a pending allocation
(`POST /api/rewards/pending-awards`) for an active recipient without a payout
wallet. It moves no funds, expires after 24 hours, and lets the recipient
submit a public address through `POST /api/rewards/pending`.

## Public inspection

`GET /api/rewards/pool` (and its alias `GET /api/accounts/central-fund`) shows
network, address, live balance, timing and amount settings, contribution modes,
recent finalized transfers, and the non-custodial notice. Retired custodial
deposit endpoints return HTTP 410. Legacy custodial keys are handled in
[Legacy Solana custody migration](legacy-solana-custody-migration.md).

## Local signer

The desktop **Control node** page ([desktop control node](desktop-control-node.md))
is the only component that can sign an outgoing community-pool transaction.
The server schedules and stores public plans but never receives a seed,
private key, passphrase, or signed transaction bytes. Signing is an
explicitly approved local flow, not an unattended hot wallet.

### Provisioning

Server configuration (public values only): `COMMUNITY_REWARD_NETWORK`,
`COMMUNITY_REWARD_RPC_URL`, `COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS` (or
`TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS`), and `REWARD_SIGNER_ACCOUNT` (fallback
`INSTANCE_OWNER_ACCOUNT`). The pool address must match the key imported on the
desktop.

On the owner's device: sign in as the signer account, open **Control node →
First-instance reward-pool signer**, import an existing 64-byte Solana CLI
keypair (JSON byte array or base58), set a strong vault passphrase, and choose
the network and a public HTTPS JSON-RPC origin. The importer rejects 32-byte
seeds, recovery phrases, and keypairs whose public half does not match; it never
generates a key. RPC URLs with credentials, query strings, paths, or plain HTTP
are rejected.

### Local vault

`reward-pool/pool-key.vault` in the application-data directory holds the public
address (authenticated as additional data), a scrypt salt (`N=32768`, `r=8`,
`p=1`), an AES-256-GCM nonce, the encrypted 32-byte Ed25519 seed, and the tag.
The file must be owner-only, symlinks are refused, and writes are atomic. The
passphrase and seed exist only during one approved operation. The key is never
written to settings, server storage, logs, or command lines. Back up the
original key with trusted wallet procedures; it cannot be recovered.

### Queue contract

```text
GET /api/rewards/signing-jobs?signer=<account>&ts=<epoch-ms>&sig=<identity-signature>
```

The identity signs `forkmesh-reward-jobs-v1\n<signer>\n<epoch-ms>`. The server
returns at most 50 jobs for the configured signer. The desktop requires custody
`external-local-signer` and validates each job: kind, status, expiry, network,
source address, plan schema 2, `custody.forkMeshHoldsUserKeys=false`,
`signing.method=external-local-qt`, an allowed policy
(`randomized-eligible-mirror-v2`, `instant-all-eligible-mirrors-v1`,
`pending-reward-claim-v1`), valid unique destinations with positive amounts
within per-policy caps, and no secret-shaped fields. Anything else stays
unsigned.

### Review and signing

**Review, sign and submit** shows source, total, every destination and amount,
policy, network, intent, and expiry; Cancel is the default. After approval the
desktop fetches a finalized blockhash and builds a legacy transaction with the
pool as sole signer and fee payer and only the reviewed System Program
transfers (at most 1,232 bytes). It reparses the serialized transaction and
rejects any deviation before unlocking the vault, then signs the exact message.

### Broadcast and reconciliation

The desktop broadcasts via `sendTransaction` with preflight, checks the returned
signature matches its own, and persists only public recovery fields. It reports
the receipt to `POST /api/rewards/signing-jobs` signed over
`forkmesh-reward-submit-v1\n<signer>\n<intent-id>\n<transaction-signature>\n<epoch-ms>`.
`202` means submitted. The server fetches the finalized transaction and marks
the intent complete only if it contains exactly the planned transfers; a
signature cannot be replayed across intents. **Reconcile last submission**
recovers after an interruption.

### Operational checks

Before funding a production pool, run `forkmesh-reward-pool-tests`, verify vault
permissions, rehearse the full flow on devnet, confirm the server account, pool
address, vault address, network, and RPC agree, and run the read-only preflight:

```bash
python3 tools/validate_reward_mainnet.py \
  --rpc-url https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com \
  --pool-address "${COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS:-${TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS:-}}"
```

It calls only `getGenesisHash`, `getAccountInfo`, and `getBalance`. Establish key
backup, compromise response, and rotation procedures before going live.

pages.title: Custodial deposit addresses for world-element purchases
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Custodial deposit addresses for world-element purchases

Part of [Operations](README.md).

The World element store accepts two payment methods. The second is optional.

| | Direct | Deposit |
|---|---|---|
| Buyer pays | the published pool address | a temporary ForkMesh address |
| Who holds the key | the buyer | **ForkMesh**, until the sweep lands |
| Confirmation | buyer submits the transaction signature | automatic; the address is watched |
| Mirror half | unsigned intent, signed on the operator's device | paid by the sweep transaction |

## Custody model

For a deposit, the server generates a fresh Ed25519 keypair, stores the seed
encrypted in `world_element_purchases`, and shows the public key as the payment
address. Once funded, it signs one transaction sending half to the treasury and
half to eligible online mirror nodes, then clears `deposit_secret`. Until the
sweep lands (a failed sweep is retried by cron), anyone who controls the server,
its database, or `DATA_KEY` can move those funds. The community reward pool key
is not involved.

The store shows custody text before purchase, and `/api/world/store/catalog`
marks the deposit entry with `forkMeshHoldsDepositKey: true`. Never describe
this method as non-custodial.

## Configuration

Deposits are off unless `TREASURY_SOLANA_ADDRESS` (or
`COMMUNITY_REWARD_POOL_ADDRESS`) is set. `CUSTODIAL_DEPOSITS = "0"` keeps the
treasury but disables deposits; buyers then see only the direct method.

## Invariants

- The shared read helper `_solana_rpc` cannot send; only `_solana_rpc_write`
  broadcasts, and only `sendTransaction`.
- The sweep is idempotent on `sweep_signature` and clears the seed on success;
  concurrent pollers cannot double-send.
- Payees come from the signed eligibility snapshot (`_eligible_reward_snapshot`),
  capped at `MAX_SWEEP_PAYEES`.

## Monitoring

A funded address with an empty `sweep_signature` and a `sweep_error` means the
server still holds a key for real funds:

```sql
SELECT purchase_id, deposit_address, sweep_error FROM world_element_purchases
WHERE method='deposit' AND deposit_secret<>'' AND sweep_signature='';
```

`treasury_not_configured` means the treasury variable was removed after the
address was minted; restore it and cron finishes the sweep.

pages.title: Direct-HTTPS independent mirror gateway
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Direct-HTTPS independent mirror gateway

Part of [Operations](README.md).

`tools/mirror_gateway.py` is the repository-byte origin of an independently
operated ForkMesh mirror. It listens on loopback HTTP only; an
operator-controlled HTTPS reverse proxy terminates public TLS. Git clients use
the mirror's standard `/<owner>/<repository>.git` Smart-HTTP URL directly. The
routing service on the core nodes keeps the stable clone URL and redirects there
only after a fresh signed mirror proof. This page is the detail under the
[mirroring](../mirroring.md) and [self-hosting](../self-hosting.md) pillars; the
daemon that drives it is the [mirror node](mirror-node.md).

Repository bytes always travel over HTTPS. The node event WebSocket only
announces changes (and renews the endpoint lease); the node daemon then fetches
over HTTPS, with a slow reconcile interval as recovery for missed events.

The Git data plane is read-only: it implements `upload-pack`, not general
`receive-pack`, issue writes or administration. Writes are opt-in per
repository (`merge-pull`, `git-receive-pack`, or a writable root for
push-created repositories). Requests without valid signed device headers get
`401 push_unauthorized` from the routing service before any body is read
(see [mobile node contract](../mobile/mobile-node-contract.md) section 7).
Owner-authorized stock Git writes use the [SSH gateway](git-ssh-gateway.md);
the [stock Git compatibility matrix](../git-compatibility.md) lists the split.

## Security boundary

- The listener must be `127.0.0.1`, `::1` or `localhost`.
- Public upload-pack reads need no capability. Every control, mutation, private
  and non-Git request needs a fresh, single-use Ed25519 capability from the
  routing service, bound to method, path plus query, body digest, node, request
  ID and issue time.
- Unknown, private, disabled and integrity-quarantined repositories all return
  the same `404 {"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}`. Health and manifest
  responses never enumerate repositories.
- Only configured public repositories are served, each pinned by a SHA-256
  over its sorted heads and tags, checked at startup and before serving.
- Git runs without a shell and with config, prompts, helpers, fsmonitor and
  pack hooks disabled.
- `refs/forkmesh/` is internal node state. Upload-pack hides the namespace and
  keeps `allowTipSHA1InWant`, `allowReachableSHA1InWant` and
  `allowAnySHA1InWant` disabled so hidden tips cannot be fetched by object ID.
  The SSH gateway applies the same rule plus `receive.hideRefs`.
- Release files are content addressed and re-hashed before sending.
- Logs hold only time, request ID, operation, status, duration and byte count.
- The configuration accepts no key, token, password or credential field.

Schemas: configuration
[`mirror-gateway-config.schema.json`](../mirror-gateway-config.schema.json);
endpoint manifest
[`mirror-gateway-manifest.schema.json`](../mirror-gateway-manifest.schema.json) (non-proxied public
A/AAAA origin, `mainProxyMode: direct`, `/{owner}/{repository}.git` template).
A node must prove its direct HTTPS endpoint before it is published.

## Identity helpers

The gateway delegates Ed25519 to two shell-free local commands, each reading one
bounded JSON object on stdin and writing one on stdout, with credential-like
environment variables removed. Neither response may contain a private-key field.
[Headless mirror identity](headless-mirror.md#identity) is the VPS
implementation.

| Command | Input `type` | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healthSignerCommand` | `forkmesh.health-challenge-signing` (`publicKey`, `messageBase64`, `messageSha256`) | `publicKey`, `signature` |
| `requestVerifierCommand` | `forkmesh.request-capability-verification` (adds `signature`) | `valid`, `publicKey` |

## Configuration

```bash
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --refs-sha256 /srv/forkmesh/mirrors/example.git
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-gateway.json --check
python3 tools/mirror_gateway.py --config /etc/forkmesh/mirror-gateway.json
```

Main keys: `schemaVersion`, `node` (`name`, `publicKey`), `routerPublicKey`,
`publicOrigin`, `listen` (`host`, `port`), `manifestPath`,
`requestVerifierCommand`, `healthSignerCommand`, `limits`, and `repositories[]`
with `owner`, `name`, `visibility`, `enabled`, `gitDir`, `releaseStore` and
`integrity.expectedRefsSha256`.

- An omitted `visibility` is private. A private entry cannot be enabled or
  carry a storage path; it is never inspected or announced.
- `gitDir` must be an absolute, real, service-owned, non-world-writable bare
  repository. Public data is not encrypted; public `encryptedArchive` entries
  are rejected.
- An omitted `releaseStore` falls back to `<gitDir>/forkmesh-releases` when that
  is a real directory.

## Independent mirror operation

A mirror on its own hostname can offer browsing, clone, push, fork and pull
requests without the control plane. Every capability is opt-in and additive,
and none changes repository identity: dashboard, SSH and mirror URLs are
replaceable metadata over the same canonical repositories.

### Same-codebase dashboard

The gateway can serve the same website as the main App, from the build outputs
(`app/public/**`, `www/public/**`) stored as Git blobs in a mirrored public
repository, so dashboard updates arrive through ordinary sync under the
integrity pin. `api-client.js` resolves its API origin to `location.origin` on
non-canonical hosts.

```json
"dashboard": {
  "enabled": true,
  "assetsRepository": "<owner>/<repo>",
  "canonicalOrigin": "https://app.example.com",
  "sshOrigin": "ssh://git@ssh.example.com",
  "replicaPath": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/gateway/dashboard-replica.json"
}
```

- `assetsRepository` must be an enabled public repository in the same file.
- `canonicalOrigin` receives `/login` and `/signup` when the browser holds no
  valid portable session grant. A mirror never receives passwords, controller
  tokens or session rows.
- `sshOrigin` is shown as each repository's clone/push URL.
- `replicaPath` is a `0600` last-good bundle of the controller's allowlisted
  public projections (`app/src/mirror_replica.py`,
  `app/src/public_snapshots.py`). It is not a database copy; failed refreshes
  keep the prior valid documents, and responses from it carry
  `X-ForkMesh-Replica: public-projection`.

Added routes: static pages and assets, read-only `/api/repositories`,
`/api/version` and `/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/<read-op>` (alias of
`/v1/public/repositories/...`), plus `GET /api/accounts/sessions` and
`POST /api/accounts/session-handoff`, which accept only a controller-signed,
expiry-bounded grant and keep it in an HttpOnly cookie. Rendered documents are
held in bounded LRU caches invalidated on generation change (SIGHUP, or SIGUSR1
for the replica), never by time; large bodies stream.

### SSH writes, pull requests and forks

`tools/ssh_gateway.py` and `tools/ssh_authorization_broker.py` can authorize
from a signed local grants file while the routing service is unreachable,
accept signed contributor pull requests over SSH, and fork a repository for
the caller. All three are configured on the SSH side:
[Git SSH gateway, controller-free operation](git-ssh-gateway.md#controller-free-operation).

### Push-created repositories

Set in the refresh configuration
([`headless-mirror-refresh.schema.json`](../headless-mirror-refresh.schema.json),
[headless refresh](headless-mirror.md#refresh-and-publication)), never by hand in the generated
gateway file:

| Key | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `writableRepositoryRoot` | absolute, real, mode-0700 directory owned by the mirror account |
| `writableOwners` | unique owner names (max 64), or exactly `["*"]`; removing an owner stops reads and pushes from the next refresh |
| `receiveMaxInputBytes` | optional, default 256 MiB; becomes `receive.maxInputSize` |

On a capability-bound push the gateway creates
`<writableRepositoryRoot>/<owner>/<repo>.git`, runs `git receive-pack` with
deletes and repository hooks refused and non-fast-forwards refused unless the
capability carries a `rewrite=` grant (then the gateway's own pre-receive
decides per ref and keeps each replaced tip under `refs/forkmesh/history/`;
see [core push](core-push.md#force-pushes)), records it in
`hosted-pushes.json` (treated as untrusted input) and touches
`/run/forkmesh-mirror-refresh/pending` to trigger a refresh. At most two pushes
run at once (`503 push_busy`). The pushing device, not the node, publishes the
catalog record. These repositories are exempt from the immutable refs pin;
their generation is re-proved on every signed health check.

## Private replicas

Private repositories are never materialized by the gateway. They are stored
as opaque `.fm-private` files (`desktop/src/PrivateMirrorStore.cpp`): a random
id, an AES-256-GCM archive, hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 key wraps per recipient
and a key epoch, with no names or paths ([encryption](../encryption.md)). Rotation re-seals to the exact
recipient set. The gateway streams `/v1/private-replicas/<opaque-id>` only
under a routing capability and cannot decrypt it.

## Routing service contract

The routing service (the App on the core nodes) owns authorization, mirror
selection and bounded failover. Its database stores discovery and health
metadata only. Generate its capability key pair:

```bash
python3 -c 'import base64;from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey as K;from cryptography.hazmat.primitives import serialization as s
k=K.generate();e=lambda b:base64.urlsafe_b64encode(b).decode().rstrip("=")
print("MIRROR_ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY="+e(k.public_key().public_bytes(s.Encoding.Raw,s.PublicFormat.Raw)))
print("MIRROR_ROUTER_SIGNING_SEED="+e(k.private_bytes(s.Encoding.Raw,s.PrivateFormat.Raw,s.NoEncryption())))'
```

Keep the seed in the operator's secret store only (on the cores,
`MIRROR_ROUTER_SIGNING_SEED` in the fleet vault, `deploy/fleet.example.toml`);
mirrors get the public key. On a Workers self-host,
`app/deploy.sh secrets` preserves it and `app/deploy.sh rotate-mirror-router`
changes it.

1. **Registration.** `POST /api/mirrors/https` (`node`, `baseUrl`,
   `mirrorUrl`, `publicKey`, `issuedAt`, `signature` over
   `forkmesh-https-endpoint-v2`). The service verifies the signed
   `/forkmesh-mirror.json` manifest, the SSRF policy and DNS.
2. **Signed health.** `GET /health?nonce=…&issuedAt=…[&owner=…&repo=…]`
   (`forkmesh-https-health-v1` / `forkmesh-https-health-repository-v1`)
   returns `available`, `integrity`, `refsSha256` and `operationsSha256`.
   Refs are checked against the owner-signed state; health is valid for two
   minutes.
3. **Capability.** `forkmesh-masked-proxy-v1` signature in `X-ForkMesh-Node`,
   `X-ForkMesh-Request-Id`, `X-ForkMesh-Issued-At`, `X-ForkMesh-Body-Sha256`
   and `X-ForkMesh-Signature`; request IDs are single-use for 60 seconds.
4. **Selection.** Upload-pack is redirected to a `mirrorUrl` only after a fresh
   proof there; other reads are proxied. Failover happens only before response
   bytes are sent; cookies, auth headers and client IPs are never forwarded.

## Operations

`/v1/repositories/<owner>/<repo>/<operation>` requires a capability.
`/v1/public/repositories/...` serves the GET/HEAD read operations of public
repositories without one.

| Operation | Method | Query | Response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `git-info-refs` | GET/HEAD | `service=git-upload-pack` | upload-pack advertisement |
| `git-upload-pack` | POST | none | streamed pack (gzip allowed, 8 MiB request bound) |
| `merge-pull` | POST | typed JSON | asynchronous exact-OID merge via a configured executor |
| `update-pull-branch` | POST | typed JSON | merge base into a pull head |
| `actions-status` | GET | none | redacted run summaries for the repository |
| `actions-control` | POST | none; typed JSON ≤ 4 KiB | `202` once queued for the executor |
| `tree` / `blob` / `blobs` / `raw` | GET/HEAD | `path`, `ref` | bounded JSON or streamed bytes |
| `history` / `commit` / `branches` | GET/HEAD | `ref` / `path` | commit metadata |
| `search` / `stats` / `sizes` | GET/HEAD | `path`, `ref` | bounded results |
| `release-blob` | GET/HEAD | `sha256` | verified release bytes |

`actions-status` (`actionsSummaryPath`) and `actions-control`
(`actionsControlPath`, mode 0700) are off by default; the gateway is only a
courier and the executor re-verifies each request. See
[Mirror Actions control and summary v2](mirror-actions-control.md) and
[`mirror-actions-control.schema.json`](../mirror-actions-control.schema.json).
Upload-pack supports protocol v2 filters (`--filter=blob:none`) and shallow
clones.

## Cloudflare Tunnel fallback

For a node without a reachable origin (an operator option, not a ForkMesh
dependency), `tools/cloudflare_tunnel_bootstrap.py`
provisions a Tunnel to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` and a signed manifest with
`mainProxyMode: masked`. It reads the API token from `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` or
stdin, supports `--dry-run`, and needs `--replace-dns` to overwrite DNS.

pages.markdown:
# Disaster recovery

This guide prepares a community for losing its normal infrastructure: the
origin host is wiped, the hosted service is down, names stop resolving, a
signing key is lost, a region is cut off, or a backup is corrupt. It covers
preparation, recovery, and proving recovery works. How the hosted service stays
up day to day is in [architecture](../architecture.md); what a community keeps
when the hosted service is blocked or gone is in
[censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md).

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Runbook](runbook.md) | The printable runbook: triage, roles and checklists, prerequisites, a decision tree per scenario, procedures with verification and rollback, and an exercise worksheet. |
| [Exercise register](exercise-register.md) | Every recorded exercise, its findings and corrective owners, and what closure still needs. |
| [`conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json`](../../conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json) | The runbook source (`forkmesh-disaster-runbook-v1`). `runbook.md` is generated from it. |
| `tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py` | Validates and renders the runbook, builds and verifies the bootstrap kit, manages the roster and key rotations, and runs drills. |

The runbook builds on
[offline and low-bandwidth sync](../offline-sync.md),
[transports and anonymity postures](../transports.md),
[self-hostable service roles](../operations/service-roles.md),
[node backup and recovery](../operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md), and
[portable identities](../portable-identities.md).

## Start here: prepare before a disaster

1. **Make keys.** One kit key, one export key per mirror operator, and one
   recovery key for each custodian. Keep the seeds on separate devices, held by
   different people.

   ```sh
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen kit.key          # prints the kit public key
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen export.key
   tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen recovery-1.key   # one per custodian
   ```

2. **Write the community roster** (below), then check it:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check roster.json
   ```

3. **Build the bootstrap kit** onto removable media, and write the kit public
   key and the manifest digest it prints on paper:

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit build /media/usb/forkmesh-kit \
     --signing-key kit.key --roster roster.json
   ```

4. **Print [runbook.md](runbook.md)** with its digest and the kit public key.
5. **Run the drills**, then tabletop and live exercises; record each one.

## The community roster

The roster (`forkmesh-recovery-roster-v1`) is how members find each other
without the website. It lists pinned keys, mirrors, and contacts, and it
travels inside the signed kit.

```json
{
  "schema": "forkmesh-recovery-roster-v1",
  "community": "example community",
  "updated": "2026-09-14",
  "recoveryThreshold": 2,
  "keys": [
    {"keyId": "export-1", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "export", "holder": "Mirror operator A", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-1", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 1", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-2", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 2", "status": "active"},
    {"keyId": "recovery-3", "publicKey": "<base64url>", "role": "recovery", "holder": "Custodian 3", "status": "active"}
  ],
  "mirrors": [
    {"name": "library mirror", "urls": ["http://mirror.example.lan:8080/project.git", "http://10.0.0.20:8080/project.git"],
     "pinnedHosts": {"mirror.example.lan": "10.0.0.20"}}
  ],
  "contacts": [{"role": "coordinator", "name": "<name>", "channel": "<phone or radio>"}],
  "rotations": []
}
```

Key roles are `export` (signs removable media), `kit` (signs bootstrap kits),
and `recovery` (signs key rotations); status is `active` or `revoked`.
`roster check` exits 3 when the roster is invalid, has no active export key, or
has fewer distinct recovery holders than `recoveryThreshold`. It warns when no
mirror URL works without DNS (literal address, onion address, or a
`pinnedHosts` name), when one custodian can rotate keys alone, or when an export
key holder also holds a recovery key.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check roster.json [--json]
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster keys roster.json --role export
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster profile roster.json --out lan.json
```

`roster profile` writes a `lan-only` [transport profile](../transports.md#postures)
that dials the roster's pinned local addresses, so a clone needs no DNS.

## The bootstrap kit

A kit is a directory holding exactly what a community needs to recover with no
network: the runbook source and printable copy, the recovery tools, the guides
they cite, and the roster. Its manifest, `forkmesh-recovery-kit.json`, is a
`forkmesh-recovery-kit-signed-v1` envelope over a `forkmesh-recovery-kit-v1`
manifest listing every file's SHA-256 and size, the runbook version and digest,
the build date, and `reviewBy`.

```sh
python3 -B tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit verify /media/usb/forkmesh-kit \
  --trusted-key <kit key from paper>
```

Run it from the kit on the disconnected machine; it never opens a network
connection. It checks the signature against the key you pass (read it from
paper, never from the kit), that every listed file matches with no extras or
symlinks, that the runbook validates against the kit's own tools and guides and
matches its digest and printable copy, and that the roster verifies.

A key that starts with `-` must be joined to its flag:
`--trusted-key=-Ab…`. Written as two words, the tool reads the key as an
unknown option and exits with code 2.

| State | Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verified` | `0` | Everything checked, and the kit is before its review date. |
| `stale` | `4` | Everything checked, but the kit is past `reviewBy`. Use it, then rebuild it from a current roster. |
| `failed` | `3` | Do not run anything from this kit. |

`--today YYYY-MM-DD` checks freshness as of another date.

## Key recovery

A lost or stolen export or kit key is replaced by a rotation signed by a
threshold of recovery custodians; no single custodian or lost key can do it.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key rotate --roster roster.json \
  --recovery-key recovery-1.key --revoke <lost key> --successor <new key> \
  --holder "<holder>" --reason "<reason>" --issued <YYYY-MM-DD> --out rotation.json
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key cosign rotation.json --recovery-key recovery-2.key --roster roster.json
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key apply roster.json rotation.json --out roster-rotated.json
```

The statement is `forkmesh-recovery-key-rotation-v1`, wrapped in
`forkmesh-recovery-key-rotation-signed-v1`. `key apply` refuses a rotation with:

| Code | Refused because |
| --- | --- |
| `statement_digest` | `statementSha256` does not match the statement. |
| `community_mismatch` | The rotation names another community. |
| `already_applied` | The roster already lists this rotation. |
| `bad_signature` | A signature does not verify. |
| `signer_not_recovery_key` | A signer is not an active recovery key. The lost key cannot sign its own replacement. |
| `below_threshold` | Fewer distinct recovery signatures than `recoveryThreshold`. |
| `revoke_unknown` | A revoked key is not an active key in the roster. |
| `revoke_recovery_key` | Recovery keys change only by building a new kit with the custodians present. |
| `successor_known` | The successor key is already in the roster. |
| `successor_role` | The successor must be an export or kit key. |
| `statement_invalid` | The successor key or issued date is malformed. |

Media signed by the revoked key then fails import; re-export from a verified
copy with the successor key. Never lower the threshold during an incident.

Mirror node identity keys move with the node's sealed identity export
([moving or replacing an identity key](../operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md#moving-or-replacing-an-identity-key)).
Personal identities recover with the portable recovery kit
([recovery drills](../portable-identities.md#recovery-drills)).

## Drills

Each scenario has a live drill that builds a small community in scratch space
(origin, mirror, maintainer clone, signed export, roster), causes the disaster,
recovers with the runbook's tools, and measures the result.

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run all --report drills.json --telemetry drills.jsonl
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run origin-loss --fault no-local-clone
```

| Scenario | What the drill does | Fault injection |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `origin-loss` | Deletes the origin, restores from mirror plus maintainer clone, refuses a stale overwrite. | `no-local-clone` |
| `main-service-loss` | Stops the hosted copy and serves a read-only static mirror a newcomer clones and verifies. | `no-surviving-mirror` |
| `dns-loss` | Clones over a `lan-only` route with roster-pinned addresses; strace flags any DNS query. | `no-pinned-address` |
| `key-loss` | Refuses invalid rotations, applies a 2-of-3 rotation, refuses media forged with the lost key. | `threshold-unreachable` |
| `regional-isolation` | Two diverged regions exchange signed media; every commit reaches both. | `unpinned-region-key` |
| `corrupted-backup` | Rejects a corrupt backup and restores the previous verified one, recording loss. | `all-copies-corrupt` |
| `offline-bootstrap` | Verifies a kit and imports offline with the network blocked; refuses a tampered kit. | `wrong-kit-key` |

A `forkmesh-disaster-drill-report-v1` report records `recoveryMs`,
`withinObjective`, `dataLoss`, `missingPrerequisites`, `unsafeSteps`, each step
and check, and `verdict`. A drill passes only when every check passes within
budget, data loss is allowed by policy, and no blocking prerequisite is missing.
`--telemetry FILE` appends one count-only `forkmesh-disaster-drill-telemetry-v1`
line per drill with no paths, keys, names, or addresses.

## Exercises and evidence

Record every exercise as
`conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/exercises/DRX-NNNN.json`
(`forkmesh-disaster-exercise-v1`): kind (`tabletop` or `live`), status, runbook
version and digest, whether only the offline runbook was used, participants
with roles and familiarity (`unfamiliar`, `familiar`, `automation`), and per
scenario the result, recovery time, data loss, missing prerequisites, and
unsafe steps. Each missing prerequisite or unsafe step taken names a finding
with a corrective owner (`person`, runbook `role`, or `issue`).

Retain automated drill reports as content-addressed evidence, then cite them:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py attest drills.json   # prints evidence/<sha256>.json references
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py gate
```

A row citing `drillReport` must match the report it cites. Editing the runbook
without bumping its version fails validation for exercises on that version.

## Closure

`closure` lists the unmet checks and exits 1 until all are met; the
[register](exercise-register.md) shows the same status.

| Check | Met when |
| --- | --- |
| `automated-drills-current` | Every scenario has a passing drill report on the current runbook digest. |
| `platform-evidence` | Those reports cover Linux, macOS, and Windows. |
| `tabletop-drills-recorded` | Every scenario was run as a tabletop exercise with at least two people. |
| `live-drills-recorded` | People recovered every scenario in a live exercise. |
| `unfamiliar-team-restored` | Two or more people unfamiliar with ForkMesh restored a verified network using only the offline runbook. |
| `findings-owned` | Every open finding has a named person as its corrective owner. |

Automation cannot meet the people checks.

## Clean restoration

When normal infrastructure returns:

- compare its refs with the restored network before anything syncs, and push
  restored work to it as fast-forwards only;
- keep any diverged branches under review, never force-push over them;
- stop emergency static mirrors and delete temporary transport profiles;
- apply any key rotations to every roster copy, then rebuild and re-sign the
  kit, and write the new key and digest on paper;
- write the exercise or incident record, with a corrective owner for every
  finding.

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py validate` | Check the runbook's roles, prerequisites, decision trees, commands, guide headings, and kit completeness against the repository. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render [--check]` | Write or check `runbook.md` and `exercise-register.md`. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py gate` | Validate the runbook, every exercise, and rendered output. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py closure` | Report the closure checks. |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check`, `roster keys`, `roster profile` | Roster commands (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key rotate`, `key cosign`, `key apply` | Key rotation (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit build`, `kit verify` | Bootstrap kit (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run` | Live drills (above). |
| `forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py attest` | Retain drill reports as evidence. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | Done. |
| `1` | Validation, a drill, the gate, or closure failed. |
| `2` | Usage error or unreadable input. |
| `3` | A kit, roster, or rotation did not verify. |
| `4` | The kit verified but is past its review date. |

## Supported platforms

The drills need Git 2.40+ and Python 3.9+. The `disaster-recovery-conformance`
quality gate runs the test suite, and CI runs the suite, gate, and every drill
on Linux, macOS, and Windows. DNS leak tracing in the `dns-loss` drill needs
strace and runs only on Linux.

## Limits

- Drills do not build the Go mirror node; node archive restores and identity
  imports are covered by `server/nodeops_test.go` instead.
- The `search` and `organization-service` roles are hosted-only, so
  main-service loss cannot restore them.
- Kits are signed by one kit key, not a threshold.

Back to [Operations](../operations/README.md) and the [documentation home](../README.md).

# Disaster recovery exercise register

<!-- Generated by tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render from conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/exercises. Do not edit by hand. -->

Part of [Disaster recovery](README.md).

Every tabletop and live exercise of the [disaster recovery runbook](runbook.md) is
recorded here with its recovery time, data loss, missing prerequisites, unsafe
steps, and a corrective owner for each finding.

Current runbook: version 1.0.1, digest `e5cd0aa7da7cb3a0902837961389ca1351d378460a64eccedaaa01913bd8242d`.

## Closure status

| Check | Status | Still missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Every scenario has a passing automated drill on the current runbook (`automated-drills-current`) | open | origin-loss, main-service-loss, dns-loss, key-loss, regional-isolation, corrupted-backup, offline-bootstrap |

## Exercises

# Fleet autoscaling

Part of [Operations](README.md).

The fleet grows and shrinks two pools without the operator box:

- **App capacity:** app replicas, label `fmnext-auto-N`, fleet name `aN`,
  WireGuard `10.77.0.2N`.
- **Burst runners:** throwaway agent-job machines, label `fmnext-burst-N`,
  fleet name `bN`.

Cores and the always-on runner are never scaled, listed, touched or destroyed
by the autoscaler; rqlite voters stay at three. The desktop (Network, Hosts)
is only the control plane: it signs settings and commands and reads status.
Scaling keeps working while it is off. Fleet map:
[fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md); availability overview:
[architecture](../architecture.md).

## Where the scaler runs

On the cores, inside the app host (`app/host/forkmesh_host/autoscaler.py`),
leaderless:

- Every 60 s each unsealed, hosting core checks whether it owns this minute of
  the cron rotation (`cluster.rotation_owner`).
- The owner takes the rqlite lease `autoscale_lease` (compare-and-set, 150 s,
  renewed while working), so only one actor runs per tick.
- Ticks are short; nodes move one step per tick through a state machine:
  `creating` → `booting` → `joining` → `serving`, and `draining` → `removing`
  → gone. A core that dies mid-action is replaced by the next tick's owner.
- Replicas never host Durable Objects (the host's emulation,
  [app host](../host/README.md)) or own cron, so they never run it.

## Settings

One JSON object: a global `killSwitch` and, per pool, `enabled`, `dryRun`,
`min`, `max`, scale-up and scale-down rules, `cooldownMinutes`, `plan`,
`region`, `monthlyCapCents` and the snapshot id.

- Signed by the operator Ed25519 key (`config/fleet/ids-operator.key`) and sent
  with `tools/next_autoscale.py settings` to `POST /api/fleet/autoscale/settings`.
- Cores verify against `FORKMESH_IDS_OPERATOR_PUBKEY` and require a `signedAt`
  newer than the stored one; every tick re-verifies, and an invalid row means
  "act on nothing".
- Status and manual commands are signed the same way with a timestamp and a
  single-use nonce (60 s window).

### Defaults

| | app replicas | burst runners |
|---|---|---|
| enabled / dry run | off / on | off / on |
| min / max extra nodes | 0 / 2 | 0 / 2 |
| scale up | p95 > 500 ms, loop lag > 250 ms or load/CPU > 0.8, for 5 min | queue ≥ 1 job waiting ≥ 2 min, and the always-on runner has no free slot |
| scale down | every signal under 50 % of its threshold for 30 min | idle 10 min |
| cooldown | 10 min | 10 min |
| plan / region | `vc2-1c-1gb` / `ewr` (the cores' plan) | same |
| monthly cap | $15 | $10 |

Both pools start off and in dry run. Two extras per pool fit a $25 combined
monthly cap. The p95 threshold is far above the normal target, so only real
overload scales. Burst runners never scale up automatically until per-job
provider credentials exist (`BURST_JOBS_READY = False` in
`autoscale_policy.py`; [runners](runners.md) mode B).

### Hard limits (in code)

At most 4 nodes and $100 a month per pool; cooldown at least 5 minutes; at
most one create or destroy per pool per cooldown and 12 changes per 24 h;
`min` is never undercut; reaching the monthly cap destroys the pool's nodes
one per tick; the kill switch stops every create and destroy. Signed manual
scale commands run even while a pool is disabled or in dry run.

## Metrics

Each node keeps a 5-minute window of request p50/p95, event-loop lag, RPS and
load per CPU (`host_metrics.py`) and upserts it into `host_metrics` every 30 s.
The tick owner aggregates rows fresher than 2 minutes (max of p95 and lag,
mean of load and RPS). No fresh metrics means hold.

The same row carries `cpuPct`, `memPct` and `diskPct` (CPU busy share between
samples at least 5 s apart, memory in use, root file system in use). The
autoscaler does not read them; `/api/status` shows them as each core's
`resources` and the iPhone draws them as tiny bars on the core node lights
([phone navigation](../native/NAVIGATION.md)).

## Cloud credential

The provider API key lives only in the vault and in unsealed core memory.
Every call goes through `vultr_guard.py`:

- no listing; only create, read one instance by id, and delete one by id;
- create only with labels `fmnext-auto-<1..9>` or `fmnext-burst-<1..9>`, the
  `forkmesh-next` tag, the configured plan, region and snapshot, recorded in
  `autoscale_nodes`;
- destroy only a recorded id after a fresh read confirms id, label and tag;
- core and always-on runner labels are always refused.

`app/host/tests_unit/test_vultr_guard.py` checks every rule. The guard binds
honest code only: a compromised core holding the key could call the provider
directly. Use a sub-user key limited to instances and snapshots, billing
alerts, and a provider account that holds nothing else.

## Provisioning without operator keys

**Snapshot.** `tools/next_autoscale.py snapshot build --execute` creates a
builder `fmnext-snap-N`, installs packages, rqlite, Caddy, the daemon and the
join agent, strips machine identity (host keys, `machine-id`, cloud-init
state, logs), installs only public keys, snapshots, destroys the builder and
publishes the id with a signed settings write. Rebuild it after changes to the
log reader, rqlite, Caddy, the daemon or the OS.

**Join.** A new instance boots with a one-time join token (name, provider id,
30-minute expiry, nonce, MACed under a key derived from `DATA_KEY`).
`fmnext-join`:

1. generates its WireGuard and IDS keys on the node;
2. calls `POST /api/fleet/join`; the core checks the MAC, expiry, single use,
   that the source IP equals the instance's address from a fresh provider
   read, and that label, tag and name match the record;
3. receives its rendered files, bootstrap credentials and release id;
4. installs and starts WireGuard; the cores' root agent `fmnext-fleet-peers`
   (every 15 s) adds the peer, firewall set element and certsync allowance;
   rqlite joins as a non-voter; certsync follows and never issues;
5. downloads and verifies the release, builds the venv offline and starts;
6. peer-unseals from a core (cores accept requesters in `autoscale_nodes` from
   their own WireGuard address).

Burst runners skip WireGuard, rqlite and the app and are registered as pool
runners with no owners.

**IDS keys.** The vault holds a sub-master derived from the IDS master; cores
can derive node keys only for `a1..a9` and `b1..b9`.

**DNS.** A serving replica enters DNS through the operator-box health loop, or
through the node reconciler when it is enabled with a DNS-scoped token.

**Scale-down.** Mark `draining` (health loops remove it from DNS), wait 3
minutes, remove the rqlite non-voter (or revoke the runner), destroy through
the guard, delete the row; peers drop the WireGuard peer within 15 s.

## Audit

Every non-trivial decision, create, destroy, join, failure, settings write and
command is recorded in `autoscale_audit`, and every real action also raises a
`security_incidents` row (detector `autoscaler`) delivered to admins.

- A dry-run pool writes `decision_dry_run` only when the decision (action and
  target node) differs from the last dry-run decision this process recorded
  for the pool, not on every 60 s tick. A tick that decides "none" forgets it,
  so the same decision coming back is written again; so does a restart.
- Rows are kept 30 days (`AUDIT_RETAIN_MS`), pruned on every audit write. The
  status view reads only the newest 30 rows.
- Why: one identical dry-run row per minute under a 90-day retention grew
  the table to 3.1 MiB and 27k rows on 1 GB nodes.

## Threat model

The fleet-wide model is [threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md);
the autoscaler adds:

- **Compromised core app:** can use the provider key directly; cannot obtain
  the IDS master or the core certsync secret.
- **Forged join:** tokens are short-lived, single-use, MACed, and bound to the
  provider id and the source IP read fresh from the provider.
- **Malicious `autoscale_nodes` rows:** the root peers agent accepts only
  expected names, mesh addresses and well-formed keys.
- **Replayed commands:** newer-than-stored settings, single-use nonces.
- **Runaway cost:** hard limits, caps, kill switch, dry run by default.
- **Split brain:** replicas host no objects or cron; voters fixed at three;
  lease plus rotation.

## Code

- App host: `autoscaler.py`, `autoscale_policy.py`, `vultr_guard.py`,
  `fleet_api.py`, `host_metrics.py`, replica mode in `cluster.py` and
  `durable_cluster.py`, replica peer unseal in `vault.py`.
- Deploy: `deploy/core/fleet_peers.py`, `deploy/core/join_agent.py`, replica
  render in `render.py`, certsync follower in `certsync.py`. Each core needs
  the `AUTOSCALE_CERTSYNC_SECRET` credential file.
- Tools: `tools/next_autoscale.py`, `tools/next_ids.py`, `tools/next_dns.py`.
- Migration: `app/migrations/0211_fleet_autoscale.sql`.
- Desktop: `desktop/src/FleetAutoscalePanel.*`.

# Fleet node ownership and version fields

Part of [Operations](README.md).

Each core and runner has a node account that belongs to an operator account.
`tools/next_node_owner.py` inspects, provisions and transfers ownership
(dry-run by default). Fleet runbook: [runbook](runbook.md).

## Where ownership lives

| Place | Field | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| `nodes` row (encrypted `data`) | `owner` | `_link_node_to_user` (`app/src/entry.py`), the only writer |
| `nodes` row, plaintext | `user_bi` = blind index of `owner` | `_mirror_account_identity_tables` when the account is saved |
| owner's `users` row | `nodes` list | `_link_node_to_user` (also removes the node from the previous owner) |
| `runner_nodes` | `registered_by`, `allowed_owners` | `POST /api/runners/register` |

`mirror_https_endpoints`, `cluster_members`, catalog records, `org_repos`,
role grants and organization members carry no node owner. A node account's
Ed25519 key signs its own requests and is not bound to the owner, so a
transfer re-signs nothing.

## Transferring ownership

```sh
python3 tools/next_node_owner.py status
python3 tools/next_node_owner.py transfer --from <old> --to <new> --accept-key <new owner's Ed25519 PEM> --execute
```

The new owner must accept, with `--accept-key PATH` (its own signing key, read
locally) or `--session-env NAME` (a session token sent as a bearer);
otherwise `--execute` refuses.

- **Cores** use the signed link grant ([node link grants](../security/node-link-grants.md)):
  the node signs `forkmesh-link-grant-v2\n<node>\n<target>\n<ts>\n<nonce>`
  with its identity key (the script arrives on stdin; only the public key and
  signature leave the node), the tool checks the public key against
  `nodes.pubkey`, and the target accepts in the same request.
- **Runners** have no API to change the registrant, so the tool runs one
  guarded update (`UPDATE runner_nodes SET registered_by=? … WHERE name=? AND registered_by=?`)
  only when the target is in `allowed_owners` (and an admin for a pool
  runner, or the sole allowed owner for a personal runner).
- Each change writes `node.owner_transfer` or `runner.owner_transfer` to the
  sensitive audit log. Re-running reports "already owned".

## Provisioning a core's node account

The daemon authenticates to the app only with its node key against
`nodes.pubkey`.

```sh
python3 tools/next_node_owner.py register            # dry run for every core
python3 tools/next_node_owner.py register nN --execute
```

For each core it creates a missing account (the node signs
`forkmesh-reserve-v1` and `forkmesh-finalize-v1` with its identity key),
refuses an existing account bound to another key (a rebuilt core reusing a
name gets HTTP 401 until the owner reclaims the name), and links an unowned
core to the account that owns the other cores through the signed link grant.
`add-core` runs the same `provision_core` in its `register` step.

## Service accounts

An admin service account without a mail domain may remain for operator
probes; mark such accounts as service accounts so they receive no mail.
Security incidents ping every admin.

## Version fields

One source: `project(ForkMesh VERSION x.y.z)` in `desktop/CMakeLists.txt`, read
by `next_common.release_version()`.

| Surface | Field |
|---|---|
| App `/api/version` | `version` (`APP_VERSION` from the release) and `rev` (`BUILD_REV`) |
| Daemon `mirror-node.json` | `version`, stamped by `next_fleet install --steps daemon` |

The daemon version reaches the catalog record, the mirrors API, the runner
status and the `ForkMesh-Mirror-Node/<v>` User-Agent. The daemon cannot report
a build revision. The desktop shows core versions from the catalog, the app
release from `/api/version`, and runner versions from daemon status only.

# Fleet operations runbook

Part of [Operations](README.md).

How to bring up, deploy, check and tear down the fleet: three core nodes
(currently `n3`, `n4` and `n5`; `n1` and `n2` are retired, `retired_cores` in
`deploy/fleet.toml`) and a runner (`r1`) on Vultr. Cloudflare serves DNS only
for the app and world names. Take node names from `[[nodes]]` in
`deploy/fleet.toml` when the fleet changes. `deploy/core/render.py` renders
node files from `deploy/fleet.toml`. Design: [served stack](served-stack.md);
tool map: [fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md); operator folders and files:
[operator files](operator-files.md).

Every tool dry-runs by default; nothing changes without `--execute`. Run
from `~/projects/forkmesh/src`. No tool prints a secret or passes one on a
command line. The tools need Go, Python 3.13, and Node with wrangler for the
www Worker.

## Bring up

```sh
python3 tools/next_fleet.py plans; python3 tools/next_fleet.py list
for n in 1 2 3; do python3 tools/next_fleet.py create-core $n --execute; done
python3 tools/next_fleet.py create-runner 1 --execute
python3 tools/next_fleet.py fleet-toml --execute
python3 tools/next_fleet.py init-secrets --execute
for n in n3 n4 n5; do python3 tools/next_fleet.py install $n --steps base,wireguard --execute; done
python3 tools/next_fleet.py fleet-toml --execute      # adds WireGuard public keys; commit it
for n in n3 n4 n5; do python3 tools/next_fleet.py install $n --steps rqlite,turn,calls,files,secrets,start --execute; done
python3 tools/next_dns.py ensure --execute
python3 tools/next_deploy.py build --execute
python3 tools/next_deploy.py upload --execute
python3 tools/next_deploy.py migrate --execute
python3 tools/next_vault.py sync --execute
python3 tools/next_deploy.py restart --execute
for n in n3 n4 n5; do python3 tools/next_fleet.py install $n --steps daemon --execute; done
python3 tools/next_fleet.py install r1 --execute
python3 tools/next_fleet.py install r1 --steps daemon --execute
```

`create-*` adopts an existing instance by label, so re-running is safe.

Operator-box user units (copy from `deploy/operator/`, then
`systemctl --user enable --now`): `fmnext-backup.timer`, `fmnext-unseal.timer`,
`fmnext-dns-health.service`. Enable lingering for the user.

The homepage Worker deploys by hand from `www/wrangler.production.toml`
([website](../www/README.md), [auto-deploy](auto-deploy.md)).

## Verify

```sh
ssh -i $K root@<core> "curl -fsS -K /etc/forkmesh-next/rqlite.curlrc 'http://127.0.0.1:4001/nodes?nonvoters'"
curl -fsS --resolve app.forkmesh.com:443:<ip> https://app.forkmesh.com/readyz
curl -fsS https://n3.next.forkmesh.com/readyz
python3 tools/next_dns.py status
python3 tools/next_ids.py status n3 n4 n5 r1
```

## Routine operations

- **Deploy.** `next_deploy.py all --execute` (autodeploy runs it on every
  merge, [auto-deploy](auto-deploy.md)): migrate through any
  healthy node, then restart one node at a time in a rotating order. Each node is
  gated on loopback `/readyz`, `/api/version` reporting the new rev, and Caddy
  serving `/readyz`; a failing node goes back to its previous release and the
  rollout stops. Activation scripts hold a lock, survive a dropped SSH
  session, and are verified by comparing `current/BUILD_REV` with the running
  version. Roll back one node with `next_deploy.py rollback nN --execute`.
- **Node files.** After editing `deploy/core/templates` or `deploy/fleet.toml`,
  run `install nN --steps files,start --execute` one node at a time.
- **Rotate a secret.** Edit `secrets.env`, then `next_vault.py sync --execute`;
  unsealed nodes reload without a restart. Bootstrap credentials
  (`RQLITE_PASSWORD`, `FORKMESH_MESH_SECRET`) need `install nN --steps secrets`
  and a unit restart. `DATA_KEY` is rotated only offline ([re-keying](rekey.md)).
- **Vault.** `next_vault.py status` shows sealed/unsealed per node and key ids.
  A restarted node is unsealed by its peers within about 15 s; the operator
  timer acts only when every node is sealed ([vault](vault.md)).
- **Backups.** `fmnext-backup.timer` runs `next_backup.py run --execute`
  nightly: it pulls `/db/backup?compress` over an SSH tunnel, keeps it only
  after `PRAGMA integrity_check` and table counts pass, encrypts it to the
  backup public key, and retains 7 daily and 4 weekly copies. Only files with
  the exact backup name pattern are ever deleted
  ([disaster recovery runbook](../disaster-recovery/runbook.md)).
- **Certificates** are leaderless (`deploy/core/certsync.py`). The
  rendezvous-first live core renews when the freshest pair anywhere is
  missing or within 30 days of expiry; every core pulls the freshest valid
  pair every 5 minutes. `journalctl -u fmnext-cert-sync` shows the mode
  (`files`, `acme`, `internal`).
- **Cron** is leaderless: the per-minute coordinator rotates across live
  nodes and hands over 45 s into each minute; `host_cron_runs` records who ran
  which minute. Keep node clocks in sync.
- **TURN relay and group calls.** Every core runs the office TURN relay
  (`fmnext-turn`, [Office](../office/README.md)) and the group-call
  server (`fmnext-calls`, [call servers](call-servers.md)). Their shared
  secrets (`OFFICE_TURN_SECRET`, `FORKMESH_CALLS_SECRET`) come from
  `init-secrets`, reach the app through `next_vault.py sync`, and reach each
  core as an encrypted credential through the `turn` and `calls` steps of a
  roll. Check calls with
  `curl -fsS https://nN.next.forkmesh.com/calls/health`.
- **Node DNS reconciler** (`app/host/forkmesh_host/dns_reconciler.py`): every
  unsealed node probes every core and votes in `dns_health_votes`. It acts
  only with a DNS token in the vault and a majority of voters; without one
  the fleet runs `[dns] reconciler = "dry"` and only votes.

### DNS health failover

`tools/next_dns.py health-loop --execute` runs as the `fmnext-dns-health`
user unit on the operator box and manages `app.forkmesh.com` and
`world.forkmesh.com` (one A record per member, AAAA for members with IPv6),
plus each core's own `nN.next.forkmesh.com`.

The old aliases `app.next.forkmesh.com` and `world.next.forkmesh.com` were
retired on 2026-11-01. They only redirected to the production names. No tool
writes them now, Caddy no longer serves them and certsync no longer renews
their certificates. `fleet.toml`'s `app_host` and `world_host` are now the
production names; `[production]` only switches on production mode and holds
`[production.vars]`. Delete any leftover `app.next` or `world.next` records
in the Cloudflare dashboard.

- Every 30 s it sends a TLS-verified `GET /readyz` to each core. A sealed,
  quarantined or locked-down node fails. A read-only core (no rqlite leader,
  503 with `"readOnly": true`) counts as healthy only while no core is fully
  ready, so a lone survivor stays in DNS and serves reads
  ([read-only mode](served-stack.md#read-only-mode)).
- A node leaves every name after 3 failed probes and returns after 2 minutes
  healthy. At most one change per 5 minutes. A set is never emptied.
- A round in which every core fails is treated as an operator-box outage and
  changes nothing.
- `next_dns.py drain nN --execute` removes a node and holds it out for
  maintenance; `undrain` releases it. Wait out the 60 s TTL after a drain.
  Never pipe `drain` into `head`.
- Rules live in `HealthState` (`tools/next_dns.py`) and
  `app/host/forkmesh_host/dns_rules.py`; state in `config/fleet/dns-health.json`.
  Restart the unit after changing `next_dns.py`.

### Adding, removing and replacing cores

- **Add:** `next_fleet.py add-core --execute` or the desktop's Add core node;
  the new core joins as a non-voter while three voters exist and enters DNS
  only when healthy.
- **Remove:** `next_fleet.py remove-core nN --execute`. Refused below three
  cores or three healthy voters; a non-voter is promoted first. The removed
  core is listed in `[hosted] retired_cores` so repositories its node account
  owns still take pushes ([core push](core-push.md)).
- **Replace:** `next_fleet.py add-core --replace nOLD --execute` or the
  desktop's **Replace…** on a core row. One run adds the new core, removes the
  old one (its instance is kept) and commits both on `fleet/add-core-nNEW`
  ([fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md#replacing-a-core-node)).
- **IPv6:** drain, `next_fleet.py enable-ipv6 nN --reboot --execute`,
  `fleet-toml --execute`, `next_dns.py ensure --execute`, undrain.

Full order of operations: [fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md#adding-a-core-node).

### Signup challenge

The app verifies a Cloudflare Turnstile token itself (`app/src/turnstile.py`)
on `POST /api/accounts/signup` and `POST /api/accounts/forgot-password`.
Signed node registrations are not gated but have a per-IP limit.

- Site key: `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` in `app/wrangler.toml` `[vars]` (the cores
  read that file's `[vars]` as app settings). Secret:
  `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` in `secrets.env` and the vault (`optional_secrets`).
- Each `GET /signup` issues a claim cookie; a token from an earlier page view
  is refused with `turnstile_stale_page`.
- Fails closed: without the secret, or on a siteverify error or timeout, the
  forms answer 503 `turnstile_unavailable`. Signup then takes the backup
  check instead ([signup backup check](../app/signup-challenge.md#signup-backup-check)),
  and so does password reset
  ([password reset challenge](../app/signup-challenge.md#password-reset-challenge)); set
  `SIGNUP_BACKUP_CHECK=off` to make both fail closed too.
- Rotate in the Turnstile dashboard, update `secrets.env`, then
  `next_vault.py sync --execute` within the grace period.
- Off the VPS platform with no secret, Turnstile's always-pass test keys are
  used locally. On a VPS they are accepted only with `TURNSTILE_TEST_MODE=1`,
  which must never be set in the fleet.

### Native app builds

Codemagic builds the native apps from a private copy of this repository on
the cores, never from a public forge.

- Each core keeps a bare repository under `/var/lib/forkmesh-next/git/`.
  Caddy serves it read-only over Git's dumb-HTTP protocol under `/git/`
  behind basic auth (`GIT_CI_PASSWORD` in `secrets.env`; only the bcrypt hash
  is on the node).
- `tools/next_git_host.py` (`setup`, `push`, `url`) manages it;
  `tools/next_codemagic.py build <workflow> --execute` pushes and starts a
  build, `status <id> --logs` shows step logs with the password masked.
- Dumb HTTP cannot serve shallow clones, so every workflow sets
  `CM_CLONE_UNSHALLOW: "true"`.
- Rotate the password with `next_git_host.py setup --execute` after removing
  its line from `secrets.env`, then give Codemagic the new repository URL.
- Signed workflows need the App Store Connect variable group on the
  Codemagic app.

### Caddy version

The cores run a pinned upstream Caddy from `/usr/local/bin/caddy`, not the
distribution package. `[caddy]` in `deploy/fleet.toml` pins the version and
tarball sha256; verify the tarball against the release checksums and their
signature before placing it in `data/fleet/dl/`.

- Install or upgrade: `next_fleet.py install nN --steps caddy --execute`. It
  verifies the tarball and binary, validates the live Caddyfile with the new
  binary, installs a drop-in that only changes `ExecStart`/`ExecReload`,
  restarts, and checks `/readyz`. On failure it runs `caddy-debian`, which
  restores the packaged binary.
- The IDS expects both files through a signed expectation.
- Roll out one node at a time, drained from DNS, and reload twice checking
  `journalctl -u caddy` for panics.
- The Caddy unit has `Restart=on-failure`; deploy gates restart Caddy once if
  it stops serving.

## Recovery

- **Every node restarted:** the site answers 503 `{"error":"sealed"}` until
  one node is unsealed (`next_vault.py unseal --execute` or the timer); peers
  unseal each other after that.
- **A node will not unseal:** check `journalctl -u forkmesh-app | grep vault:`.
  `wrong_key`/`vault_tampered` mean a key mismatch, `vault_empty` means `sync`
  never ran, `db_unavailable` means no rqlite leader yet.
- **Lost `DATA_KEY`:** the vault and every encrypted row are unrecoverable.

## Destroy

`next_fleet.py destroy r1 --yes --execute` (a runner holds no state).
Destroying a core is refused while fewer than three healthy voters would
remain. Tearing down the cluster: back up first, set `[dns] reconciler =
"off"`, then `destroy nN --yes --execute --force`. `--force` skips only the
quorum check; the label and tag checks cannot be bypassed.

## Cost

About $5 per month per 1 GB instance, DNS and the www Worker on a free plan,
no object storage. Burst runners are billed hourly on top.

## Known gaps

- Country lookup: Caddy sets no country header on direct requests.
- The restore drill into a throwaway instance is not automated.
- Runner CLIs are installed and signed in through the relayed login
  ([runners](runners.md)).
- Monitoring and intrusion detection: [intrusion detection](intrusion-detection.md), [node logs](node-logs.md).

## Security hardening

Enforced by `deploy/core/render.py` and `tools/next_fleet.py`:

- **Caddy:** admin API on a unix socket only; header, body and idle
  timeouts; body caps (16 MB app/world, larger for pull uploads and Git
  pushes); HSTS and `nosniff` on every response; sandboxed unit.
- **App host:** requests for hosts outside `FORKMESH_PUBLIC_HOSTS` get 421;
  the edge header is verified before the app sees the request; outbound
  calls go through an egress guard (`FORKMESH_EGRESS_ALLOW` is the only
  exception list).
- **certsync:** pairs must chain to a system CA, cover the name and expire
  within 100 days; the pair server uses its own `FORKMESH_CERTSYNC_SECRET`,
  which the app does not hold.
- **nftables output rules by socket uid:** rqlite ports only from rqlite,
  root and the app; mesh and certsync ports only from their services;
  metadata service only from root.
- **System:** no swap for secret-holding services, `ptrace_scope = 1`,
  hardened sshd (no forwarding except local, no password auth), root
  password locked, vendor console users removed.
- **Runner:** jobs run as an unprivileged job user with no access to the node
  key or daemon config; nftables refuses the job user private, metadata,
  loopback and mesh addresses.
- **Operator box:** encrypt the disk, protect the fleet key with a
  passphrase, use a scoped cloud sub-user key, keep `DATA_KEY` and the backup
  decryption key offline, enable account 2FA.
- CAA records apply to the whole zone; add them only after checking every
  issuer in use.

Rollout order for node-file hardening: node files on every core first (they
render the host allowlist), then the app release, then the runner.

pages.markdown:
# Fleet SSH port

Part of [Operations](README.md).

Every core, runner and autoscaled node runs sshd on `ssh_port` from
`deploy/fleet.toml` (822), not 22. Bots sweep port 22 all day, filling the
journal, fail2ban and the IDS feed with noise. Few of them try 822. The port is
below 1024, so only root can listen on it, even while sshd is down. Fleet
map: [fleet tooling](fleet-tooling.md).

## What follows the port

| Piece | Where |
| --- | --- |
| sshd | `/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/05-fmnext-port.conf` (`Port 822`), written by the `ssh-port` step; the `base` step's `10-fmnext.conf` stays port-free |
| Node firewall | `public_tcp` in `render.nftables_conf` (core and runner) |
| IDS | `ssh.port` and the `listeners.tcp` set in `ids.json`; the lockdown table (`ids.firewall_ruleset`) keeps SSH open on that port |
| fail2ban | `/etc/fail2ban/jail.d/fmnext-sshd.local` (`[sshd] port = 822`) |
| Operator tools | `next_common.Ssh`: `-o Port=822 -o HostKeyAlias=<ipv4>`; `next_git_host.py` push; `next_aws.py` security group (22 and 822, so a fresh instance is reachable before its `ssh-port` step) |
| Desktop log feed | `CoreNodeLogs.cpp` reads `ssh_port` from `~/projects/forkmesh/src/deploy/fleet.toml` (`FMNEXT_FLEET_TOML`, `FMNEXT_SSH_PORT` override) |
| Autoscale snapshot | `next_fleet.ssh_port_image_script` writes the drop-in into the image (no reload: the builder keeps its session) |

`HostKeyAlias` keeps `known_hosts` keyed by the bare address, so the pins
made on 22 stay valid on 822 (OpenSSH otherwise looks up `[ip]:822`), and
`ssh-keygen -R <ip>` still removes them.

## Moving a node

```
python3 tools/next_fleet.py install n2 --steps ssh-port --execute
```

The step connects on whatever port answers. `Ssh` tries `ssh_port` first and
falls back to 22 when only 22 answers. The step then:

1. tells the IDS to expect changes to sshd, `nftables.conf`, `ids.json`,
   fail2ban and ufw;
2. backs up those files to `/run/fmnext-ssh-port` and arms
   `fmnext-ssh-port-rollback.timer` (180 s) before changing anything;
3. installs the rendered `nftables.conf`, `ids.json` and fail2ban jail and the
   port drop-in, checks `sshd -t`, and checks that `sshd -T` lists exactly the
   new port (a `Port 22` line left in `sshd_config` would keep 22 open), rolling
   back at once otherwise;
4. opens the port: loads the new ruleset when ours is in charge, else
   `ufw allow 822/tcp` on a fresh Vultr image;
5. reloads sshd (open sessions survive) and restarts the IDS and fail2ban;
6. reconnects on the new port with strict host-key checking and checks the
   node's name, then disarms the timer.

If the new port does not answer, the step fails and the node puts the old
files back by itself and reloads sshd and the firewall.

Move one core at a time, then the runner. New nodes run `ssh-port` between
`base` and `files` in every step list. Before a `files` step, `install` also
moves any node that still answers only on 22, so an automatic roll after this
change cannot load the new firewall in front of an sshd that is still on 22.

## Autoscaled nodes

App replicas and burst runners boot from the autoscale snapshot. Rebuild it
(`python3 tools/next_autoscale.py snapshot build --execute`,
[autoscaling](autoscaling.md)) so new nodes
start on 822; nodes made from an older snapshot keep sshd on 22 behind a
firewall that now admits only 822, until they are replaced.

## Changing the port again

Edit `ssh_port`, then run the `ssh-port` step on each node. `fleet-toml`
regeneration keeps the value.
