pages.markdown:
# Fleet tooling

Part of [Operations](README.md).

`deploy/` turns one fleet description, `deploy/fleet.toml`, into every file a
fleet node needs. The operator tools in `tools/next_*.py` create instances,
install nodes, push secrets and roll out releases. Node kinds: **core** nodes
(trusted: Caddy, the app on CPython, rqlite, the Go daemon and Git gateway)
and **runners** (untrusted, outbound-only agent compute,
[runners](runners.md)). This page is the map of the code and the core
lifecycle; the commands to run are in the [runbook](runbook.md). How the cores
fit together and what happens when one fails:
[architecture](../architecture.md); running your own:
[self-hosting](../self-hosting.md).

## Code map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `deploy/fleet.toml` | the live fleet: `[[nodes]]`, `[[runners]]`, `[paths]`, `[wireguard]`, `[rqlite]`, `[caddy]`, `[app]`, `[production]`, `[autoscale]`, `[turn]`, `[calls]`, `[dns]`, `[ids]`, `[self_deploy]`, `[logs]`, `[hosted]`. No secrets, no addresses. |
| `deploy/fleet.example.toml` | annotated template |
| `deploy/core/render.py` | renders a node's files into a tree plus `MANIFEST.json`; never reads secrets |
| `deploy/core/caddy_routes.py` | Caddy route snippets shipped with each release |
| `deploy/core/request_rules.py` | renders request block rules into a Caddy include |
| `deploy/core/certsync.py` | leaderless certificate sharing |
| `deploy/core/ids.py` | host intrusion detection ([intrusion detection](intrusion-detection.md)) |
| `deploy/core/self_deploy.py` | phone-approved merges deployed by the cores ([self-deploy](self-deploy.md)) |
| `deploy/core/templates/`, `deploy/runner/templates/` | unit files and configs |
| `deploy/operator/` | operator-box user units: backup, unseal, DNS health |
| `deploy/tests/` | renderer, Caddy, certsync, IDS and tool tests |
| `tools/next_common.py` | SSH, fleet loading, dry-run plumbing, ops log tee |
| `tools/next_fleet.py` | create, install, secrets, roll, add/remove/replace core, destroy |
| `tools/next_cloud.py`, `tools/next_aws.py` | provider interface; AWS EC2 provider (standard-library SigV4) |
| `tools/next_add_core.py`, `tools/next_remove_core.py` | resumable add/remove runs |
| `tools/next_deploy.py` | `build`, `upload`, `migrate`, `restart`, `all`, `rollback` |
| `tools/next_autodeploy.py` | auto-deploy of `main` ([auto-deploy](auto-deploy.md)) |
| `tools/next_vault.py`, `next_ids.py`, `next_dns.py`, `next_backup.py`, `next_rekey.py`, `next_git_host.py`, `next_codemagic.py` | vault, IDS, DNS, backup, re-key, private Git and native builds |

## Architecture

- **Render, then push.** `render.py` produces files only;
  `next_fleet.py install <node> --steps …` copies them and runs each step over
  SSH. Core steps: `base`, `wireguard`, `rqlite`, `turn`, `calls`, `ssh-port`,
  `files`, `secrets`, `start` (plus `daemon`, `caddy`, `ids`, `logread`).
  Runner steps: `base`, `ssh-port`, `files`, `start`, `daemon`. SSH runs on
  `ssh_port` ([SSH port](ssh-port.md)).
- **Secrets never rendered.** Units load encrypted credentials by name
  (`LoadCredentialEncrypted=`). With `[app] vault = true` the app gets only
  bootstrap credentials and starts sealed ([vault](vault.md)).
- **Releases.** `next_deploy.py build` makes a tarball (app host and source,
  built assets, World, an offline venv, Caddy snippets, `BUILD_REV`) that lands
  in `/opt/forkmesh-next/app/releases/<rev>` with `current` and `previous`
  symlinks. The operator box keeps the `KEEP_RELEASES` newest tarballs.
- **Rolling restart gate.** Each node must report `/readyz` and the new
  `BUILD_REV`; a failing node goes back to its previous release and the rollout
  stops. The node's own messages (Caddy, unseal, gate, rollback) are printed as
  `nN: activation: ...` lines in the deploy log, so a rollback names its cause.
  Migrations run once, through any healthy rqlite node.
- **A core down does not block a release.** `upload`, `restart` and `all`
  leave out a core that is held or out of DNS (`dns-health.json`, the
  `next_dns.py` health loop) or that SSH cannot reach, as long as a majority
  of the cores and at least two still get it (`deploy_quorum`); otherwise
  they refuse. `--skip nN` names the cores to leave out instead. The deploy
  manifest records `skipped`, and `restart nN` of that release later clears
  it (`caughtUp`). See [auto-deploy](auto-deploy.md#skipped-cores).
- **Speed.** One multiplexed SSH connection per node
  (`FMNEXT_SSH_MULTIPLEX=0` disables it), parallel uploads with the migration
  alongside, venv reuse when requirements are unchanged, a wheelhouse cache,
  and batched schema replay.

## No fixed main node

No core is special. Every role is rendered identically from `fleet.toml` or
chosen at run time among live cores:

| Role | How it is chosen |
| --- | --- |
| rqlite bootstrap and join | every voter renders the same `-bootstrap-expect` and `-join` |
| rqlite leader | Raft; `remove-core` hands it over first |
| migrations | first core with a healthy rqlite |
| rollout order | rotates per release (`rollout_order`, sha256 of `rev:name`) |
| self-deploy order | rendezvous per approval |
| backups | the current Raft leader |
| certificates, cron, Durable Object emulation ([host](../host/README.md)), autoscaler | rendezvous or rotation over live `cluster_members` |
| WireGuard, firewall, mesh, certsync, IDS keys, Git upstreams | full mesh from `fleet.toml` |
| runner-pool and hosted-git core lists | rendered into `app.env` from the fleet's cores |
| group calls | every core runs `fmnext-calls`; the app places each room by rendezvous over the healthy cores in `FORKMESH_CALLS_NODES` ([call servers](call-servers.md)) |

`deploy/tests/test_no_main_node.py` checks this.

## Adding a core node

`python3 tools/next_fleet.py add-core [--region R] [--plan P] [--provider P] --execute`
(the desktop's **Add core node** runs the same). Without `--execute` it prints
the plan. Steps:

| # | Step | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | plan | next number, region and plan, rqlite role |
| 2 | hold | mark the node `held` in `dns-health.json` before anything names it |
| 3 | vm | create or adopt the labelled instance (IPv6 at creation) |
| 4 | fleet | upsert the `[[nodes]]` block |
| 5 | keys | WireGuard and IDS keys generated on the node |
| 6 | mesh | re-render peers one at a time while the new core installs |
| 7 | join | start; rqlite joins over the mesh; the IDS starts last |
| 8 | services | daemon, calls, files, start; sync every repository from peers |
| 9 | activate | deploy the served release, unseal |
| 10 | repos | provision the core's node account, then wait until every repository is present and synced |
| 11 | ids | install the log reader, sign the baseline |
| 12 | health | node and external health checks |
| 13 | dns | undrain after probes |
| 14 | register | confirm DNS release and the node account |
| 15 | commit | commit `deploy/fleet.toml` on `fleet/add-core-nN`, then merge it into `main` |

- **rqlite role:** keep an odd number of voters; with three voters a fourth
  core joins as a non-voter (`rqlite_voter = false`).
- **DNS:** a newly seen core is held out of DNS until an explicit undrain.
- **Resume:** state in `config/fleet/add-core/nN.json`; every step is
  idempotent; a failure drains the node and keeps the VM for a retry.
- **Node account before repos:** without its `fmnext-nN` node account the relay
  answers the new daemon with HTTP 401, so repositories it learns from the
  catalog never sync. `repos` registers the account first (idempotent) and nudges a sync.
- **Snapshots:** only keyless builder images are accepted; cloning a live
  core would copy its keys and Raft state.
- **Merge:** the commit step merges the branch into `main` itself (see
  [Landing the fleet change on main](#landing-the-fleet-change-on-main)).

`python3 tools/next_fleet.py add-core` alone prints the plan;
`add-core-status` shows a run's progress.

To abandon a new core: keep it out of DNS, `rqlite remove` it from a peer,
`next_fleet.py destroy nN --yes --execute`, delete its `[[nodes]]` block, and
re-render the peers with `next_fleet.py roll --steps files,start --execute`.

## Removing a core node

`python3 tools/next_fleet.py remove-core nN [--destroy-instance] --execute`
(the desktop's **Remove…**). Steps: preflight (refused below three cores or
three healthy voters), promote a non-voter if voters would drop below three
or become even, hand over leadership, drain from DNS, stop services, leave
rqlite and delete its membership row, remove the fleet block, re-render
peers, deregister DNS names, commit on `fleet/remove-core-nN` and merge it into
`main`, and optionally destroy the instance.

Only the destroy step talks to a cloud provider. Other steps identify the
node over SSH by its pinned host key and recorded WireGuard public key. State
is in `config/fleet/remove-core/nN.json`; runs resume.

### Landing the fleet change on main

Autodeploy, roll and backups read `deploy/fleet.toml` on `main`, and every
deploy first asks each core listed there for `/api/version`. A fleet change
left on its branch breaks every deploy ("n2 did not answer /api/version
(HTTP 0)" for a removed core). So the commit step of `add-core` and `remove-core` lands the change itself
(`land_on_main` in `tools/next_add_core.py`):

1. `git merge-tree --write-tree main <commit>` first; a conflict is refused
   and nothing is touched.
2. Where `main` is checked out (normally `~/projects/forkmesh/src`), it runs
   `git merge --no-ff` there. A changed file holding exactly the merge result
   (the tool's own edit of `deploy/fleet.toml`) is set back to `main`'s copy
   first and rewritten if the merge fails. Any other unsaved or staged change
   to that file refuses the merge. Unrelated unsaved work stays as it is, and
   no stash is used.
3. When no checkout holds `main`, it writes the merge commit with plumbing and
   moves `refs/heads/main` by compare-and-swap.

The merge in the source checkout is published like any other commit
([source publisher](../tools/source-publisher.md)), and that push starts
the next deploy. A refused merge does not fail the run (the core is already
added or removed): the run records `merge_error` and prints the
`git -C <main checkout> merge --no-ff <branch>` to run. Until then, gate 1
names the pending branch: autodeploy lists `fleet/add-core-nN` branches whose
core is not in `main`'s file and `fleet/remove-core-nN` branches whose core
still is (`unmerged_fleet_branches` in `tools/next_autodeploy.py`).

## Replacing a core node

`python3 tools/next_fleet.py add-core --replace nOLD [--region R] [--plan P] --execute`
(the desktop's **Replace…** on a core row in Network, Hosts) adds a new core
and then takes `nOLD` out in the same run, so the fleet never drops below
three cores and there is one fleet commit, which lands on `main` like any
add or remove.

- The add steps run as usual. A `remove` step before `commit` then runs
  `remove-core nOLD`: it promotes the new core to a voter if needed, drains,
  stops and removes `nOLD`, and re-renders the peers.
- If the `remove` step fails, the new core stays serving and in DNS. A re-run
  (or **Retry**) resumes the removal from its own state file. Failures before
  `remove` drain the new core, as in a plain add.
- `commit` writes one commit on `fleet/add-core-nNEW` with the new block (made a
  voter if it was promoted), without the `nOLD` block, and with `nOLD` in
  `[hosted] retired_cores`. The removal's own `fleet/remove-core-nOLD` commit is
  skipped.
- The old instance is kept. Delete it later with
  `remove-core nOLD --destroy-instance --execute` (**Remove…** with the instance
  box ticked), which resumes the finished removal and runs only `destroy`.
- `add-core-options --replace nOLD --json` gives the step list and estimate;
  `add-core-status --json` includes `replaces` and `step_list`.

The manual route still works: `add-core`, then `remove-core <old>`; each
lands its own commit on `main`.
The legacy `replace-core nOLD --new nNEW` is the older, partly manual path.

## Node addresses

The repository holds no real node address. Addresses live only in
`~/projects/forkmesh/config/fleet/fleet-instances.json`, keyed by label
(`{"ip", "ipv6", "provider"}`). `render.load_fleet` fills them in; a missing
address is a `RenderError` naming the node and that operator file, and nothing
renders an empty address. Tests and docs use documentation ranges
(`203.0.113.0/24`, `198.51.100.0/24`, `2001:19f0:ffff::/48`).

### Reaching nodes over IPv6

The operator box can lose IPv4 while IPv6 still works. Node configs, firewall rules and DNS A records keep using
`ip`; only the operator's own connections can switch address family. Those are
`next_common.Ssh` (ssh, scp, tunnels) and the autodeploy `/api/version` probe,
and both go through `next_common.route_address`. `FMNEXT_ROUTE_FAMILY` picks
the family:

- `auto` (the default): use `ip` while it answers on port 22. If it doesn't
  and the node's `ipv6` does, use `ipv6`. The choice is made once per process.
- `4`: always use `ip`.
- `6`: use `ipv6` for every node that has one.

Over IPv6, ssh passes `-o HostKeyAlias=<ip>`, so the host key pinned under the
IPv4 address is still checked; no new key is accepted. A node without `ipv6`
(the runner today) always uses `ip`. Tests that inject a fake runner never
route.

## Cloud providers

Vultr and AWS EC2 sit behind `next_cloud.Provider`; the label's `provider`
field selects the client, so a mixed fleet works.

`python3 tools/next_fleet.py create r2 --provider aws [--execute]` picks the
cheapest x86_64 type with at least 1 GiB, the official Debian 13 image
(owner-checked), imports the fleet key pair, creates a tagged security group
mirroring the public nftables rules, and launches exactly one instance with
IMDSv2 only, an encrypted root volume, standard CPU credits, and tags
`Name=<label>` and `forkmesh-next=1`.

Guards: every instance must carry a `Name` matching the label rules and the
tag `forkmesh-next=1`, re-checked on every read and before every delete;
`destroy` needs `--yes` and `--execute` and respects the quorum guard.

Credentials: `config/fleet/aws.env` (0600) with `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
`AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION` (and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` for temporary
keys). The desktop can write it from Settings, Cloud.

### IAM policy

Give the fleet tools a dedicated IAM user with this policy, not administrator
access:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "Read", "Effect": "Allow",
     "Action": ["ec2:DescribeInstances", "ec2:DescribeImages",
                "ec2:DescribeKeyPairs", "ec2:DescribeSecurityGroups"],
     "Resource": "*"},
    {"Sid": "DebianAmiParameter", "Effect": "Allow",
     "Action": "ssm:GetParameter",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:*::parameter/aws/service/debian/*"},
    {"Sid": "RunTaggedInstances", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:RunInstances",
     "Resource": ["arn:aws:ec2:*:*:instance/*", "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:volume/*",
                  "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:network-interface/*"],
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestTag/forkmesh-next": "1"}}},
    {"Sid": "RunInstancesInputs", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:RunInstances",
     "Resource": ["arn:aws:ec2:*::image/*", "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:subnet/*",
                  "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:security-group/*",
                  "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:key-pair/fmnext-fleet"]},
    {"Sid": "TagOnCreateOnly", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:CreateTags",
     "Resource": "*",
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"ec2:CreateAction":
       ["RunInstances", "CreateSecurityGroup", "ImportKeyPair"]}}},
    {"Sid": "ImportFleetKey", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:ImportKeyPair",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:key-pair/fmnext-fleet",
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestTag/forkmesh-next": "1"}}},
    {"Sid": "CreateTaggedGroup", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:CreateSecurityGroup",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:security-group/*",
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:RequestTag/forkmesh-next": "1"}}},
    {"Sid": "CreateGroupInVpc", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ec2:CreateSecurityGroup",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:vpc/*"},
    {"Sid": "OpenPortsOnTaggedGroups", "Effect": "Allow",
     "Action": "ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:security-group/*",
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:ResourceTag/forkmesh-next": "1"}}},
    {"Sid": "TerminateTaggedInstances", "Effect": "Allow",
     "Action": "ec2:TerminateInstances",
     "Resource": "arn:aws:ec2:*:*:instance/*",
     "Condition": {"StringEquals": {"aws:ResourceTag/forkmesh-next": "1"}}}
  ]
}
```

Known AWS gaps: no IPv6 in the default VPC, the public IPv4 changes on
stop/start (do not stop AWS nodes), no reverse DNS, default VPC required.
Snapshot builders, `enable-ipv6`, reverse DNS and the autoscaler are
Vultr-only.

## Target checks

`install`, `roll` and `secrets` verify an existing node by its pinned SSH host
key, its own hostname or instance label, and the `/etc/forkmesh-next` marker,
so provider API outages do not block rolls. The provider key is needed only to
create or destroy instances.

## Protocols and configuration

- Cores mesh over WireGuard; rqlite Raft between voters; the app reads
  locally and writes through rqlite HTTP.
- Unseal: `DATA_KEY` over SSH stdin to the app's unix socket.
- The forkmesh.com Worker (`forkmesh-www`) signs `x-forkmesh-edge-client`
  ([edge client](../www/edge-client.md)).
- Operator config in `~/projects/forkmesh/config/fleet/` (`FMNEXT_CONFIG_DIR`);
  `FMNEXT_DIST_DIR` for builds; the label prefix guard
  `instance_label_prefix = "fmnext-"` cannot be bypassed.

## Build, run, test

```sh
python3 -m pytest deploy/tests
python3 deploy/core/render.py --help
python3 tools/next_fleet.py install n1 --steps files      # dry run
python3 tools/next_deploy.py all --execute
```

## Services on every core

- Office TURN relay: `fmnext-turn.service`, `[turn]`
  ([Office](../office/README.md)).
- Group-call server (SFU): `fmnext-calls.service`, `[calls]`, UDP 3479 and
  `/calls/*` on each per-node name ([call servers](call-servers.md)).

## Traps

- `fmnext-ids` takes `--config` before the subcommand.
- A fleet branch that is not merged into `main` makes every deploy fail on
  gate 1 ([Landing the fleet change on main](#landing-the-fleet-change-on-main)).
- Operator units must not use `PrivateTmp`.
- rqlite's default snapshot WAL size makes small databases snapshot every few
  minutes and rewrite the whole file; `[rqlite] snap_wal_size` (and optional
  `snap_entries`) raise it. The `files` step restarts rqlite only when its unit
  changed, one node at a time.
- The `files` step restarts `forkmesh-mirror-node` when its unit changed, never
  restarts zram swap while it is active, masks the systemd SSH generator on
  VMs without vsock, and stops orphaned generated sockets.
- Caddy's global server options are scoped per listener (`:443` with h1/h2/h3,
  `:80` with h1).
- Cores fetch `main` from each other after each sync; a clean code-only
  divergence becomes a deterministic merge commit so cores converge
  (`server/gateway.go`, `convergePeerMains`).
- Memory on a 1 GB core (650-740 MiB used, 220-320 MiB available). rqlite
  runs with `MemoryHigh=260M`, `MemoryMax=320M`, `GOMEMLIMIT=150MiB` and no
  swap. The page cache of the ~100 MB database counts against the unit, so at
  `MemoryMax=220M` rqlite sat at its limit and a leader was OOM-killed under a
  burst of analytics reads; `MemoryHigh` makes the kernel reclaim first.
  Details: [rqlite findings](../host/rqlite-findings.md).
- `forkmesh-mirror-node` (`MemoryHigh=96M`, `MemoryMax=128M`) also holds its
  `mirror_gateway.py` child, so the gateway's in-memory caches must stay well
  under the unit (larger caps pushed ~185 MiB per core into swap). Caps:
  responses 24 MiB, assets 12 MiB, catalog 8, sessions 2; entries in those
  two caches are counted with 1 KiB of overhead (`entry_overhead`) because
  the wrapper and headers are not in the body length; finished merge-job
  records are capped at 1,000.
- The gateway hashes a release blob before serving it. A verified
  (path, size, mtime, inode) is remembered for an hour (512 entries), so the
  `/status` download checks and repeat downloads do not re-read 60 MB files.
  The checks send `HEAD` (`status_monitoring.py`): a cancelled `GET` made the
  core stream part of each blob every minute (Caddy's "aborting with
  incomplete response").

pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh Ads

Part of [Operations](README.md).

ForkMesh Ads is a first-party, text-only ad network. Members write short ads,
a person reviews every one, and approved ads run on a product surface: the web
app, the website, the desktop app, the mobile apps, and World.

Three rules govern it:

1. **Placement is by surface, never by viewer.** The serve call takes only a
   surface name; no session, account, location, or history is read, and the
   network never learns who saw an ad.
2. **A person approves the exact words that run.** Automated screening only
   raises flags.
3. **The [prohibited list](#what-is-never-accepted) always applies**, and any
   signed-in member can report an ad.

Approval is not an endorsement and expires after 180 days. This network is
separate from [community-reviewed placements](../world-community-services.md#community-reviewed-placements)
and does not change the [business-model contract](../business-model.md):
personal data is never sold or used for advertising.

## Who can advertise

Any verified account can submit ads. There is no ad billing or bidding; an
active membership level (read from `role_grants`, see [Patreon](patreon.md))
funds live slots:

| Level | Ads running at once | Rotation weight per ad |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | 0 | — |
| Supporter | 1 | 1 |
| Pro | 2 | 2 |
| Builder | 5 | 5 |
| Studio | 10 | 10 |

Ads beyond the allowance wait; without a membership they pause. An account may
hold 25 ads and 5 pending review. The numbers live in the `advertising` block
of [`business-model.json`](/business-model.json) and are pinned by
`app/tests/test_ad_network.py`.

## What an ad is

A headline (60 characters), optional body (160), call-to-action label (24),
sponsor name (48), one public `https://` destination, one category, surfaces,
and an optional schedule. No images, scripts, embeds, or HTML. Clients render
plain text, label the slot **Sponsored**, and open the destination with
`rel="sponsored noopener noreferrer"`. Link shorteners and cross-site click
identifiers (`gclid`, `fbclid`, ...) are refused; `utm_*` tags are allowed.

Allowed categories cover developer tools, open source, hosting and
infrastructure, defensive security and privacy, education, events, hiring,
accessibility, nonprofits, climate, open hardware, independent software, and
community projects.

## What is never accepted

Gambling; tobacco, alcohol, and drugs; weapons; adult content; promised returns
or speculative tokens; predatory credit; unproven health claims; tracking, data
brokers, and stalkerware; malware or offensive hacking services; political
persuasion; hate or harassment; misleading or dark-pattern claims; illegal
goods; exploitative labor; anything aimed at children; destinations that
fingerprint, force downloads, or redirect through trackers. Reviewers cite these
rules by code. `GET /api/ads/policy` serves the machine-readable policy.

## Review

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `draft` | Saved, not submitted |
| `pending` | In the review queue |
| `approved` | May run, subject to membership, schedule, and slots |
| `rejected` | Declined with a reason and cited rules |
| `suspended` | Held by a reviewer; only a reviewer reinstates (back to `pending`) |
| `withdrawn` | Pulled by the owner |

- Reviewers are platform administrators (`users.is_admin = 1`) working at
  `/dashboard/ads`; the server enforces the role on every review route.
- Approval is pinned to the content hash of the words reviewed. An edit during
  review is refused (`creative_changed`); editing an approved ad's words sends
  it back to `pending`. Schedule changes and pauses need no review.
- Decisions are appended to `ad_network_reviews` and the audit log
  (`ad_network.approve|reject|suspend|reinstate`) without ad text. Self-review
  is allowed but recorded as such.
- Five open member reports on a running ad suspend it automatically.

## Serving and measurement

`GET /api/ads/serve?placement=web|www|desktop|mobile|world` returns one ad or
`null`. The pick is weighted by level and rotates on a five-minute bucket with
no randomness and no viewer input, so responses are cacheable
(`public, max-age=300`) and a suspension takes effect within five minutes.

The only measurement is an aggregate click counter per ad, surface, and UTC day
(`ad_network_daily_stats`, via `POST /api/ads/{id}/click`), with no viewer
columns, deleted after 400 days. Impressions are not measured, and nothing is
billed on clicks.

Clients send no credentials to the serve call, render nothing on failure, never
delay the host surface, let users hide a slot for seven days, keep legal and
documentation pages ad-free, and in World request a network ad only when no
community placement exists.

## Operating it

Storage is `ad_network_ads`, `ad_network_reviews`, `ad_network_reports`, and
`ad_network_daily_stats`. Ad text is public; the submitting username is sealed
and shown only to reviewers. Renaming an account moves its ads; deleting it
deletes ads, reports, and counters. The down migration drops the four tables
and touches no membership data. No third-party ad code runs anywhere, ads never
affect ranking or moderation, and self-hosted instances run their own
instance-local network.

pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh deployment and scheduled automation

Part of [Operations](README.md).

Deployment and automation tools. None of them writes wallet keys, API tokens or
GitHub tokens to the repository.

## Workers self-host bootstrap

The hosted service runs on self-hosted core nodes, not Workers
([architecture](../architecture.md)); the usual self-host is a VPS
([self-hosting](../self-hosting.md)). `tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py` sets up the
optional Workers self-host on your own Cloudflare account. It
creates or reuses D1 and KV storage, applies all
migrations, deploys one complete App Worker, creates proxied DNS, attaches
one broad `hostname/*` App route, and verifies health, release identity, public
snapshots and an authenticated database/encryption probe. Repository bytes stay
on independently operated mirrors ([mirroring](../mirroring.md)); the Worker
provides discovery and routing.
`--main-relay-url https://app.forkmesh.com` joins the instance to an existing
relay mesh once that relay approves it.

The scoped API token needs only: Account Settings read, Workers Scripts edit,
Workers KV Storage edit, D1 edit, Cloudflare Tunnel edit, Zone read, and DNS
edit plus Workers Routes edit for the selected zone. With exactly one account
and one active zone, `--auto-configure` derives every name; otherwise pass
`--hostname`, `--zone`, `--worker-name`, `--database-name` and `--node-name`.

```bash
export CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN="locally-supplied-token"  # forkmesh-secret-scan:ignore-line
python3 tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py --auto-configure
```

### Secrets and identities

- **`DATA_KEY`.** On a new database the bootstrap generates `DATA_KEY` with the
  OS CSPRNG, writes a mode-`0600` recovery copy outside the repository
  (`--data-key-backup` selects the path), uploads it as a Worker secret and
  proves D1 plus encryption work. Losing both copies makes encrypted data
  unrecoverable. A rerun without a recovery copy fails closed until the value
  is restored with `--secret-env DATA_KEY`.
- **Router identity.** A new one-click installation needs no
  router secret in the environment: an Ed25519 router seed and public key are
  generated, cross-checked and saved to an owner-only recovery file
  (`--router-identity-backup`). For a restore, supply
  `MIRROR_ROUTER_SIGNING_SEED` and `MIRROR_ROUTER_PUBLIC_KEY`; the seed must
  derive the key exactly. The seed is never put in argv, a temporary config,
  a log or JSON output. Staging uploads the signing seed
  first and the public key last, so an interrupted install fails closed.
- **Token handling.** There is no `--api-token` flag; the token reaches
  Wrangler only through the child environment. `--secret-env NAME` pipes other
  secrets to `wrangler secret put`. The checked-in `wrangler.toml` is untouched.

### Rerun safety

Before any change the bootstrap confirms the App Worker exists, that the
hostname has only proxied address records, and that only the canonical App
route overlaps it. A legacy exact control route is a blocker that
`--replace-route` cannot remove. It then reads the public App identity route
`https://<hostname>/api/mirrors/https`; an unavailable, redirected or
unexpected response fails before D1, DNS, routes, secrets or the Worker change,
and a local key can never rotate a published one. Success requires
`/api/mainnode` and `/api/version` to report the same build and the matching
key. `--dry-run` performs all checks without mutation. `--with-world` also
deploys the optional World Worker on its own hostname.

### Direct-HTTPS mirror discovery contract

Trusted mirrors publish `https://<mirror-host>/forkmesh-mirror.json`
(schema: [`mirror-endpoint.schema.json`](../mirror-endpoint.schema.json),
gateway: [direct-HTTPS mirror gateway](direct-https-mirror-gateway.md)), signed with the node's
Ed25519 key over sorted compact JSON (`forkmesh-json-sort-v1`). It names the
node key, health URL, repository URL template, `transport: direct-https`,
`mainProxyMode: masked` and `repositoryBytesInD1: false`. The node key comes
from `FORKMESH_NODE_PUBLIC_KEY`; signatures come from the shell-free command in
`FORKMESH_MIRROR_MANIFEST_SIGNER`. `--skip-mirror-manifest` installs a
relay-only node.

## Daily one-way GitHub issue synchronization

`.github/workflows/github-issue-sync.yml` (daily, manual runs default to
dry-run) copies issues from `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_SOURCE` to
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION`, one direction only. Cross-repository runs
need `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_SOURCE_TOKEN` and
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION_TOKEN` (or one `FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_TOKEN`). A
hidden `forkmesh-issue-sync:v1` marker maps each copy and its content digest, so
unchanged issues are not rewritten. `tools/github_issue_sync.py sync` runs the
same logic locally with token names passed via `--*-token-env`. Until
`FORKMESH_ISSUE_SYNC_DESTINATION` is set, the scheduled run writes a notice
and skips the sync instead of failing; a manual run without it still fails.

## Native daily public-safe security scan

`tools/native_security_scan_runner.py` runs hourly on the owner's node, decides
whether a scan is due, and leases a one-use capability bound to the repository
and commit. `tools/security_scan.py` inventories lockfile dependencies against
OSV (names and versions only), flags credential-shaped content without
recording values, and runs focused static checks. Artifacts
(`security-scan.json`, `security-clipboard.json`, `security-scan.md`) contain no
source excerpts or secret values; offline runs keep them locally and retry. The
relay encrypts ingested reports with `DATA_KEY`, keeps the 90 newest per
repository, and serves `security-scans/latest` and `/history`: public
repositories expose the redacted clipboard, everything else needs owner
authorization. Reports are not a guarantee of security.

## External Solana signer and reward scheduling

`tools/reward_scheduler.py` selects one eligible, attested mirror per round from
a frozen snapshot using public entropy, and never generates or accepts a private
key. An external signer receives the intent on stdin and returns a signed
transaction; responses containing key material are rejected. Pending rewards
are 24-hour reservations; funds move only after the signer approves a claim
([community reward pool, local signer](community-reward-pool.md#local-signer)).

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh desktop control node

Part of [Operations](README.md).

The desktop client's **Control** page is the operator surface for the current
device. It never makes ForkMesh a custodian. Its tabs are Site deployment,
Export, Import, Mirror client, Repository permissions, Keys and wallet, Reward
pool, Cloudflare relay, and API token (`desktop/src/MainWindowControlNode.cpp`).
Host management lives under **Network → Hosts**. Other ways to run an instance
are in [self-hosting](../self-hosting.md).

## Mirror client and permissions

The status card shows the relay connection, tracked local mirrors, managed-node
repositories, and sync jobs. The desktop itself never serves repositories or
registers endpoints. **Sync all mirrors** fetches every mirror; **Run health
check** verifies the local identity, Git, bootstrap tooling, mirror paths, and
relay connection.

Per-repository permissions: **Private** (discovery and authorized access),
**Serve** (whether managed hosts may publish it), **Run actions** (local
`.forkmesh` workflows), and **Secret scan** (push protection). Only a device
holding the owner's signing identity can change visibility or serving, and
every change is recorded in the local audit log.

## Identity and wallet

The Ed25519 identity key is generated locally with owner-only permissions and
can be backed up as a passphrase-encrypted keyfile. The wallet field accepts
only a 32-byte base58 Solana public address and rejects seed phrases and
private keys. Connecting an address authorizes nothing; private keys stay in
the user's own wallet.

## Export, import, and deployment

- **Export complete system…** writes one `forkmesh-complete-system-v1` JSON
  file with every setting, Actions variable and secret, the deployment
  environment file, and all application data (identity, SSH keys, stores),
  each with size, mode, and SHA-256. It is written owner-only and refuses
  symlinks. It contains private keys in clear text: store it encrypted.
- **New deployment…** validates a bundle's schema, paths, sizes, and digests
  before showing values, then applies it and hands off to the durable host
  provisioner.

Deployment runs the bundled
[`tools/cloudflare_bootstrap.py`](automation-and-cloudflare-bootstrap.md), which
sets up the user's own Workers self-host (the hosted service
itself runs on core nodes, see [architecture](../architecture.md)). With a token
scoped to one account and zone it discovers the topology; with several it
requires explicit selection rather than guessing. **Validate** is a read-only
dry run; **Deploy** creates or reuses the database, deploys the server,
configures DNS and routes, provisions the tunnel, and runs health checks.

Credential rules: the token is never saved by the deploy card, never placed in
process arguments, passed only as `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in the child
environment, never turned into a server secret, and redacted from output. A
missing `cloudflared` is installed by a bundled installer that verifies pinned
SHA-256 digests. Endpoint manifests are signed by launching the desktop binary
with `--sign-mirror-manifest`, which validates the manifest and returns only the
public key and signature.

## API token

**Check token permissions** verifies a Cloudflare token, reads its own policy
when allowed, and probes each capability read-only (a read probe cannot prove
edit rights).

| Cloudflare permission | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Account Settings: Read | discovering the account |
| Workers Scripts: Edit | uploading the server, assets, triggers, and secrets |
| D1: Edit | creating and migrating the database |
| Zone: Read | finding the zone |
| DNS: Edit | relay and mirror records |
| Cloudflare Tunnel: Edit | the mirror gateway tunnel |

Optional: Workers Tail: Read, API Tokens: Read/Edit. **Generate and install a
new token** mints a replacement scoped to the resolved account, zone, and user,
replaces `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` in the device variables and deployment
environment file (owner-only, other entries preserved), and re-checks it. The
new token is shown only by its last four characters; the old one stays valid
until deleted, allowing rollback.

## Connected hosts

**Network → Hosts** adds remote machines, installs, updates, or removes
ForkMesh, signs in agent CLIs, and shows logs. Every host operation
authenticates with one shared fleet SSH key generated on first use and kept
owner-only on the desktop. Passwords are an optional fallback, stay on the
desktop, and are passed via environment or stdin, never arguments.

## Reward-pool signer

The Control page hosts the local signer for the community reward pool; see
[community reward pool, local signer](community-reward-pool.md#local-signer).

pages.markdown:
# ForkMesh disaster recovery runbook

<!-- Generated by tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py render from conformance/disaster-recovery/v1/runbook.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Part of [Disaster recovery](README.md).

Version **1.0.1**, updated 2026-09-14. Runbook digest: `e5cd0aa7da7cb3a0902837961389ca1351d378460a64eccedaaa01913bd8242d`.

This runbook works with no network and no forkmesh.com. Print it, write the
digest above and the kit public key on the printed copy, and keep it with
the signed bootstrap kit. `kit verify` prints the same digest, so a reader
can tell that the paper and the kit agree. Review it at least every 90 days.

## How to use this runbook

1. The coordinator assigns the roles below. The verifier never checks a copy they produced.
2. Walk the triage tree. It sends you to one scenario.
3. Follow that scenario's decision tree. Each step names a procedure.
4. Do not skip a procedure's verification. Stop at any unsafe step until the verifier agrees.
5. The scribe fills in the exercise worksheet at the end, for incidents as well as drills.

Commands use placeholders in angle brackets, such as `<KIT>`. Run them from
the kit directory, which holds the same `tools/` as the repository.

## Triage

1. **Has the bootstrap kit verified against the kit key written on paper?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3.
2. **Is a signing key, recovery key, or passphrase lost or possibly stolen?** Yes: go to 4. No: go to 5.
3. Do [Verify the bootstrap kit](#verify-the-bootstrap-kit-verify-bootstrap-kit), then go to 6.
4. Go to scenario [Key loss](#key-loss-key-loss).
5. **Did a backup or export fail to verify?** Yes: go to 7. No: go to 8.
6. **Did the kit verify (exit 0, or exit 4 stale)?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 9.
7. Go to scenario [Corrupted backup](#corrupted-backup-corrupted-backup).
8. **Do hostnames fail to resolve while addresses still answer?** Yes: go to 10. No: go to 11.
9. **Escalate.** Stop. Do not run tools from unverified media. Get the second custodian's kit and the printed runbook.
10. Go to scenario [DNS loss](#dns-loss-dns-loss).
11. **Is your region cut off from every other region?** Yes: go to 12. No: go to 13.
12. Go to scenario [Regional isolation](#regional-isolation-regional-isolation).
13. **Is a repository's origin host gone or wiped?** Yes: go to 14. No: go to 15.
14. Go to scenario [Origin loss](#origin-loss-origin-loss).
15. **Are hosted services (website, index, sign-in, collaboration inboxes) unavailable?** Yes: go to 16. No: go to 17.
16. Go to scenario [Main-service loss](#main-service-loss-main-service-loss).
17. **Does a new member or machine need to join with no internet?** Yes: go to 18. No: go to 19.
18. Go to scenario [Offline bootstrap](#offline-bootstrap-offline-bootstrap).
19. **No incident.** No scenario applies. Record what you saw and keep watching.

## Roles

### Incident coordinator (`coordinator`)

Declares the incident, walks the triage tree, assigns the other roles, keeps the clock, and decides when normal service may take over again.

- [ ] Write down the time the incident was declared.
- [ ] Walk the triage tree aloud with at least one other person.
- [ ] Assign a key custodian, a mirror operator, a verifier, and a scribe. One person may hold two roles, but the verifier never checks their own copy.
- [ ] Stop any step a checklist marks unsafe until the verifier agrees.
- [ ] Declare recovery only after the verifier's checks pass, and hand the scribe the time.

### Key custodian (`key-custodian`)

Holds offline recovery keys and backup passphrases, and signs key rotations. Never types a recovery key into a shared or unverified machine.

- [ ] Bring your recovery key and your paper copy of the pinned public keys.
- [ ] Check the rotation statement's revoked and successor keys against paper before signing.
- [ ] Refuse any request to lower the recovery threshold during the incident.
- [ ] Sign only on a machine that verified the bootstrap kit.
- [ ] Return recovery keys to separate physical storage afterwards.

### Mirror operator (`mirror-operator`)

Stands up emergency mirrors, writes and imports removable media, and restores origins and nodes.

- [ ] Never delete or force-push refs on a surviving copy.
- [ ] Keep every copy you start from untouched until recovery is declared.
- [ ] Serve emergency mirrors read-only unless the coordinator approves writes.
- [ ] Record every command you ran and when it finished for the scribe.

### Verifier (`verifier`)

Independently checks signatures, digests, and refs against pinned keys and signed pins. Must not be the person who produced the copy being checked.

- [ ] Read pinned public keys from paper, never from the media being checked.
- [ ] Verify the bootstrap kit before anyone runs a tool from it.
- [ ] Check restored refs against a signed export or a second independent copy.
- [ ] Run git fsck on every restored repository.
- [ ] Say out loud which checks passed and which were skipped.

### Scribe (`scribe`)

Records the exercise or incident: times, missing prerequisites, data loss, unsafe steps, and a corrective owner for every finding.

- [ ] Record declared, recovered, and verified times.
- [ ] List every prerequisite that was missing and who will fix it.
- [ ] List commits, refs, issues, or pull requests that were lost.
- [ ] List every unsafe step, whether it was taken or refused.
- [ ] Give every finding a corrective owner before the debrief ends.

## Prerequisites

Check these before a disaster. The scribe records any that were missing.

| Prerequisite | Owner | How to check | Needed by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A printed or offline copy of this runbook, with the kit digest written on it (`printed-runbook`) | Incident coordinator | Two people can find a copy without a network connection. | `offline-bootstrap` |
| A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`) | Verifier | kit verify passes against the kit key written on paper, before the review date. | `origin-loss`, `main-service-loss`, `dns-loss`, `key-loss`, `regional-isolation`, `corrupted-backup`, `offline-bootstrap` |
| Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`) | Key custodian | The keys on paper match roster check output. | `origin-loss`, `key-loss`, `regional-isolation`, `corrupted-backup`, `offline-bootstrap` |
| Enough recovery key custodians, in separate places, to meet the roster threshold (`recovery-key-threshold`) | Key custodian | roster check reports the threshold is met by distinct holders. | `key-loss` |
| A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`) | Incident coordinator | roster check reports dnsFree true. | `origin-loss`, `main-service-loss`, `dns-loss`, `key-loss`, `offline-bootstrap` |
| At least two copies of each repository under separate control (`independent-copies`) | Mirror operator | A mirror and a verified removable-media export, or two mirrors run by different people. | `origin-loss`, `main-service-loss`, `corrupted-backup` |
| A backup or export verified within the review interval (`tested-backup`) | Mirror operator | forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify or forkmesh-mirror-node --restore-drill passed recently. | `corrupted-backup` |
| Node backup passphrases stored away from the node (`backup-passphrase-off-host`) | Key custodian | The custodian can produce the passphrase file without the node. | `corrupted-backup` |
| Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region (`recovery-toolchain`) | Mirror operator | git --version and python3 --version. | `origin-loss`, `main-service-loss`, `dns-loss`, `regional-isolation` |
| Blank removable media large enough for every repository (`removable-media`) | Mirror operator | The media is labelled and stored with the kit. | `regional-isolation` |
| A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet (`local-network`) | Mirror operator | Two machines can reach each other by address. | `main-service-loss`, `dns-loss`, `regional-isolation`, `offline-bootstrap` |

## Scenarios

### Origin loss (`origin-loss`)

Signals:

- The origin host is gone, wiped, or refuses every read.
- Mirrors still hold copies, possibly a little behind.

Objectives: recover within 60 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`), At least two copies of each repository under separate control (`independent-copies`), Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`), Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region (`recovery-toolchain`).

Decision tree:

1. Do [Find mirrors and contacts without the website](#find-mirrors-and-contacts-without-the-website-discover-from-roster), then go to 2.
2. Do [Inventory every surviving copy](#inventory-every-surviving-copy-inventory-surviving-copies), then go to 3.
3. **Does at least one surviving copy verify against a signed export or a second copy?** Yes: go to 4. No: go to 5.
4. Do [Restore an origin from surviving copies](#restore-an-origin-from-surviving-copies-restore-origin-from-mirror), then go to 6.
5. **Is there a verified removable-media export?** Yes: go to 7. No: go to 8.
6. Do [Return to normal service cleanly](#return-to-normal-service-cleanly-return-to-normal-service), then go to 9.
7. Do [Carry repositories on removable media](#carry-repositories-on-removable-media-carry-removable-media), then go to 4.
8. **Escalate.** No verified copy survives. Ask every roster contact for clones, and follow crisis preservation for public copies elsewhere.
9. **Recovered.** The new origin is verified and serving.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run origin-loss
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run origin-loss --fault no-local-clone
```

### Main-service loss (`main-service-loss`)

Signals:

- forkmesh.com, its sign-in, index, or collaboration inboxes do not answer.
- Service role probes exit 4 (unreachable).

Objectives: recover within 60 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`), At least two copies of each repository under separate control (`independent-copies`), A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet (`local-network`), Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region (`recovery-toolchain`).

Decision tree:

1. Do [Find mirrors and contacts without the website](#find-mirrors-and-contacts-without-the-website-discover-from-roster), then go to 2.
2. **Does a roster mirror answer reads?** Yes: go to 3. No: go to 4.
3. Do [Check that a surviving mirror serves reads](#check-that-a-surviving-mirror-serves-reads-verify-mirror-role), then go to 5.
4. Do [Serve a read-only emergency mirror from plain files](#serve-a-read-only-emergency-mirror-from-plain-files-serve-static-emergency-mirror), then go to 5.
5. **Must the community accept pushes and pull requests before service returns?** Yes: go to 6. No: go to 7.
6. Do [Accept pushes and pull requests without the hosted service](#accept-pushes-and-pull-requests-without-the-hosted-service-run-independent-gateway), then go to 7.
7. Do [Return to normal service cleanly](#return-to-normal-service-cleanly-return-to-normal-service), then go to 8.
8. **Recovered.** The community reads, and if needed writes, without the hosted service.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run main-service-loss
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run main-service-loss --fault no-surviving-mirror
```

### DNS loss (`dns-loss`)

Signals:

- Hostnames do not resolve, or resolve to the wrong place.
- Addresses on the roster still answer.

Objectives: recover within 30 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`), A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet (`local-network`), Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region (`recovery-toolchain`).

Decision tree:

1. **Does the roster list an address or pinned host for a mirror you can reach?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3.
2. Do [Clone over the local network with no DNS](#clone-over-the-local-network-with-no-dns-clone-over-lan-without-dns), then go to 4.
3. Do [Carry repositories on removable media](#carry-repositories-on-removable-media-carry-removable-media), then go to 5.
4. **Did the transport exit 0 (not unreachable or exposed)?** Yes: go to 5. No: go to 3.
5. **Do other people on the network need the repository?** Yes: go to 6. No: go to 7.
6. Do [Serve a read-only emergency mirror from plain files](#serve-a-read-only-emergency-mirror-from-plain-files-serve-static-emergency-mirror), then go to 7.
7. **Recovered.** Repositories move by address or media, with no DNS.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run dns-loss
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run dns-loss --fault no-pinned-address
```

### Key loss (`key-loss`)

Signals:

- A signing key, device, or passphrase is lost.
- A key may be in someone else's hands.

Objectives: recover within 120 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`), Enough recovery key custodians, in separate places, to meet the roster threshold (`recovery-key-threshold`), A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`).

Decision tree:

1. **Can the roster's threshold of recovery key custodians sign?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3.
2. Do [Replace a lost or stolen signing key](#replace-a-lost-or-stolen-signing-key-rotate-lost-export-key), then go to 4.
3. **Escalate.** Do not lower the threshold. Treat media signed by the lost key as untrusted and wait for custodians.
4. Do [Carry repositories on removable media](#carry-repositories-on-removable-media-carry-removable-media), then go to 5.
5. **Is media signed by the revoked key refused, and media signed by the successor imported?** Yes: go to 6. No: go to 3.
6. Do [Return to normal service cleanly](#return-to-normal-service-cleanly-return-to-normal-service), then go to 7.
7. **Recovered.** The successor key is trusted and the lost key is revoked.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run key-loss
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run key-loss --fault threshold-unreachable
```

### Regional isolation (`regional-isolation`)

Signals:

- A region has no connection to other regions, while its local network still works.
- Work continues on both sides.

Objectives: recover within 1440 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`), Blank removable media large enough for every repository (`removable-media`), A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet (`local-network`), Git 2.40 or newer and Python 3.9 or newer on at least one machine in each region (`recovery-toolchain`).

Decision tree:

1. **Does anyone in your region hold a mirror or clone?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3.
2. Do [Serve a read-only emergency mirror from plain files](#serve-a-read-only-emergency-mirror-from-plain-files-serve-static-emergency-mirror), then go to 4.
3. Do [Carry repositories on removable media](#carry-repositories-on-removable-media-carry-removable-media), then go to 2.
4. **Can someone carry media between regions?** Yes: go to 5. No: go to 6.
5. Do [Reconcile regions that worked apart](#reconcile-regions-that-worked-apart-reconcile-after-isolation), then go to 7.
6. **Escalate.** Keep working locally, export on a schedule, and carry media when a route opens.
7. **Has the network between regions returned?** Yes: go to 8. No: go to 9.
8. Do [Return to normal service cleanly](#return-to-normal-service-cleanly-return-to-normal-service), then go to 10.
9. **Recovered.** Regions stay in step by carried media until the network returns.
10. **Recovered.** Both regions hold every commit, and diverged work is under review.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run regional-isolation
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run regional-isolation --fault unpinned-region-key
```

### Corrupted backup (`corrupted-backup`)

Signals:

- A backup or export fails verification.
- A restore drill fails its checks.

Objectives: recover within 60 minutes; data loss allowed: commits newer than the last verified copy; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), At least two copies of each repository under separate control (`independent-copies`), A backup or export verified within the review interval (`tested-backup`), Node backup passphrases stored away from the node (`backup-passphrase-off-host`), Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`).

Decision tree:

1. **Is the failing backup a mirror node archive (.fmbackup)?** Yes: go to 2. No: go to 3.
2. Do [Restore a mirror node from its encrypted backup](#restore-a-mirror-node-from-its-encrypted-backup-restore-node-backup), then go to 4.
3. Do [Restore from the newest backup that verifies](#restore-from-the-newest-backup-that-verifies-choose-good-backup), then go to 5.
4. **Does a mirror or clone hold commits newer than the restored copy?** Yes: go to 6. No: go to 7.
5. **Did any copy verify?** Yes: go to 4. No: go to 8.
6. Do [Restore an origin from surviving copies](#restore-an-origin-from-surviving-copies-restore-origin-from-mirror), then go to 7.
7. Do [Return to normal service cleanly](#return-to-normal-service-cleanly-return-to-normal-service), then go to 9.
8. **Escalate.** No copy verifies. Do not repair bundles by hand; ask roster contacts for clones.
9. **Recovered.** Restored from the newest verified copy; losses are recorded.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run corrupted-backup
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run corrupted-backup --fault all-copies-corrupt
```

### Offline bootstrap (`offline-bootstrap`)

Signals:

- A new member or machine must join with no internet.
- The only material is the printed runbook, the kit, and keys on paper.

Objectives: recover within 30 minutes; data loss allowed: none; automated drill budget 120 seconds.

Prerequisites: A printed or offline copy of this runbook, with the kit digest written on it (`printed-runbook`), A signed bootstrap kit on removable media (`verified-kit`), Kit, export, and recovery public keys written on paper held by two people (`pinned-keys-on-paper`), A roster of mirrors and contacts with at least one address that needs no DNS (`community-roster`), A switch, hotspot, or community network the region can join without the internet (`local-network`).

Decision tree:

1. Do [Verify the bootstrap kit](#verify-the-bootstrap-kit-verify-bootstrap-kit), then go to 2.
2. **Did the kit verify?** Yes: go to 3. No: go to 4.
3. Do [Find mirrors and contacts without the website](#find-mirrors-and-contacts-without-the-website-discover-from-roster), then go to 5.
4. **Escalate.** Do not run anything from the kit. Get the second custodian's kit.
5. Do [Clone over the local network with no DNS](#clone-over-the-local-network-with-no-dns-clone-over-lan-without-dns), then go to 6.
6. **Recovered.** The new member holds a verified clone and the verified kit.

Automated drill:

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run offline-bootstrap
python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py drill run offline-bootstrap --fault wrong-kit-key
```

## Procedures

### Verify the bootstrap kit (`verify-bootstrap-kit`)

Topic: `offline-bootstrap`. Lead: Verifier. Reference: `docs/disaster-recovery/README.md#the-bootstrap-kit`.

Steps:

1. **Verifier:** Copy the kit from removable media to a local directory. Do not run anything from it yet.
2. **Verifier:** Verify the kit with the kit public key written on paper.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit verify <KIT> --trusted-key <KIT KEY FROM PAPER>
   ```

   Expect: Exit 0 and the manifest digest you wrote on the printed runbook.

   **Unsafe:** Never take the trusted key from the kit itself; a forged kit carries its own key.

3. **Incident coordinator:** If verification exits 4 (stale), continue, but give the scribe a finding to rebuild the kit.

Verify:

- [ ] kit verify exits 0 or 4 with the pinned kit key.
- [ ] The printed manifest digest matches the digest the tool prints.

Roll back:

- Discard the copy and verify the second custodian's kit instead.

### Find mirrors and contacts without the website (`discover-from-roster`)

Topic: `independent-discovery`. Lead: Incident coordinator. Reference: `docs/disaster-recovery/README.md#the-community-roster`.

Steps:

1. **Incident coordinator:** Check the roster from the verified kit and list its mirrors, addresses, and contacts.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check <KIT>/roster.json
   ```

   Expect: Exit 0, the active keys, and every mirror address.

2. **Mirror operator:** Try each mirror address, starting with the ones that need no DNS.

   ```sh
   git ls-remote <MIRROR URL>
   ```

3. **Incident coordinator:** Reach roster contacts over the channels the roster lists: phone, radio, or in person.

Verify:

- [ ] At least one mirror answered, or every contact was tried and the answers are written down.

Roll back:

- Nothing to undo: discovery only reads.

### Inventory every surviving copy (`inventory-surviving-copies`)

Topic: `clean-restoration`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#start-here-carry-a-repository-on-a-usb-stick`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** List the refs of every mirror, clone, and export people still hold.

   ```sh
   git -C <COPY> for-each-ref '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)'
   ```

2. **Verifier:** Verify each removable-media export against the pinned export keys.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify <MEDIA> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>
   ```

3. **Mirror operator:** For each ref, find the most advanced copy: the one whose tip contains every other copy's tip.

   ```sh
   git -C <COPY> merge-base --is-ancestor <OLDER TIP> <NEWER TIP>
   ```


Verify:

- [ ] Every ref has one chosen source, and diverged refs are written down rather than chosen.

Roll back:

- Nothing to undo: the inventory only reads.

### Restore an origin from surviving copies (`restore-origin-from-mirror`)

Topic: `emergency-mirror`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#start-here-carry-a-repository-on-a-usb-stick`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Create the new origin from the verified surviving mirror.

   ```sh
   git clone --mirror <SURVIVING MIRROR> <NEW ORIGIN>
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Push newer work from each local clone. Git refuses anything that is not a fast-forward.

   ```sh
   git -C <LOCAL CLONE> push --atomic <NEW ORIGIN> 'refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*' 'refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*'
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never add --force. A rejected push means the copies diverged; keep both and review.


Verify:

- [ ] Connectivity check passes. `git -C <NEW ORIGIN> fsck --connectivity-only`
- [ ] Every ref in the newest signed export is present, or contained in the restored ref. `python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify <MEDIA> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>`
- [ ] Collaboration records under .forkmesh/ are present on their branches.

Roll back:

- Delete the new origin directory. The surviving copies were never changed.

### Serve a read-only emergency mirror from plain files (`serve-static-emergency-mirror`)

Topic: `emergency-mirror`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#fetch-over-a-link-that-keeps-dropping`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Copy a verified repository into a directory to serve.

   ```sh
   git clone --mirror <VERIFIED COPY> <SERVE DIR>/<NAME>.git
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Write the files a static HTTP clone needs.

   ```sh
   git -C <SERVE DIR>/<NAME>.git update-server-info
   ```

3. **Mirror operator:** Serve the directory on the local network.

   ```sh
   python3 -m http.server 8080 --bind <LAN ADDRESS> --directory <SERVE DIR>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** A static mirror has no access control. Serve only public repositories, and only on networks the coordinator approves.


Verify:

- [ ] A second machine clones the mirror. `git clone --mirror http://<LAN ADDRESS>:8080/<NAME>.git <CHECK DIR>`
- [ ] The clone's refs match a signed export or a second copy. Integrity comes from those pins, not from the server.

Roll back:

- Stop the HTTP server and delete the serve directory.

### Check that a surviving mirror serves reads (`verify-mirror-role`)

Topic: `emergency-mirror`. Lead: Verifier. Reference: `docs/operations/service-roles.md#checking-a-running-role`.

Steps:

1. **Verifier:** Probe the mirror's relay role.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role relay --base-url <MIRROR URL> --param owner=<OWNER> --param repository=<REPOSITORY>
   ```

   Expect: Exit 0 (pass) or 3 (degraded). Exit 4 means nothing answered: treat it as loss, never as an empty repository.


Verify:

- [ ] The probe verdict is pass or degraded.

Roll back:

- Nothing to undo: the probe sends only reads.

### Accept pushes and pull requests without the hosted service (`run-independent-gateway`)

Topic: `emergency-mirror`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/operations/service-roles.md#starting-the-independent-profiles`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Check the node before starting it.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --preflight --json
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Start the node with the hosted tunnel disabled and your own endpoints.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --disable-cloudflared --upstream <ROSTER MIRROR URL> --catalog-url <ROSTER CATALOG URL>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Leaving --upstream at its default points the node at forkmesh.com, which is unavailable.


Verify:

- [ ] The relay role probe passes against the node. `python3 tools/forkmesh_service_roles.py probe --role relay --base-url <NODE URL>`

Roll back:

- Stop the node. Submissions it spooled but did not commit are kept in its pull submission spool.

### Clone over the local network with no DNS (`clone-over-lan-without-dns`)

Topic: `local-network`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/transports.md#postures`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Write a lan-only transport profile from the roster's pinned addresses.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster profile <KIT>/roster.json --out <LAN PROFILE>
   ```

2. **Verifier:** Confirm the mirror's route uses a pinned address and needs no DNS.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_transports.py plan --profile <LAN PROFILE> <MIRROR URL>
   ```

3. **Mirror operator:** Clone over that route. On Linux the Git process is traced for DNS queries and off-route connections.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_transports.py git --profile <LAN PROFILE> <MIRROR URL> -- clone --mirror @URL <DIR>
   ```

   Expect: Exit 0. Exit 5 means a DNS query or off-route connection was seen.


Verify:

- [ ] The transport exits 0, not 4 (unreachable) or 5 (exposed).
- [ ] The clone's refs match a signed export or a second copy.

Roll back:

- Delete the clone and the profile.

### Carry repositories on removable media (`carry-removable-media`)

Topic: `removable-media`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#start-here-carry-a-repository-on-a-usb-stick`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Export a signed copy to the media.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export <REPO> <MEDIA> --signing-key <EXPORT SEED> --repository <OWNER/NAME>
   ```

2. **Verifier:** On the receiving side, verify the media against the pinned export key.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify <MEDIA> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>
   ```

3. **Mirror operator:** Import it. Diverged refs are kept aside, never overwritten.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import <MEDIA> <REPO> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never pass --allow-unpinned during an incident: anyone can sign media.


Verify:

- [ ] Import exits 0, or 5 with conflicts kept aside for review.

Roll back:

- Undo the import's ref changes. `python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py rollback <REPO> <IMPORT ID>`

### Replace a lost or stolen signing key (`rotate-lost-export-key`)

Topic: `key-recovery`. Lead: Key custodian. Reference: `docs/disaster-recovery/README.md#key-recovery`, `docs/portable-identities.md#recovery-drills`, `docs/operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md#moving-or-replacing-an-identity-key`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Generate the successor key on a machine that verified the kit.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py keygen <SUCCESSOR SEED>
   ```

2. **Key custodian:** The first custodian writes and signs the rotation statement.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key rotate --roster <ROSTER> --recovery-key <RECOVERY SEED> --revoke <LOST KEY> --successor <SUCCESSOR KEY> --holder <HOLDER> --reason <REASON> --issued <YYYY-MM-DD> --out <ROTATION>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** The lost key must never sign its own replacement, and the threshold must never be lowered during an incident.

3. **Key custodian:** Each further custodian checks the keys against paper and adds a signature until the threshold is met.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key cosign <ROTATION> --recovery-key <RECOVERY SEED>
   ```

4. **Verifier:** Apply the rotation to write the new roster.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py key apply <ROSTER> <ROTATION> --out <NEW ROSTER>
   ```

5. **Mirror operator:** For a mirror node identity, import the node's sealed identity export instead.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --passphrase-file <PASSPHRASE FILE> --import-identity <IDENTITY EXPORT> --replace-identity
   ```


Verify:

- [ ] key apply exits 0 and roster check lists the lost key as revoked. `python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py roster check <NEW ROSTER>`
- [ ] Media signed by the revoked key now fails import, and media signed by the successor imports.

Roll back:

- A rotation cannot be unsigned. Keep the old roster file for the record, and issue a further rotation if the successor was wrong.

### Restore from the newest backup that verifies (`choose-good-backup`)

Topic: `clean-restoration`. Lead: Verifier. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#start-here-carry-a-repository-on-a-usb-stick`.

Steps:

1. **Verifier:** Verify copies newest first. Stop at the first that verifies.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py verify <MEDIA> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never import a copy that failed verification, and never repair a bundle by hand.

2. **Mirror operator:** Import the verified copy into an empty repository.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import <MEDIA> <EMPTY REPO> --trusted-key <EXPORT KEY>
   ```


Verify:

- [ ] Connectivity check passes. `git -C <EMPTY REPO> fsck --connectivity-only`
- [ ] The scribe records which newer copies were rejected, and which commits they held that are now lost.

Roll back:

- Delete the restored repository; the backups were only read.

### Restore a mirror node from its encrypted backup (`restore-node-backup`)

Topic: `clean-restoration`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/operations/node-backup-and-recovery.md#restoring-a-node`.

Steps:

1. **Verifier:** Rehearse the archive in scratch space first.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --passphrase-file <PASSPHRASE FILE> --restore-drill <ARCHIVE>
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Dry-run, then restore onto the new host.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --passphrase-file <PASSPHRASE FILE> --restore <ARCHIVE> --dry-run
   ```

3. **Mirror operator:** Restore for real.

   ```sh
   forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --passphrase-file <PASSPHRASE FILE> --restore <ARCHIVE>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never run the old host and its restored copy at the same time.


Verify:

- [ ] Preflight reports no errors. `forkmesh-mirror-node --config <CONFIG> --preflight --json`

Roll back:

- A failed restore deletes everything it created. Try the next older archive.

### Reconcile regions that worked apart (`reconcile-after-isolation`)

Topic: `removable-media`. Lead: Mirror operator. Reference: `docs/offline-sync.md#start-here-carry-a-repository-on-a-usb-stick`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Each region exports with its own key, and the media travels both ways.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py export <REGION REPO> <MEDIA> --signing-key <REGION SEED>
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Each region imports the other's media. Diverged branches are kept under refs/forkmesh-offline/conflicts/.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py import <MEDIA> <REGION REPO> --trusted-key <OTHER REGION KEY>
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never force-push a region's branch over the other's kept-aside work.

3. **Incident coordinator:** Review each kept-aside branch and merge it through a normal pull request.

Verify:

- [ ] Every commit from both regions is reachable in both repositories. `git -C <REGION REPO> rev-list --all`

Roll back:

- Undo an import's ref changes. `python3 tools/forkmesh_offline_sync.py rollback <REGION REPO> <IMPORT ID>`

### Return to normal service cleanly (`return-to-normal-service`)

Topic: `clean-restoration`. Lead: Incident coordinator. Reference: `docs/disaster-recovery/README.md#clean-restoration`.

Steps:

1. **Mirror operator:** Compare the returning service's refs with the restored network before anything syncs.

   ```sh
   git ls-remote <RETURNING SERVICE URL>
   ```

2. **Mirror operator:** Push restored work to the returning service as fast-forwards only.

   ```sh
   git -C <RESTORED> push --atomic <RETURNING SERVICE URL> 'refs/heads/*:refs/heads/*'
   ```

   **Unsafe:** Never let the returning service overwrite work done during the incident.

3. **Mirror operator:** Stop emergency static mirrors and temporary profiles.
4. **Incident coordinator:** Rebuild and re-sign the bootstrap kit with the current roster.

   ```sh
   python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit build <NEW KIT> --signing-key <KIT SEED> --roster <ROSTER>
   ```

5. **Scribe:** Write the exercise or incident record with a corrective owner for every finding.

Verify:

- [ ] The new kit verifies against the kit key on paper. `python3 tools/forkmesh_disaster_recovery.py kit verify <NEW KIT> --trusted-key <KIT KEY FROM PAPER>`

Roll back:

- Keep serving from the restored network, and try the return again later.

## Exercise worksheet

Fill in one worksheet per scenario, for drills and real incidents alike.

| Field | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Exercise or incident | |
| Kind (tabletop or live) | |
| Scenario | |
| Runbook version and digest | |
| Participants, roles, and whether each was unfamiliar with ForkMesh | |
| Only the offline runbook and kit were used (yes or no) | |
| Declared at | |
| Recovered and verified at (recovery time) | |
| Verified repository network restored (yes or no) | |
| Data loss: refs, commits, issues, pull requests | |
| Missing prerequisites, each with a finding | |
| Unsafe steps taken or refused, each with a finding | |
| Runbook defects | |
| Findings and their corrective owners | |
