pages.description: How a version is numbered, built, signed, published, promoted and installed: the desktop app on every platform, the Go mirror daemon, the Android APK, the macOS .dmg, and the App…
pages.markdown:
# Releases

How a version is numbered, built, signed, published, promoted and installed:
the desktop app on every platform, the Go mirror daemon, the Android APK, the
macOS `.dmg`, and the App Store submission of the iOS app. The metadata layout
and publisher flags are documented beside the data in
`.forkmesh/releases/README.md`; binaries never enter git. Why signed releases
on mirrors keep software reachable: [mirroring](../mirroring.md) and
[encryption and signatures](../encryption.md). Part of
[Operations](../operations/README.md); back to the
[documentation home](../README.md).

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| This page | Versions, the publish and promote flow, trust rules, platforms, build numbers, daemon rollout |
| [apt repository](apt.md) | The signed apt repository for Debian and Ubuntu |
| [Linux release baseline](linux-baseline.md) | Linux builds in a pinned Debian 12 container |
| [Self-setup node](self-setup-node.md) | One install command or cloud-init script brings up a mirror node without the desktop |

## Code map

| Path | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `desktop/CMakeLists.txt` (`project(ForkMesh VERSION …)`) | the release version |
| `desktop/src/MainWindowReleases.cpp`, `MainWindowRemoteReleases.cpp`, `ReleaseDraft.*` | draft a release, stamp versioned files, tag (also from MCP and phones) |
| `desktop/tests/validate_release_version_stamp.py` | fails when a tracked file declares the version outside the stamp list |
| `.forkmesh/release.yml` | Actions workflow that builds the mirror daemon on the release event |
| `tools/forkmesh-release-publish.sh` | hashes binaries, copies them into the content-addressed store, writes and signs channel metadata |
| `tools/forkmesh-release-promote.py` | promotion gate from a candidate to `latest`; regenerates the appcast |
| `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py`, `tools/release-host/*` | builds what the Actions sandbox cannot, promotes, seeds mirrors, rolls out the daemon, submits iOS, checks the homepage |
| `tools/package/linux-baseline.sh`, `tools/package/linux-baseline/` | Linux build in a pinned Debian 12 container ([Linux baseline](linux-baseline.md)) |
| `tools/package/` | per-platform packaging (`appimage.sh`, `deb.sh`, `macos.sh`, `windows.sh`, NSIS, appcast) |
| `tools/forkmesh-apt-repo.py`, `.forkmesh/releases/apt/` | the signed apt repository ([apt repository](apt.md)) |
| `tools/package/macos_universal_on_mac.sh` | universal (arm64 + x86_64) `.dmg` build on a Mac |
| `codemagic.yaml` (`macos-desktop`, `ios-native-release`), `native/ios/tools/asc_appstore.py` | cloud Mac fallback for the `.dmg`; iOS archive, upload, TestFlight and App Store submission |
| `.forkmesh/releases/<channel>/` | `SHASUMS256.txt`, `release.json`, `release.json.sig`, `appcast.xml` |
| `.forkmesh/releases/builds.json` | the build number each platform is on for the current version |
| `.forkmesh/shortcuts/deploy-build-*.sh`, `deploy-new-version.sh` | one-tap per-platform builds and the new-version workflow ([Build numbers](#build-numbers)) |
| `www/public/install.sh`, `www/public/uninstall.sh` | one-line installer and uninstaller |
| `desktop/src/MainWindowSetup.cpp` (`tryPrebuiltAutoUpdate`) | in-app update to a signed prebuilt |
| `app/src/releases.py`, `app/src/urls.py` | content-addressed download route |

## Flow

1. **Version.** Drafting a release stamps the version into every versioned file
   (including the Android versionCode `MAJOR*10000 + MINOR*100 + PATCH`) and
   tags the result. For `forkmesh/forkmesh` the stamp and tag go on a new
   `release/<tag>` branch cut from the target, so `main` keeps the previous
   version until the release is promoted ([The version flips
   last](#the-version-flips-last)).
2. **Build.** `.forkmesh/release.yml` builds the static Go mirror daemon in the
   Actions sandbox; it refuses a dirty tree because binaries embed their build
   commit.
3. **Publish a candidate.** `forkmesh-release-publish.sh --channel
   candidate-<version>` stores bytes under
   `<mirror>/forkmesh-releases/sha256/<aa>/<hash>/data` and writes signed
   metadata.
4. **Host-built assets.** `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py` (timer every five
   minutes) builds the Linux binary, AppImage and `.zsync`, the signed APK, the
   signed Windows installer and the universal macOS `.dmg`, publishes them into
   the candidate, runs the gate, verifies the promoted signature against the
   key in `install.sh`, seeds mirror release stores, merges the metadata to
   `main` and moves the tag onto that commit. It then rolls out the mirror
   daemon, submits the iOS app and checks the homepage; each step runs even
   if an earlier one failed.
5. **Promote.** The gate copies a candidate to `latest` only when it has every
   required asset (`FORKMESH_RELEASE_REQUIRED_ASSETS`) and drops nothing
   `latest` already offers. Exit 3 means held back, 2 a configuration error.
6. **Install and update.** `install.sh` authenticates `release.json`, checks it
   binds `SHASUMS256.txt`, downloads blobs by hash from
   `/api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/releases/blob/sha256/<sha256>` and verifies them.
   The desktop updater accepts a manifest only if its `tag` is the release
   being installed.

## Data paths

The release host's keystores (`release/`) and the served mirror
(`mirrors/forkmesh-forkmesh.git`, whose `forkmesh-releases/` is the blob store)
sit under `forkmesh_paths` `LAYOUT.core` (`data/core/`, `data/` before the
2026-10-19 move; [projects layout](../tools/projects-layout.md)). Never use
`LAYOUT.data`, the container: there the host finds no Android keystore and
publishes into an unserved `data/mirrors` folder.

## The version flips last

`main` only names a new version once every platform can download it. The
status page's per-platform "latest version" rows check the newest version
`desktop/CMakeLists.txt` on `main` names, so a version on `main` whose
candidate is still building shows as four outages until the builds finish.

- The desktop cuts `forkmesh/forkmesh` releases on `release/<tag>`
  (`cutRelease`, `MainWindowReleases.cpp`); the release workflow and the host
  build from the tag as before.
- The Actions runner copies the candidate metadata onto `main` but no longer
  the version line when the tag is not in `main`'s history
  (`ActionRunner::landVersionHeader`).
- The release host merges the tag commit into the same worktree that
  promotes `latest` (`bring_release_onto_main`), so one merge into `main`
  carries both the version and the promoted manifest. A conflict stops the
  promotion and leaves `main` alone.
- `--deploy-build --from-main` still needs the tag commit in `main`, so it only
  works once the release is promoted.

## Release trust rules

Every consumer of `release.json` checks `release.json.sig` against the one
Ed25519 release key pinned in `www/public/install.sh`. The desktop pins the
same key in `desktop/src/ReleaseTrust.cpp`;
`desktop/tests/validate_auto_update_release_trust.py` fails if the two differ.

- **Channel.** A manifest must name the channel being installed. A promoted
  `latest` is a byte copy of its signed candidate, so under `latest` the
  channel `candidate-<tag version>` is accepted too, for that tag only.
- **install.sh** (signature trust only) also refuses a manifest whose tag is
  older than `FORKMESH_MIN_RELEASE_VERSION`. The value is embedded in
  `install.sh`, an empty or malformed value refuses every manifest, and it must
  never be newer than the tag in `latest`
  (`test_installer_minimum_release_is_set_and_not_above_latest`). Raise it when
  a release must not be rolled back. A controller that pins a manifest SHA-256
  or an exact build commit has already chosen the exact release, so neither
  check applies there.
- **Desktop auto-update** (`maybeAutoUpdate`, `tryPrebuiltAutoUpdate`):
  - It orders tags by version number, not by tag date, and only looks at a tag
    newer than the running `FORKMESH_VERSION`.
  - The manifest must be signed, name `forkmesh/forkmesh`, match the tag and
    channel, and be strictly newer than the running version
    (`forkmesh::releasetrust::checkManifest`).
  - If no prebuilt fits, or its download fails, the source fallback
    fast-forwards only to the signed `tag_commit` and builds it once `HEAD`
    equals that commit. It never builds what `git pull` brings.
  - A release without a signed manifest, or one that fails a check, is logged
    and left alone. The manual Update button still pulls and builds by hand.
- **Release host** (`tools/forkmesh-release-host.py`): `manifests_at` drops
  any channel whose `release.json.sig` does not verify against the installer
  key. A candidate's `build_commit` must equal its `tag_commit` or descend from
  it.

Why: the auto-updater used to trust the newest-dated tag's unsigned
`release.json`. That included its `repo` field, which chose where the binary
was downloaded from. When no prebuilt fit, it built whatever `git pull`
returned. `install.sh` accepted any signed manifest from any channel or
version, so an old signed release could be replayed to roll a machine back.

## Platforms

- **Linux:** static Qt and OpenSSL in a Debian 12 container; a release fails if
  any ELF needs glibc above 2.35, so binaries run on Ubuntu 22.04+ and
  Debian 12+.
  The same build makes `forkmesh-linux-x86_64.deb`, which the apt repository
  serves, so `sudo apt install forkmesh` and `sudo apt upgrade` work once the
  source is added ([apt repository](apt.md)).
- **Windows:** cross-built with MinGW-w64; NSIS installer, Authenticode-signed
  with osslsigncode; the uninstaller deletes only files in its manifest.
- **macOS:** one ad-hoc signed universal `.dmg`, published under both arm64 and
  x86_64 names. Built on a dedicated Mac reached over SSH with a pinned host
  key, under a shared build lock, from `git archive` of the build commit; a
  cloud Mac build is the fallback only when the Mac cannot be reached. The
  image must carry the build commit and, for the Intel name, contain only
  universal Mach-O files. `FORKMESH_RELEASE_ALLOW_DROPPED_ASSETS=1` and
  `--macos-dmg PATH` are manual escape hatches.
- **Build commit checks:** the build commit sits in a `QStringLiteral`
  (`DesktopBuildCommit.cpp`), which clang stores as UTF-16, so
  `inspect_macos_dmg` and the Windows `forkmesh.exe` check look for the UTF-16
  form as well as ASCII. The Mac build gets the release version as
  `FORKMESH_VERSION` and stamps it with `-DFORKMESH_VERSION_OVERRIDE`, as Linux
  and Windows do; otherwise a rebuild from `main` takes `main`'s `project()`
  version.
- **iOS:** an App Store app with its own version
  (`native/ios/Config/Version.xcconfig`); each desktop release submits the
  newest build once (recorded in `<work>/ios-vX.Y.Z.json`), with the annotated
  tag message as What's New.
- **Android:** `forkmesh-android-universal.apk`, signed with the
  direct-distribution keystore; versionCode must grow, so it is
  `(MAJOR*10000 + MINOR*100 + PATCH) * 100 + BUILD`.
- **Homepage:** `www/public/homepage-downloads.js` reads and verifies `latest`
  in the browser; the release host checks the served manifest after promotion.

## Build numbers

Each platform can ship a new build of the current version without a new tag,
so a fix reaches the homepage for one platform without a release.

- `--deploy-build PLATFORM` (`android`, `linux`, `windows`, `macos`) builds the
  next build number from `main`, publishes it into the newest candidate (or
  `--tag`), promotes it to `latest` when nothing else is missing, seeds the
  mirrors, merges the metadata to `main` and moves the tag. With `--dry-run`
  it only prints the plan. With `--first-build` it does nothing when the
  version already has a build for that platform.
- `--deploy-build PLATFORM --from-main` is for a platform the release's build
  commit cannot build: it builds from `main` as build 1 and leaves build 0
  unused. `main` must contain the tag commit. (v1.5.0's desktop builds needed
  it: the static builds have no Qt WebEngine and the tag had an unguarded
  `QWebEngineView`.)
- A rebuild from `main` builds `code_commit(main)`: the newest commit that
  changed anything outside `.forkmesh/releases`, which is what the desktop's
  build provenance (`GenerateForkMeshVersion.cmake`) stamps. `main`'s tip is
  often a release-metadata commit or a `--no-ff` merge with its branch's tree,
  and building it fails with "FORKMESH_BUILD_COMMIT_OVERRIDE does not match
  the clean checkout".
- `--check-build PLATFORM` waits up to 30 minutes until app.forkmesh.com
  serves the promoted manifest. While the version is still held back for
  other platforms it reports that and succeeds.
- `--reset-builds` writes `builds.json` with every platform at 0 for the
  version; `--wait-candidate --tag vX.Y.Z` waits up to two hours for the
  release workflow's candidate manifest on `main`.
- These modes wait up to four hours for the timer's run to release the host
  lock instead of exiting.
- Build numbers live in `builds.json` and in each rebuilt asset's signed
  `build` and `commit` fields; the details and the reasons are in
  `.forkmesh/releases/README.md`, "Per-platform builds". The homepage shows
  `Build N` on a rebuilt download.
- Every platform starts a new version at build 0, iOS included (since v1.5.0,
  at the maintainer's request); App Store Connect only needs the number unique
  within a `MARKETING_VERSION` ([iOS release](../native/IOS_RELEASE.md#version)).
  The Android versionCode still grows, because the version is its high digits.
- The Android stamp patterns match `versionCodeOverride ?: N` and
  `versionNameOverride.ifEmpty { "X.Y.Z" }` in `build.gradle.kts`; if that
  file changes form, update the patterns, or drafts silently leave Android
  behind. The pattern spells `{` as `\x7B` because
  `validate_release_version_stamp.py` counts braces without skipping strings.

The shortcuts run these modes as named steps, so the desktop, phone and web
canvas show each operation:

| Shortcut | Steps |
| --- | --- |
| `Deploy Android build`, `Deploy Linux build`, `Deploy Windows build`, `Deploy macOS build` | Plan the build → Build, sign and publish → Check the homepage |
| `Deploy new version` | Cut the new version (`tools/forkmesh_release_request.py create`) → Wait for the release candidate → Reset build numbers to 0 → Deploy Android, Linux, Windows and macOS build (each runs the linked shortcut with `--first-build`) |

They are shortcuts rather than Actions workflows because they need the
release host's signing material, the office Mac and the primary checkout,
none of which the Actions sandbox can reach. Arguments given to the
new-version shortcut go to `forkmesh_release_request.py create` (for example
`--tag v1.3.0`).

## Mirror daemon rollout

`roll_out_release` in `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py` installs the promoted
`forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64` on managed mirror hosts listed in
`config/fanout/hosts`, all hosts in parallel. Core nodes are excluded (they
get the daemon through `tools/next_fleet.py`, which announces changes to the
IDS); a host whose unit is rendered by `deploy/core/render.py` answers
`next-managed` and is left alone. Per host: verify unit and config
ownership, skip if already current, verify the blob's sha256, keep the old
binary as `.bak-update`, swap, `--set-version`, restart, wait for health and
readiness, and restore the previous binary on failure. Outcomes are recorded
in `<work>/rollout-vX.Y.Z.json`; failed passes retry after a backoff. The
desktop's own rollout skips hosts that already run the release.

## Release store prune on nodes

Publishing, `seed_mirrors` and the desktop's push to managed hosts only ever
add blobs to `<gitDir>/forkmesh-releases` (about 5 GB a month), and the desktop
prunes only its own store, so the Go daemon prunes its own stores
(`server/releaseprune.go`).

The sync loop runs it five minutes after start and then every
`releasePruneInterval` (default `6h`, 10m to 168h). Per release store (aliases
sharing one store are pruned once, with the union of their manifests):

- The referenced set is every `assets[].blob_sha256` in every
  `.forkmesh/releases/<channel>/release.json` at the repository's `HEAD`.
- If `HEAD` is unborn, a manifest cannot be read or parsed, an asset digest is
  malformed, or the set is empty, nothing is deleted.
- If the `HEAD` commit is older than `releasePruneMinAge`, nothing is deleted:
  a node whose sync has stalled would otherwise read an old channel list and
  delete blobs that only a newer `HEAD` references.
- A referenced blob missing from the store is counted (the log's "referenced
  not in the store") but does not stop the run; stopping there once kept
  stores from ever shrinking (12 GB, 98% disk). A blob landing for a publish in
  progress is still safe, because nothing younger than `releasePruneMinAge` is
  a candidate.
- Only `sha256/<aa>/<64 lowercase hex>` directories whose name starts with
  `<aa>` are candidates, and only when the directory and every file in it are
  older than `releasePruneMinAge` (default `168h`, at least `24h`), because
  `seed_mirrors` lands blobs before their metadata.
- Deletes go through `removeTreeUnder(<store>/sha256/<aa>, <hash dir>)`; an
  emptied shard is removed with `os.Remove`. At most 200 blobs per store per
  run; each run logs one `release store prune` line per store with the count
  and bytes.

Releases dropped from every channel at `HEAD` lose their blobs after the
minimum age, so an old version stays downloadable by hash only while some
channel still names it.

Old candidates are retired by removing their `.forkmesh/releases/candidate-*`
folders on `main`; nothing removes them on its own. Keep `latest` and the
candidate it was promoted from. `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py` never revisits
a candidate older than `latest`, so removing older ones changes no rollout or
completion.

## Protocols

- `release.json`: `schema`, `repo`, `tag`, `tag_commit`, `build_commit`,
  `channel`, `created_at`, `checksums_sha256`, `assets[]` (`name`,
  `blob_sha256`, `size`, `os`, `arch`, and on a per-platform rebuild `build`
  and `commit`). `release.json.sig` is a raw 64-byte
  Ed25519 signature over the exact file bytes.
- `tag_commit` is the commit the tag pointed to at signing; verifiers check
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <tag_commit> <tag>`. An empty `build_commit` is
  left out of the signed header so legacy manifests keep their bytes.
- After publishing, the release host moves the tag onto the metadata commit
  that carries the promoted manifest (`parked_tag_target()` in
  `tools/forkmesh-release-host.py`), so `git rev-parse <tag>^{commit}` is
  normally a later commit than `tag_commit`, not equal to it. That is the
  defined relation, not tampering (v1.5.0 signs `510b0448b745`; its tag peels
  to `0193ce5d3e88`, 105 commits later). This is the one definition; other
  documents link here.
- Asset names: `forkmesh-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`, `.AppImage`, `.dmg`,
  `-setup.exe`, `forkmesh-mirror-node-linux-x86_64`,
  `forkmesh-android-universal.apk`.
- `appcast.xml` is generated on promotion but not read by the desktop;
  Windows and macOS update by installing the newer installer.

## Configuration

Names only:

- Actions: `FORKMESH_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY_PEM`, `FORKMESH_RELEASE_REQUIRED_ASSETS`,
  `FORKMESH_RELEASE_ALLOW_DROPPED_ASSETS`, `FORKMESH_WIN_CERT_PFX`,
  `FORKMESH_WIN_CERT_PASSWORD`.
- Publisher: `FORKMESH_RELEASE_CAS`, `FORKMESH_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY`,
  `RELEASE_CHANNEL`, `FORKMESH_TAG`, `FORKMESH_TAG_COMMIT`,
  `FORKMESH_BUILD_COMMIT`.
- Release host: signing material under `<data>/release/`
  (`FORKMESH_ANDROID_KEYSTORE`, `FORKMESH_ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD_FILE`,
  `FORKMESH_WIN_CERT_PFX_FILE`), `CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN`, `CODEMAGIC_APP_ID`,
  the build Mac's key and pinned host key under `<ssh>/mac-build/`,
  `MAC_BUILD_HOST`, `MAC_BUILD_GIT_URL`.
- Build: `-DFORKMESH_BUILD_COMMIT_OVERRIDE`, `-DFORKMESH_VERSION_OVERRIDE`.
- Installer: `FORKMESH_PUBLIC_HOSTNAME`, `FORKMESH_LINK_CODE`,
  `FORKMESH_DNS_WAIT_SECONDS` ([self-setup node](self-setup-node.md)),
  `FORKMESH_RELEASE`, `FORKMESH_TRUSTED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE`,
  `FORKMESH_EXPECTED_RELEASE_MANIFEST_SHA256`, `FORKMESH_FROM_SOURCE`.

## Build, run, test

```sh
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --tag vX.Y.Z --dry-run
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --auto --rollout-only --dry-run
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --tag vX.Y.Z --ios-only
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --auto --skip-ios
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --deploy-build android --dry-run
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-host.py --reset-builds --tag vX.Y.Z --dry-run
python3 tools/forkmesh-release-promote.py --candidate candidate-X.Y.Z --dry-run
python3 desktop/tests/validate_release_version_stamp.py
tools/package/linux-baseline.sh check <binary> <AppImage>
python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_linux_release_baseline.py app/tests/test_install_lifecycle.py app/tests/test_installer_source.py app/tests/test_releases.py
python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_release_host_completion.py tools/test_ios_app_store_release.py
python3 -m pytest app/tests/test_release_host_builds.py app/tests/test_deploy_build_shortcuts.py
python3 -m pytest tools/test_forkmesh_release_host_rollout.py tools/test_forkmesh_release_host_seed.py
```

## Operations

- Cut a release from the desktop's Releases panel, the MCP `create_release`
  tool, or a phone request; the release host completes it within minutes.
- Watch it: `journalctl --user -u forkmesh-release-host.service -f`.
- Check a release: fetch `.forkmesh/releases/latest/release.json{,.sig}` and
  verify with the public key in `www/public/install.sh`.

## Security

- A prebuilt install trusts either the release publisher's Ed25519 key (built
  into `install.sh`, or a local PEM) or a manifest digest from an
  authenticated controller; a checksum copied from the fetched manifest is
  never trusted alone.
- Private signing keys, keystores and certificates never enter git or docs.
- Desktop fleet installs also pin `build_commit` and check `--version` and
  `--build-commit` on each host.
- `install.sh --uninstall/--reinstall/--purge` and `uninstall.sh --purge`
  refuse to erase anything outside `HOME` and refuse a user-data wipe from an
  agent shell. Agents must never run them (`AGENTS.md`,
  [destructive actions](../engineering/destructive-actions.md)).

## Traps

- **Manifest before tag:** the tag is moved onto the metadata commit; the
  updater rejects a manifest whose `tag` differs.
- **No-drop rule:** a candidate without both `.dmg` names is held back until a
  universal image exists; the host still publishes the other assets into the
  candidate and retries the macOS build after a backoff.
- **Mac build lock:** a killed host run leaves its remote step running; the
  next attempt of the same release takes the lock over, and stale locks expire.
- **Dirty tree:** any untracked file in the build worktree marks the build
  commit dirty.
- **Installer tests** must sandbox `HOME` and `XDG_*_HOME` and drop
  `FORKMESH_HOME`/`FORKMESH_PROJECTS_DIR`.

pages.markdown:
# Repositories hosted on the core nodes

Part of [Operations](README.md).

A user with no desktop node and no external forge account can create a
repository on the website and use it with plain `git` over HTTPS. Every core
keeps a full replica, so the repository survives the loss of any one core
([architecture](../architecture.md)); later the user can move it to
their own node. User guide: [hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md).

Code: `app/src/hosted_git.py` (create, push routing, quotas, private reads),
`app/src/hosted_repos.py` (replica exchange, templates), migration
`0199_hosted_repositories`, daemon `server/hosted.go` and
`server/hosted_push_mirror.go`, the `restricted` visibility in
`tools/mirror_gateway.py`, and the create page `/dashboard/repos/new`. On a self-hosted instance the
operator command `instance-repo` creates and fills one from a repository on
the server through the same create helpers ([self-hosted instances](instances.md)).

## What a user gets

**New repository** fields: name (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, at most 64 characters, not
starting with `.` or ending in `.git`), owner (self or an organization where
the user can maintain), description, visibility (public or private), README,
`.gitignore` template, license. A public `https://` URL on a host in
`HOSTED_IMPORT_HOSTS` imports a cloneable copy.

After creation the page shows the remote URL
`https://app.forkmesh.com/<owner>/<name>`, the commands, and a username and
password. The password is the session-bound push credential (`fmp1.…`): 7
days, never stored, revoked with the session, renewable with
`POST /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential`. It also clones private
repositories. There are no personal access tokens and no SSH access.

**Quotas** (`app/wrangler.toml [vars]`, which the host on the cores reads as
its settings): `HOSTED_REPO_MAX_PER_ACCOUNT`
(default 10) and `HOSTED_REPO_MAX_BYTES` (default 200 MiB, compared with the
largest copy any core reports; over it a push answers
`413 repository_quota_exceeded`). A core reports `git count-objects -v`
`size` plus `size-pack` (loose and packed object bytes), not the directory
size, and [maintenance](#maintenance) keeps duplicate packs from counting
for long. Push bodies are streamed, up to
`FORKMESH_MAX_GIT_PUSH_BODY_BYTES` (256 MiB). The creating account must have a
verified email.

**Git rules** (gateway receive-pack): the default and protected branches
fast-forward only; other branches may be force-pushed by accounts that may
write them ([core push](core-push.md#force-pushes)); no ref deletes, new
tags allowed but never moved, only `refs/heads/*` and `refs/tags/*`, objects
fsck-checked, no hooks, every accepted push audited per ref.

**Deleting branches.** The owner (or an organization owner or admin) deletes
branches on the repository's Branches page, one at a time or several at once
(`POST /api/repo/<owner>/<name>/branches/delete`, at most 200 per request).
The default branch and protected branches are refused; any name Git accepts
can be deleted. The request becomes a job that one background worker runs a
branch at a time: a router-signed request to the core's merge executor, which
moves the tip to `refs/forkmesh/trash/branch/` and deletes the branch in one
ref transaction, then the same on every other core, each audited as
`repository.branch_delete`. When the job ends the app notes the change like a
push, so the cores wake and a push mirror with prune drops the branches on
its next push, and updates the catalog's `branchCount`. Details: [branch ops](../app/branch-ops.md#deleting-branches).

## Design

```
browser ── POST /api/hosted-repositories ──► app (any core; rqlite)
                                             │ catalog record + hosted_repos row
                                             └─ "hosted" node event ──► every core daemon
core daemon ── POST /api/hosted-repositories/replicas (node-signed) ──► app
            ◄── desired set: {id, owner, name, visibility, pushedAt, primary?, init?, sources[]}
    ├─ create <root>/<id>.git + gateway entry ("public" | "restricted")
    ├─ primary + empty: deterministic first commit, or a bounded import
    └─ behind / empty: fetch from a peer with a router-signed read grant, fast-forward only
git push ─► app (Basic credential) ─► last pusher, else rendezvous-first live core
git clone ─► app ─► public: a core whose signed refs proof matches the pin
                    private: owner or organization reader, then a core via capability
```

- **State** lives in rqlite: `hosted_repos` (spec, `pushed_at`, `pushed_by`)
  and `hosted_repo_copies` (each node writes only its own rows).
- **Primary:** the rendezvous-first live core for the repository id. Only it
  writes the first commit (deterministic, so two would-be primaries agree) or
  runs an import.
- **Pushes** go to the last pusher when live, else rendezvous order.
- **Replicas** behind `pushed_at` fetch from the pusher first using a
  runner-format read grant (at most 1 h) and apply refs with the same
  fast-forward-only reconciliation as upstream sync.
- **Wake-ups:** the payload-free `hosted` node event after create, push or
  first pin; a 2-minute safety reconcile; `POST /v1/control/sync`.
- **Gateway config** is rewritten by the daemon, one entry per repository and
  per organization alias. Public entries also get web merge operations when
  the node runs the merge executor; restricted entries do not.
- **Routing pin:** public reads go only to cores whose signed proof matches
  the pinned `stateHash`, recorded after each push or web merge
  (`record_hosted_push_state`).
- **Catalog head:** the record's `branch` and `commit` (read by the logo,
  banner, About and README lookups) move with the pin. Whenever
  `record_hosted_push_state` pins a new `stateHash`, it reads the default
  branch tip from the hosting core with a router-signed `branches` request
  (`_hosted_head`); if that read fails the pin is still written and the old
  commit stays until the next push. `_admit_core_push_state` calls it too
  (no notifications), which covers pushes that bypass the push proxy, such
  as an Actions commit-back on the runner route (`runner_actions.report` →
  `admit_push_state`); otherwise a busy instance's About and logo read stale
  files. Tests in `app/tests/test_hosted_repositories.py`.
- **Online badge:** `liveHost` normally means "the record owner's node has a
  fresh, verified HTTPS endpoint", but a hosted record is owned by a user
  account, never a node. So the catalog (`catalog_routes.catalog_handler`)
  also marks a `hosted-web` record live when a core that reported a non-empty
  copy in `hosted_repo_copies` has a fresh verified endpoint
  (`app/tests/test_catalog_signed_endpoint_liveness.py`).
- **Commit count and activity:** the app writes hosted records, so each core
  adds its copy's stats to the replica report (`hostedCopyState`: `commit`,
  `commitCount`, `mergeCount`, `activityWeeks`, `mergeActivityWeeks`). The
  full `git rev-list --count` and the 52-week walk run once per
  default-branch tip per UTC day (`hostedReplicator.historyStats`). The app
  (`hosted_repos.clean_stats`, `hosted_git.record_hosted_stats`) writes them
  only when the reporting copy's routing digest is the pinned `stateHash` and
  its tip is the record's `commit`, so a copy that is behind never overwrites
  them, and only when a value changed, at most once per `COPY_REFRESH_MS`.
  A node reports stats only once its binary has this code; until then
  rerunning `instance-repo` refreshes an imported repository (it caps the
  count at 10,000). Tests in `app/tests/test_hosted_core.py`,
  `app/tests/test_hosted_repositories.py` and
  `TestHostedCopyStateReportsTheWholeHistoryCachedPerTip`.
- **Attested state:** the router checks clones against the routing digest
  (default branch plus tags, `routingRefsSHA256`). Pushes, the collaboration
  intake acknowledgement (`server/intake.go`) and merge results
  (`server/merge.go`) all attest that digest; an all-branches digest would
  add a pin no node can match. The gateway's own generation pin still uses
  the full digest (`server/merge_test.go`).

### Private repositories

A private repository is a `restricted` gateway entry reachable only by a
router capability or runner grant; public routes, dashboards and counts never
see it. The app serves Git and `/api/repo/...` reads through
`hosted_private_read` to the owner or organization readers; others get `401`
(Git) or `404` (web). This is access control, not end-to-end encryption: the
cores hold plaintext. Owner-sealed repositories need the owner's own node
([encryption](../encryption.md)).

### Organizations

The repository is stored under the creator's namespace, linked in `org_repos`
so `/<org>/<name>` works, and pushes use organization roles (write or better;
private reads need read or better).

`org_repos.repo` is always the lowercase name: every reader (the git and API
alias rewrite, org read and push permissions) looks it up lowercased. A
mixed-case link is unreachable (`/<org>/Bolt.git` answers `not_found` and
other members cannot push), so `link_organization` stores the lowercase name
and renames an existing mixed-case link; re-running `instance-repo` relinks
an older repository.

#### The organization is the public owner

The member who created the repository stays its storage owner: the
`repositories` row, its `key_bi`, the `owner` field of the catalog record, the
hosted copy and every signature (`catalogSig`, `stateSig`) name the member,
because the member's key or the core signs them and nodes, mirrors and the
desktop find their own rows by that owner. Everything a visitor sees uses the
organization instead:

- **Catalog.** `/api/repositories` keeps `owner` (the storage and signing
  owner) and projects the public identity into unsigned fields: a row linked
  to exactly one organization gets `ownerKind: "organization"`,
  `logicalOwner: <org>` and `logicalOwners` with only the organization; the
  creating member is no longer listed. The link lookup is case-insensitive
  (it used to compare the stored lowercase `org_repos.repo` with the record's
  name as typed, so a mixed-case repository such as `Project` had no
  organization at all and every client fell back to the member). An unsigned
  row's default `channel` (`#<member>-<name>`) is shown as `#<org>-<name>`,
  and with an SSH gateway the organization's SSH address is preferred.
  Rewriting `owner` itself was rejected: a node-published record's `catalogSig`
  v2 and `stateSig` bind it, the record key is its blind index, and nodes,
  mirrors and the desktop select their own repositories by it.
- **Public facts.** `_public_repo_owner` (stars, fork lists and edges, views,
  issue views, remote forks, pull batches, advisories) and the fediverse
  actor resolve a member address to the organization even when the request
  names the member (`_repo_organization`, memoized with the alias lookups), so
  `/api/repo/<member>/<repo>/forks` and `/api/repo/<org>/<repo>/forks` read
  the same list. A new fork records `forkedFrom: <org>/<repo>`, and
  `_index_repo_fork_edge` keys the edge on the organization even for an
  older record that still names the member.
- **Pages and links.** Without the single-owner short addresses, a page
  request for `/<member>/<repo>[/...]` redirects (308) to `/<org>/<repo>[/...]`,
  and the same mapping makes clone URLs, OG cards, the about record's
  fediverse handle and notification links name the organization;
  notification titles and bodies that quoted `<member>/<repo>` quote the
  public address. With short addresses on, the existing canonical redirect
  already sends both to `/<repo>`, and the display stays the bare name. The
  API keeps answering under the member address, so old links and clients work.
- **Dashboard.** `repoMatchesKey` matches a row by its organization address,
  so a fork whose `forkedFrom` is `<org>/<repo>` nests under the repository in
  every list, and the signed-in Top repositories entry of an organization
  repository is found by that address instead of by the linked member node.
  A fork's "forked from" line shows the parent's display name.

A repository linked to two organizations keeps the member as its public owner
(neither organization is preferred): `_repo_organization` returns nothing for
it, and the catalog keeps the member first in `logicalOwners` (`ownerKind:
"user"`) with both organizations after it, so the catalog, the public facts
and the redirect agree. Data stored before this change under the
member address is moved by `forkmesh_host org-repo-identity`
([instances](instances.md)).

### Imports

The primary fetches heads and tags from an allowed `https` host (no
credentials, port or query), stops past the size limit or 10 minutes, and
points HEAD at `main`, `master`, `trunk` or `develop`. Private sources are not
supported. The separate metadata importer (`app/src/repository_imports.py`)
imports issues, pulls and releases only.

### Contributor pushes

So that a contributor without a node of their own can open a pull request,
an operator can open named public repositories to contributor pushes
(`HOSTED_GIT_CONTRIBUTOR_PUSH`, user guide in
`docs/hosted-repositories.md`): any active, email-verified user account
may then push branches under `refs/heads/pr/<account>/` of the repository
itself (the namespace the SSH gateway's pull-request grant uses), with the
same session-bound credential an owner uses.

- **Allowlist** (`hosted_git`): `*`, `owner/*` or `owner/repo` items,
  separated by whitespace or commas, case-insensitive; a route alias or its
  backing node matches. Unparseable entries are ignored, so a typo narrows
  access rather than widening it. The repository must be listed and public,
  and the account an active, email-verified user; every check fails closed
  and is repeated on each push.
- **Credential.** `POST /api/hosted-repositories/push-credential` mints the
  session-bound Basic credential. Owners and writers get full access; a
  contributor gets one limited to its namespace, and the push answer names
  that one ref namespace (an owner or writer gets no prefix). Signing out
  revokes it.
- **Enforcement.** The app's router (`app/src/edge_routing.py`) signs
  `pushPrefix` into the receive-pack capability, so a contributor cannot widen it, and the gateway
  (`tools/mirror_gateway.py`) refuses any command outside it, with at most
  `MAX_CONTRIBUTOR_BRANCHES` (32) branches there. A refusal is answered as a
  receive-pack report (`ng <ref> <reason>`), so stock Git prints the reason
  beside each ref instead of an opaque HTTP failure. Deletes and force pushes
  are refused for everyone on this path, so only a maintainer removes a
  contributor's merged branches. Only new objects cross the wire.
- **No workflows.** A contributor's push runs nobody's workflows
  (`core_push`): `on: push` would execute untrusted code with the
  repository's runner access.
- **No quota.** There is no per-account byte quota or rate limit on this
  path beyond the gateway's `receive.maxInputSize` per push.

## Forks

A hosted repository made private from the website
(`POST /api/hosted-repositories/visibility`) first writes the public catalog
snapshot tombstone, as a node's own catalog publish does, and then drops its
`repo_forks` row, so its name leaves the parent's fork list. The fork list
(`GET /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/forks`) also leaves out any fork that is
private now, and its count with it.

**Forks → Fork this repository** on a public hosted repository (or one
published from a node, below) creates
`<you>/<name>`, a hosted repository you own, marked `forkedFrom` the parent
and listed on its forks (`repo_forks`). Code: `hosted_git.hosted_fork_create`
(reached from `POST /api/repo/<owner>/<repo>/forks` before the managed-mirror
path), `hosted_repos.fork_of`, `server/hosted_forks.go`.

- **Storage.** The hosted record carries `fork: {of, network}`; the replica
  exchange passes `forkOf` and `network` (the root repository's id) to every
  core. Each core builds the fork from its own copy of the parent: the
  network pool `<root>/.pools/<network>.git` is a `git clone --local` of the
  root (hard links, so no extra disk until the parent repacks), refreshed
  from the parent into `refs/pools/<parent>/…` before each new fork, and the
  fork's `objects/info/alternates` points at it. Refs are copied from the
  parent with nothing transferred. A fork costs about 26 KB (measured in
  `TestHostedForkBorrowsFromTheNetworkPool`); its own pushes stay in it.
- **One core picks the refs.** Only the fork's primary core copies the
  parent's heads, tags and HEAD into a new fork. Every other core sets up the
  pool and the alternates and then fetches the fork's refs from its peers,
  which transfers almost nothing, so all cores agree on the fork's refs (and
  refs digest) even when their copies of the parent differ for a moment
  (`TestHostedForkRefsComeFromThePrimaryOnly`).
- **Parent still public.** The replica exchange names `forkOf` only while the
  parent is a live public hosted repository, and the core also refuses to
  pool a parent its own answer lists as private. A parent made private after
  the fork never feeds a fork that a core builds later (a new core, or a
  wiped directory), nor the shared pool
  (`test_a_fork_of_a_parent_made_private_is_not_built_from_it`,
  `TestHostedForkOfAPrivateParentIsNotPooled`).
- **Built under the parent's lock.** Creating and refreshing the pool and
  copying the fork's refs hold a shared lock on the parent's
  `forkmesh-maintenance.lock`, so a geometric repack cannot delete objects
  mid-clone; when maintenance holds it, the fork is built on the next cycle.
  A new pool must pass `git fsck --connectivity-only` before it is renamed
  into place.
- **Never pruned.** The pool is not served and not maintained (maintenance
  walks only `<root>/hr*.git`, and repacks forks with `-l`), so a
  force-push, repack or deletion of the parent never removes an object a
  fork needs. An operator may delete a pool only when no fork in its network
  is left.
- **Limits.** Public parents only (shared objects would leak across a
  private network); active users with a verified email; one fork per
  account per parent (a second click links to the first);
  `HOSTED_MAX_FORKS_PER_ACCOUNT` (default 20), separate from the repository
  quota. Forks of forks join the root's network.
- **Pull requests.** The composer on a fork targets the parent
  (`forkedFrom`) and sends a patch-backed pull request (patch and commits),
  so merging into the parent needs no fetch from the fork.
- **Repositories published from a node.** A public repository published from
  someone's own node (such as `forkmesh/forkmesh`) has no `hosted_repos` row,
  so `hosted_fork_create` reads its catalog record instead. It must be public,
  not `hosted-web`, and carry a `cloneUrl` that is plain `https` with a host
  name (no IP address or `localhost`), no credentials, query or fragment
  (`hosted_repos.fork_clone_url`). An account that has a linked headless
  managed mirror, or names a `targetNode`, keeps the managed-mirror fork
  (`_web_fork_create` gets the already-read body); everyone else gets a
  hosted fork instead of `409 headless_mirror_required`.
  - The fork's record carries `fork: {upstream: {owner, name, cloneUrl},
    network}`. The network id is `hr` plus the first 24 hex digits of
    `sha256("forkmesh-fork-network-v1\n<owner>/<name>")`, so every fork of the
    same parent, and every fork of those forks, shares one pool on each core.
  - The exchange sends `forkUpstream` and `network` only while the parent's
    catalog record is still public and node-published (re-read once per
    exchange, `_ReplicaRuntime.fork_parent`), with that record's current
    `cloneUrl`.
  - The stored `upstream.owner` is the publishing node, the catalog key
    (`fmnext-n1` for `forkmesh/forkmesh`). The cores serve such a repository
    under its organization name, so the exchange sends the organization in
    `forkUpstream.owner` when the node's repository is linked into one
    (`org_repos` joined to `orgs`, the name checked against the link's blind
    index; `_ReplicaRuntime.fork_parent_alias`). With the node name no core
    finds its local copy, and the fallback fetch fails on the app's 307 to a
    core (redirects are refused), leaving the fork empty. A core retries an
    empty fork each cycle
    (`test_cores_are_told_the_organization_name_they_serve_the_parent_under`).
  - On each core (`forkFromUpstream`), the local copy is the gateway
    repository served as `<owner>/<name>` (the upstream mirrors the cores
    already serve), only when it is enabled, public, not a hosted copy and
    has a branch. The pool is a `git clone --local` of it and is refreshed
    from it into `refs/pools/<network>/…`, as for hosted parents. Gateway
    copies have no maintenance lock; when one has the lock file the build
    holds it shared, and no lock file is ever created in a gateway copy (the
    gateway would then start marking it for maintenance). A new pool still
    has to pass `fsck --connectivity-only`.
  - With no local copy, only the primary fetches the `cloneUrl` into the
    pool (`git init --bare`, then `+refs/heads/*` and `+refs/tags/*` into
    `refs/pools/<network>/…`). The fetch allows only `https` (plain `http`
    only to loopback, for tests), clears credential helpers and is held to
    the hosted size limit and fetch timeout like an import (`boundedGit`).
    The `cloneUrl` comes from the publishing node's catalog record, so the
    core only fetches it from the network's own git origin (the host of
    `catalogUrl`) or a forge on `hosted.importHosts`, on the default port,
    and never follows a redirect (`http.followRedirects=false`); anything
    else would let a publisher point a core at an internal address
    (`forkFetchHostAllowed`).
    Replicas with no local copy fetch nothing from the parent: they borrow
    from the pool if it already exists and take the fork's refs from their
    peers.
  - The primary copies the fork's heads and tags from the pool namespace and
    points `HEAD` at the local copy's `HEAD` (or `main`, then `master`).
  - Tests: `test_a_node_published_repository_forks_onto_the_cores`,
    `test_an_account_with_a_managed_mirror_keeps_the_mirror_fork`,
    `TestHostedForkOfANodePublishedRepositoryBorrowsTheGatewayCopy`,
    `TestHostedForkOfANodePublishedRepositoryFetchesItsCloneURL`,
    `TestHostedForkOfANodePublishedRepositoryStaysWithinTheSizeLimit`.
- Contributors who would rather not fork can push `pr/<account>/` branches
  where `HOSTED_GIT_CONTRIBUTOR_PUSH` allows it.

## Moving to your own node

When the owner's node publishes the repository through the signed catalog,
the hosted record is replaced; the next exchange marks the row deleted, frees
the quota, stops routing pushes and moves core copies to `.trash`. Steps:
`git clone --mirror`, add it on the node, publish from the node.

## Push mirrors

The owner can mirror a hosted repository to GitHub or GitLab with a personal
access token. Only the primary pushes. The exchange carries an optional
`pushMirror` (`revision`, `provider`, `url`, `username`, `token`, `prune`,
`refs`) to the primary, and the daemon reports `pushMirrors` results
(`revision`, `digest`, `ok`, `at`, `error`, and `refs`, the count of updated
refs).

- Valid only for `github`/`gitlab`, URL exactly
  `https://<host>/<owner>/<name>.git` on `hosted.pushHosts`, a token of at most
  512 characters without whitespace.
- Push when settings change, when refs change, or every 6 hours; retry
  failures after 10 minutes; each push is limited to 10 minutes.
- `refs` is `all` (the default, also when absent) or `default`. With `all`:
  `git push --porcelain [--prune] <url> +refs/heads/*:refs/heads/* +refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*`.
  With `default`, only the branch the hosted repository's `HEAD` points at,
  plus tags: `git push --porcelain [--prune] <url> +refs/heads/<head>:refs/heads/<head> +refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*`.
  `--prune` alone never deletes branches outside that refspec, so with prune
  the daemon first runs `git ls-remote --heads <url>` (same header, timeout
  and redaction) and adds `:refs/heads/<name>` for every other branch on the
  target to the same push (at most 1000; names git would refuse are skipped).
  In `default` mode only the head and tags count as a change, so pushes to
  other branches do not trigger a push. Changing `refs` triggers a push even
  with the same `revision`. The owner sets it in the mirror form ("Branches")
  or with `refs` in the `save` action of the provider-mirror API.
- Both commands run with the token only in an `http.extraHeader` passed
  through `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment variables, no credential helper, no
  redirects, HTTPS only.
  Errors are redacted (token and header value replaced) and folded to 300
  characters.
- A branch deleted on the Branches page changes the refs digest, so it
  triggers a push, and with prune the branch is removed from the target.

## Internet Archive backups

The owner can upload a public hosted repository to an archive.org item on a
schedule ([archive sync](../app/archive-sync.md)). The exchange carries an
optional `archiveSync` (`revision`, `url`, `accessKey`, `secret`,
`intervalSeconds`, `collection`, `title`, `source`, and `uploaded`: the
`revision`, `digest` and `at` of the last upload the app recorded) to the
primary, only for public repositories, and the daemon reports `archiveSyncs`
results (`revision`, `digest`, `ok`, `at`, `error`, `bytes`).
`server/hosted_archive_sync.go` does the work:

- Valid only for `https://s3.us.archive.org/<item>/<file>.bundle`, keys of 8
  to 64 letters and digits, an interval from 1 hour to 400 days, and
  printable ASCII metadata.
- Due when the `revision` differs from the last upload (new settings or
  **Back up now**), or when the refs digest (every branch and tag) changed and
  the interval has passed since the last upload. `uploaded` seeds the last
  upload after a daemon restart, so nothing is uploaded twice. Failures retry
  after 1 hour.
- The upload runs in the background, one at a time per core, so a large
  repository never holds up replication: `git bundle create <root>/.archive/<id>-*.bundle
  HEAD --branches --tags` (30 minutes at most), then one `PUT` with
  `Authorization: LOW <access>:<secret>`, `x-amz-auto-make-bucket: 1`,
  `x-archive-queue-derive: 0` and `x-archive-meta-*` (mediatype `software`,
  the collection, title, description, source). Redirects are not followed;
  the whole job is limited to 2 hours. The bundle file is removed afterwards.
- Errors (the archive's `<Message>` when it sends one) are redacted (both
  keys replaced) and folded to 300 characters.

## Operations

- Root on each core: `/var/lib/forkmesh/hosted/<id>.git` (owned by the daemon
  user, 0700). Removed repositories go to `.trash/<id>-<unix>.git`; nothing
  deletes them automatically. Empty it by exact name after the retention
  window.
- Logs: `journalctl -u forkmesh-mirror-node | grep hosted`.
- Database: `hosted_repos`, `hosted_repo_copies`.
- Watch disk use; lower the per-account quota if needed.
- `deploy/core/render.py` writes `FORKMESH_VAR_HOSTED_GIT_CORE_NODES` (every
  core, or empty with `[hosted] enabled = false`) and
  `FORKMESH_VAR_HOSTED_GIT_CORE_OWNERS` (plus `[hosted] retired_cores`) into
  `app.env`. An empty list makes the create form fall back to the node flow.
- Rollout order: node files (`files,start`), then daemon, then the app
  release, one core at a time.

## Maintenance

Every accepted push (web, `git push` through the app, Actions commit-back
pushes on the runner route `/v1/runner/<owner>/<repo>.git`) is received by
`tools/mirror_gateway.py` with `receive.unpackLimit=0`, so each one adds a
pack, and replica fetches add more. Git's own `gc --auto` waits for 50 packs,
long after duplicate packs trip the size check, so the node maintains hosted
repositories itself (`server/hosted_maintenance.go`):

- **Trigger.** After a push that moved refs the gateway touches
  `<id>.git/forkmesh-maintenance-due` (only in a repository that has the
  maintenance lock file, which the node creates, so configured mirrors are
  left alone). `instance-repo` touches it after a fill. A goroutine of the
  node daemon looks for the marker every minute, and every 15 minutes also
  scans each hosted repository for more than 4 packs or 256 loose objects.
  The work never runs on the request path.
- **What runs.** `git repack -d -l -q --geometric=2`: small packs and loose
  objects are rolled up while the large pack stays untouched, and two packs
  of similar size (a duplicate history) are merged into one, each object
  written once. `-d` removes only packs and loose objects the new pack made
  redundant; nothing unreachable is pruned, so git's default grace is kept
  and a concurrent push never loses a base object
  ([destructive actions](../engineering/destructive-actions.md)).
- **Low cost.** The command runs under `nice -n 19` and `ionice -c 3` when
  they exist, with `pack.threads=1`, `pack.windowMemory=64m`,
  `pack.deltaCacheSize=16m`, `core.deltaBaseCacheLimit=16m` and a 256 MiB
  pack window limit, so it fits beside the app on a 1 GB server, and is
  stopped after 30 minutes. The node also sets `receive.autogc=false` and
  `maintenance.auto=false` in each hosted repository, so neither a push nor a
  replica fetch starts an unbounded `gc --auto` of its own.
- **Lock.** `<id>.git/forkmesh-maintenance.lock`. The gateway holds a shared
  `flock` on it while `receive-pack` runs; maintenance takes it exclusively
  and non-blocking, so it never starts while a push is being received and
  retries on the next tick. A push that arrives during a repack waits for it,
  up to `MAINTENANCE_LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS` (120 s), and then proceeds: git's
  repack removes only the packs it rewrote, so a pack written meanwhile is
  safe. A repack that fails puts the marker back.
- **Replica fetches.** The fetch guard in `boundedGit` compares the stored
  object bytes at the start plus what the directory grew by during the fetch
  with `hosted.maxRepositoryBytes`, so old duplicate packs no longer stop a
  replica from catching up.
- **Logs.** `hosted maintenance <id>.git: <before> -> <after> bytes in <time>`
  in the node's journal.

## Known gaps

- `git push` cannot delete a branch or force-push; delete branches on the
  Branches page instead.
- A core offline longer than the removal window keeps an orphaned copy.
- Concurrent divergent pushes on two cores during failover converge to the
  newer commit.

pages.markdown:
# Runners: trusted core and untrusted agent compute

Part of [Operations](README.md).

Untrusted agent work runs on a separate runner tier, never on the cores that
hold the data ([architecture](../architecture.md), [threat
model](../protocol/threat-model.md)).
The Go daemon (`server/`) has three roles:

| Role | Serves repositories | Gateway, catalog, merge executor | Agent jobs | Actions |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mirror` (default) | yes | yes | yes, unless `disableAgentJobs` | if `enableActions` |
| `core` | yes | yes | never | never |
| `runner` | no | none | yes | if `enableActions` (leased from the app) |

A runner starts no gateway, publishes no catalog, keeps no repositories and
talks to the app only through `/api/runners/*`. It has no node account and
opens no node event channel.

## Job flow

```
 website ── queue ──► app (org_agent_jobs)
                        │  POST /api/runners/claim  (runner-signed, long poll)
                        ▼
                     runner ──clone (read grant)──► core gateway /v1/runner/<owner>/<repo>.git
                        │  claude/codex in a per-job systemd scope
                        ├──push HEAD:refs/heads/agent/<session> (push grant)──► core gateway
                        └─ POST /api/runners/report (runner-signed) ──► app
```

1. **Claim.** `{max, providers, allowedOwners, burst, waitMs}`; the app holds
   the request up to 20 s when nothing is leasable.
2. **Lease.** Each job carries `cloneUrl`, `readGrant`, `pushGrant`, `pushRef`
   (under `refs/heads/agent/`), expiry (at most 3 h), attachment metadata, and
   for pool runners a `modelGrant` used to sign a commit attestation trailer.
3. **Check.** The runner rejects leases whose grants disagree with the job or
   expire within 5 minutes.
4. **Clone** into a fresh 0700 workdir from a per-repository cache. The grant
   travels as `X-ForkMesh-Runner-Grant` via `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment
   variables, never on a command line or in the clone's config.
5. **Run** the CLI inside the job sandbox.
6. **Publish.** Git inside the job repository runs only as the job user, with
   hooks and fsmonitor disabled, and produces a bundle of new commits. The
   daemon reads the bundle with `O_NOFOLLOW`, imports it into its own bare
   repository and pushes only the lease ref, with a minimal git environment
   (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, no global config, hooks off, only HTTPS).
7. **Report**, then remove the workdir and publish repository (only paths
   strictly inside `workRoot`).

Code: `server/runner.go`, `sandbox.go`, `runnergrant.go`, `jobhome.go`,
`runnerauth.go`, `runnerlogin.go`, `runneraccounts.go`, `agentstream.go`,
`runnerpool.go`; app `app/src/runner_leases.py` (migration
`0193_runner_nodes`), `runner_logins.py` (`0195_runner_login_sessions`),
`runner_setup.py`, `runner_ssh_setup.py`, `runner_auth.py`; dashboard
`/dashboard/runners`; gateway route in `tools/mirror_gateway.py`.

An instance installs one runner next to its core with
`install-runner.sh --preregistered --name <name> --owner <owner> --binary
<daemon>`: no token handshake (the instance registers it with
`python -m forkmesh_host instance-runner`), `enableActions: true`, job user
`forkmesh-job` unless `--job-user` says otherwise, and the last output line
`FM_RUNNER_PUBLIC_KEY=<base64url raw Ed25519 key>`
([instance actions](../server/instance-actions.md)).

## Security model

A runner can read the one leased repository for the lease lifetime,
fast-forward exactly its lease ref, report on its own leases, and run
arbitrary code inside its sandbox. It cannot:

- **Write any other ref.** The gateway parses the receive-pack commands before
  git runs and refuses the whole push for another ref, more than one command,
  a delete, a push certificate or malformed input; non-fast-forward pushes are
  denied. An instance's own Actions runner may hold an `actions-push` grant
  for one `refs/heads/<branch>` instead, accepted only as a fast-forward of
  the existing tip; that grant also fetches the same repository, so a
  workflow can rebase before it pushes
  ([instance actions](../server/instance-actions.md)).
- **Mint or extend a grant.** Grants are Ed25519-signed by the router key,
  which only the app holds, over `forkmesh-runner-grant-v1` plus node, owner,
  repo, access, ref, runner, grant id and times.
- **Claim ineligible jobs.** Claims are signed with the runner's node key over
  method, path, body hash, single-use request id and time. Only `active`
  runners claim; pinned jobs go only to their runner; a `personal` runner
  serves only the account that registered it (see [Private runners](#private-runners));
  a `pool` runner serves only the cores in
  `RUNNER_POOL_TARGET_NODES` and only owners in its non-empty
  `allowed_owners` (the owners' opt-in). Steer jobs stay on their session's
  ref and hand over to another runner when the original is gone.
- **Reach core secrets, other jobs or the node key.** Jobs run as a dedicated
  unprivileged user (`fmjob-<account>` on a personal runner, `forkmesh-job`
  on the fleet) that cannot read the node key, daemon config or connector
  token.

### Private runners

A personal runner belongs to the account that added it and to nobody else:
otherwise admins see its provider account (sign-in email, usage) and
teammates can steer sessions on it, spending its owner's plan.

- **Seen only by its registrant.** `GET /api/runners`, `GET
  /api/runners/attention` and every `/api/runners/<name>/…` route answer
  only for `runner_nodes.registered_by`; admins get no wider view. Anyone
  else gets `404`, the same as for a runner that does not exist. Pool
  runners follow the same rule (the admin who registered one sees it); only
  revoking a pool runner stays open to any admin.
- **Used only by its registrant.** Registration refuses a personal runner
  whose `allowedOwners` is not exactly the registrant, admins included. A
  personal runner leases a job only when its owner is the registrant and its
  `requestedBy` is the registrant (`runner_leases._owner_allowed`,
  `_requester_allowed`), so a row edited to list other owners serves nobody
  extra.
- **Hidden from teammates.** A session started on a personal runner records
  `runnerPrivate`; organization members other than the runner's owner see the
  queue node instead of the runner name and no runner status
  (`_org_agent_hide_private_runner`). A follow-up from anyone else is
  refused with `403 runner_private` (`_org_agent_private_runner_block`)
  instead of queueing a job only that runner could take.
- **Alerts go to the registrant only.** An expired or expiring sign-in on a
  personal runner pings its registrant; admins are pinged (and nobody is
  emailed) only for pool runners.
- **One job user per account.** The installer creates `fmjob-<account>`
  (`fmjob-<first 19 characters>-<6 hex of SHA-256>` when the account name is
  longer than 26 characters, to fit the 32-character user name limit), with
  its own home for the provider sign-in and its own work root for stored
  accounts and session homes. See [Several accounts on one
  machine](#several-accounts-on-one-machine).

Residual risks:

- All jobs of one runner share its job user's uid; keep a pool runner at
  `maxConcurrentRuns: 1`. `/tmp` is shared with the daemon's namespace and
  swept between jobs.
- The provider login is readable by agent code. Use a dedicated provider
  account for a pool that serves other people.
- **The persistent home (HOME gap).** `systemd-run --scope --uid` resets
  `HOME` from passwd, so the sandbox restores the per-session `HOME` after
  the uid switch (`env -- HOME=<session home>`). Between sessions the job
  user's persistent home is daemon-owned 0700, so no job reads the stored
  sign-ins or plants files there. A sign-in or terminal session scrubs it
  down to `.claude/.credentials.json` and `.codex/auth.json`, then hands it
  to the job user until the last session ends; a job running during a
  sign-in can still reach it. `.claude.json` keeps only `oauthAccount` (to
  tell Claude accounts apart), `userID` and the onboarding flags; plantable
  `mcpServers`, `projects` and hooks go, and an unparsable file is removed.
  Only a job user whose passwd comment starts with `ForkMesh runner jobs`
  (what `install-runner.sh` creates) is locked and scrubbed; any other
  account set by hand in `runner.jobUser`/`jobUid` is left alone with a log
  warning, since scrubbing would erase a person's home.
- The read grant exposes the whole repository; loopback is blocked for jobs,
  so agents cannot reach dev servers on `127.0.0.1`.
- A non-root daemon runs jobs as its own user; a root daemon refuses to start
  without `runner.jobUid` or `runner.jobUser`.

### Job sandbox

```
systemd-run --scope --quiet --collect [--user] -p MemoryMax=<jobMemoryMax> -p MemorySwapMax=<jobMemorySwapMax> \
  -p CPUQuota=<jobCPUQuota> -p TasksMax=512 [--uid=<jobUid> --gid=<jobUid>] -- claude ...
```

- Root daemon: system manager with the job uid and an `IPAddressDeny` filter
  for loopback, link-local and private ranges. Non-root daemon: user manager,
  no IP filter. No manager: `ulimit -v` plus the Go-side timeout.
- Each session gets `<workRoot>/.homes/<id>` and an empty `TMPDIR`. Only the
  provider credential files are copied in (regular file, owned by the job
  user, at most 256 KiB, valid JSON, no symlinks) and copied back atomically.
- The environment is an allowlist: locale and `PATH`, proxy variables,
  provider keys the operator set on the daemon, the job's own `HOME`,
  `TMPDIR`, `USER`, and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.
- On small runners the daemon unit binds a disk-backed `/tmp`
  (`/var/lib/forkmesh-runner/tmp`) instead of `PrivateTmp`, and
  `jobMemorySwapMax` lets cold pages reach swap rather than OOM-killing jobs.

## App endpoints

| Endpoint | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/runners/register` | session plus key proof | register name and public key |
| `POST /api/runners/revoke` | registrant (pool runners: also any admin) | revoke |
| `POST /api/runners/pause`, `/resume` | registrant (pool runners: also any admin) | stop or restart new claims ([runners](../marketplace/runners.md#pause)) |
| `POST /api/runners/claim` | runner-signed | lease up to N jobs |
| `POST /api/runners/report` | runner-signed, lease holder | report result |
| `POST /api/runners/attachment` | runner-signed, lease holder | bytes of one prompt image |
| `POST /api/runners/pool-status` | core-signed | queue depth for the autoscaler |
| `POST /api/runners/poll` | runner-signed | availability and sign-in hand-off |
| `POST /api/runners/stream` | runner-signed, lease holder | live output while watched |
| `POST /api/runners/login/output`, `/login/input-poll` | runner-signed | sign-in terminal relay |
| `GET /api/runners` | registrant | the caller's own runners, availability, open sign-ins |
| `GET /api/runners/attention` | registrant | the caller's runners whose provider login is expired or expiring |
| `POST /api/runners/<name>/login` and `/login/<id>/{output,input,cancel}` | registrant | web sign-in |
| `POST /api/runners/setup-tokens`, `GET …/<id>`, `POST …/<id>/revoke` | session | one-time install tokens |
| `POST /api/runners/register-token` | setup token plus key proof | register a personal runner |
| `POST /api/runners/ssh/probe`, `/ssh/install`, `GET /api/runners/ssh/<id>` | session | server-side SSH setup |

Registration proof: the runner key signs
`forkmesh-runner-register-v1\n<name>\n<publicKey>\n<account>\n<ts>`. Only an
admin may register a `pool` runner, and a `personal` runner always serves
only its registrant. `forkmesh-mirror-node --print-public-key`
prints the key. Prompt images are fetched per lease, checked for size, digest
and type, and written under `.forkmesh/attachments/` without following
symlinks.

## Runner config

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "role": "runner",
  "gatewayConfig": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/mirror-gateway/config.json",
  "identityKey": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/identity/ed25519.pem",
  "runner": {
    "appUrl": "https://app.forkmesh.com",
    "maxConcurrentRuns": 1,
    "workRoot": "/var/lib/forkmesh-mirror/runner-work",
    "jobMemoryMax": "700M",
    "jobCPUQuota": "90%",
    "allowedOwners": ["<owner>"],
    "jobUser": "fmjob-<owner>",
    "burst": false
  }
}
```

Defaults: `maxConcurrentRuns` 1 (max 8), `jobMemoryMax` `700M`, `jobCPUQuota`
`90%`, `jobMemorySwapMax` `0`. `appUrl` must be HTTPS except on loopback.
The fleet installer (`tools/next_fleet.py`, `deploy/core/render.py`) creates
the job user (home 0700, no shell, no groups), runs the daemon as root with
`runner.jobUid`, keeps keys owner-only, and adds nftables output rules that
deny the job user metadata, private, CGNAT, loopback (except a local DNS
stub), mesh and private IPv6 ranges.

To opt owners into a pool runner, re-register it with the new
`allowedOwners`, or update `runner_nodes.allowed_owners` as an admin. An
empty list serves nobody.

## Setting up a personal runner

Any account can add a runner from `/dashboard/runners`:

- **One command.** The page mints a setup token and shows
  `curl -fsSL https://forkmesh.com/install-runner.sh | sudo bash -s -- --token fmrt_… --name <runner> --app https://app.forkmesh.com`.
  Tokens are 256-bit, stored as SHA-256 only, single use, valid 30 minutes,
  bound to one name and owner, and rate-limited. The runner proves its key
  with `forkmesh-runner-register-token-v1\n<name>\n<publicKey>\n<sha256(token)>\n<ts>`.
  A token always registers `scope: personal` for its owner.
- **Installer** (`www/public/install-runner.sh`): validates arguments, installs
  prerequisites and folders, gets the signed daemon release, generates a key,
  registers, learns the owning account from the answer (`registeredBy`),
  creates that account's job user `fmjob-<account>` and work root, writes the
  config, installs the service and its own nftables table (never touching the
  machine's firewall), installs the CLIs, runs `--check` and starts. It
  deletes nothing and has no uninstall mode.
- **Re-running it** updates the instance that already holds the runner
  name, keeping its key, job user, work root and port. Another runner name of
  the same account replaces that account's instance: the old key moves aside
  to `ed25519.pem.<old runner>` and the new name gets a fresh key, so two
  runner rows never share a key, while the job user and sign-ins stay.
- **macOS** (macOS 12 or newer, Xcode Command Line Tools): the same command
  works. See [macOS runners](#macos-runners).
- **From the desktop** (preferred for SSH): a `forkmesh://` hand-off fills the
  Hosts form; the desktop verifies the host key and runs the install line over
  its own SSH session, so the password never leaves the desktop.
- **From the servers:** `fmnext-ssh-helper` (`app/host/forkmesh_host/ssh_helper.py`)
  runs SSH in a socket-activated `DynamicUser` sandbox with no credentials and
  private networks blocked. Addresses must be public; the host key is pinned
  after the user confirms the fingerprint; a password reaches `ssh` only via
  `SSH_ASKPASS` from the child environment and a key only via a private
  `ssh-agent`; output is scrubbed. Without the helper socket the endpoints
  answer `503 ssh_setup_unavailable`.

### Several accounts on one machine

Each account that installs a runner on a machine gets its own instance
next to the others; installing one never stops or rewrites another.

| | Per account (`<account>` = the registrant) |
|---|---|
| Config | `/etc/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>/runner.json` (0700 folder) |
| State | `/var/lib/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>/{identity,gateway,work,tmp,home}` |
| Service | `forkmesh-runner@<account>.service` from the template `forkmesh-runner@.service`; `ReadWritePaths` is only its own state folder and its `/tmp` is its own `tmp` |
| Job user | `fmjob-<account>`, home `…/accounts/<account>/home` (0700), GECOS `ForkMesh runner jobs for <account>` |
| Loopback ports | `listen`/`gatewayProbe` pair from 8795 upward, skipping pairs another instance's config names or that are taken; kept on re-install |

- **Finding instances.** The installer reads `/etc/forkmesh-runner/runner.json`
  (the older single-runner layout) and every
  `/etc/forkmesh-runner/accounts/*/runner.json`. Before registering it looks
  for the instance holding the runner name; a new name signs with a staged
  key (`/var/lib/forkmesh-runner/pending-<name>.pem`) and moves into the
  owner's instance once ForkMesh names the owner.
- **Older installs.** The single-runner layout (`forkmesh-runner.service`,
  `/var/lib/forkmesh-runner`, user `forkmesh-job`, ports 8795/8796) stays
  that account's instance. Re-installing it rewrites its unit with
  `InaccessiblePaths` over the `accounts` folders, so it cannot read the
  other instances.
- **Job users are never shared.** A job user that another instance's config
  names is refused, and an existing system user is taken over only when its
  GECOS (`RealName` on macOS) names the same account, so an account whose
  name collides with another's derived user name, or with an unrelated user,
  cannot inherit it.
- **One firewall.** `jobs.nft` (Linux) and `jobs.pf` (macOS) are rebuilt on
  every install with the rules for every instance's job user; a job user
  that no longer exists is left out with a warning. A loaded nft table is
  reloaded with `nft -f` in place.
- The daemon needs no change: its idle sweep kills and deletes only what its
  own job uid owns.

## macOS runners

On Darwin the installer differs from Linux in these ways:

| | Linux | macOS |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon | `forkmesh-runner@<account>.service` | launch daemon `com.forkmesh.runner.<account>` (`/Library/LaunchDaemons`), log `/private/var/log/forkmesh-runner-<account>.log` |
| Paths | `/etc/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>`, `/var/lib/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>` | `/private/etc/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>`, `/private/var/db/forkmesh-runner/accounts/<account>` (real paths, so no `/etc` or `/var` symlink sits inside `workRoot`) |
| Job user | `useradd --system fmjob-<account>` | `dscl` hidden user `fmjob-<account>`, first free uid from 400 down to 300, shell `/usr/bin/false`, home `…/accounts/<account>/home` |
| Job firewall | nftables table `inet forkmesh_runner` | pf anchor `com.apple/forkmesh-runner` (`jobs.pf`, rules `user <uid>`), loaded by `com.forkmesh.runner-firewall` at boot and every 5 minutes; it enables pf if pf is off and never loads `/etc/pf.conf` |
| Daemon binary | signed release via `install.sh` | built from `https://forkmesh.com/forkmesh/forkmesh` (`server/`, sparse clone) with Go, because releases publish only Linux `forkmesh-mirror-node` assets; `FORKMESH_RUNNER_SOURCE_URL` overrides the clone URL |
| OpenSSL | system `openssl` | OpenSSL 3 (Homebrew `openssl@3`): the LibreSSL in macOS has no Ed25519 `genpkey` |
| Agent CLIs | `npm -g` as root | `npm -g` as the `sudo` user, so the Homebrew prefix stays theirs |

Homebrew runs as the user who ran `sudo` (`SUDO_USER`), never as root, to
install a missing Go, `openssl@3` or Node.js. The Go build folder stays in
`/private/tmp`, which macOS clears when it restarts; the installer deletes
nothing.

### Job sandbox on macOS

macOS has no systemd, so `detectJobSandbox` (`server/sandbox_darwin.go` sets
`directJobUID`) runs a root daemon's jobs directly: the child gets the job
uid and gid via `SysProcAttr.Credential` with no supplementary groups, in its
own process group. The sign-in pty uses the same credential. When no job is
running, the daemon runs `/bin/kill -KILL -1` as the job user, which ends
everything that user left behind, then sweeps the shared temp folders
(`/private/tmp`, `/private/var/tmp`).

What macOS lacks next to Linux:

- No memory, CPU or task limits; only the job timeout. `ulimit -v` is not
  applied because macOS refuses `RLIMIT_AS`.
- No per-scope `IPAddressDeny`; the pf anchor is the only network control and
  covers TCP and UDP only.
- HOME is set after the uid switch, so the per-session HOME does apply here
  (the Linux HOME gap above does not occur).

Untested as root on a live Mac: the launch daemon, `dscl` user and pf anchor.
`pfctl -n` parses `jobs.pf` and `plutil -lint` accepts both plists (macOS
15). Claude Code on macOS normally keeps its login in the Keychain, while the
runner copies credential files; check that a web sign-in as the job user
writes `~/.claude/.credentials.json`.

The daemon builds for `darwin`: `pty_darwin.go` opens a pty with
`TIOCPTYGRANT`/`TIOCPTYUNLK`/`TIOCPTYGNAME`, and `memory_darwin.go` reports
no memory figures (`/proc` and `sysinfo` are Linux only).

## Provider credentials

- **Mode A (implemented):** the runner uses its own signed-in `claude` or
  `codex` CLI, signed in from the website or on the host as the job user.
- **Web sign-in:** a `runner_login_sessions` row (10-minute TTL, one open per
  runner and provider) is handed to the runner on its next claim or poll. The
  runner runs the provider's fixed login command on a pty as the job user
  inside the sandbox and relays the screen in numbered chunks; token-shaped
  text is scrubbed before it leaves the runner. Only the account that
  registered the runner may drive it.
- **Several accounts per provider:** up to 12, stored under
  `<workRoot>/.accounts/<provider>/`; one is active, and refreshed credentials
  go back to the account the job used.
- **Expired logins:** the runner classifies authentication failures, stores a
  `needs_login` mark keyed by the credential's tokens, stops leasing that
  provider, and reports `auth` state (`ok`, `expiring`, `expired`) on every
  claim and poll from the credential file without a network call. The app
  pings the registrant (and, for a pool runner, the admins), turns a pool
  runner's `/status` row red, and
  refuses new jobs with `409 runner_login_expired` when no runner can take
  them. `GET /api/runners/attention` lets the web, desktop and phones show a
  sign-in prompt; its shape is stable.
- **Mode B (not built):** burst runners would receive the owner's provider
  token sealed to a one-time in-memory key, passed only through the job
  environment, for owners who opted in to cloud runs.

## The runners page

`/dashboard/runners` (`partials/views/runners.html`, `js/09-runners.js`): a
short header (sign-in help folded under "How sign-in works"), then one list.
Each runner is a header row (name, scope, online status, last check-in) with
flat provider and account rows, no nested boxes. Accent blue marks links,
focus and the active account; green only the "Set up a runner" button, the
online dot and "Signed in"; usage bars turn amber at 80 % and red at 95 %.
Online means a check-in within 10 minutes (`ONLINE_MS` in
`runner_logins.py`). The sign-in panel shows the authorize URL (Copy, Open),
the terminal as one code block, then the code form. The settings page
renders the same rows
([settings agents and runners](../app/settings-agents-and-runners.md)).

The desktop and both phones manage the same runners through the `runners`
Market package ([runners](../marketplace/runners.md)), which also
pauses, resumes and revokes them.

## Live agent output

While someone watches a run, the runner streams validated stream-json lines
to `POST /api/runners/stream` (mirrors use the per-repository stream route).
A heartbeat every 5 s learns whether anyone is watching; chunks are numbered
per job and deduplicated; the terminal report ends the stream.

## Burst pool (`server/runnerpool.go`, `server/vultr.go`)

Off by default; configured as `runnerPool` in a core's daemon config
(`maxBurstRunners`, `monthlySpendCeilingCents`, `hourlyPriceCents`,
`scaleUpAfter`, `idleTimeout`, region, plan, snapshot, `apiKeyFile`). Every
30 s it reads `/api/runners/pool-status`, lists instances and applies the pure
`decidePool`:

- scale up one instance per round when the queue has waited `scaleUpAfter`,
  no always-on runner has a free slot, and the count and spend ceiling allow;
- destroy instances idle for `idleTimeout` (5-minute boot grace);
- at the spend ceiling destroy every managed instance;
- touch only instances labelled `fmnext-burst-<n>` and tagged
  `forkmesh-next`, re-checked before every destroy.

The runner snapshot and its one-time registration are not built yet, so keep
`enabled: false`. Policy defaults are in [autoscaling](autoscaling.md).

## Failed runs

A failed run reports one error in `lastError`, chosen by
`server/agent_errors.go` from the CLI's result errors, an API-error message,
the stderr tail, or the exit status, capped at 600 runes. An outdated CLI gets
an explicit update message and is not retried with `--resume`. A run publishes
its branch only when it committed something.

## Node logs

Burst runners must be discoverable and carry the log reader for their logs to
reach the desktop ([node logs](node-logs.md)). A runner's own IDS reports
to `/api/runners/security-incident` ([intrusion detection](intrusion-detection.md)).

pages.title: Secrets vault
pages.description: Part of Operations.
pages.markdown:
# Secrets vault

Part of [Operations](README.md).

The app's variables (`ADMIN_PASS`, the router seed, integration tokens and so
on) are stored in the database encrypted under `DATA_KEY`. `DATA_KEY` is kept
only on the operator box; on a node it exists only in the app's memory while
that node is unsealed. Fleet runbook: [runbook](runbook.md);
encryption overview: [encryption](../encryption.md).

Switches in `deploy/fleet.toml` `[app]`: `vault = true` turns the vault on
(the example config defaults to plain systemd credentials);
`vault_peer_unseal = true` lets a sealed node get the key from an unsealed
peer, so the steady state needs no operator.

## What is where

| Item | Location |
|---|---|
