pages.markdown:
# Getting started on a phone

From install to your first agent run on iPhone, iPad or Android in a few
minutes. Back to the [phone apps](README.md).

```text
   1 Install ──► 2 Sign in ──► 3 Permissions ──► 4 Starter pack ──► 5 Tour
                     │            asked only        Minimal ·         Essentials ·
                     │            when needed       Standard ·        Advanced ·
                     ▼                              Everything        whole shebang
         the phone makes its own key
         and joins your account as a node
```

## 1. Install

| Platform | Where | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iPhone and iPad | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735) | iOS 17 or later |
| Android | `forkmesh-android-universal.apk` from [forkmesh.com/#downloads](https://forkmesh.com/#downloads) ([Android guide](android.md)) | Android 8.0 or later |

The Apple Watch app comes with the iPhone app ([Apple Watch](apple-watch.md)).

## 2. Sign in

- **Log in** with your ForkMesh account, and your authenticator code if you
  turned on two-factor sign-in.
- **Sign up** opens the sign-up page in a sheet; confirm your email, then log
  in on the form the app returns you to.
- **Forgot password?** opens the reset page.
- **Explore as guest** lets you look around first; a guest can post only in
  `#general` and `#mesh`.

Signing in makes the phone a node of your account. It creates its own
Ed25519 key on the device and registers it, with no QR code and no second
step. Your other devices get a "new node added" notice, so a sign-in you did
not make is easy to spot ([privacy and security](privacy-and-security.md)).

**Your own instance.** To use a self-hosted ForkMesh, add a project with your
instance's address and press **Check instance**, or pick one from
**Instances on ForkMesh**, the public list of instances. A project can also be
local only, with no server.

## 3. Permissions, only when they matter

The first screen after sign-in explains that the app asks for each permission
(notifications, microphone, camera, photos, contacts, local network and the
rest) only the first time a feature needs it. A fresh install shows no system
prompts.

## 4. Pick a starter pack

Choose how much the Home screen starts with: **Minimal**, **Standard** (the
default) or **Everything**. Each Home tile is a Market package, so you can add
or remove any of them later. Then a short tour (**Essentials**, **Advanced**
or **The whole shebang**) shows the way around.

## 5. Connect to your desktop

There is nothing to pair. When your desktop runs ForkMesh under the same
account, the phone finds it and the desktop admits it after checking the
phone's key against your account:

```text
   phone ──── same Wi-Fi: direct, encrypted channel ────► desktop
     │                                                       ▲
     └── away from home: through the relay ──► cores ────────┘
         (end to end encrypted; the relay sees only routing)
```

- On the same network the phone talks to the desktop directly.
- Away from home it goes through the relay, encrypted end to end. The desktop
  must be online.
- A phone signed in to a **different** account pairs on the local network
  with a six-digit code shown on the desktop.

Then open **Agents**, tap the new agent button, pick a repository and write a
prompt. Details: [agent access](mobile-agent-access.md).

## Notifications

| What pings you | You can act from the banner |
| --- | --- |
| An agent waiting for approval, done, or stuck | **Approve**, **Deny**, **Continue**, **Merge & clean up** |
| A direct message or a chat message sent with notify | **Reply** |
| Pushes to your repositories, review requests, mentions | Open the item |

The ping settings screen has a switch per kind,
**Pause**, **quiet hours**, email and a test push. Quiet hours do not apply to
`#mesh`, `#general` or channel pushes. Chat text in a notification is
decrypted on the phone. Android has no push service: see
[Android](android.md#notifications).

## Widgets and system features

On iPhone:

- 🏝️ **Live Activity**: one summary of your running agents in the Dynamic
  Island and on the Lock Screen.
- 🧱 **Widgets**: running agents, Inbox, a pinned repository's pull requests,
  a timer, and Lock Screen widgets.
- 🎚️ **Controls**: **New agent** and **Approvals** in Control Center.
- 🌙 **Focus filter**: choose what ForkMesh shows in each Focus.
- 🗣️ **Siri and Shortcuts**: [Siri](siri.md).

## When something does not work

| Symptom | What is going on |
| --- | --- |
| Lists show but nothing can be changed | You are offline. Cached lists stay readable; signed changes wait in an outbox and go when you reconnect |
| The desktop is not found | Away from home the desktop must be online; on the same Wi-Fi allow **Local network** access for ForkMesh |
| Live agent updates stop when the app is in the background | iOS suspends the live connection in the background; a push wakes it, and it resumes when you open the app |
| File transfer to the desktop fails away from home | File transfer works only on the local network |
| A file will not open in the editor | Files over 512 KB, binary files and files that are not UTF-8 are refused ([file editing](mobile-file-editing.md)) |
| Siri does not run a command | See the troubleshooting table in [Siri](siri.md) |

Related: [privacy and security](privacy-and-security.md) ·
[agent access](mobile-agent-access.md) · [phone apps](README.md)

pages.title: Mobile access to owner-encrypted agent sessions
pages.description: Part of Phone apps.
pages.markdown:
# Mobile access to owner-encrypted agent sessions

Part of [Phone apps](README.md).

Agent sessions are end-to-end encrypted to the owner's devices. The phone is an
owner device with its own key, so it can read sessions, queue prompts for a
mirror, and control a desktop live on the LAN or through the relay. The
cryptography is summarised in [encryption](../encryption.md); the device
model is the [mobile node contract](mobile-node-contract.md).

## The owner-device model

Each owner device holds a hybrid recipient key and registers only the public
halves at `POST /api/security/owner-keys`. The desktop seals every session
snapshot and transcript tail into one `forkmesh.owner-sealed` envelope with one
wrap entry per enrolled device. The relay stores ciphertext and holds no
private key.

```json
{
  "kind": "forkmesh.owner-sealed", "v": 1,
  "alg": "x25519+mlkem768/aes256gcm",
  "nonce": "…", "tag": "…", "body": "…",
  "recipients": [{ "kid": "…", "x25519": "…", "mlkem768": "…", "nonce": "…", "tag": "…", "key": "…" }]
}
```

- One random AES-256-GCM content key encrypts the payload; it is wrapped per
  device under X25519 + ML-KEM-768.
- 1 to 6 recipients (`MAX_OWNER_ENVELOPE_RECIPIENTS`), no duplicates; the
  sealing device's entry comes first.
- A recipient id is `base64url(SHA-256(x25519Pub || mlkemPub))`.
- Wrap key: `HKDF-SHA256(ssX25519 || ssMlKem, salt "forkmesh-mirror-kem-v1",
  info ephemeralX25519Pub || mlkemCiphertext)`.
- Each device opens its own entry by key id.

**Authorization is membership.** The repository privacy policy names the
desktop vault key (`ownerKeyId`). The relay requires that key to be among the
recipients, so the desktop can seal to itself plus every companion device; an
envelope without it is rejected with `wrong_owner_key`.

The desktop refreshes companion bundles every ten minutes and re-seals when the
set changes. Revocation is not retroactive: stored envelopes stay readable by
the devices they were sealed to.

| Runtime | Role | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Relay | Validates framing and bounds, never decrypts | `app/src/security_controls.py` |
| Desktop | Generates the vault key, seals to vault plus companions | `desktop/src/MirrorCrypto.cpp` |
| iOS, Android | Enroll the device key, open their own entries | `FMCrypto/OwnerCrypto.swift`, `security/OwnerCrypto.kt` |

When sessions exist but are sealed to other devices, the app says how many
and how to enroll this one, instead of showing an empty list. Cross-runtime
tests seal with the desktop binary and open in Swift and Kotlin.

## Sending a prompt to a mirror

A prompt typed on the phone uses the relay-readable agent queue, as the web
does. `GET /api/repo/{o}/{r}/agent-sessions` (or the organization
`agent-bots` route) lists nodes that can take the job; an online mirror is
suggested first. Failed or stopped runs can be retried: a claimed session
continues on its branch, an unstarted one is re-queued. Prompts can carry
photos, downscaled to 2048 px with metadata stripped, within a 10 MB total.
The Cloud section lists runs that mirrors are working; the relay's
`cloud-agents` event topic refreshes it. A queued session shows its chain:
prompt, mirror, branch, pull request, merge.
Merging a mirror agent's branch straight onto its base is owner-only: the
node's owner, or an owner of the organization. Anyone else gets `forbidden`
and opens a pull request instead.

## Controlling a desktop on the LAN or through the relay

Live control opens the desktop's local-control protocol directly over the mesh
TCP port on the same network, or inside `{"type":"control"}` chunks forwarded
by the account event relay when away. The Ed25519-authenticated handshake
derives per-direction AES-256-GCM keys, so the relay sees only routing
metadata.

Discovery: `GET /api/accounts/desktops` returns the caller's enabled desktop
keys and labels. The phone caches the list for ten minutes, tries at most four
candidates, and checks the answering desktop's public key. No LAN pairing is
needed: this is automatic same-account desktop discovery.

Admission: the desktop checks the phone key against its account's enabled
`owner_sign` devices. A same-account phone is accepted without a code and
stored as an account-held, desktop-local pairing (`"approval": "account"` in
`data/local_control/paired-devices.json`). The desktop re-checks the account on
connect and every ten minutes, and closes the channel (`revoked`) when the
phone is gone. Through the relay, a phone is admitted only if the account
confirmed it within 24 hours (`account_check_failed` otherwise). A phone from
another account must pair on the LAN with a six-digit code.

Channel recovery: idle relayed channels are pinged every 30 seconds; a desktop
that lost a channel answers `channel_gone` so the phone redials; the desktop
closes channels silent for 15 minutes, holds at most eight, and limits
half-open relayed hellos to 16 with a 30-second expiry.

| Action | Methods | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| List, start, read, prompt, stop, continue | `agents.*` | Authenticated channel |
| Attach photos | `agents.image.begin`, `agents.image.chunk` | Desktop checks size, type and SHA-256 |
| Answer tool requests | `agentops.approvals`, `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.answer` | One-use desktop confirmation plus phone device authentication |
| Review changes and images | `agentops.diff`, `agentops.file` | Read-only; credentials redacted; images up to 2 MiB |
| Merge and clean up | `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.merge` | Agent must be idle; unstaged edits in the desktop checkout that clash with the merge can be set aside first (**Set aside and merge**, backed up on a `wip/` branch) |
| Delete agent, worktree and branch | `agentops.prepare`, `agentops.delete` | Explicit confirmation; agent must be idle |

An older desktop answers `unsupported` and the phone asks for an update.

## Limitations

- Away-from-home control needs the desktop online, signed in and connected to
  the relay.
- A relay reconnect closes the live channel; the next action opens a new one.
- File transfer is LAN-only.

pages.description: Part of Phone apps.
pages.markdown:
# Mobile node contract

Part of [Phone apps](README.md).

The wire and policy contract that makes the iOS and Android apps **mobile
nodes** of a ForkMesh account: peers of the desktop node, coupled to it through
the account on the relay. The owned Git engine is specified in
[`owned-git-engine-spec.md`](owned-git-engine-spec.md).

Principle 1.2's "never device-to-device" boundary is
superseded for optional desktop control: a phone may open the desktop's authenticated, end-to-end
encrypted control protocol on the LAN or through the relay. See
[Mobile access to owner-encrypted agent sessions](mobile-agent-access.md#controlling-a-desktop-on-the-lan-or-through-the-relay).
The phone stays independently useful and never hosts repositories.

## 1. Principles

1. **Nodes author and publish; mirrors serve.** A mobile node creates, commits
   and publishes repositories. It never hosts clones and never runs in the
   background.
2. **Coupled through the account.** Desktop and phone are each fully useful
   alone (optional desktop control aside).
3. **Login is the bind.** Password (plus TOTP when enrolled) authenticates the
   person; the phone's Ed25519 key is registered as a `mobile_node` device on
   that login. No QR code or second ceremony.
4. **The web app is the node registry.** Listing and revoking nodes happens on
   the web.
5. **User presence only for destructive actions** (section 6).
6. **Capabilities limit blast radius.** A `mobile_node` key can publish and
   sign as the owner but never host, mirror, or touch payout settings, secrets
   or mirror process control.

## 2. Device kinds and capabilities

| Kind | Capabilities |
| --- | --- |
| `desktop_node` | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr,host_repo,mirror_repo,publish_repo,owner_sign` |
| `mobile_node` | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr,publish_repo,owner_sign` |
| client (web) | `browse,comment,submit_issue,submit_pr` |

`contribution_key_proof` is appended once the device proof verifies. A
`mobile_node` row never satisfies a hosting check (`host_repo`, `mirror_repo`,
mirror process control, node reservation). `_owner_signing_pubkeys(owner)`
unions every enabled, unrevoked `owner_sign` device, so a phone key signs
sync, catalog publications and other owner-signed requests.

## 3. Bind (login)

`POST /api/accounts/login` with `identifier`, `password`, optional `totp`,
`pubkey`, `deviceTs`, `deviceSig`, `deviceKind: "mobile_node"` and
`deviceLabel`.

- `deviceSig` signs `forkmesh-device-bind-v1\n{account}\n{pubkey}\n{deviceTs}`.
- A mobile bind registers the device with `MOBILE_NODE_CAPABILITIES`, never
  becomes the account's primary key and never counts as `desktopCapable`.
  Unknown kinds return `400 invalid_device_kind`.
- The session records the device (`account_sessions.device_bi`). The response
  reports `sessionKind`, `capabilities`, `canHost: false`, `canPublish`,
  `canOwnerSign`, `deviceId` and the account's devices.
- The first bind of a new device raises a "new node added" notification.

## 4. Node registry

| Route | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/accounts/devices` | Devices with kind, label, capabilities, enabled, last seen, and `current` |
| `DELETE /api/accounts/devices/{id}` | Re-authenticated (password, TOTP). Revokes the device and every session it opened |
| `POST /api/accounts/devices/check` | Whether a key belongs to the caller's account; used by the desktop to admit same-account phones |
| `POST /api/accounts/devices/revoke-all` | Re-authenticated. Revokes every other device and session, optionally by kind |

Revocation removes the key from owner signing at once, sessions fail with
`401` and `device_revoked`, and a revoked row is permanent: the app rotates its
seed, keeps local repositories and returns to login.

## 5. Audit

`account.device_bind`, `account.device_revoke` and
`account.device_revoke_all` are audited. Catalog records store the signing key
as `maintainer`, so the web can show which node published.

## 6. Destructive actions

Deleting a local repository; deleting, transferring or archiving a published
one; revoking devices; changing password or security settings. These require
Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode, or an explicit confirmation when none
is enrolled.

## 7. Publish and push

The engine speaks smart HTTP to the app origin only; the relay (the core
nodes, see [architecture](../architecture.md)) is a masked proxy in front of
the [mirror gateway](../operations/direct-https-mirror-gateway.md).

- `GET /{owner}/{repo}/info/refs?service=git-receive-pack`
- `POST /{owner}/{repo}/git-receive-pack`

Writes carry `X-ForkMesh-Pubkey`, `X-ForkMesh-Ts` and `X-ForkMesh-Sig` over
`forkmesh-git-push-v1\n{owner}\n{repo}\n{method}\n{ts}\n{sha256hex(body)}`. The
relay accepts the owner's primary key, an enabled `owner_sign` device with
`publish_repo`, or a key with organization write permission, then forwards
under a per-request masked-proxy capability for
`/v1/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/git-receive-pack`.

- Bodies up to 8 MB are verified in full. Larger packs send
  `X-ForkMesh-Body-Sha256`; the relay streams the body and binds the capability
  to that digest. Otherwise `413 push_too_large`.
- The gateway runs `git receive-pack --stateless-rpc` with deletes and
  non-fast-forwards denied, `fsckObjects` on, hooks disabled and a bounded
  input size. It creates a bare repository on first push only for owners on
  its `writableOwners` allowlist, and removing an owner revokes push and read.
- With no healthy push endpoint, the first push goes to
  `HOSTED_GIT_WRITE_NODE`, else `503 push_unavailable`.
- After a first push the phone publishes the signed catalog record itself. A
  publish from a non-authoritative device is accepted only as a subordinate
  mirror (`202`, `mirror: true`); replays get `409 stale_update`.
- Stock Git can push with a Basic credential the website issues from a
  signed-in session (see [hosted repositories](../hosted-repositories.md)).

Client guardrails: no force, no delete, no hooks, foreground only, resource
caps and cancellation.

## 8. Platform notes

No background modes, no runtime code download, no hook execution. Store
listings say "publish", never "host" or "server".

pages.markdown:
# Phone apps

ForkMesh on iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Android. A phone is a node of your
account: it holds its own keys, clones and commits with its own Git engine,
reads your end-to-end encrypted agent sessions, and can drive your desktop
from the couch or the other side of the world.

How the apps are built is on the [phone app internals](../native/README.md)
home page; every ForkMesh app side by side is on [ForkMesh apps](../apps.md).

```text
            ┌──────────────────────── your phone ─────────────────────────┐
            │  own Ed25519 key (Keychain / Keystore)  ·  own Git engine   │
            │  Agents · Inbox · Repos · Chat          ·  widgets, Siri    │
            └──────┬──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────┘
                   │ same Wi-Fi           │ HTTPS                 │ paired
                   │ (direct, LAN)        │                       │ (watch)
                   ▼                      ▼                       ▼
         ┌──────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────┐    ┌────────────────┐
         │  your desktop    │   │  ForkMesh cores   │    │  Apple Watch   │
         │  agents, repos,  │◄─►│  relay sees only  │    │  follows the   │
         │  worktrees       │   │  ciphertext and   │    │  phone's keys  │
         └──────────────────┘   │  routing          │    └────────────────┘
                                └───────────────────┘
```

## Get the app

| | Platform | Get it | Requires |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 📱 | iPhone and iPad | [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/forkmesh/id6803060735) | iOS 17 or later |
| ⌚ | Apple Watch | Installs with the iPhone app | watchOS 10 or later, with the iPhone nearby |
| 🤖 | Android | Signed APK `forkmesh-android-universal.apk` from [forkmesh.com/#downloads](https://forkmesh.com/#downloads) | Android 8.0 or later |

Then follow [getting started on a phone](getting-started.md).

## The app at a glance

| | Tab | What lives there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🤖 | **Agents** | Every agent you run, on your desktop, a cloud runner or the phone itself; the default tab |
| 📥 | **Inbox** | Pings, review requests, assigned issues and tasks, mentions and approvals |
| 📦 | **Repos** | Your repositories: code, commits, pull requests, issues, releases and Actions |
| 💬 | **Chat** | Channels, direct messages, `#mesh` and office rooms |

Always on screen: the **new agent** button (tap for the composer, hold to
speak a prompt). Your avatar opens the **You** hub; **Home** holds the tiles
of the Market packages you turned on, and **Search** finds anything.

## What you can do

| | Area | Highlights | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 🤖 | Agents | Start, steer, stop, continue, retry and merge agents on your desktop or cloud runners; answer approvals; review diffs file by file; run an agent on the phone with your own API key | [Agent access](mobile-agent-access.md) |
| 📦 | Repositories | Browse code, commits and releases; review and merge pull requests; unified or side-by-side diffs; clone to the phone, commit and publish | [Owned Git engine](owned-git-engine-spec.md) |
| ✏️ | Quick edits | Edit one file and open a pull request, with no clone or fork | [File editing](mobile-file-editing.md) |
| 💬 | Chat and calls | End-to-end encrypted direct messages with safety numbers; voice and video calls to a person or a private channel; `#mesh` over the local network and Bluetooth | [Calls](../calls.md) · [Safety numbers](../chat-safety-numbers.md) |
| 🔔 | Notifications | Pings, pushes, direct messages and chat; act from the banner (Approve, Deny, Continue, Merge, Reply); per-kind switches, pause and quiet hours | [Getting started](getting-started.md#notifications) |
| 🧩 | iPhone system features | A Live Activity in the Dynamic Island, Home and Lock Screen widgets, Control Center controls and a Focus filter | [Getting started](getting-started.md#widgets-and-system-features) |
| 🗣️ | Siri and Shortcuts | Start, check, approve, message, stop and merge agents by voice | [Siri](siri.md) |
| 🛍️ | Market tools | Turn on the packages you want as Home tiles: Password Vault with AutoFill, RSS Reader, Notes, Tasks, phone security checkup and more | [Apple Health](apple-health.md) · [Phone security](../marketplace/phone-security.md) |
| ⌚ | Apple Watch | Follow, steer and hear your agents from your wrist | [Apple Watch](apple-watch.md) |

## Guides

| | Page | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🚀 | [Getting started on a phone](getting-started.md) | Install, sign in, first run, connecting to your desktop, notifications and widgets |
| 🔐 | [Privacy and security on the phone](privacy-and-security.md) | Where your keys live, what is encrypted, what the server sees, and what to do if you lose your phone |
| 🤖 | [Android](android.md) | Installing and updating the APK, and how the Android app differs on purpose |
| ⌚ | [Apple Watch](apple-watch.md) | What the watch app does today and what it needs |
| 🎛️ | [Agent access](mobile-agent-access.md) | Reading encrypted agent sessions, queueing prompts and controlling a desktop from the phone |
| ✏️ | [File editing](mobile-file-editing.md) | Editing one file and opening a pull request from the phone, with no clone or fork |
| 🗣️ | [Siri](siri.md) | Siri and Shortcuts commands for agents on iPhone |
| ❤️ | [Apple Health](apple-health.md) | The seven optional tools that read or write Apple Health, and what reaches your account |

## Contracts

For people building clients or checking the design:

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Mobile node contract](mobile-node-contract.md) | The wire and policy contract that makes a phone a node of your account |
| [Owned Git engine](owned-git-engine-spec.md) | The Swift and Kotlin Git engine the phones carry, and its security boundary |

Core pages: [architecture](../architecture.md),
[encryption](../encryption.md), [mirroring](../mirroring.md),
[censorship resilience](../censorship-resilience.md). Back to the
[documentation index](../README.md).

pages.description: Where your keys live on a phone, what is end-to-end encrypted, what the ForkMesh servers can still see, and what to do if a phone is lost. The full picture for every app is in…
pages.markdown:
# Privacy and security on the phone

Where your keys live on a phone, what is end-to-end encrypted, what the
ForkMesh servers can still see, and what to do if a phone is lost. The full
picture for every app is in [encryption and signatures](../encryption.md).
Back to the [phone apps](README.md).

## Your keys stay on the phone

Each phone makes its own Ed25519 key when you sign in, and that key never
leaves it.

| | Platform | Where the key lives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 📱 | iPhone and iPad | The Keychain, in a private group no app extension can read, marked this-device-only so it is not copied to a backup or another phone |
| 🤖 | Android | The Android Keystore |

The key signs what the phone does (commits, pull requests, merges) as a node
of your account ([mobile node contract](mobile-node-contract.md)). Destructive
actions (deleting or archiving a repository, revoking devices, changing your
password or security settings) and approvals and merges ask for Face ID,
Touch ID or the device passcode first.

## What is encrypted end to end

```text
   phone ══════════ sealed ═══════════► your other devices
     │                                        ▲
     └──► ForkMesh relay ─────────────────────┘
          stores and forwards ciphertext;
          sees who, when, and how much
```

| | What | Who can read it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🤖 | Agent sessions and transcripts | Your own enrolled devices only; the relay stores ciphertext |
| 🎛️ | Desktop control traffic | The phone and your desktop; the relay sees only routing |
| 💬 | Direct messages, channels and group calls | The people in the conversation ([safety numbers](../chat-safety-numbers.md)) |
| 🔔 | Chat text in notifications | Decrypted on the phone |
| 🔑 | Password Vault | You; the server keeps ciphertext |

## What the servers can see

- Who talks to whom, when and how much (metadata).
- Public channels, which are not end-to-end encrypted.
- Prompts you send to an agent on a mirror or runner, which use a queue the
  relay can read, as the web app's do.
- The text of pings (alerts), which are not sealed.

The RSS Reader is local only: nothing it reads reaches the server.

## If you lose a phone

1. On the web, open the devices list in your account settings.
2. Revoke the lost phone, or use **revoke all** to remove every other device
   at once. Both ask for your password and authenticator code.
3. The phone's key stops being able to sign and its sessions end at once;
   your desktop drops it within ten minutes.

```text
   revoke ──► key refused (device_revoked) ──► desktop drops it within 10 min
```

Revocation is not retroactive: a phone can still read agent sessions that were
sealed to it before you revoked it. A new sign-in on any device sends a "new
node added" notice to your others, so check those notices.

## Permissions

The app asks for each system permission only when a feature first needs it
([getting started](getting-started.md#3-permissions-only-when-they-matter)).
The Market's phone security checkup reviews the phone's own settings
([phone security](../marketplace/phone-security.md)).

Related: [encryption and signatures](../encryption.md) ·
[agent access](mobile-agent-access.md) ·
[threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md) · [phone apps](README.md)

pages.markdown:
# Using Siri with ForkMesh on iPhone

Part of [Phone apps](README.md).

The ForkMesh iPhone app adds its commands to Siri and the Shortcuts app. You
can start an agent, ask what your agents are doing, answer their requests, and
stop, continue, message, merge or delete them without opening the app. How the
phone reaches the desktop is in
[mobile agent access](mobile-agent-access.md).

## Before you start

- Install the app and sign in. For commands that control an agent, sign in to
  the ForkMesh desktop app with the same account; the phone reaches it through
  the relay.
- Open the app once after installing or updating it so Siri learns your
  agents' names.
- In **Settings → Siri**, turn Siri on and allow ForkMesh to work with it.

Apple requires the app's name in every built-in phrase: say "in ForkMesh" (or
"for", "on", "with ForkMesh"). For shorter phrases, see
[Your own phrases](#your-own-phrases).

## Naming an agent

Siri knows each desktop agent by its session number ("Agent 754"), spoken as a
number or digit by digit, or by part of its title or repository. Leave the
agent out and Siri lists your agents and asks which one.

## What you can say

| Goal | Example phrases |
| --- | --- |
| Start an agent | "Start a new agent in ForkMesh", "Start a ForkMesh agent on *repository*" |
| Check status | "What are my ForkMesh agents doing?", "What did agent 754 change in ForkMesh?" |
| Answer a request | "Approve ForkMesh request", "Deny the ForkMesh request" |
| Message | "Tell agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Stop or continue | "Stop agent 754 in ForkMesh", "Continue agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Merge | "Merge and clean up agent 754 in ForkMesh" |
| Delete | "Delete agent 754 in ForkMesh", "Delete all agents in ForkMesh" |
| Open a screen | "Open inbox in ForkMesh", "Open *owner/repository* in ForkMesh" |
| Listening | "Start listening in ForkMesh", "Turn the ForkMesh Genie on", "Stop listening in ForkMesh" |

- Starting an agent opens the prompt composer, even if the app was closed.
- Approving, merging and deleting read a summary from the desktop, ask for
  confirmation, and need the iPhone unlocked. Merge and continue work only on
  desktop agents. "All agents" means the agents ForkMesh started on your
  desktop; deleting removes each agent with its worktree and branch.
- Listening turns on the in-app voice assistant while ForkMesh is on screen.
  Speech is recognised on the device and nothing is kept.

## Apple Watch

Say "Start a new agent in ForkMesh" on the watch, dictate the prompt and
confirm. The iPhone starts the agent with the last model you used, on the last
repository you used unless you name one. The **Start an agent** action takes an
optional **Repository** (`owner/name` or just the name), so a shortcut can fix
it. The iPhone must be nearby and signed in.

## Commands without a built-in phrase

Apple allows ten built-in commands per app, so **Stop all agents**, **Start a
timer**, **Open agent run**, **Open inbox**, **Open agent approvals**, **Open
issue**, **Open note** and **Start a new iOS build** are available in the Shortcuts
app only.

## Start a new iOS build

"Hey Siri, start a new iOS build" builds `main` ad hoc on the Office MacBook
and emails the install link to the iOS testers, like the iOS button on the
office MacBook row of the Desktops page. Set it up once:

1. In the Shortcuts app, tap **+**, then **Add Action**, and pick ForkMesh's
   **Start a new iOS build**.
2. Keep the shortcut's name, **Start a new iOS build**, and tap **Done**.

Siri asks you to confirm before the build starts, and needs the iPhone
unlocked and paired with the desktop. If a build is already running, Siri says
so and leaves it running.

## Your own phrases

In the Shortcuts app, add a ForkMesh action (for example **Start an agent**),
fill in fixed values, and name the shortcut with the phrase you want. "Hey
Siri, *shortcut name*" then runs it without saying "ForkMesh".

## Troubleshooting

| Siri says | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Agent number not recognised | Open the app to refresh the agent list, or pick from the list |
| "Sign in to ForkMesh first." | Sign in on the phone |
| "Pair this phone with your desktop first." | Run the desktop app, signed in to the same account |
| "Siri can only do that for agents on your desktop." | Manage cloud agents in the app |
| "Update ForkMesh on the desktop to delete agents from here." | Update the desktop app |
| "Allow the microphone and speech recognition…" | Enable both in **Settings → ForkMesh** |
| A web search opens instead | Include "ForkMesh" in the phrase |

A record marked *pre-charter* was made before the charter existed. It is kept for the public
history but does not count as a completed charter process.

## Records

| Record | Process | Title | Stage | Outcome | Opened | Decided | Counts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [FMP-0000](#fmp-0000) | proposal | Protocol certification program with expiring, evidence-derived badges | implemented | accepted | 2026-09-14 | 2026-09-14 | pre-charter |
| [FMP-0001](#fmp-0001) | proposal | Adopt the protocol and ecosystem governance charter | review | — | 2026-09-14 | — | charter |

### FMP-0000

**Protocol certification program with expiring, evidence-derived badges**

Pre-charter record of issue #512: certification profiles, a language-neutral adapter protocol, retained attested reports, and badges that expire when vectors or profiles change or after 90 days.

> Recorded retroactively from commit 1652ac060. It landed through the issue and pull request workflow before this charter existed, with no review window, vote, or dissent solicitation, so it does not count as a completed charter process.

### FMP-0001

**Adopt the protocol and ecosystem governance charter**

Adopt charter 1.0.0-rc.1: a protocol council, security response team, and appeals panel with seats reserved for independent implementers and community operators; published timelines for proposals, security decisions, appeals, and deprecation; conflict and funding disclosures linked to every decision; and rights that no plan, token, or funder can remove.

### FMS-0001

**Block a stable protocol suite while any critical or high threat is open**

Pre-charter record of the stable release rule in the threat register: the suite stays a candidate until each critical or high threat is mitigated by a numbered requirement or accepted with a reviewer, date, and rationale. Open high threats at the time of recording: TM-004, TM-006, TM-008, TM-014, TM-018.

pages.markdown:
# Protocol and ecosystem governance

The charter governs the protocol suite, certification, compatibility and the
moderation baseline; repositories follow their own policy documents. Charter,
records and participant disclosures live in
[`conformance/governance/v1/`](../../conformance/governance/v1/charter.json);
the [decision register](decision-register.md) and
`/docs/governance/register.json` are generated from them.

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| This charter | Bodies and quorum, proposals, security decisions, appeals, running the ledger |
| [Decision register](decision-register.md) | Every proposal, security and appeal record with its votes and disclosures (generated) |

Related: the [protocol suite](../protocol/README.md), the
[threat model](../protocol/threat-model.md) and
[public-interest funding](../funding/README.md). Back to the
[documentation index](../README.md).

## Roles

| Body | Seats | Quorum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol council | 2 maintainers, 2 independent implementers, 2 community operators | 4 |
| Security response team | 1 maintainer, 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator | 2 |
| Appeals panel | 1 independent implementer, 1 community operator, 1 community member | 3 |

Independent constituencies must vote, and no employer or funder may cast more
than half the votes, so maintainers cannot decide alone.

## Proposals

`FMP-NNNN`: review at least 14 days (30 if breaking), last call 7 days, decision
within 14 days. A `no` vote needs a dissent statement. Narrowing a protected
right (free protocol, portable identity and repositories, token-free
governance) needs two thirds. See the [protocol suite](../protocol/README.md).

## Security decisions

Report as in [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md): acknowledge in 3 days, embargo
at most 90 days, publish `FMS-NNNN` within 7 days of disclosure, ratify within 30.

## Appeals

`FMA-NNNN` within 30 days, decided within 30 days by uninvolved panel members.

## Running the ledger

`python3 tools/protocol_governance.py validate|render|gate|status|closure`;
tests are `app/tests/test_protocol_governance.py`. Disclosures stay current for
180 days. Records are fixed or annotated, never deleted.

pages.markdown:
# Public-interest funding

The program funds public repositories, volunteer mirrors, accessibility,
documentation, education and independent tooling through donations,
sponsorship, grants and matching. Funding never buys access, votes or network
rights. Program and rounds live in
[`conformance/funding/v1/`](../../conformance/funding/v1/program.json); the
[funding register](funding-register.md) and `/docs/funding/register.json` are
generated from them.

| Page | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| This guide | Eligibility, selection, conflicts, payment, disclosure, recovery, closure |
| [Funding register](funding-register.md) | Offers, areas, rounds, reviewers, awards and payments (generated) |

Related: [incentive independence](../incentive-independence.md), the
[governance charter](../governance/README.md) and the
[business model](../business-model.md). Back to the
[documentation index](../README.md).

## Eligibility

Public, openly licensed work in a program area. No ForkMesh account, plan,
wallet or token is needed. The forkmesh.com operator, its staff, and a round's
funders and reviewers are excluded.

## Selection

Weighted 0-5 scores (benefit 30, feasibility 20, accessibility 20,
sustainability 15, decentralization 15); an award needs 60/100 from at least 3
reviewers including a non-maintainer, and no recipient may exceed 25% of a round.

## Conflicts

Reviewers with a shared employer or funder, or who are the applicant, must
recuse; funders never review.

## Payment rails

Recipient's choice of bank transfer, Open Collective, Liberapay or Solana; a
conventional rail is always offered.

## Independence

An award's `grants` list must be empty, and the business-model flags such as
`tokenOrBlockchainRequired` must stay `false`.

## Disclosure and reporting

Pool, funders, administrative cost (at most 10%), reviewers, scores, recusals,
awards and receipted milestone payments are published; the outcome report is
recomputed by the ledger.

## Community review

At least 14 days on concentration, accessibility and conflict findings.

## Failure, rollback, and recovery

Fix failing records; never waive the gate or delete records. Use `returned`,
`missed`, `waived` and `cancelled` states, and `render` for a stale register.

## Measures

`status` reports money flows, recipients, milestones, concentration and overdue
reports.

## Closure criteria for issue #515

A pilot round is reported, paid on chosen rails, reviewed, and nothing is
overdue (`closure` exits zero).

## Linked automated evidence

`python3 tools/public_interest_funding.py gate` runs in CI with
`app/tests/test_public_interest_funding.py`.

# Public-interest funding register

Program `1.0.0-rc.1` · Status: **proposed**. How to apply, review, and report is in the [program guide](README.md). The same data is published as searchable JSON at `/docs/funding/register.json`.

## Offers

| Offer | Status | Eligibility | Selection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Donation | planned | Anyone may donate. Gifts that carry conditions beyond an area restriction are declined. | Donations join the pool of the next announced round in their area. |
| Recurring sponsorship | planned | Anyone may sponsor. Sponsorship buys no placement, ranking, seat, vote, or say in selection. | Sponsorship funds rounds in the sponsored area. Sponsors are listed as funders of the rounds they fund. |
| Targeted grant | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. | Disclosed reviewers score the published selection criteria. Awards go to eligible applications above the minimum score, in score order, within the pool and the concentration limits. |
| Matching | planned | The area eligibility and general eligibility rules. Matched contributions need public receipts. | Scored like a targeted grant. The award may not exceed the matched contributions times the ratio. |

## Areas and eligibility

- **Public repositories** (`public-repositories`): The repository is public, and anyone can read and clone it without an account. The code or content is under an OSI-approved or Creative Commons license. Where it is hosted does not matter: forkmesh.com, a self-hosted mirror, or another forge.
- **Volunteer mirrors** (`volunteer-mirrors`): The applicant operates a public mirror, relay, or gateway that people other than the operator have used for at least 60 days. The service publishes a health endpoint or status page.
- **Accessibility** (`accessibility`): The work improves a ForkMesh-compatible client, website, or document against WCAG 2.2 AA or the platform's accessibility guidelines. The plan includes testing with at least one person who uses assistive technology.
- **Documentation** (`documentation`): Public documentation, translations, or tutorials under an open license.
- **Education** (`education`): Courses, workshops, or learning materials about decentralized collaboration, under an open license and free to attend or read.
- **Ecosystem tooling** (`ecosystem-tooling`): An independent client, relay, index, verifier, or library with a public https source under an OSI-approved license. A certification badge is welcome but not required.

Every application must also meet these rules:

- Individuals, informal groups, and organizations in any jurisdiction the funder can lawfully pay may apply.
- Applying, being reviewed, and being paid need no ForkMesh account, plan, client, wallet, or token.
- The operator of forkmesh.com and people it pays are not eligible for awards.
- A round's funders and reviewers are not eligible in that round.
- Work whose use requires a paid plan on any ForkMesh-operated service is not eligible.

## Selection criteria

| Criterion | Weight | What reviewers score |
| --- | --- | --- |
| public-benefit | 30 | How many people outside the applicant benefit, and how directly. |
| feasibility | 20 | Whether the milestones, budget, and schedule are realistic for the applicant. |
| accessibility-inclusion | 20 | Whether the work serves people with disabilities, low bandwidth, or languages the ecosystem under-serves. |
| sustainability | 15 | Whether the result keeps working, or is handed on, after the award ends. |
| decentralization | 15 | Whether the work adds a new operator, region, implementation, or maintainer, and so reduces concentration. |

Reviewers score each criterion from 0 to 5. An award needs a weighted score of at least 60 out of 100, from at least 3 reviewers, of whom at least 1 is not a ForkMesh maintainer.

- Conflicts: A reviewer who is the applicant, or who shares an employer or funder with the applicant, must record a recusal and must not score that application. Any other conflict a reviewer declares is recorded and recused the same way. A funder never reviews, never chooses a recipient, and may restrict a gift only to an area.
- Concentration: at most 25% of a round's awards to one recipient. More than 50% to one area, or more than 50% of the pool from one funder, must be addressed in community review.
- Administrative cost: at most 10% of the pool. Administrative cost covers payment fees, accounting, and reviewer stipends. It is published per round before applications open.

## Payment rails

| Rail | Kind | Recurring | ForkMesh account or plan needed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Bank transfer (SEPA, ACH, or international wire) | conventional | yes | no |
| Open Collective, through the recipient's own fiscal host | conventional | yes | no |
| Liberapay | conventional | yes | no |
| Solana transfer to an address the recipient controls | on-chain | no | no |

## Independence

An award, donation, or sponsorship pays for work. It never changes who can reach a repository, what an identity may do, who votes, or what the network requires.

Awards never grant: `repository-access`, `identity-rights`, `protocol-votes`, `governance-seats`, `ranking-or-discovery`, `moderation-outcomes`, `required-network-behavior`, `hosted-product-use`.

The only obligations an award may carry: `milestone-report`, `outcome-report`, `open-license`, `accessibility-statement`, `public-receipt`, `conflict-disclosure`.

## Rounds

| Round | Title | Pilot | Stage | Pool | Awarded | Disbursed | Recipients |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PIF-0001](#pif-0001) | Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation | yes | draft | not published | USD 0 | USD 0 | 0 |

### PIF-0001

**Pilot round: volunteer mirrors, accessibility, and documentation**

Milestone grants and matching for people who run public mirrors, make ForkMesh-compatible clients and documents accessible, and write open documentation. Recipients choose their own payment rail.

- Areas: volunteer-mirrors, accessibility, documentation. Offers: targeted-grant, matching.
- Payment rails: bank-transfer, open-collective, liberapay, solana.
- Apply through: An issue labelled funding-application on any forge mirror of forkmesh/forkmesh. Email to the address in the round announcement, for applicants who cannot apply in public.
- Timeline: announced —; applicationsOpen —; applicationsClose —; selectionsPublished —; finalReportDue —; reported —
- Pool: not published. Administrative cost: not published.

The round opens when:

- A funder commits the pool and publishes the amount, source, conflicts, and any area restriction.
- Administrative cost is published and stays within 10% of the pool.
- At least three reviewers with current governance disclosures are seated, and at least one is not a ForkMesh maintainer.
- The application window is announced with at least 21 days to apply.

#### Funders

None committed.

#### Reviewers

None seated.

#### Applications and selections

No applications.

#### Conflict handling

No conflicts recorded.

#### Milestones and disbursements

No awards.

#### Community review

Window: — to —.

#### Outcome report

Not published.

> No funder has committed a pool and no reviewer is seated, so the round has not opened. It has no applications, selections, or disbursements to report.

pages.markdown:
# terminology.json

Machine-readable data file.

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "guide": "docs/terminology.md",
  "approvedTerms": [
    {
      "term": "repository",
      "definition": "A Git repository: its files, commits, branches, and tags, together with its issues, pull requests, and releases.",
      "insteadOf": ["project (for source code)"],
      "notes": "Use \"repo\" only in URLs, command names, and space-constrained labels."
    },
    {
      "term": "branch",
      "definition": "A named line of commits in a repository. The default branch is the one a clone checks out."
    },
    {
      "term": "commit",
      "definition": "A recorded change to a repository, identified by its hash."
    },
    {
      "term": "fork",
      "definition": "Your own copy of a repository under your account. Change it freely and open pull requests back to the original."
    },
    {
      "term": "clone",
      "definition": "Download a repository with Git, for example git clone https://forkmesh.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY."
    },
    {
      "term": "issue",
      "definition": "A tracked bug report, task, or request in a repository."
    },
    {
      "term": "pull request",
      "definition": "A proposal to merge commits from one branch or fork into another, with its discussion, checks, and reviews.",
      "insteadOf": ["merge request", "patch (for a proposed change)"],
      "notes": "\"PR\" is acceptable in compact labels and CLI output; spell it out in sentences."
    },
    {
      "term": "review",
      "definition": "An approval, a request for changes, or comments on a pull request.",
      "insteadOf": ["peer approval"]
    },
    {
      "term": "mirror",
      "definition": "A complete copy of a repository on another host that stays in sync and can serve clones when the source is offline.",
      "insteadOf": ["peer", "seed node", "mesh node", "replica (for public copies)"]
    },
    {
      "term": "seed",
      "definition": "The first push that fills a new mirror from an existing copy. After seeding, the mirror keeps itself in sync.",
      "insteadOf": ["seeder"]
    },
    {
      "term": "trusted maintainer",
      "definition": "A person the repository owner trusts to merge, release, and change settings. Their signed actions are accepted by every mirror.",
      "insteadOf": ["delegate"]
    },
    {
      "term": "host",
      "definition": "A computer that serves repositories: your own machine, a server you run, or a ForkMesh-managed host."
    },
    {
      "term": "desktop app",
      "definition": "The ForkMesh desktop application. Say \"desktop app (Qt)\" only where build instructions need the toolkit.",
      "insteadOf": ["Qt client", "Qt app", "Qt desktop node"]
    }
  ],
  "protocolTerms": [
    {"term": "node", "explanation": "A running copy of ForkMesh (desktop app, server, or phone) that signs and syncs on behalf of an account."},
    {"term": "relay", "explanation": "The ForkMesh web service that routes requests to healthy mirrors. It is not the canonical Git store."},
    {"term": "refs attestation", "explanation": "The signed list of branch and tag commits a mirror must match before it can serve a repository."},
    {"term": "signed repository proof", "explanation": "A host's signature over the branch and tag commits it serves."},
    {"term": "commit DAG", "explanation": "Commit history: each commit points at its parents."},
    {"term": "CRDT / fold", "explanation": "How signed issue and pull request events merge into one current state without conflicts."},
    {"term": "lease", "explanation": "A short-lived claim that stops two hosts from processing the same issue or pull request at once."},
    {"term": "outbox", "explanation": "The queue of signed events waiting to be delivered to other hosts."},
    {"term": "opaque replica", "explanation": "An encrypted copy of a private repository that a host stores without being able to read it."},
    {"term": "federation", "explanation": "Sharing repository activity with the fediverse (Mastodon and other ActivityPub servers)."}
  ],
  "discouragedTerms": [
    {
      "id": "merge-request",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bmerge(?: |-)requests?\\b",
      "preferred": "pull request",
      "reason": "ForkMesh uses the GitHub-style name for proposed changes; the /pulls route and API already say pull."
    },
    {
      "id": "peer-approval",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bpeer approvals?\\b",
      "preferred": "review",
      "reason": "Approving a pull request is a review."
    },
    {
      "id": "peer-to-peer",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bpeer(?: |-)to(?: |-)peer\\b|\\bP2P\\b",
      "preferred": "independent hosts, or mirrors",
      "reason": "The promise is independent hosts and mirrors; peer-to-peer suggests file sharing and hides Git workflows."
    },
    {
      "id": "qt-product-name",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bQt (?:desktop(?: node| app)?|client|app)\\b",
      "preferred": "ForkMesh desktop app",
      "reason": "Qt is the UI toolkit, not a product name users recognize."
    },
    {
      "id": "delegate",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bdelegates?\\b",
      "preferred": "trusted maintainer",
      "reason": "Delegate is protocol jargon from other decentralized forges."
    },
    {
      "id": "seed-node",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bseed(?:ers?| nodes?)\\b",
      "preferred": "mirror",
      "reason": "Seed is the first push into a mirror; the copy itself is a mirror."
    },
    {
      "id": "mesh-node",
      "category": "replace",
      "pattern": "\\bmesh (?:nodes?|peers?)\\b",
      "preferred": "host, or mirror",
      "reason": "Users choose hosts and mirrors; the mesh is an implementation detail."
    },
    {
      "id": "attestation",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\battestations?\\b",
      "preferred": "signed branch and tag state, or explain the term where it appears",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "refs-pin",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\brefs? pins?\\b|\\bsigrefs\\b",
      "preferred": "signed branch and tag state",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "commit-dag",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\bDAG\\b",
      "caseSensitive": true,
      "preferred": "commit history",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "crdt",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\bCRDTs?\\b",
      "caseSensitive": true,
      "preferred": "conflict-free merging of issue and pull request events",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "gossip",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\bgossip(?:ed|ing|s)?\\b",
      "preferred": "sync between hosts",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "lease",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "(?<![-\\w])leases?\\b",
      "preferred": "claim, or explain the term where it appears",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    },
    {
      "id": "outbox",
      "category": "explain",
      "pattern": "\\boutbox(?:es)?\\b",
      "preferred": "delivery queue",
      "reason": "Protocol term; allowed on a primary surface only next to a plain explanation."
    }
  ],
  "primarySurfaces": [
    "README.md",
    "docs/README.md",
    "docs/getting-started.md",
    "docs/product-promise.md",
    "docs/hosted-repositories.md",
    "docs/repository-imports.md",
    "www/public/index.html",
    "www/public/about.html",
    "www/public/press.html",
    "www/public/careers.html",
    "www/public/features.html",
    "www/public/desktop.html",
    "www/public/docs/index.html",
    "www/public/docs/onboarding/index.html",
    "www/public/docs/product-promise/index.html",
    "app/public/start.html",
    "app/public/signup.html",
    "app/public/login.html",
    "app/public/dashboard/partials/**/*.html",
    "app/public/dashboard/js/*.js"
  ],
  "extendedAuditSurfaces": [
    "www/public/**/*.html",
    "docs/**/*.md",
    "app/public/**/*.html",
    "desktop/src/*.cpp",
    "desktop/src/*.h"
  ],
  "allowances": [
    {
      "path": "www/public/about.html",
      "term": "peer-to-peer",
      "reason": "A team member's biography names their field of interest, not the product."
    },
    {
      "path": "docs/repository-imports.md",
      "term": "merge-request",
      "reason": "Names the GitLab source object an import reads."
    },
    {
      "path": "docs/hosted-repositories.md",
      "term": "attestation",
      "explanation": "the signed list of branch and tag commits",
      "reason": "Explains what a public read is routed against for people pushing to a web-created repository."
    },
    {
      "path": "app/public/dashboard/js/02-helpers.js",
      "term": "attestation",
      "explanation": "runner signed under a router-issued grant naming one of these models",
      "reason": "Names the ForkMesh-Attestation commit trailer a pull rule requires and says who signs it."
    }
  ],
  "compatibilityAliases": [
    {
      "id": "repo-pulls-record",
      "kind": "route",
      "resolver": "repo_alias_redirect",
      "alias": "/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pulls/NUMBER",
      "canonical": "/OWNER/REPOSITORY/pull/NUMBER",
      "policy": "Permanent 308 that keeps the query and any section such as /files; never removed. One pull request lives at /OWNER/REPOSITORY/pull/NUMBER and the list stays at /OWNER/REPOSITORY/pulls, as on GitHub."
    },
    {

      "kind": "route",

    },
    {

    },
    {

      "kind": "route",

    },
```
